caseno:
Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2199 of 2011 
with 
Civil Petition Nos. 1671-1672 and 2198 of 2011.
parties:
Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza ------ Petitioner. (In CP No. 2199 of 2011)
Vs.
Anwarul Hasan and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
"Respondent Nos.1-5 of Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal (CP) Nos.2199 of 2011 and 1672 of 2011 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.81 of 2006 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka impleading the petitioner of CPNo.2199 of 2011, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, son of late Yeadul Hossian of plot No.34(old), 113 (New), B1ock-C WN(B), Gulshan Model Town, Gulshan, Dhaka as defendant No.3 and another Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza describing him as the son of Md Hossain, subsequently, as son of late Md Yeadul Hossain (in Bengali it was written “পরবর্তীতে পরিবর্তিত) House No.31, Lane No.2, Section-6/A, Mirpur, Dhaka as defendant No.2; MA Hashem, petitioner of CP Nos. 1671 and 1672 of 2011 as defendant No.1 and MNH Bulu as defendant No.4 and Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (RAJUK), represented by its Chairman and its other officials as defendant Nos.5-8 and Eastern Housing Ltd. as defendant No.9 for the following reliefs: 

 5. Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar applied to RAJUK on 30-1- 2001 to change the character and nature of the suit plot from residential to commercial plot. RAJUK by its letter dated 14-8-2001 asked Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar to pay Taka 38,28,125 as conversion fee and accordingly, he paid the said amount and the suit plot was converted as a commercial plot from residential one. Thereafter, Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar gave a power of attorney to Eastern Housing Limited, a company of Islam group on 21-12-2003 vide No.15920 dated 21-12-2003 for constructing a commercial building on the suit plot with the power to sell and to do other necessary things. RAJUK duly approved the said power of attorney- Eastern Housing Limited as the attorney of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar, got a plan passed by RAJUK on 8-2-2003 for constructing a 5th (৬ষ্ঠ তলা) storied building. As per the approved plan, while Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar through his attorney, Eastern Housing Limited, was going to start the construction work in the middle of November, 2003, he got the information that defendant No.1, MA Hashem (petitioner of CP Nos.1671 and 1672 of 2011) in order to grab the suit plot illegally, was engaged in forging papers by using his name (Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza) showing his address at House No.31, Lane No.2, Section 6/A, Mirpur, Dhaka. On coming to know about the said information, the plaintiffs' father Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar published a caution notice (সর্তক বিজ্ঞপ্তি) in the daily Janakantha, the Ittefaq, the Observer, the Inquilab and the Protham Alo on 18-11-2003 to the effect that he was the actual owner and was in possession of the suit plot and he entered into a contract with Eastern Housing Limited for constructing a commercial building thereon, and if anyone claimed the suit plot by creating any forged papers using . his name, he would not be responsible by such deed. Long after 1 (one) month of the publication of the said caution notice (notice was published on 18-11-2003) defendant No.1 published a protest notice in the daily Janakantha on 10-12- 2003 that defendant No.2, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, son of Md Hossain of Mirpur was the actual Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and he entered into an agreement with him on 29-12- 2002 to sell the suit plot to him and handed over the original documents to him at the time of execution of the agreement. On seeing the said protest notice, the plaintiffs' father became astonished as all the original documents regarding the lease of the suit plot, such as: the letter of allotment, the original lease deed by RAJUK, the original chalans by which installments were paid against the plot, the original letter of delivery of possession of the suit plot, the rent receipts showing payment of rents, mutation with the City Corporation and payment of tax, the lease agreements with the tenants, the bills showing payment of water, electricity and gas, were with him and now with the plaintiffs as his heirs. Father's name of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar was never Md Hossain, but Yeadul Hossain. In the circumstances, the plaintiffs' father being accompanied by two officers of Eastern Housing Limited, namely: Md Amjadul Haque and Md Emdadul Haque, went to the office of defendant No.1 at Sena Kallyan Bhavan on 10-12-2003 at 4 PM along with the documents mentioned above in respect of the suit plot, his identity card and by showing all those papers tried to convince defendant No.1 that Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur(supra), son of late Md Hossain with whom he had allegedly entered into a contract to purchase the suit plot, was a fake person and he (the plaintiffs' father) was the actual Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and was the owner of the suit plot and was in possession thereof. On hearing the plaintiffs' father Engineer Shamsul Kabir Hurnayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar and seeing his papers in respect of the suit plot and his identity card, defendant NO.1 was sure and certain that the plaintiffs father was the actual Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and was the actual owner of the suit plot, he assured him that he would not harass the plaintiffs father by claiming the suit plot on the basis of said agreement. But it was a matter of sorrow that defendant No.1 after coming to know from the plaintiffs father that the actual name of his father was Md Yeadul Hossain not Mohammad Hossain published a corrigendum in the daily Janakantha on 11-12-2003 that father's name of his vendor; Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, was Yeadul Hossain, it was wrongly written as Md Hossain in the protest notice published in the daily Janakantha on 10-12-2003. 

 6. The plaintiffs' father died on 2-2-2004 while living at 157, Bara Moghbazar. As the plaintiffs mother died before the death of their father, they became the 16 annas owner of the suit plot. After the death of the plaintiffs father, they also executed and registered three powers of attorney in favour of Eastern Housing Limited keeping in tact the terms on which their father gave the powers of attorney for constructing the commercial building and Eastern Housing Limited has been possessing the suit plot on behalf of the plaintiffs on the basis of the power of attorney. Since defendant No.1 claimed ownership of the suit plot through defendant No.2 (another Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza) denying the plaintiffs' father as the actual Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, they approached the Ward Commissioner of Ward No.53 for giving a certificate to the effect that they were the heirs of actual Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza. The Ward Commissioner himself enquired the matter physically on the spot (সরে জমিনে) and found that the plaintiffs were the heirs of actual late Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and issued a certificate of heirs-ship “ওয়ারিশান সার্টিফিকেট” on 16-3-2004. In the mean-time, on 18-3-2004, the plaintiffs through their attorney, Eastern Housing Limited, could know about the filing of Title Suit No.51 of 2004 in the Court of First Joint District Judge, Dhaka by defendant No.1 MA Hashem on 8-2-2004, i.e. 6(six) days after the death of their father for Specific Performance of Contract on the basis of a bainapatra dated 29-12-2002 created by using the name of their father late Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar through a fake person showing his address at House No.31, Lane No.2, Section 6/A, Mirpur (The plaintiffs father died on 2-2-2004) showing the value of the suit plot at Taka 1,65,00,000 (one crore sixty five lakh) only though it was valued at Taka 15,00,00,000 (fifteen crore). On coming to know about the filing of the said suit (Title Suit No.51 of 2004) by defendant No.1, the plaintiffs as the heirs of late Engineer Shamsul KabirHumayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar filed an application on 20-3-2004 under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the meantime, Mr M Kutubuddin, learned Advocate for the plaintiffs on going through the record of the suit (Title Suit No.51 of 2004) found that the service return of summons of the suit on defendant No.1 (Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur) had not been filed with the record. In the circumstances, the plaintiffs' learned Advocate enquired the matter in the nejarat and found that summons of the suit had been shown to have been served upon defendant No.1, i. e. fake Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur on 29-3-2004 by the process server, Mehedi Hassan, in presence of the witnesses mentioned in the service return. However, the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs collected a photostat copy of the service return from the process server, Md Mehedi Hasan, from where it was found that at the time of service of the summons upon defendant No.1, on 29-3-2004 (Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur), he was shown alive and the summons was received by him by signing in his own hand. The learned Advocate of the plaintiffs approached the learned Advocate for defendant No.1 for giving him, the photostat copies of the documents filed in support of his case, i.e. in Title Suit No.51 of 2004 and then he gave him the photostat copies of the documents including the deed of agreement dated 29-12-2002 and the legal notice; on going through the documents supplied to their learned Advocate, the plaintiffs became sure that those were created fraudulently in a very tactful manner (অত্যন্ত সুকৌশলে). An officer of the plaintiffs' attorney, Eastern Housing Limited went to the address of defendant No.2 of the instant suit, who is defendant No.1 of Title Suit No.51 of 1984, on 25-4-2004 and on enquiry could ascertain that it was a 3(three) storied (তিন তলা) building and the actual owner of the building was one Md Sekander Ali. On query Md Sekander All told that no one named Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza (defendant No.2), lived in the house. Defendant No.1 (of the instant suit) filed Title Suit No.51 of 2004 for specific performance of contract by creating forged papers in order to grab the suit plot by using the name of the plaintiffs father showing him a resident of Mirpur and got the summons served upon him. There was no existence of the witnesses mentioned in the service return of the summons of defendant No.1. The plaintiffs as the heirs of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar filed Succession Case No.439 of 2004 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Third Court, Dhaka in order to withdraw the money left behind by their father and they proved that they were the actual heirs of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza Accordingly, succession certificate was issued in their names on 18-5-2004 and they withdrew the money kept by their father in various banks and organizations without any objection from any quarters within the knowledge of defendant Nos.1-4. 

 7. The learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka on hearing the application of the plaintiffs dated 20-3-2004 for adding them as defendants in Title Suit No.51 of 2004 by his order dated 15-7-2004 substituted them as the heirs of fake Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, i.e, defendant No.1 instead of adding them as the heirs of late Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar although Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur was alive till then. Against the order dated 15-7-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, in Title Suit No.51 of 2004, the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No.358 of 2004 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Additional District Judge, Seventh Court, Dhaka who heard the revision application allowed the same and set-aside the order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and added the plaintiffs as the defendants as the heirs oflate Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar. Challenging the said order of the learned Additional District Judge, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.51 of 2004 (defendant No.1 of the instant suit) filed Civil Revision No.4608 of 2004 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 18-7-2005 made the Rule absolute and rejected the application of the plaintiffs for adding them as defendants in their own capacity as the heirs of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar and thus they remained in the suit as the heirs of fake Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur as defendant Nos.1 (a)-1(e). The plaintiffs' father late Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza was the resident of 157, Bara Moghbazar and he always resided there permanently and he never resided at House No.31, Lane No.2, Section-6/A, Mirpur or in any other house and even not in the suit plot. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, i.e. defendant No.2 of the instant suit (defendant No.1 in Title Suit No.51 of 2004) was an imaginary person created by defendant NO.1 of the instant suit. Defendant No.1 in order to grab the suit plot through fraud and forgery created the bainapatra on 29-12-2002 showing defendant No.2 of the instant suit as his vendor. After obtaining the certified copy of the judgment of Civil Revision No.4608 of 2004, on 28-11-2005, Md Amjadul Haque, an officer of the plaintiff’s attorney, Eastern Housing Limited met defendant No.1 again and requested him either to withdraw Title Suit No.51 of 2004 filed by him or not to prose- cute the same, but he refused to concede to the request and further told that he would prosecute the suit. On 26-2-2006, when Emdadul Haque, another employee of the plaintiffs' attorney went to RAJUK's office to enquire about the file of the suit plot, its Estate Officer handed over him the photostat copy of the plaint of Title Suit No.176 of 2004 of the same Court, i.e. the First Joint District Judge and the documents filed therewith (the suit was filed on 26-2-2006) and informed him that another fake Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza filed the said suit showing his address at the suit plot claiming to be its owner. The suit was filed as he failed to obtain permission from RAJUK to sell the suit plot to defendant No.4 on the basis of an agreement allegedly entered by him with defendant No.4 on 18-1-2004. Defendant Nos.2 and 3 are fake Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and none of them was the owner of the suit plot and was never in possession thereof and the bainapatras created by them were collusive, ineffective, illegal and were mere paper transactions. The bainapatras created by the said defendants were not binding upon the plaintiffs or their father late Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar. The creation of two bainapatras by two fake Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and the other documents created cloud over the plaintiffs' title in the suit plot and also their parentage for which they were compelled to file the suit. The agreement dated 29-12-2002 being a forged one was not binding upon the plaintiffs and defendant No.1 was liable to be proceeded with under section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure after disposal of the suit for using the forged agreement in Court. 

 8. Defendant No.1, MA Hashem (hereinafter referred to as the defendant) contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint and con- tending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintain- able in its present form. The plaintiffs had no cause of action to file the suit and the same was also barred by limitation. The plaintiffs' father got allotment of the suit plot from the then DIT now RAJUK on 2-3-1962 vide Memo No.DIT/ Gulshan/2409. Lease deed was executed and registered on 1-8-1962 being deed No.7194 and possession of the suit plot was delivered to him. The plaintiffs' father remained in possession of the suit plot by mutating-his name and paying rents to the Government and also by opening holding number with the Dhaka City Corporation. The plaintiffs' father created a temporary structure on the suit plot and while he had been in possession thereof, he entered into an agreement with the defendant on 29-12-2002 for selling the same at Taka 1,65,00,000 and on receipt of a sum of Taka 35,00,000 in presence of the witness on the same date handed over the original deed of the suit plot to him on the condition that after obtaining per- mission from RAJUK and the other authorities, he would register the deed on receipt of the balance consideration. It was further agreed that the plaintiffs' father would pay the gain tax, stamp duty, registration fees and other expenses necessary for registration of the deed. RAJUK was informed about the said bainapatra on 6-1-2003. The defendant by a letter dated 1-8-2003 requested the plaintiffs' father to register the kabala quickly obtaining permission from RAJUK which was received by him on 3-8-2003. The plaintiffs' father by a letter dated 11-8-2003 informed the defendant that he could not take step for registration of the kabala for various physical and mental problems. He also requested the defendant to pay Taka 5,00,000 more and accordingly, the defendant paid him Taka 3,20,000 by a cheque dated 12-8-2003 which was duly encashed. But in spite of receipt of the said money (Taka 3,20,000), the plaintiffs' father did not take any step for permission from RAJUK to sell the suit plot. As per terms of the agreement, the plaintiffs' father was supposed to register the deed before 28-12-2003 on receipt of the balance consideration, but he did not do so. In the circumstances, the defendant requested the plaintiffs' father on 29-12-2002 in presence of the witnesses to register the deed on receipt of the balance money, but he refused to register the deed. Thereafter, on 1-12-2003, the defendant through his lawyer sent a legal notice to the plaintiffs' father requesting him to execute and register the sale deed taking all necessary steps in the matter and on receipt of the balance consideration of Taka 1,26,80,000 which was duly received by him on 3-12-2003. On 8-12-2003, the defendant could know that one Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza in a notice dated 18-11- 2003 published in the daily Janakantha stated that he did not enter into any contract with anyone for selling the suit plot and that he started construction work therein by obtaining a plan from RAJUK through a contract entered into with Eastern Housing Limited. The defendant did not know about the notice published by Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza in the daily Janakantha dated 18-11-2003. However, subsequently, the defendant published a protest notice in the daily Janakantha on 10-12-2003 denying the contents of the notice dated 18-11-2003. But after publication of the protest notice, it was found that father's name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza was mistakenly, (ভুল বশতঃ) written as only Md Hossain in place of Md Yeadul Hossain for which letter was written to the daily Janakantha to publish the father's name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza correctly and accordingly, on 11- 12-2003, corrigendum of the protest was published stating the father's name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as Md Yeadul Hossain. After publication of the protest notice, the defendant went to RAJUK and on seeing the record found that a plan was passed by it, but name and address of the person was not available in the record. Since the plaintiffs are the legal heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, they were bound by the terms of the bainapatra executed by their father. After the death of the plaintiffs' father, on 2-2-2004, they filed an application in Title Suit No.51 of 2004 on 20-3-2004 for adding them as defendants in the suit. The defendant who was the plaintiff of Title Suit No.51 of2004 also filed a counter application in the suit supporting the application of the present plaintiffs to add them as defendants in the suit. The application was allowed on 15-7-2004. Against the said order, the plaintiffs (of the instant suit) filed Civil Revision No.358 of 2004 before the District Judge, Dhaka which was allowed. Against the said order allowing the civil revision, the defendant filed Civil Revision No.4608 of 2004 before the High Court Division. The Rule in the civil revision was made absolute and the judgment and order passed by the Additional. District Judge, Seventh Court, Dhaka was set-aside and thus, the plaintiffs remained substituted as defendant Nos.1(a)-1e) in place of defendant No.1 and got chance to contest Title Suit No.51 of 2004, so there was no necessity on the part of the plaintiffs to file the instant suit. 

 9. Defendant No.3, another Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, who also claimed to be the son of late Yeadul Hossain also filed a written statement to contest the suit. In his written statement, it was contended, inter alia, that the plaintiffs had no cause of action to file the suit and the suit was not maintainable in its present form. The suit was also barred by limitation. Defendant No.3 joined the then C & B department under the Ministry of Communications in 1952 as an Assistant Engineer and in 1960 was appointed as Executive Engineer (Design). While in service, the defendant applied to the then DIT now RAJUK to allot him a plot at Gulshan and on his application, he was allotted the suit plot vide allotment letter No.2409 dated 21-3-1962. After the defendant paid the price of the suit plot by installments, possession thereof was delivered to him and then the standard lease deed was executed and registered in his favour on 1-8-1962 being deed No.7198 and thus the defendant became the sixteen annas owner of the suit plot. Defendant No.3 mutated his name with the Government record, City Corporation and also recorded his name with the various utility services authorities, such as: electricity, WASA, Titas gas in respect of the suit plot and has been in possession thereof by paying rents, taxes and bills. In the last RS record and Metropolitan Survey, the suit plot was correctly recorded in the name of defendant No.3. The defendant applied to RAJUK on 25-1-1996 for permission to construct building on the suit plot and accordingly, RAJUK gave him permission to construct a two storied building vide Memo No.4452 dated 29-10-1996. Defendant No.3 constructed a two storied building on the suit plot and started living there. He being in urgent need of money entered into a contract for selling the suit plot with defendant No.4, MNH. Bulu at Taka 2,35,00,000 (two crore thirty five lakh) and on receipt of a sum of Taka 5,00,000 as advance executed a bainapatra in his favour. The defendant applied to RAJUK on 18-2- 2004 for sale permission of the suit plot, but RAJUK did not pay any heed to his said prayer. He sent four legal notices to defendant Nos.5- 8(RAJUK and its officials) separately on 20-4- 2004 which they received on 22-4-2004, but they did not reply to the notices. In the circumstances, the defendant was compelled to file Title Suit No.176 of 2004 in the same Court on 31-5-2004. On receipt of the summons of the said suit, the defendants appeared therein on 28-8-2004, but did not file any written statement for. a long time and when the suit was fixed for ex-parte hearing suddenly on 8-3-2006, the defendants have filed written statement and are contesting the suit which is still pending for hearing. Defendant No.3 applied to the Parliamentary Standing Committee of the Ministry of Housing and Works for giving back possession of his house (the suit plot). On such application, a Sub-Committee was formed with Joynal Abedin Farooqui as its Convener and Chairman, RAJUK as its member Secretary and they were requested to take necessary steps in the matter. The Sub-Committee decided to hold a Commission in RAJUK's Building on 25-7-2004, but due to the terrorist activities of the plaintiffs, the next date was fixed on 28-7-2004 (Title Suit No.176 of 2004 was filed by the defendant on 31- 5-2004). On the date, defendant No.3 appeared before the Sub-Committee and gave his statement, but none appeared on behalf of the plaintiffs and defendant No. I. After hearing the Commission decided that since defendant No.3 was a government servant, RAJUK would collect particulars as to his job from the concerned Department and then the Standing Committee would be informed about the decision of the sub-commit- tee. On 16-9-2004, the Secretary, RAJUK requested the concerned section of the Ministry of Communications to send the information in respect of the service of defendant No.3. The Superintendent Engineer, Accounts Department (স ও জ) of the Ministry of Communications sent information on 5-3-2005 from where it appeared that defendant No.3, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza joined the Design Department-1 of C & B in project circle No.2 as Assistant Engineer on 19-8- 1952 and was promoted to the post of Executive Engineer (Design Department) and Building project circle on 19-7-1960. From the report, it further appeared that the accounts maintained with the Department showed that defendant NO.3 had withdrawn his salary and other allowances upto 18-8-1963. In the report, the address of defendant No.3 was shown at T-75, Railway Colony, Babupara, Sub-Division, Ishwardy. The report proved that the defendant was the actual Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and the plaintiffs' father, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, was a fake person. The plaintiffs and defendant No.1 both claiming to be the heirs and “বায়না গৃহিতা” respectively of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza were conspiring to grab the property of defendant No.3, actual Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza by resorting to forgery. The defendant paid the lease money to RAJUK and he was in his possession of the original letter of allotment of the suit plot, the receipts of the payment of installments against the suit plot, the letter of delivering possession of the suit plot, the original lease deed, the permission letter to undertake pucca construction on the suit plot, the approved plan and design. If the plaintiffs or their attorney filed any of the above-mentioned documents, those would be false and forged. The plaintiffs had no right, title and possession in the suit plot and it is the defendant who has been possessing the suit plot as the lessee of RAJUK himself and through his men. The plaintiffs, being instigated (প্ররোচিত) and influenced  (প্রভাবিত) by their attorney, Eastern Housing Limited, created some false and forged papers showing a fake Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as their father and then in collusion with defendant Nos.5-8 filed the false suit as a test case just to harass and cause financial loss to defendant No.3, actual Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza. 

 10. Defendant Nos.5-8 (RAJUK and its officials) in their written statement contended, inter alia, that the suit plot was allotted to Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, the predecessor- in-interest of the plaintiffs by the then DIT and after he paid the installments against the plot, possession thereof was delivered to him. And then the lease deed was executed and registered on 1-8-1962 being deed No.7198 and the lessee after getting possession thereof took water, electricity and gas connection therein. The lessee also mutated his name in the concerned tahsil office and municipality and paid rents, taxes and other utility service bills. While the plaintiffs' predecessor-in-interest had been in possession of the suit plot, he applied to RAJUK for approving a plan and accordingly, a plan was approved. Then he constructed the building on the suit plot and remained in possession thereof through 'bharatias'. Subsequently, Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza entered into an agreement with Eastern Housing Limited for making construction of a multistoried building on the suit plot after obtaining due permission from RAJUK and also appointed Eastern Housing Limited as his attorney by executing and registering a power of attorney on 21-12-2003 being No.15942 and delivered possession of the suit plot to it. Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza died on 2-2-2004 while residing at 157, Bara Moghbazar owned by his wife leaving behind the plaintiffs as his two sons and 3(three) daughters and their names have been duly mutated with RAJUK as the lessees. Neither the original lessee, Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza nor after his death, the plaintiff sentered into any contract with MNH Bulu or anybody else for selling the suit plot and there was no proof of filing any such paper with RAJUK. MNH Bulu in order to grab the suit plot created an imaginary story of entering into an agreement with a fake Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as a lessee of RAJUK long after the death of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza on 2-2-2004 and got Title Suit No.176 of 2004 filed through him for getting permission to sell the suit plot to him. RAJUK has been contesting Title Suit No.176 of 2004 by filing written statement denying the statements made in the plaint and stating the actual facts. One MA Hashem, son of late Alhaj Abdul Aziz also filed Title Suit No.51 of 2004 in the same Court for specific performance of contract on the basis of a bainapatra impleading one Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as a lessee and others as defendants to grab the suit plot and RAJUK as defendant No.3 has been contesting the suit by filing written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint and stating actual facts. There was no existence of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as claimed in the plaint of Title Suit Nos.176 of 2004 and 510f 2004 with the record of RAJUK and Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs was the valid lessee of the suit plot and after his death on 2-2-2004, the same has been mutated in the name of the plaintiffs as its owners in the records of RAJUK and, in fact, they are the actual owners and are in possession thereof. RAJUK is the actual owner of the suit plot. No application was filed to RAJUK by the actual lessee for permission to sell the suit plot either to MNH Bulu of Title Suit No. 176 of 2004 or MA Hashem of Title Suit No.51 of 2004. 

 11. The petitioner of CP No.1671 of 2011 who was defendant No.1 in Title Suit No:81 of 2006 filed Title Suit No.51 of 2004 in the same Court (Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka) for specific performance of contract impleading Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of House No.31, Lane No.2, Section 6/A, Mirpur as principal defendant No.1 and one Mr Akhtaruzzaman, Director Eastern Housing Limited as principal defendant No.2, the Chairman, RAJUK and the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka as pro-forma defendant Nos.3 and 4 (although in law there is nothing as principal or pro-forma defendants). 

 12. In the plaint, it was stated, inter alia, that the then DIT now RAJUK allotted the suit plot to defendant No.1 vide allotment letter No.DIT/ Gulshan /2409 dated 2-3-1962 and the lease deed was registered between RAJUK and defendant No.1 on 1-8-1962 being deed No.7198 and possession of the suit plot was delivered to him. Defendant No.1 mutated the suit plot in his name and has been possessing the same in his own right, title and interest. Defendant No.1 constructed some temporary structures on the suit plot and paid rents and taxes regularly to the Government and also opened separate holding with Dhaka City Corporation. Defendant No.1 entered into an agreement with the plaintiff on 29-12-2002 for sale of the suit plot at a consideration of Taka' 1,65,00,000 (Taka one crore sixty five lakh) only and a deed of agreement for sale was signed and executed on the said date on receiving Taka 35,00,000 only in cash as advance money. Defendant No.1 handed over all original documents to the plaintiff in presence of the witnesses. In the agreement, it was stipulated that defendant No.1 as the seller "shall apply for and obtain all necessary permission/clearance certificate" from RAJUK and to the other relevant authorities for sale of the suit plot in favour of the plaintiff and that the plaintiff will be responsible for payment of transfer fee to RAJUK, gain tax, stamp duty, registration fee and all other charges and incidental costs and expenses and the execution and registration of the sale deed by defendant No.1 shall be completed within one year and that the balance amount of Taka 1,30,00,000 only will be received by defendant No.1 from the plaintiff at the time of registration of the sale deed and that upon failure of defendant NO.1 to execute and register the deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff, he shall be entitled to get the sale deed executed and registered through Court. The plaintiff informed RAJUK through its Deputy Director (Estate) by letter dated 6-1-2003 about transfer of the suit plot by defendant No.1 in his favour on the basis of the said deed of agreement for sale. The plaintiff by letter dated 1-8-2003 requested defendant NO.1 to take immediate step for permission from RAJUK for registering the deed of sale in his favour. In response to the letter dated 1-8-2003, defendant No.1 informed the plaintiff by letter dated 11-8- 2003 that due to physical and mental difficulties, he could not take appropriate steps for registration of the sale deed. By the said letter (11-8-2003), defendant No.1 asked the plaintiff to make further payment of Taka 5,00,000 (Taka five lakh) only against the said deed of agreement with the assurance that he would take appropriate step immediately and would also inform the plaintiff very soon thereabout. The plaintiff paid a further sum of Taka 3,20,000 (Taka three lakh twenty thousand) only to defendant No.1 vide cheque No.1279703 dated 12-8-2003 drawn on AB Bank Ltd. Principal Branch, Dhaka, the cheque was given through a covering letter dated 12-8-2008 wherein request was made by the plaintiff to the defendant to take all necessary steps immediately so that he could register the deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff within the schedule time, that is, by 28-12-2003. Defendant No.1 was further requested to inform the plaintiff about the steps taken by him in that regard. The cheque was duly encashed by defendant No.1, but unfortunately until 1st December, 2003, he did not inform the plaintiff anything about the steps taken by him for registration of the deed of sale especially with regard to obtaining sale permission from RAJUK. In the circumstances, the plaintiff issued a notice on 1-1-2003 to defendant NO.1 through his lawyer requesting him to complete all formalities and obtain permission from RAJUK and to execute and register the deed of sale in his favour by the 20th day of December, 2003 and to receive the balance amount of Taka 1,26,80,000 only from him. In spite of the above requests and persuasions of the plaintiff, defendant No.1 failed to execute and register the deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff by 28-12-2003. Lastly on 29-12-2003, the plain- tiff in presence of the witnesses offered the balance amount to defendant No.1 and requested him to execute and register the sale deed, but the defendant refused to do so. The plaintiff to his utter shock and surprise learnt "on or about 8th December, 2003" about publication of a (বিজ্ঞপ্তি) in the daily "Janakantha", i.e. after issuance of the legal notice dated 1-12-2003 published by one Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza that he was the owner of the suit plot and he had entered into a contract with Eastern Housing Limited for constructing a building thereon and on the basis of the contract Eastern Housing Limited had already started all the works in that respect after approval of the plan by RAJUK. Thus, the plaintiff hunched a foul play in the matter for which he was compelled to publish a protest notice (বিজ্ঞপ্তি) in the daily Janakantha on 10-12-2003 protesting the aforementioned notice (বিজ্ঞপ্তি) dated 18-11-2003 and stating that the contents of the notice dated 18-11-2003 were false, imaginary and fraudulent as he became the owner of the suit plot on the basis of bainapatra entered into with him by its owner Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, son of Md Hossain and all the original documents relating to the suit plot were with him. In the protest notice, it was further stated that the fact of entering into contract by Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, original owner, was intimated to RAJUK by a letter dated 6-1-2003 which was received by RAJUK on 7-1-2003. As some mistakes occurred in the protest notice dated 10-12-2003 as to the father's name of Md Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, a corrigendum was issued stating his father's name as Md Yeadul Hossain in place of Md Hossain. Thereafter, the plaintiff could manage to look into the records of RAJUK and found his application dated 5-1-2003 was in the file and further learnt that a plan had been approved by RAJUK IMc construction on the suit plot, but the plaintiff could not collect the exact name and address of the person in whose favour or upon whose request, the alleged plan was approved by RAJUK. There had been no protest from any quarter against the protest notice issued by the plaintiff in the daily Janakantha on 10-12-2003. The plaintiff went to the suit plot on 22-12-2003 and found that some people were taking steps for construction removing the old structures and on query he learnt that they were the employees/workers of defendant No.2 who was claimed by them to be the owner of the suit plot and on hearing the same, the plaintiff Was further surprised and puzzled. The failure/ inaction/refusal of defendant No.1 to execute and register the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff in spite of the request and legal notice mentioned hereinabove and also in applying for and in obtaining permission for sale of the suit plot in favour of the plaintiff in spite of his readiness and willingness to perform his obligation under the deed of agreement compelled the plaintiff to file the suit for specific performance of contract.
