parties:
Abdur Rab Faraji and others Appellants
VS
Nur Mohammad Mia and others Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ali Reza, J: This appeal at the instance of defendants 1-6 is directed against judgment and decree dated 3-6-2008 passed by the Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Jhalakati in Title Suit 05 of 2004 decreeing the suit in part. 

 2. Respondents as plaintiffs filed Title Suit 05 of 2004 on 19-6-2004 for partition and for further declaration that the judgment and decree dated 4-4-1985 and its correction order dated 4-3-2007 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Court No. 1, Jhalakati in Title Suit 126 of 1983 is fraudulent, collusive, null and void and not binding upon-the plaintiffs. 

 4. Defendants 1-6 appeared and contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all material statements made in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit is barred by limitation and also under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It was further stated that Rashid, Hachen, Tachen, Samed, Rafizuddin, Atabar were owners in possession and they settled 9.77 acres of land at a yearly rental of 50 taka 6 anna to Abdur Rahman Faraji by registered dakhila dated 1-3-1946 but his brothers' names were wrongly inserted in RS khatian 487 along with his name. Rahman died leaving behind daughter Kulsum, wives Shamsunnessa and Rahima, sons defendants 1-6 named Rob, Sobhan, Huq, Wahid, Barek, Awal. Sons and mothers filed Title Suit 166 of 1978 on 26-4-1978 for declaration of title against the wrong record. Suit was renumbered as 389 of 1981 and 126 of 1983. Defendants 6(Ka)/6(Ga)/15-17/18(Ka)-18(Kha) /20(Ka) and plaintiffs filed compromise petition in the suit and accordingly suit was decreed on 4-4-1985 and title of Rahman's heirs was declared. Later on defendant 12 of that suit named Fulboru filed Miscellaneous Case 34 of 1985 which was allowed on 30-7-1988. Present defendants then preferred Civil Revision 186 of 1988 in the then Barishal Bench of this Division which was transferred to Dhaka High Court and renumbered as Civil Revision 10205 of 1991. Sufia is the wife of Lehaj Uddin and mother of present plaintiffs 13-18. She died and her heirs executed a deed of relinquishment on 5-5-1991 and admitted title of the present defendants. Accordingly parties entered into compromise on 5-3-1998 which was allowed and the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 remained intact and the Rule was made absolute on 25-3-1998. The case of the plaintiffs is false. Predecessor of plaintiffs 6-10 named Hachen also registered a nadabi dated 5-6-1995 admitting the title and possession of the present defendants. Hachen Ali is still alive. Meanwhile present defendants filed GR Case 31 of 1998 in which the statement of Title Suit 126 of 1983 was given. Earlier Hachen filed Miscellaneous Petition Case 213 of 1991 in which possession was found in favour of these appellant-defendants. Plaintiffs have definite knowledge of earlier Title Suit 126 of 1983. Present defendants have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land by living in their homestead and through cultivation upon payment of rent. Son of plaintiff 3 recently purchased from the defendants on 1-4-2003 admitting the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983. The suit being false is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 5. The Joint District Judge framed as many as 06(six) issues as to maintainability, defect of party, hotch potch, whether plaintiffs have title and possession in the suit land, whether the judgment dated 4-4-1985 and decree dated 9-4-1985 passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Jhalakati are binding upon the plaintiffs, whe they plaintiffs can get the relief as prayed for. 

 7. The Joint District Judge decreed the suit in part by judgment and decree dated 3-6-2008 on the finding that defendants could not offer satisfactory answer against the correctness of record of rights and records were correctly prepared and plaintiffs have acquired 3.92 acres of land through transfers and the nadabi document as claimed by defendants do not confer title and DW 1 admitted that there is only one plaintiff who was party to earlier suit thus the impugned decree is not binding upon the rest 19 plaintiffs and since plaintiffs have title in the instant suit land the decree of Title Suit 126 of 1983 passed in favour of defendants becomes inoperative. 

 9. Mr Swapon Kumar Dutta, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the plaintiffs did not make out any case as to why the decree of `Ga' schedule is fraudulent and not binding upon them and plaintiffs cannot escape from discharging such heavy onus which squarely lies upon them. RS record was wrongly prepared in the names of all sons of Sonamuddi Faraji for which settlement holder Rahman's heirs filed Title Suit 166 of 1978 renumbered as 126 of 1983 for declaration of title against such wrong record impleading other sons of Sonamuddi or their heirs and got their title declared which was affirmed by this Division in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 on 25-3-1998. That judgment was not challenged and examined by our Appellate Division and this suit was filed after 06(six) years on 19-6-2004. On the strength of such decree defendants have mutated their names and have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land upon payment of rent. Plaintiffs are never their co-sharers and this suit being false is liable to be dismissed outright. He further submits that the deeds of relinquishment executed by the then defendants in the suit and revision although do not confer title but those are strong admissions and the present plaintiffs are now estopped from denying the title of the appellants. He then submits that Title Suit 126 of 1983 was mentioned in Criminal PS Case 04 of 1986 and after a long lapse of time the instant suit for declaration against the 'Ga' schedule decree dated 4-4-1985 is barred by limitation. He then referring to `Ga' schedule decree strongly submits that the heirs of some of the defendants of earlier suit along with others filed the instant suit thus this suit suffers multifariousness because parties to earlier suit although does not require declaration of title but the rest requires such relief thus their claim is vague and suit cannot run in accordance with law. In furtherance of such submission he proceeds that the rest defendants of earlier suit who did not file the instant suit must be made defendants to protect their valuable rights but the same having been not done the instant suit suffers defect of party. He finally submits that the Joint District Judge misquoted the evidence of DW 1 and arrived at a wrong conclusion. In support of his submission he refers the cases of Subitri Bari vs Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property and other; 39 DLR 172; Rezaul Karim and others vs Shamsuzzoha and others, 49 DLR (AD) 68; Abu Naser Mohd. Wahidun Nabi and another vs Balai Roy and others, 10 MLR (AD) 121; Akitullah and others vs Zafala Begum and others, 54 DLR (AD) 74 and prays for allowing the appeal. 

 10. Mr Sarder Abul Hossain, learned Advocate on the other hand appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that the Joint District Judge upon proper appreciation of evidence has rightly passed the judgment. He draws our attention to RS record 487 and submits that the RS record has got its presumptive value and defendants could not dislodge such presumption by any convincing evidence. The Joint District Judge upon perusal of Exhibits-3-9 has correctly found that the plaintiffs are entitled to a decree in part which may not be interfered with by this Court. The claim of the defendants relying upon two nadabi documents does not deserve any consideration because those do not confer any title. He laid much emphasis on the statement of DW 1 made in cross and submits that according to the admission of DW 1 the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 is not binding upon the plaintiffs and plaintiffs have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land. He referring to the deposition of DW 1 submits that the Joint District Judge has passed the judgment upon due consideration of materials on record and the appeal is liable to be dismissed. In course of hearing Mr Hossain filed an application for amendment of the plaint on 15-3-2023 and on 30-3-2023 filed another application for production of additional evidence. In support of those applications he submits that at the time of hearing of this appeal plaintiffs have come to know some important facts and documents with regard to their title which are very much necessary for proper adjudication of the dispute and unless those are considered and allowed the respondents shall suffer irreparable loss and injury. 

 12. From reading of paragraph 2 of the plaint it appears that plaintiffs cited two auction issues. First auction was purchased by Hachen Uddin and the second one was by Gogon Ali and Mafizuddin. Plaintiffs claim their title through settlement from Gogon and Mafizuddin on the other hand defendants claim their title through settlement from Hachen Talukder and others. Plaintiffs claim that according to the settlement RS record 487 Exhibit-IX was correctly prepared in the names of six sons of Sonamuddi Faraji named Rahman, Kader, Hakim, Gani, Motaleb, Khaleque Rahman is the predecessor of contesting defendants 1-6. Plaintiffs did not produce any document of title showing settlement in their favour nor did they bother to mention the date of taking such settlement. Plaintiffs also did not produce the suit registers of those two rent suits despite availability of such documents in the concerned office. From reading of Exhibits-Kha and Kha(1) which are judgment and decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 it appears that the dispute arose in 1978 when defendants filed Title Suit 166 of 1978 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit 126 of 1983 for declaration of title against wrong entry in RS khatian 487 Exhibit-IX. In that suit the present defendants were plaintiffs and claimed that their father Rahman took settlement from Hachen and others by a registered dakhila dated 1-3-1946 Exhibit-Ka at an annual rental of 50 taka 6 anna but Rahman's brother named Gani managed to procure such wrong- record Exhibit-IX in collusion with the survey employees by dishonest means and out of greed. That suit was decreed on compromise against defendants 6(Ka)- 6(Ga)/15-17/18(Ka)-18(Gha)/20(Ka) and ex-parte against the rest. Defendants 15-18 of the earlier suit are RS tenants and consenting parties. The non-contesting defendant 12 named Fulbaru filed. Miscellaneous Case 34 of 1985 which was allowed on 30-7-1988. Present defendants filed Civil Revision 186 of 1988 which was subsequently renumbered as Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 wherein the heirs of deceased defendant 13 Lehajuddin executed a registered deed of relinquishment on 5-5-1991 Exhibit-Uma and admitted the title of the present defendants. The heirs of deceased Lehajuddin are plaintiffs 13-18 in this suit. Hachen who is the predecessor of plaintiffs 6-10 also admitted title and possession of the present defendants and executed a deed of relinquishment dated 5-6-1995 Exhibit-Cha. Subsequently heirs of deceased Fulbaru filed compromise with present defendants and admitted their title and possession in the suit land and accordingly Rule was made absolute on 25-3-1998 in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 as apparent from Exhibits-Ga and Gha. Furthermore present defendants ailed GR Case 31 of 1998 in which the statement of Title Suit 126 of 1983 was given and the order sheet of GR Case is Exhibit-Chha. There is no reason to believe that the present plaintiffs had no knowledge of the earlier Title Suit 126 of 1983. 

 13. There are three aspects important here to be considered. First is the judgment and order dated 25-3-1998 passed in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 wherein the judgment and decree dated 9-4-1985 passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 was maintained with regard to the same land but no one challenged that judgment and order passed in revision in the Honourable Appellate Division. Plaintiffs did not make out any case of fraud, forgery, collusion et cetera against Exhibits- Kha series, Ga and Gha. This suit is barred under Order 6, rules 2 and 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Plaint should contain material facts which constitute the cause of action. All primary facts which must be proved to establish the existence of the cause of action are material facts. Decree has been challenged in this case but it is very surprising to us that no single word has been spelt out against the decree mentioned in schedule-Ga to the plaint. There is no reason to go against such a decree being passed by a competent Court of law and affirmed by the High Court Division. We cannot sit over the judgment passed by this Court except any allegation of fraud. The cause of action of the instant case is apparently false. 

 14. Second is the question of limitation. The `Ga' schedule decree was challenged after 19(nineteen) years. The judgment and decree was passed in Title Suit 126 of 1986 on 9-4-1985 Exhibit-'Kha series'. The instant suit challenging that decree was filed on 19-6-2004. The judgment of Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 was passed on 25-3-1998 Exhibits-Ga and Gha. There is sufficient and satisfactory evidence available in the instant case to decide the question of limitation although no issue on such point was framed by the trial Court despite its legal inevitability and necessity in order to reach to a satisfactory conclusion. This Court finds no reason to send the suit down on remand for framing an issue on question of limitation thereby shirk its responsibility. This Court has ample co-extensive power as like as the trial Court to question whether the suit is barred by limitation by framing an issue naming the same as issue No. 7 and disposing of the same under Section 107(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure when sufficient evidence are obtainable from the record to the satisfaction of the Court. The predecessor of plaintiffs 6-10 and 13-18 were defendants in Title Suit 126 of 1983 and they executed two deeds of relinquishment dated 5-6-1995 Exhibit-Cha and 5-5-1991 Exhibit-Uma and according to compromise the Rule was made absolute on 25-3-1998 and both Exhibits-Uma and Cha remained unchallenged in the instant suit although the executants are the plaintiffs in the suit. Thus it evidently transpires to us that plaintiffs have every knowledge of Exhibit-Kha series with Ga and Gha but they have challenged the decree after the statutory period of time. If it were argued that knowledge of some of the plaintiffs is not the knowledge of others in that case the suit fails on ground of multifariousness. Therefore issue No. 7 as framed by this Court goes against the case of the plaintiffs. 

 15. Third is that the suit was decreed in part relying on the denial part of DW 1. We paid our keen attention and went through the entire deposition of DW 1. From reading of the decree of Title Suit 126 of 1983 Exhibit-Kha(1) it is apparent that present plaintiffs 5, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 along with others were defendants in Title Suit 126 of 1983. Thus it appears that while recording the deposition of DW 1 the word "not a fact" was mistakenly omitted from some places at the time of taking denial part by the presiding Judge. It becomes evidently clear when DW 1 immediately denied the suggestion at the end of his deposition as he stated that it was not a fact that plaintiffs possessed the suit land. Thus the finding of the Joint District Judge that since DW 1 admitted that there was only one defendant who is now the plaintiff and since the other plaintiffs were not parties the decree is not binding is abjectly perverse and misconceived and against documentary evidence. The lower Court failed to apply its judicial mind and did not even notice Exhibit-Kha(1) showing names and numbers of defendants of Title Suit 126 of 1983 and compare the same with the present plaint. The lower Court also went against the settled principle of law that plaintiff has to prove his own case independent of defence weakness. 

 16. Now we are going to consider the title of the parties. Plaintiff 14 who was one of the executants of Exhibit-Uma dated 5-5-1991 has deposed as PW 1. Although Exhibit-Uma is a deed of relinquishment and the same does not confer title but it is a registered document of admission and since no relief was prayed against Exhibits-Uma and Cha the documents stand good and plaintiff 14 is bound by such admission made in Exhibit-Uma and he is estopped from denying such admission thus the value of his testimony is greatly diminished. PW 2 and PW 3 deposed on possession and PW 3 failed to corroborate PW 2 as he admitted in cross that the land of Abdur Rahman is enjoyed by his sons. However since this is mainly a suit for partition evidence on possession does not carry much value except title. Plaintiffs claim title through settlement from auction purchasers Gogon and Mofijuddin. But they did not file any document of such settlement. It was not also explained away by them as to why they could not put forth such document. The document of title of the defendants for the selfsame land has been validated in Title Suit 126 of 1983 and Civil Revision 10205 of 1991. Defendants claim title through settlement from Hachen and others by registered dakhila Exhibit-Ka dated 1-3-1946. It appears from the pleadings and evidence that plaintiffs have relied on RS record 487 Exhibit-IX as the basis of their claim. Record of right is not a document of title. Moreover this Exhibit-IX has lost its value' by virtue of the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 and the judgment passed by this Division in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991. Defendants on the strength of decree mutated their names by Exhibit-Jha series and have been maintaining possession upon payment of rent Exhibit-Jha series. Earlier respondents filed three applications for amendment of the plaint and for taking additional evidence along with a supplementary affidavit but according to the order dated 30-11-2017 passed by a bench of this Court respondents did not press those applications at the time of hearing. So those applications are rejected being not pressed. Respondents also filed another application for amendment of the plaint on 15-3-2023 and also for acceptance of additional evidence on 30-3-2023 and those applications were heard. In the amendment of plaint respondents have made out a new case of kabuliyat and dakhila and in its support filed certified copies of kabuliyat and dakhila through application for acceptance of additional evidence. We have carefully examined those two documents and it appears that the kabuliyat dated 17-8-1944 was accepted by Hachen and others and they granted a dakhila on the same day to Rahman and his brothers. The second auction as drawn in the original plaint has been disowned in this amendment. Earlier plaintiffs claimed through Gogon and Mofijuddin and the rent was 50 taka 6 anna and quantum of the holding was 9.72 acres according to schedule-Ka. Now they are claiming through Hachen and others and the joma is 44 taka 8 anna and quantum of joma is 8.75 acres which is inconsistent with schedule-Ka. The dakhila shows that education cess is fixed at 2 taka 4 anna which actually was not imposed at the time in 1351 BS as found our Appellate Division in the case of Joynal Abedin Molla vs Aliyar Rahman and others, 1983 BLD (AD) 105. Plaintiffs were acquainted with Exhibit-Ka dated 1-3-1946 since 1978 when Title Suit 166 of 1978 renumbered as Title Suit 126 of 1983 was filed. That document stands good in the suit and revision Exhibit-Kha series, Ga and Gha. Now after around 26(twenty-six) years plaintiffs have come forward with those applications in view to fill up their lacuna by making out a new case on their acquisition of title to the surprise of the other party. The other party cannot be taken by surprise specially when a valuable right is accrued in their favour by lapse of time. Had Exhibit-Kha series been found fraudulent according to pleading and evidence in that case these proposed applications would have been taken in adjudication. It also calls for our attention that in Title Suit 126 of 1983 the RS tenants Gani Faraji, Abul Khaleque, Tofayel Ahmed admitting the title of Rahman Faraji which he acquired through Exhibit-Ka entered into compromise which was not denied in revision Exhibits-Ga and Gha. Court has to follow the principles of law and we have no option but to reject those applications filed after such a belated stage. It has also come to our notice that in paragraph 2 of the application for production of additional evidence it is admitted that the original kabulyat was under the custody of executant Abdur Rahman Faraji thus it appears that the same was not acted upon being not accepted by the landlord. 

 17. Khaleque, Gani, Motaleb claiming through settlment from the so-called auction purchasers Gogon and Mofijuddin sold 0.304 acres to plaintiff 1 and Erfan by kabala dated 24-3-1955 Exhibit-3. Schedule-2 of this document shows that 1112 decimals of land situated in Rajapur was shown to have been sold but plaint does not show any land belonging to them in Rajapur and document was also registered in Rajapur Sub-registry office instead of Kathaliya. Erfan being one of the transferees of Exhibit-3 sold 0.32 acres which is more than his share to plaintiffs 2, 3, 4 by two documents dated 21-4-1983 Exhibits-4 and 5. Plaint does not say anything about Exhibit-6. The transferee of Exhibit-7 made an oral gift to plaintiff 2 but no evidence was led in its support. One of the transferees of Exhibit-8 named Lehajuddin was the predecessor of defendants 13(Ka)-13(Da) in Title Suit 126 of 1983 who are now plaintiffs 13-18 and executants of Exhibit-Uma. The identity and claim of the plaintiffs are so inconsistent that there is no way to make any sense out of it. As discussed above the basis of plaintiffs' title is unfounded and this suit cannot be decreed without ascertaining title first. Without a definite case of declaration of title this suit for partition simpliciter is not at all maintainable specially when Exhibit-Kha series along with Ga and Gha stand against plaintiffs' title as a bar and those have never been confronted. Those are unanswered and kept untouched. Plaintiffs have failed to prove their case and the present suit is barred by limitation as discussed above. 

 19. We are of the view that plaintiffs are not entitled to any decree and judgment and decree passed by the trial Court is set-aside and the appeal is allowed. There will be no order as to costs.

parties:
Bilquis Jahan and another ------ Appellants
VS
Syed Abdul Hafiz and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Sole defendant Bilquis Jahan has preferred First Appeal No. 299 of 2007. On the other hand plaintiffs Syed Abdul Hafiz and Mijanur Rahman have preferred First Appeal No. 309 of 2007. Those two appeals arose out of the judgment and decree dated 18-6-2007 passed by the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 34 of 2005. Initially Title Suit No. 44 of 2002 was filed in the Court of Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka on 17-3-2002 and subsequently on transfer on 9-6-2005 it was registered as Title Suit No. 34 of 2005. 

 3. The suit was filed for declaration of title on the basis of purchase and adverse possession, confirmation of possession, alternatively for recovery of khas possession and also for permanent injunction. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit land measuring 0.1093 acres appertaining to RS plot 8187 of RS Khatian 926 corresponding to SA plot 5329 of SA khatian 2132 originated from CS plot 143 of CS khatian 13021 of mouja Lalbagh belonged to Sheikh Nanna. CS plot 143 contains 0.2256 acres of land from which Sheikh Nanna transferred 0.1163 acres of land to the father of plaintiff 1 before SA operation. While Nanna was owner in possession in remaining 0.1093 acres died leaving behind 05(five) sons named Chand Miah, Chunnu Miah, Sona Miah, Bachchu Miah and Suruj Miah. Chand Miah died leaving behind 2(two) sons named Tara Miah, Pier Ali and 2(two) daughters named Dulari Begum and Kosturi Begum. Tara Miah died leaving behind 03(three) sons named Rahman Miah, Badal Miah and Iqbal Miah. Chunnu Miah died leaving behind 1(one) daughter Anarzadi Begum. Sona Miah died leaving behind 1(one) son Babul Miah and I (one) daughter Piyari Begum. Bachchu Miah died leaving behind 1(one) son Solaiman Miah and 1(one) daughter Nurjahan Begum. Suruj Miah died leaving behind wife Irani Begum, 03(three) sons named Tara Miah, Kalu Miah and Abdul Kader and 05(five) daughters named Jabeda Begum, Meherun Begum, Hasna Begum, Rashida Begum and Rehana Begum. All the descendants of late Nanna Miah executed an unregistered agreement for sale of the suit land on 25-6-1991 to the plaintiffs at a consideration of Taka 5,00,000 (five lac) from which Taka 1,00,000 (one lac) was paid as earnest money. Subsequently, the rest Taka 4,00,000 (four lac) was paid on 19-6-1993, 15-6-1995, 10-6-1997, 13-1-2000 and ultimately document in favour of the plaintiffs was executed and registered on 13-1-2000. On 15-1-2001 plaintiffs came to know from the settlement office that defendant mutated and separated her name in respect of the suit land. The vendors of the plaintiffs gave the photo copy of the SA record prepared in the name of Sheikh Nanna. Meanwhile, the city survey record was prepared in the name of Jahanara against which plaintiffs filed Miscellaneous Case No. 651 of 2000 under Rule 30 of the State Acquisition Rules but plaintiffs failed in the case on 7-6-2000. Then they preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 13149 of 2000 which was also disallowed. Defendant threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession on 25-1-2001. Then plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 103 of 2001 for permanent injunction in the 3rd Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka. The suit was withdrawn on 7-3-2002 with liberty to sue afresh. Now the present Title Suit No. 44 of 2002 was filed on 17-3-2002 and the same was renumbered as Title Suit No. 34 of 2005 showing cause of action arose in the suit on 07-6-2000, 15-1-2001, 25-1-2001 and 7-3-2002. 

 4. Sole defendant appeared and contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all material statements made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that Devendra and Surendra filed Mortgage Suit No. 9 of 1919 against Satyendra and Monosha in the Court of 4th Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and got decree. Decree-holders filed Decree Execution Case No. 154 of 1919 and auction was held on 3-6-1920 and Birendra alias Dhirendra purchased the same in the benami of Jogendra which was confirmed by the Court on 10-7-1920. There-after, Jogendra executed a deed of relinquish-ment on 20-3-1922 to Birendra who sold 6(six) kathas from the west side of CS plot No. 143 to Ram Gopal by kabala dated 29-8-1923 and delivered possession. Ram Gopal sold the suit land to Jahanara by kabala dated 29-9-1942 and delivered possession. SA khatian 2132 was correctly prepared in the name of Jahanara in respect of suit land measuring 0.1090 acres in SA plot 5329 with reference to holding number 4 Hosseni Dalan Road, Dhaka. Then Jahanara died on 10-2-1965 leaving behind husband Abdul Majid, 3(three) sons named Tariqul, Reazul, Enamul and 3(three) daughters named Khurshid Jahan, Kamar Jahan and defendant Bilquis Jahan. Majid then died on 10-12-1976. Khurshid Jahan also died in 1987. Thereafter, defendant and Enamul filed Title Suit No. 235 of 1989 for partition in the 2nd Subordinate Judge Court, Dhaka against Tariqul, Reazul, Kamar Jahan which ended in compromise on 24-3-1991 and the suit land exclusively fell into the saham of the defendant. Subsequently, she mutated her name in separate khatian No. 2132 on 19-11-1991 by Separation Case No. 1992 of 1991-92 and has been maintaining title and possession upon payment of rent and other taxes. Subsequently in Certificate Case No. 17 of 1997-98 defendant paid Taka 10,222.45 on 13-6-1999 by rent receipt 496817. It is further stated that enhanced rate was realised from the defendant considering the suit land as commercial for which defendant filed Land Development Case No. 30 of 1999 to reduce the rent treating the suit land as residential and the case was allowed. During liberation war the original documents of Mortgage Suit, sale certificate, writ of delivery of possession, nadabi document, 1923 document, 1942 document, rent receipt, holding taxes were lost. The city survey DP khatian 5140 was prepared in the name of the defendant against which plaintiff filed Objection Case No. 651 of 2000 under Rule 30 which was rejected on 7-6-2000. Then plaintiffs filed Appeal Case No. 13149 of 2000 under Rule 31 which was also rejected on 24-1-2001. Plaintiffs admitted the address of defendant in 4 Hosseni Dalan Road, Lalbag in the memorandum of Miscellaneous Appeal. The second schedule of plaint and decree of Mortgage Suit No. 9 of 1919 attracts the land covered by CS plot 143. Defendant and her predecessors have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land upon payment of taxes and all utility bills for more than 80(eighty) years within the knowledge of others. Plaintiffs have no title and possession in the suit land and the suit being false is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 5. The trial Court framed as many as 06(six) issues as to maintainability, whether the suit is barred under Article 144 of the Limitation Act, whether the plaintiffs have title in the suit land, whether the plaintiffs have possession until dispossession, whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get the relief as prayed for. 

 7. The trial Court dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 18-6-2007 on the finding that the certified copy of the SA khatian (Exhibit 2) was not issued by the proper authority but the certified copy of the SA khatian (Exhibit C) prepared in the name of Jahanara was duly issued and it supports possession of Jahanara and further found that admittedly the suit land is situated at 4 Hosseni Dalan Road, Dhaka for which rent and taxes are paid by the defendant through series of exhibits and those are evidence of possession and collateral evidence of title which prevail over RS khatian (Exhibit 3). The Court found that plaintiffs failed to prove their or their predecessors' possession and RS record has no basis. The Court further found that the plaintiffs also failed to prove their dispossession from the suit land and the suit is not maintainable and also found that Exhibit 2 does not correspond to CS khatian 13021 (Exhibit 1) and again found that Exhibit 6 shows that execution was done on 16-1-2000 but the document was presented for registration on 13-1-2000 which is absurd and also found that defendant did not file the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession and the nadabi document does not confer title and since plaintiffs or their predecessors were not parties to Title Suit No. 235 of 1989, Jahanara Begum did not acquire any title and accordingly both the parties have failed to prove their title over the suit land. 

 9. Mr Mrinal Kanti Biswas, learned Advocate appearing with Advocates Mr Md Aktaruzzaman and Ms. Biroza Mala for the appellant (hereinafter be called as defendant) of First Appeal No. 299 of 2007 submits that the trial Court was wrong in finding that the defendant failed to prove her title to the suit land and such finding is apparently illegal and uncalled for and required to be reversed. The finding on the deed of relinquishment dated 10-12-1921 is a blunder and the Court misjudged the document which is not tenable in the eye of law. He further submits that the trial Court failed to appreciate that many documents including the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession were lost during liberation war and adverse finding upon such documents are misconceived when long possession of the defendant in the suit land is evidently found. He also submits that the observation along with the finding arrived at by the Joint District Judge in respect of title of defendant is against the evidence on record and the same being misconceived and illegal is liable to be reversed and set-aside. He lastly submits that there are good grounds in the appeal and the same might be allowed. In support of his submission he referred the cases of Golzar Ali Pramanik vs Saburjan Bewa, reported in 6 BLC (AD) 41; Moksed Ali Mondal vs Abdus Samad Mondal, reported in 9 BLC (AD) 220; Government of Bangladesh vs Md Sharif Uddin reported in 22 BLC (AD) 204; Shishir Kanti Pal vs Nur Muhammad reported in 55 DLR (AD) 39. 

 10. Learned Advocate Mr Mansur Habib, appearing on behalf of the appellants (hereinafter called as plaintiff) of First Appeal No. 309 of 2007 submits that the trial Court erred in law in dismissing the suit beyond the evidence and law. He submits that the trial Court ought to have decided that plaintiffs being purchaser from the successive heirs of CS tenant Sheikh Nanna hold good title and the finding on possession of the plaintiffs is wrong and beyond the evidence on record. The witnesses of plaintiffs prove the possession in accordance with the law and the finding that the suit is not maintainable for want of possession is wrong. He submits that the SA record submitted by the defendant has got no basis and defendant has no title and possession in the suit land. He finally submits that since there is merit in the appeal the same would be allowed. 

 12. Defendant's case starts with a suit for recovery of money of a mortgage of the year of 1917 filed by Devendra against Satyendra and others. That was Title Suit No. 180 of 1917 filed on 23-4-1917 before the CS record was finally published in the Calcutta Gazette for the concerned area on 26-6-1917. The suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 240 of 1917 and finally as Title Suit No. 9 of 1919 by Order No. 27 dated 9-1-1919. The identity of the present suit land with boundary is found in schedule 2 of the plaint and decree of that suit which are Exhibit B series wherein it is mentioned that the land within the boundary is "mudafate Gobinda Moisal" which in other words means "in the name of Gobinda Moisal". Title Suit No. 9 of 1919 was decreed on 15-1-1919 and final decree was passed on 21-8-1919 Exhibit B(iii). Decree-holder filed Execution Case No. 154 of 1919 and auction was held on 3-6-1920 and Birendra purchased the same in the benami of his cousin's son Jagendra which was confirmed by the Court on 17-7-1920. Jagendra acknowledging ownership of Birendra executed and registered a deed of relinquishment on 20-3-1922 (Exhibit T) in respect of all lands including the suit land covered by Exhibit B(iii). Jagendra then sold the suit land situated at the west side of CS plot 143 to Ram Gopal Roy by kabala dated 29-8-1923 (Exhibit U) and delivered possession. Ram Gopal subsequently transferred the same in favour of defendant's mother Jahanara by kabala dated 22-9-1942 (Exhibit V) and delivered possession. Accordingly SA record 2132 (Exhibit C) comprising plot No. 5329 was prepared in her name with reference to holding number 4 Hosseni Dalan Road, Dhaka. Jahanara died in 1965 leaving behind husband Majid and 03(three) sons namely Tariqul, Reazul, Enamul and 03(three) daughters Khurshid Jahan, Kamar Jahan and defendant Bilkis Jahan. Majid and Khurshid Jahan died later on. For the convenience of possession in the joint property defendant and brother Enamul filed Title Suit No. 235 of 1989 for partition against brothers Tariqul, Reazul and sister Kamar Jahan and according to item 4 of the decree (Exhibit D series) the suit land fell in the saham of this defendant. There was arrear of rent for the year 1398 BS to 1405 BS for which Certificate Case No. 70 of 1997-98 started and accordingly notice (Exhibit F) was served and arrear of Taka 10222.45 was paid on 12-3-1998 by receipt number 896902 and the case was disposed of as evident from Exhibit H. Subsequently defendant filed Land Development Tax Case No. 30 of 1999 for decrease the rent of the suit land and the Assistant Commissioner reassessed the rent which is Exhibit I. City Survey DP khatian 5140 with plot No. 2065 (Exhibit J) was also prepared in the name of the defendant. Plaintiffs filed Objection Case No. 651 of 2000 against Exhibit J but failed (Exhibit L). Plaintiff also failed in the following Appeal Case No. 13149 of 2000 (Exhibit N). Defendant filed rent, tax, utility bills (Exhibit G, 0 series, P series, Q series). 

 14. On 15-1-2001 plaintiff went to the local settlement office and came to know that the suit land was mutated and separated in the name of the defendant. Later on when the city survey khatian was prepared in the name of the defendant they filed Objection Case No. 651 of 2000 in the settlement office but plaintiffs lost in the said case on 7-6-2000. As against the same plaintiffs filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 13149 of 2000 and the appeal was also disallowed. On 25-1-2001 defendant threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession for which Title Suit No. 103 of 2001 was filed for permanent injunction and due to formal defect the suit was withdrawn on 7-3-2002 with liberty to sue afresh and the present suit for declaration of title by purchase and adverse possession and for further declaration that the documents, judgment and decree of the defendant are illegal, fraudulent, collusive, inoperative, mere paper transaction and not binding upon the plaintiffs along with confirmation of possession and alternatively for recovery of khan possession and also for permanent injunction was filed on 17-3-2002. 

 15. The title document of the plaintiffs dated 13-1-2000 is filed in original and the same is Exhibit 6. There are as many as 20(twenty) executants in the kabala who are the successive heirs of CS tenant Sheikh Nanna. There is a reference of an agreement dated 25-6-1991 in the kabala. Plaintiff did not offer any explanation for not filing the agreement in order to prove the passing of consideration money. From perusal of the kabala it comes into view that all the executants reside in different addresses other than the address of the suit land. Exhibit-6 was executed and presented for registration on 13-1-2000 and the document itself shows that the same was registered on 13-1-2000. But it appears that Pear Ali, Soleman Miah and Nurjahan Begum being executants 1, 10 and 11 respectively executed the document on 16-1-2000. The document is shown to be registered without some of the vendors. It is incredible that how the sub-registrar proceeded with the registration process with the endorsement seals and sign violating the registration rules. It is a fraud upon registration. This is not a document registered in accordance with the law and the same is a forged, fraudulent, collusive and void document. 

 16. The prayer portion of the plaint shows that the plaintiff made a simultaneous claim of declaration of title on the basis of purchase and adverse possession. It is the settled principle of law that declaration of title on the basis of a document and adverse possession cannot go together because such claim conflicts with each other. In paragraph 4 of the plaint it has been stated that all the heirs of Sheikh Nanna have been in possession in the suit land. In paragraph 7 it has been stated that defendant might dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land at any time. The last dates of cause of action are 25-1-2001 and 7-3-2002 and the suit was filed on 17-3-2002. PW 1 stated in examination-in-chief that the holding number of the suit land is 4 Hosseni Dalan Road. He further stated that after withdrawal of Title Suit No. 103 of 2001 defendant dispossessed him. He admitted in cross-examination that dispossession was done before filing of the suit. In order to get a decree for recovery of possession a definite case of possession followed by dispossession has got to be made out in the plaint and accordingly evidence has to be led. Plaintiff did not even amend the plaint to the effect that they had been dispossessed on such date and time by such person or persons in such manner. Plaintiffs have no case on possession followed by dispossession and question of decree on recovery of possession does not arise at all under Article 142 of the Limitation Act and their factum of actual position on possession is beyond pleading. From reading of the deposition of PW 2 and PW 3 it does not appear that plaintiffs or their predecessors had possession in the suit land. PW 2 expressed his ignorance about the possession of DW 6 in the suit land. From the oral evidence of both the parties along with the series of documentary evidence filed by the defendant it transpires that defendant's mother Jahanara had been maintaining title and possession in the suit land till her purchase in 1942 by Exhibit V and after her death defendant Bilkis maintains the same. 

 17. Defendant has stated in paragraph 23 (Jha) of the written statement that the original documents of foreclosure suit, sale certificate, writ of delivery of possession, deed of relinquishment, title documents, rent-receipts, khatian, receipts of holding taxes were lost during the war of independence. The trial Court found since no sale certificate, writ of delivery of possession were produced, the predecessor of defendant acquired no title. But the trial Court failed to appreciate that sale certificate is not a document of title and auction can be proved by other evidence independent of sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession. This proposition finds support from the case of Thanda Nessa Bibi and others vs Monowar Joarder and others reported in 5 BLC (AD) 189, Bazlur Rahman and others vs Sadu Mia and others reported in 45 DLR 391. In the present case the certified copies of most of the lost documents were produced and marked in evidence. The reason for not filing the previous original documents has been explained away by the defendant. From reading of all those documents it appears that the details of the fact are chronologically and very clearly presented in the recital of those documents in consonance with the statements made in the written statement. Trial court also found that Birendra did not acquire any title by the deed of relinquishment (Exhibit T) executed by Jogendra. Trial Court did not appreciate that this deed of relinquishment although is not a document of title but of admission and declaration about the benami nature and transaction. In the instant case Birendra is the real owner and Jogendra is the ostensible owner. The admission made by the ostensible owner is sufficient to prove that Birendra was the real owner and from reading of Exhibit T, it appears that Jogendra admitted that the auction was purchased by Birendra by his own money and for his own interest. This aspect of the case has been discussed in the case of Mst. Khaleda Razia and others vs Mahatub Uddin Chowdhwy reported in 30 DLR (SC) 27. Recently in a judgment passed on 26-2-2019 in Civil Appeal No. 535 of 2009 in the case of Lalmon Bibi and another vs Mohammad Del war Hossain and others our Appellate Division only relying upon a nadabi document dismissed the appeal. Exhibit-T is proved by calling the volume book from the concerned office. The trial Court failed to appreciate the preponderance of evidence and being driven by whim made adverse observations and findings against the title of the defendant which is absolutely unwanted because in the instant case plaintiffs failed at possession but even then if they could prove title to the suit land in that case title of defendant might be investigated but it is not wise to disbelieve defendant's title when plaintiffs holding a void document without possession summoned defendant to take a chance on her. Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case even if had the defendant failed to prove her title, her and her predecessor's possession for more than 12 (twelve) years would have given birth to her title although she did not specifically claim title by adverse possession and this aspect of the case has been decided in the case of Nurjahan Begum vs Nur Rahman, reported in 6 ADC 469 = 59 DLR 98. Exhibits-C, E series, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N, 0 series, P series, Q series are good evidence in support of the case of the defendant and those documentary evidence also terminate the case of the plaintiff. 

 18. The son of defendant holding a power of attorney Exhibit-A examined himself as DW 1 in support of defence case. DW 2 came from land office and proved SA khatian 2132 Exhibit C prepared in the name of defendant. DW 3 came from the record room with volume book and proved the deed of relinquishment (Exhibit T) dated 20-3-1922. He also proved the kabala dated 29-8-1923 executed by Birendra to Ram Gopal (Exhibit U). DW 3 also proved the kabala dated 22-9-1942 (Exhibit V) executed by Ram Gopal in favour of the mother of the defendant named Jahanara Begum and this document is described in Volume 46 of the year of 1942 at page numbers 27-31. The deposition of DW 3 remained undisturbed in cross. Defendant has successfully proved her title to the suit land. There are series of documents in support of her title and possession in the suit land. DW 4 deposed on possession. DW 5 is the full brother of defendant and he upheld the relevance of Exhibit D series and stated that defendant acquired the suit land. It is stated in paragraph (Kha) of written statement that Lal Miah and his family have been living in the suit land as care taker. Lal Miah as DW 6 deposed in the suit and in cross examination his position got stronger. 

 19. It is an age-old principle of law that plaintiff has got to prove his own case independent of defence weakness. In the instant case plaintiffs have utterly failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land. Exhibit-6 dated 13-1-2000 is a forged, fraudulent, collusive, void document. They did not even make out any case on possession followed by dispossession. Their prayer is vague and their simultaneous claim on title by purchase and adverse possession is not permitted under the law. Plaintiff with a view to grab the suit land filed this false suit. 

 20. The title and possession of the defendant in the suit land is evidently proved. The adverse observations and findings arrived at by the trial Court with regard to the title of the defendant being apparently unwanted and misconceived are hereby set-aside and expunged. Accordingly, First Appeal 299 of 2007 is allowed. Since plaintiffs have miserably failed to prove their case First Appeal No. 309 of 2007 is dismissed. The judgment and decree of the trial Court is affirmed in the modified form by expunging the findings of title and possession against the defendant.

parties:
Md. Delwar Hossain Molla alias Dilu Molla and others.
Vs.
Abul Kashem Molla being dead his heirs Md. Salim Molla and others.
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Haque, J: This Rule, on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) was issued at the instance of the defendant–appellant-petitioners calling upon the opposite party no.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.03.2008 passed by the Additional District Judge, Patuakhali in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.11.2005 passed by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Patuakhali in Title Suit No. 16 of 2001 decreeing the suit should not be set aside and/ or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the present opposite party no. 1, Abul Kashem Molla (now dead) filed Title Suit no. 16 of 2001 initially against the defendant nos. 1-8, later on, defendant nos. 9-22 were added in the suit for partition of the suit land described in the schedule `ka' to the plaint. 

 3. The plaintiff asserted in the plaint that 4.58 acres of land appertain to RS plot no. 2381, 8.47 acres of R.S plot no. 2386 under RS khatian no. 36 and 5.62 acres under plot no. 2418 and 5.18 acres under plot no. 2419 of RS khatian no. 47 of Londa Mouja were the subject matter of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 of Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Barishal. 

 4. In the said suit (Title Suit No. 40 of 1954) the plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla was defendant no. 13 and his sister Mominjan was defendant no. 12. The said title suit was decreed on compromise on 23.04.1954 in preliminary form and the said decree was made final on 26.04.1954. The defendant nos. 12 and 13 (Mominjan and present plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla) of that suit got 2.86 acres of land from plot no. 2381 and 3.25 acres of land from plot no. 2386 of RS khatian No. 36 and 3.17 acres of land from plot no. 2418 and 2.85 acres of land from plot no. 2419 of RS khatian No. 47 in their saham, that is, in total defendant nos. 12 and 13 of the said suit got 12.13 acres of land in their share and pursuant to the said decree the defendant nos. 12 and 13 were possessing, the said land with the knowledge of all. 

 8. The plaintiff requested the co-sharers for partition of the land but they refused to do the same. It is also asserted in the plaint that the government constructed embankment in the area which is known as WAPDA embankment and in the said WAPDA embankment the government acquired .305 acres of land from the share of the plaintiff, so the plaintiff is entitled to get a saham for his remaining 8.18 acres of land in his share. The defendant no. 1 denied to partition the suit land amicably, finally on 20th Chaitra, 1407 BS, thus the plaintiff has been constrained to file the present suit. 

 11. The case of the defendant nos. 18-21 is that the plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla and his sister Mominjan had two full brothers, their names are Abdul Ha.mid and Hafizur Rahman. Abul Kashem Molla and his sister Mominjan in collusion with the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 made them defendants in the said suit leaving the two full brothers, Abdul Hamid and Hafizur Rahman and also obtained the decree collusively for their illegal gain although the lands belonged to Abul Kashem Mollah, Mominjan, Abdul Ham id and Hafizur Rahman. 

 12. The 3 full brothers, Abul Kashem Molla, Abdul Hamid and Md. Hafizur Ra.hman and their full sister Mominjan got settlement of 12.13 acres of land from the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954.Later on, Abdul Hamid, the predecessor of defendant nos. 18-21, Hafizur Rahman the present plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla and their sister Mominjan jointly filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Barishal for declaration of their title and the said suit was also decreed on compromise on 11.12.1956. Since Abul Kashem Molla was one of the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 he cannot avoid the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and he cannot rely upon the decree passed in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 denying the decree passed in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. So, the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed. Since the other defendants ultimately did not contest in the suit I find no reason to aver their case. 

 13. On the above pleadings, the trial Court framed issues and the plaintiff upon the issues framed, examined 3 witnesses and submitted some papers which were marked as exhibit nos. 1, 1(Ka) and 2 while the contesting defendant nos. 18-21 examined one witness and submitted the decree and the plaint in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 which were marked as exhibit 'Ka' series. 

 14. The trial Court considering the evidence adduced by the parties and relying upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 decreed the suit in preliminary form on 13.11.2005 allotting a saham for 8.18 acres of land in favour of plaintiff, Abul Kashem Mollah and 2.42 acres of land in favour of the defendant no. 1 with a direction to partition the land amicably within 60 days failing which parties will be entitled to get the land partitioned through Court. 

 15. The defendant nos. 18-21 being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment of the trial Court dated 13.11.2005 filed Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 in the Court of District Judge, Patuakhali which was ultimately heard by the Additional district Judge, Patuakhali on transfer who by his impugned judgment and decree dated 20.03.2008 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment of the trial Court. The defendant nos. 18-21 as against the said judgment of the appellate Court below moved this Court by filing this application under section 115(1) of the Code and obtained the present Rule as stated hereinbefore. 

 19. The learned Advocate for the petitioners also submits that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was filed by some other persons and there were more than 106.00 acres of land in the schedule. In the said suit Mominjan and Abul Kashem Molla were made defendant Nos. 12 and 13. They did not (defendant nos. 12 and 13) file the said suit and the nature of the suit, its filing, service of summons and decree itself are sufficient to hold that the plaintiff of that suit had no knowledge as to who were the owners and who have been possessing the huge 106.00 acres of land. 

 21. The learned Advocate also submits that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was filed on 12.04.1954 in the Court and without waiting for service of return of summons solenama was filed on 15.04.1954 within 3 days of its filing and preliminary decree was passed on the basis of so called solenama on 23.04.1956 and decree was made final on 26.04.1954. The learned Advocate thus submits that within 14 days a suit for 106.00 acres of land was decreed in the name of the various persons and such a solenama might have been prepared at the time of filing of the suit, so the trial Court should not have relied upon such a decree which was passed within 14 days only. Over and again, the suit was not filed by Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi rather it was filed by some other persons who may not have knowledge about the acquisition of suit land by 3 brothers and their full sister. 

 22. The learned Advocate also submits that whenever the 3 brothers and sister subsequently, filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 in the same Court of Barishal for declaration of their title jointly with reference to the decree passed in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and their settlement has been admitted by the landlord in the said suit. So, the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 is not antagonistic to the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 rather, since 3 brothers and 1 sister had filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 for declaration of their title and since the said suit was decreed, the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 will get more preference upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 so far it relates to the brother and their 1 sister have been merged with the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. 

 23. The learned Advocate also submits that the trial Court below relied much upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 since its original record was called for and came in the Court for its perusal, and did not rely upon the certified copy of decree and plaint of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 as the original record was not called for by the defendant nos. 18-21, but after filing of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006, the defendant nos. 18-21 (as appellants) to remove any sort of suspicion and cloud regarding the decree passed in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 called for the original records of the said suit from the Barishal record room and though the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was received by the appellate Court below on 10.03.2008, the appellate Court below without going through the same disallowed the appeal by its judgment dated 20.03.2008 agreeing with the judgment of the trial court. 

 24. The learned Advocate also submits that in the said judgment the appellate Court below unfortunately relied upon the findings and observations of the trial Court and also held that the decree of the Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 is not believable without calling for the records whereas original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was lying with the Appellate Court. 

 25. The learned Advocate also submits that from the judgment of the appellate Court below it clearly appears that the appellate Court did not take notice of the tagging of the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 with the record of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006.The appellate Court below without going through the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 did the same job like the trial Court that the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 is not believable relying on its certified copy only. 

 26. Thus the learned Advocate also submits that had the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 been perused by the appellate Court below the decisions would have been otherwise but unfortunately, the appellate Court below without going through the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 made a ditto to the judgment passed by the trial Court, thus it is a case of non-consideration of materials and evidence on record by the appellate Court below occasioning serious failure of justice. 

 27. The learned Advocate also submits that pursuant to the decree in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956, 3 brothers and their sister had mutated their names in the record of rights which ultimately established that the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was not acted upon, moreover it was obtained at the instance of others having no actual knowledge of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan bibi. 

 30. On the other hand Mr. Bazlur Rashid, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party nos.1(a) -1(h) the Rule submits that it is fact that Abul Kashem Molla, Md. Abdul Hamid, Hafizur Rahman and Mominjan Bibi are the full brothers and sister but through Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 the suit land has been fallen in the share of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi and since Mominjan Bibi died leaving full brother Abul Kashem Molla and Hafizur Rahman and since the decretal land has not been partitioned by metes and bounds and since the defendant no. 1 denied to partition the land amicably, the plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla under compelling circumstances filed the suit in question claiming partition of the schedule land. 

 31. The learned Advocate for the opposite party also submits that Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 might have been filed and decreed but the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 has not been cancelled through the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. The plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla has been possessing the suit land on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and the plaintiff of the present suit successfully proved their right, title and interest in the suit land both before the trial Court and the appellate Court below and both the Courts below considering the materials on record rightly decreed the suit which do not call for any interference by this Court. 

 33. I have considered the above submissions of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record particularly the record of Title Suit No. 16 of 2001 filed by Abul Kashem Molla whose heirs are opposite party nos. 1(a)-1(h) in this Rule, the record of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 and the records of two former suits being Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and 190 of 1956 decided by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Barishal and the other papers connected thereto. In order to appreciate the arguments of both the parties let us have a look into the evidence on record. 

 34. Abul Kashem Molla as PW 1 deposed that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was filed in the Court of 2nd Subordinate Judge, Barishal for the land under RS khatian nos. 36 and 47 and in that suit he and his full sister Mominjan were the defendant nos. 12 and 13 and in that suit they got a decree on 23.04.1954 for 10.80 acres of land, the said decree was made final on 12.8.1955, his sister Mominjan Bibi died leaving him and the defendant nos. 1 and 2, he has been possessing 8.48 acres of land of which WAPDA has acquired .305 acres of land and deducting the said .305 acres of land he will get decree for 8.18 acres of land. 

 35. He also stated that it is not a fact that they got a decree in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. He filed the certified copy of RS khatian nos. 36 and 47 marked as exhibits 1 and 1(Ka) and the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 marked as exhibits-2 series. He also stated that they have brought the record of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 before the trial Court. 

 36. In cross examination, he stated that defendant no. 1 is his full brother, the defendant no. 1 is entitled to get a saham for 2.42 acres of land. In cross examination by defendant nos. 18-21 he stated that there were many owners in the said two khatians, he cannot say the names of all owners but can say the name of Sattya Ranjan and Vabo Ranjan, the predecessor of defendant nos. 18- 21 is his brother, he (predecessor of defendant nos. 18-21) is also entitled to get the share of his sister. He also stated that they are 3 brothers and 4 sisters. He categorically stated that he cannot say whether they, the 3(three) full brothers and sister Mominjan took the settlement of the land or not. He cannot say whether they filed the Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. He denied the defendants suggestion that they all the 3 brothers and sisters have been possessing the suit land. He also stated that his brothers have been possessing the land forcibly. 

 38. PW 3 Abdul Aziz Molla told that all the parties are known to him, the plaintiff has been possessing 8.18 acres of land, the plaintiff got decree in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. In cross examination by defendant nos. 18-21 he stated that the Hindu Babus were the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and the tenants that is the raiyot were the defendants in the suit, he cannot say the name of the parties, defendant Delowar is known to him. They have been possessing their land also. 

 39. DW 1 for the defendant no. 1, Md. Forkan Majid deposing in the Court prayed for saham for 2.42 acres of land in favour of defendant no. 1. In cross examination by the defendant nos. 18-21 he stated that his father and uncle are 3 brothers and 4 sisters, they are Abdul Hamid, Hafizur Rahman and Abul Kashem Molla, his father has been possessing the land, he cannot say whether their father and uncles filed any suit after the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954, in the suit land the plaintiff, and the predecessor of defendants nos. 18-21 have dwelling huts. 

 41. DW 3 Md. Delowar Hossain was examined on behalf of the defendant nos. 18-21 who deposed that he is defendant no. 18 and defendant nos. 19-21 is his sisters, 22.76 acres of land were recorded in RS khatian nos. 36 and 47, the said lands were in the schedule of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 in the said suit his father Abdul Hamid and his uncle Hafiz were not made party, thereafter his father and uncles jointly filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956, the said suit was decreed on compromise and pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 their predecessors have been possessing the suit land now, they have been possessing the suit land and they have homestead on the suit land. He filed the plaint, petition of compromise and judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 marked as exhibits 'Ka' series. He stated that it is not fact that the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. 

 42. In cross examination by the plaintiff he stated that no suit was filed for setting aside the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 but Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was filed jointly. They purchased some land from Altu. 

 43. These are the evidences that have been given by the plaintiff and the defendants of the original suit. From the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the trial Court relied much upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and considered the said decree thereof as an admitted suit in favour of the plaintiff and accepted the arguments of the plaintiff that the certified of the decree and other papers of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was created through forgery for the purpose of the present suit. 

 44. But unfortunately, the trial Court did not consider the evidence regarding the possession of the suit land adduced by the parties. Had the evidence relating to possession of the parties is considered the trial Court would have found that the defendant nos. 18-21 are in possession of the suit land along with the late plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla and then trial Court could have realized that the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 has been acted upon among the parties. 

 47. The reality regarding the possession of all the co-sharers and the effectiveness of the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 has been revealed from the following evidence of PW 1 Abul Kashem Molla who stated in his evidence in the following manner: 

 49. Pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956, the same type of evidence regarding the possession of all 3 brothers have been echoed by the evidence of PW 2, Akter Peada, PW 3 Abdul Aziz Mollah. PW 2 Akter Peda in his cross examination stated in the following ways: 

 53. The trial Court relied much upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 as its original record was called for. From the record of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 it appears that the said suit was filed on 12.04.1954 for 106.60 acres of land and before the date of service of summons all the defendants appeared and filed solenama on 15.04.1954 within 3 days of its filing and the suit was decreed on 23.04.1954 within 11 days and the decree was made final on 26.04.1954 within 14 days. Now is it not enough to consider the category of the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. From the date of its filing the suit was decreed within 14 days although the suit was related for 106.00 acres of land. 

 54. Over and again, Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan did not file the said suit. There was a narration about their portion made by others and the suit was decreed as it is. From a decree of this nature it can safely be said that all the activities relating to filing of the suit, appearance of the parties, filing of solenama and the decrees were made as part of a design, though there was a saham in favour of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi but that might have been done by others to save their interest having no knowledge of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan (defendant nos. 12/13 of Title suit no. 40 of 1954 and it is clear from the evidence of PW 1 himself and others that the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 has not been acted upon for the suit land. Had it been acted upon, the suit land would have been possessed by Abul Kashem Mollah and Mominjan Bibi only but PW 1 clearly stated in his evidence that his other brothers have been possessing the suit land forcefully which ultimately indicates that all the brothers have been in possession of the suit land pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and not pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. Moreover, by filing subsequent Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and obtaining decree in that suit Abdul Kashem Mollah admitted his other brothers as owners of the property. 

 55. The appellate Court below made a great ditto to the judgment of the trial Court without perusing his own record. Before pronouncing judgment by the appellate Court below on 20.03.2008, the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was tagged with the record of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006, but the Appellate Court below failed to appreciate that fact and did not peruse the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. From the order dated 10.03.2008 it appears that the Appellate Court below received the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 on that day. The order of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 dated 10.03.2008 runs as follows: 

 56. From the above order dated 10.03.2008 in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 it appears that the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was tagged with the appeal in question on 10.03.2008 and obviously, the defendant nos. 18-21 rightly called for the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 for the adverse observations of the Trial Court that the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was not called for and the certified copy of the said suit might have been created by means of forgery by the defendant nos. 18-21 and for the aforesaid reasons the trial Court did not believe the decree of Title Suit No. 90 of 1956. The defendants appellants to remove all sorts of confusion regarding the genuines of the decree of Title suit no. 190 of 1956 rightly called for the original records of Title suit no. 190 of 1956 for perusal by the appellate Court below. 

 57. However, since the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was tagged on 10.03.2008 with the appeal, the appellant prayed for time for hearing of the appeal but that was not allowed by the Appellate Court. In my consideration the appellate Court below should have allowed the adjournment petition giving a short time to the appellant for placing the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 which shows the non-application of judicial mind of the Judge of the Appellate Court below in disposing the appeal. 

 58. However, be that as it may, from the judgment of appellate Court below it is crystal clear that the appellate Court did not peruse the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and from the judgment it further appears that it was not within the knowledge and notice of the appellate Court below that the record of 

 Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was available before him for his perusal and it would be clear from the judgment of the appellate Court below itself. The appellate Court below in the last portion of the judgment made observations in the following way: 

 59. From the above noted observations of the appellate Court it appears that the trial Court did not consider the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 as genuine as its original record was not called for and also made a blind endorsement to the said observations of the Trial Court although on the very date of pronouncement of the judgment the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was lying with the record of the Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 and it is a serious non-application of judicial mind on the part of the appellate Court. 

 60. The record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 shows that this suit was filed on 28.05.1956 by 3 brothers Abdul Hamid, Abul Kashem Molla and Hafizur Rahman along with Mominjan Bibi, that is, by 3(three) full brothers and one sister. Solenama was filed on 11.12.1956 and decree was passed on 18.12.1956.The time for disposal of the suit appears to be rational. Over and again, in the said suit (Title Suit No. 190 of 1956) there is a statement that through in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 the landlord admitted the claim of the plaintiffs which ultimately establishes that the claim of the 3 brothers and one sister as made in was not contradictory with the claim of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. 

 61. I have stated it earlier that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was not filed by Abul Kashem Molla and his sister Mominjan rather it was filed by some other persons. Whenever the 3 brothers and one sister filed a subsequent suit being Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 where their title in the suit land has been declared the decree and the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 appears to be more genuine and rational and binding upon the plaintiffs, the 3 brothers and one sister and there is no scope to deny the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. 

 62. More so, it is not natural and probable that with any ill motive or for some illegal gain in the year 1956 a suit was filed in the name of 3 brothers and one sister. Abul Kashem Molla filed the present suit in the year of 2001. It is unthinkable that 45 years ago a suit was filed for any other purpose without any genuine reasons. Since the 3 brothers and 1 sister acquired the suit land from the landlord and since a suit which was filed by some other persons which was decreed against the interest of the two remaining brothers namely Hafizur Rahman and Abdul Hamid, all the 3 brothers and 1 sister to have a genuine declaration regarding their title filed the Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and from the evidence of PW 1 (plaintiff Abul Kashem Mollah) that his other brothers have been possessing the suit land forcibly is very much significant in this Rule and ultimately has strengthened the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 in all the ways. 

 63. If the evidence of PW 1 is considered along with the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 it would be clear that pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 all the 3 brothers and sister have been possessing the suit land. Over and again, in this Rule, the petitioners filed an application for taking additional evidence to prove that pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 the name of 3 brothers and 1 sister have been mutated through Mutation Case No. 25 of 1961.This small piece of paper is enough to hold that the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 has been acted upon among the 3 brothers and 1 sister. 

 64. However, be that as it may, I find that both the trial Court and appellate Court below without considering the evidence and other materials on record came to a very wrong and illegal conclusion that Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi got the suit land through the decree in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954.The appellate Court below without considering the evidence on record and without going through the records of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 made a simple ditto to the judgment of the trial Court which cannot be appreciated rather I deprecate the attitude and non application of judicial mind and non consideration of important materials on record by the appellate Court below. 

 68. In this Rule, it has been found earlier that the Courts below did not consider the evidence of possession of the defendant petitioners although their possession has been strongly supported by the witnesses of the plaintiff himself and the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 which was called for, for perusal of the appellate Court below and though the said record came before the appellate Court below before the pronouncement of judgment, the appellate Court below did not consider the same rather made a great ditto to the judgment of the trial Court. 

 75. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The judgment and decree dated 20.03.2008 passed in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 are hereby set aside and consequently the judgment and decree dated 13.11.2005., passed in the Title Suit No.16 of 2001 by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Patuakhali is also set aside. Title Suit No. 16 of 2001 is sent back on remand to the trial Court for trial afresh.
