full_judgment:
Fatema Najib J: These First Appeal No. 212 of 2009, First Appeal No. 230 of 2009, Transfer Appeal No. 1 of 2014 and Transfer Appeal No. 2 of 2014 are directed against the judgment and decree dated 30-11-2008 passed by learned Joint District Judge, Third Court, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 51 of 2001, Title Suit No. 93 of 2014 and Title Suit No. 52 of 2001 which were heard analogously and now are being disposed of by this single judgment. 

 2. The respondent Nos. 1-3 of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 32 of 1997, in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Golapgonj, Sylhet impleading principal respondents Nos.4 and 5 as principal defendant Nos. 1 and 2, pro-forma respondent Nos. 6 and 7 as pro-forma defendant Nos. 3 and 4, Abdus Sattar, the predecessor of appellants Nos. 1 and 2 as the defendant Nos. 5 and appellants Nos.3-13 as 6-16 Nos. defendants for redemption of mortgage and khas possession in respect of 0.34 acres of land as described in schedule to plaint. Subsequently, it was transferred to the Joint District Judge Third Court, Sylhet and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 51 of 2001. The respondent No. 3 Pulin Ram Malakar died during the pendency of appeal and his legal heirs have been duly substituted. The plaintiff No.1 Gakul Ram Malakar of Title Suit No. 32 of 1997 (re-number as 51 of 2001) died during the pendency of the suit and his legal heir Nikhil Ram Malakar has been duly substituted as plaintiff No. 1(ka). 

 3. The appellant Nos. 1 and 2 of Title Appeal No. 147 of 2009 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 14 of 1994 in the Court of Joint District Judge, First Court, Sylhet impleading Abdus Sattar, the predecessor of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 as defendant Nos. 2, respondents Nos.3-12 as defendants Nos. 3-12, Seraj the predecessor of respondent Nos. 13-17 as defendant No. 13, the respondent Nos. 18 to 24 as defendant Nos. 14-20 praying for partition in respect of 0.7 acres of land as described in schedule 1, declaration of right, title and interest in respect of second schedule property to the plaint. It may be mentioned that the heirs of Abdur Rahman who are also appellants in this Title Appeal No.147 of 2009 were added as plaintiffs 3-7 in the original suit by order No.144 dated 18-11-2008. During pendency of the suit the defendant Nos. 13 and 16 died whose legal heirs has been duly substituted. Subsequently, it was transferred to Joint District Judge, First court, Sylhet and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 93 of 2014. The said Title Appeal No.147 of 2009 was ultimately transferred to the High Court Division by Order dated 14-5-2012 passed in Civil Miscellaneous Case No.16 of 2010 and re-numbered as Transfer Appeal No.1 of 2014. 

 4. The heirs of Seraj (defendant No.13) of the said Title Suit No. 14 of 1994/93 of 1994 as appellants filed First Appeal No. 230 of 2009 against the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 as pro-forma respondent Nos. 4, 5 and the defendants Nos. 19-20 as pro-forma respondent Nos. 6 and 7, the defendant Nos. 3-12, and 15 as respondent Nos. 8-16, Gakul Ram Malakar, the predecessor of the defendant No.16, the defendant Nos.17 and 18 as principal respondents 1-3. 

 5. The appellant No. 2, the predecessor of appellant No. 1, the predecessor of appellant Nos. 3-6 of Title Appeal No.108 of 2009 as plaintiff Nos. 1-3 instituted Title Suit No.15 of 1994 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Golapgonj, Sylhet impleading the respondents as defendants Nos. 1-22 for declaration of title by adverse possession for more than 12 years of the statutory period, correction of record in respect of first schedule to plaint as shail in place of canel and Khas possession in respect of second Schedule to plaint. Subsequently, it was transferred to the Sub-Judge, Third Court, Sylhet and re-numbered as Title Suit No.52 of 2001. The said Title Appeal No.108 of 2009 was transferred to the High Court Division by Order dated 14-5-2012 passed in Civil Miscellaneous Case No.17 of 2010 and re-numbered as Transfer Appeal No. 2 of 2014. 

 6. The case of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 32 of 1997/51 of 2001 who are the defendant Nos.16-18 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 is that Gagan Ram Malakar, Raman Ram Malakar, and Avoy Ram Malakar who are successive owners by in-heritance of the suit land and subsequently executed and registered a sale deed on 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS in favour of Jahir Ali, (the predecessor of the defendant Nos.1 and 2) receiving Taka 100 as consideration money in respect of suit land and on the same date Jahir Ali executed a registered Ekrarnama in favour of the aforesaid Gagan Ram Malakar and others in respect of the same suit land promising to reconvey the suit land to the vendors on repayment of the consideration money within, 30th chaitra, 1361 BS. The transaction was not a sale, it was a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period of 7 years in accordance with the provisions of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and after the expiry of 7 years it was redeemable by operation of law. The plaintiffs on several times requested the defendants to redeem the mortgage by receiving the consideration money. But the defendants refused to comply on the end of Bhadra, 1400 BS. Hence the plaintiff is constrained to file the present suit. 

 7. The heirs of Jahir Ali that is Md Manik Mia and Mst. Sabiya Begum the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 14 of 1994/93 of 1994 who are the defendant Nos.1 and 2 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 in brief their case is that Raman Ram Malakar, Gagan Ram Malakar and Ador Ram Malakar were owners of the first schedule land and while possessing the first schedule land Raman Ram Malakar and his two aforesaid brothers sold the first schedule land to Jahir Ali, (the predecessor of the plaintiffs) on 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11 Baisakh 1359 BS through a saf kabala. After getting the scheduled land they paid rent regularly to Zamidar. While possessing the first schedule land, Jahir Ali Sold 0.33 acres of land out of the land as described in first schedule land to Abdur Rahman (the predecessor of 4-12 defendants), the defendant Nos.1-3 on different dates by saf kabala and Jahir Ali has been possessing the remaining 0.07 acres of land by constructing tin shed building where made a tea-stall for long years. Subsequently, he died leaving behind the plaintiff No.1 as son and the plaintiff No. 2 as daughter. Later on the aforesaid Md Manik Mia and Mst Sabiya Begum came to know that on 24-4-1952 Gagan Ram Malakar and his two brothers executed a sale deed, in respect of suit land in favour of Jahir Ali who also executed ekrarnama (deed of agreement) promising to recovery the land to the vendors on repayment of the consideration money within 30th Chaitra 1361 BS corresponding to 24-4-1946. The plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by running tea-stall. The defendant Nos. 4-12 recently started construction a new building in first schedule of the plaint and threatened the defendants to destroy their restaurant from the suit land. In the meantime the defendants through Daroga of local thana on 8-5-1994 issued a notice alleging that the plaintiffs are illegal possessor and the plaintiffs are restraining the defendant No.4 from constructing. After getting the said notice the plaintiffs requested the defendant No. 4 on 9-5-1994 for partition in respect of 0.07 acres. But the defendant No. 4 refused the request. The plaintiffs have been possessing the second schedule land which is included of first schedule for more than 12 years of the statutory period since their predecessors. But the land of second schedule was inadvertently recorded in the name of the defendant No.14 in separate khatian and Mouja. The plaintiffs came to know on first part of January, 1994 that 0.34 acres of first schedule was recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs on RS Dag No. 2771 of RS Khatian No. 557. Since the defendant No.14 in collusion of defendant No. 4 refused the title of the plaintiffs, it clouded the right, title and interest of the plaintiff. Hence, the plaintiffs constrained to file the instant suit. 

 8. The defendant Nos. 1 and 5-16 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 contested the suit by filing separate written statement. The contents of defendant Nos.1 and 5-16 are almost same. It is contended by the defendant Nos. 5-16 that they purchased the land in total 29.875 decimals from Jahir Ali and his two brothers by 6 kabalas dated 1-2-1990, 16-11-1974, 12-12-1974 and 12-4-1975 and by 2 more kabalas, both dated 22-4-1975. They have been possessing the purchased lands by constructing building thereon. 

 9. The defendants Nos. 2(ka)-2(kha), 4-12 and 13 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 filed written statement separately. Their case are that Jahir Ali and his brother Junayed Ali together sold 0.1225 acres to the defendant No.13 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 on different dates. The defendant Nos. 4-12 purchased 0.1175 acres on different date from Jahir Ali and his brothers. The defendant No.2 purchased 0.0550 acres from Jahir Ali and his brother. 

 10. The case of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 in brief, is that the predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants Charan Ram Malakar were owners of the first schedule land as described in schedule to the plaint. Subsequently, the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants became successive owners by inheritance, Gagan Ram and his 2 brothers, predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendant Nos. 9-10 during their life time produced CS Khatian and other documents before the employee of settlement Jarip at the time of preparation of SA Khatian. They believed SA Khatian was prepared in their names. The predecessors of the plaintiffs for their convenience of enjoyment partitioned the suit land along with other lands and accordingly Gagan Ram Malakar got the suit land in his saham. The plaintiffs filled up the suit land with earth. But the defendant Nos. 3-8 evicted the plaintiffs from the suit second schedule land by constructing tin shed building. The plaintiff on several times requested the defendant Nos.3-8 to leave the suit second schedule land in their favour. But the defendants claimed that the land of second schedule was recorded in the name of Government and they took lease from the Government. On searching in the local Tahsil Office, the plaintiffs came to know on 18-2-2014 that the land of first schedule of plaint was recorded in SA Khatian as canal খাল which was incorrect. In fact the suit land should be recorded as সাইলউরা in CS Khatian in the name of predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants. Thus the plaintiffs were cons-trained to file the suit for declaration of title by adverse possession for statutory period of 12 years in respect of first schedule land, decla-ration that SA Khatian is wrong in respect of first schedule land and Khas possession in respect of second schedule land as described in schedule to plaint. 

 11. The defendant No.3 and the defendant Nos.11-22 contested the suit by filing separate written statement. The statements of the defendant No. 3 is same to the statements of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 which was discussed above. The case of the defendants Nos.11-22 is that the First schedule land is a part of Fulbari Mouja. The First Schedule land had no existence in Tikorbari Mouja. Jahir Ali, the predecessor of these defendants purchased the schedule land along with other lands from the Original owner Gokul Malakar and others on 24-4-1952. Jahir All and his two brothers Jayed Ali and Tasir Ali, while possessing the suit land, Tasir Ali died. Thereafter Jahir Ali and Jonayed All sold 0.06 acres to Serajuddin, Jahir All and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 4 Jaista 3 pon,10 Gonda to the defendants No.11 on 1-2-1970 by saf kabala. Then Jahir Ali and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 0.0625 acres to the predecessor of defendant Nos. 13-21 on 7-11-1974. Again on 16-11-1974 Jahir Ali and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 0.0150 acres to the mother of defendant No.11 and grandmother of defendant Nos.13-21. Subsequently, Jahir Ali and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 0.0625 acres, 0.0550 acres 0.0550 acres, to defendant No.12, Abdur Rahman, the predecessor of defendant Nos.13-22 and the defendant No.11 respectively and after selling the aforesaid lands Jahir All and his brothers had no land in suit jote. 

 12. On Scrutiny the pleadings of the above mentioned suits i.e. Title Suit Nos.32 of 1997/51 of 2001, 14 of 1994/93 of 1994 and 15 of 1994/52 of 2001 the trial court had framed the issues as follows: 

 13. Manik Mia, the plaintiff No.1 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 deposed on behalf of all plaintiffs as PW 1 on Commission and 3 more witnesses were examined as PWs 2-4 and the documents produced by them were marked as Exhibit ক-ছ and Exhibits-x-x(1). 

 14. Gakul Ram Malakar, the plaintiff No. 1 of Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 and Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 deposed on behalf of all the plaintiffs as PW 1 on Commission and three more witnesses were examined as 2-4. 

 16. On considering the oral and documentary evidences the trial court decreed the Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 against the contesting defendant Nos.1 and 5-16 and ex-parte against the rest, dismissed the Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 against the contesting defendant Nos. 16-18 and 2ka, 2(kha) and defendant Nos. 4-13 and ex-parte against the rest and also dismissed the Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 against the contesting defendant Nos. 3 and 11-22 and ex-parte against the rest. 

 17. Being aggrieved by judgment and decree dated 30-11-2008, the defendant Nos. 5-16 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 as appellants preferred First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 and the heirs of defendant No.13 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 preferred First Appeal No. 230 of 2009. It is pertinent to note that the appellants of the said First Appeal No. 230 of 2009 claimed ownership through purchase some portion of the land from the chronological recipient of the kabala in question dated 24-4-1952. The appellants claimed the said deed is out and out sale. But the learned trial court decreed the Title Suit. No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 considering the said deed in question is mortgage deed and, as such, they filed the instant First Appeal No. 230 of 2009. 

 18. In the same way being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 30-11-2008, the plaintiffs 1-7 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 as appellants preferred Title Appeal No. 147 of 2009 before the District Judge, Sylhet which was subsequently transferred to the High Court Division and re-numbered as Transfer Appeal No. 1 of 2014. 

 19. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the same judgment and decree the plaintiff Nos.1-3 of Title Suit No. 15 of 1994/52 of 2001 as appellants preferred Title Appeal No. 108 of 2009 before District Judge, Sylhet which was being transferred to the High Court Division and re-numbered as Transfer Appeal No. 2 of 2014. 

 20. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Advocate on behalf of defendants Nos.5-16 appellants of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 submits that the root of disputes between the parties based on the deed in question being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS and the agreement for reconveyance of the said land executed on the same date stipulated a period of 3 years from the said date that is to say, the time for reconveyance expired on 30th chaitra 1361 corresponding to 24-4-1956 and the said transaction is not attracted by section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. He further submits that a transaction by way of out and out sale with an separate agreement to reconvay deed was not a mortgage before coming into effect of the Presidents Order (PO 88 of 1972) read with Presidents Order 136 of 1972, because of facts such transaction was not a mortgage by definition of "Mortgage" as provided in section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act. He next submits that where the agreement to recovery is embodied in the same document by which sale is effected the transaction is conditional mortgage. He also submits that the deed in question is out and out sale with an agreement to recovery which has been treated to be mortgage under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and same was not alive on 3-8-1972, the date of coming into effect of the Presidents Order 88 of 1972. He further submits such transaction is past and closed and the property involved in such transaction will not be redeemable. He finally submits that the trial court erroneously held that the deed in question is out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey constituted a complete usufructuary mortgage for 7 years and ignoring the doctrine past and closed decreed the Title Suit No.51 of 2001 for redemption of mortgage and khas of possession in respect of 0.34 acres of suit land is totally illegal. In support of his submissions learned advocate referred the decision reported in 32 DLR(AD) 233, 16 BLD (AD) 210 = 1 BLC (AD) 90 and 1 BLC (AD) 164. 

 23. Mr Dider Alam Kollol, the learned Advocate on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 of Transfer Appeal No. 2 of 2014 argued that the learned trial court without considering the evidence of the plaintiff appellants reached into erroneous decision. CS Khatian was filed by the original owner Charan Ram Malakar which was marked as Exhibit-1. But the learned court erroneously found that the plaintiff could not file documents in his support. In the plaint it was specifically mentioned that the plaintiffs were evicted by the defendants on first part of poush in 1400 BS. But the court below did not consider it. He finally submits the trial court in its judgment did not mention about the commissioners report which is totally misconceived on law. He also argued that learned court below on misconception of law found the deed in question dated 24-4-1952 is a mortgage deed. In fact that deed is within the mischief of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but it was not alive at the date of commencement of Presidents Order No. 88 of 1972 on 3-8-1972. So, the said transaction does not attract section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Jahir Ali became owner on the basis of deed No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 and subsequently after selling the property 0.7 decimals remain with Jahir Ali. After death of Jahir Ali his heirs the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 and plaintiff of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 became owner and they are entitled for partition of 0.7 decimals of land. 

 24. In reply the learned Advocate Mr Khan Ezaz Maswood argued that the heirs of Jahir Ali will not get 0.7 decimals of land for partition as the heirs of Jahir Ali did not pray for declaration of title over 0.7 decimals of land. Moreover Md Manik Miah son of Jahir Ali deposed as PW 1 in Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 that 0.33 decimals of land was sold out by Jahir Ali and 02 decimals of land was acquired by CNB. The total disputed land is 0.34 decimals. So, the heirs of Jahir Ali will not get partition for 0.7 decimals as prayed for and the learned court did not commit any error of law and facts by dismissing the Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994. 

 26. Admittedly the first schedule land of three Suits i.e. Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 and Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 were originally belonged by Charan Ram Malakar. It may be noted that total land of first schedule to the plaint of three suits are 1 kader, 1 powa, 4 jaista in local measurement equivalent to 39 acres as argued by learned Advocate Khair Ezaz Maswood. Charan Ram Malakar died leaving behind 4 sons namely, Gagan Ram Malakar, Behari Ram Malakar, Raman Ram Malakar and Avoy Ram Malakar. Behari Ram Malakar died leaving behind 3 brothers as childless. Raman Ram Malakar died leaving behind two sons namely Naresh Ram Malakar, Gopesh Ram Malakar (pro-forma defendant Nos.3 and 4 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001). Then Avoy Ram Malakar died leaving only brother Gagan Ram Malakar. During the life time of Gagan Ram Malakar, Raman Ram Malakar, Avoy Ram Malakar they executed a registered sale deed on 24-4-1952 corres-ponding to 11-1-1359 BS in favour of Jahir Ali (father of Abdul Manik and Mst Sabiya Begum of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001) receiving Rupees 100 only and on the same date Jahir Ali executed a registered Ekrarnama Deed in favour of Gagan Ram Malakar, Roman Ram Malakar and Avoy Ram Malakar. It was stipulated in the Ekrarnama deed that the consideration money Rupees 100 will be paid back by 30th chaittra 1361 BS i.e. within 3 years. 

 27. It is alleged by the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 32 of 1997/51 of 2001 and Title Suit No: 15 of 1994/52 of 2001 and defendant Nos.16-20 of Title Suit No. 14 of 1994/93 of 1994 that the deed in question dated 24. 04.1952 was never a sale deed. It was a usufractuary Mortgage within the mischief of section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It is also alleged that the consideration money was paid and moreover it should be re-deemed after 7 years as per section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 28. It is alleged by the defendant Nos. 5-16 of Title Suit No. 32 of 1997/51 of 2001 the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 the defendant Nos.3, 11-22 of Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 that the deed in question dated 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS and on the same date the agreement for reconveyance was executed which is not mortgage as defined in section 58 of the Transfer Property Act. In other words, it was not a mortgage proper before 3-8-1972 (the date of coming into effect of President Order No. 88 of 1972 and President Order No. 136 of 1972). By the said president Order the deed in question dated 24-4-1952 was treated to be mortgage. But the deed in question was not alive on 3-8-1972 inasmuch as the period mentioned in the Deed of reconveyance was fixed to reconvey the land by 30 chaittra, 1361 BS i.e within 3 years of the Deed which had expired long before 3-8-1972. So, the transaction of the deed in question is past and closed and it was not liable to be redeemed. This deed in question is treated to be mortgage. The defendant appellants are owners by subsequent purchase and they have been possessing the suit land. 

 29. The core issue in this appeal is that whether the Deed No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 and reconveyance deed No.720 dated 24-4-1952 (Exhibit-X, X(I) are the basic documents upon which the parties claimed their respective title is complete usufructary mortgage or treated to be mortgage under section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and whether the deed in question is attracted to section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 35. On careful reading the registered saf kabala deed dated 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS (Exhibit-X) and the deed of reconveyance on the same date (Exhibit-X-(1), it appears that the predecessors of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 sold the suit property i.e. 1 Kader, 1 powa 4 jaista in local measurement to Jahir Ali, father of defendant Nos.1 and 2 of said suit with a condition of re-purchase of the same within 3 years that is 30th chaittra 1361 corresponding to 24-4-1956. 

 36. The learned Advocate Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, argued that an out and out sale accompanied by an agreement for reconveyance is within the purview of the Presidents Order Nos. 88 and 136 of 1972 and No.24 of 1973 whereby provisions of section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have been amended and a new section being section 95A has been inserted in the said Act. The Presidents Order No.88 of 1972 came into effect on 3-8-1972 (PO No.136 of 1972) and the condition giving right of repurchase having expired the sale became a past and closed transaction and on the same reason the plaintiffs are not entitled for redemption of mortgage of the suit land. In this respect he referred the decision reported in 32 DLR (AD), 233. 

 41. Therefore Exhibit-X, X(i) coupled with section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the decision reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233, 16 BLD (AD) 210 = 1 BLC (AD) 90, 1 BLC (AD) 164 clearly proved that the deed in question being No.719 dated 24-4-1952 with registered agreement deed being No.720 dated 24-4-1952 treated to be mortgage but since the transaction was not alive on 3-8-1972, at the promulgation of President Order 88 of 1972, the said transaction is not hit by section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 42. Therefore, we find the trial court held the deed in question being No.719 dated 24-4-1952 with an agreement to reconvey being 720 dated 24- 4-1952 constituted a complete usufructuary mortgage for a maximum period of 7 years based on totally misconception of law and facts. So, the decree passed by the trial court for re-deemption of mortgage and khas possession in favour of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 is erroneous. 

 43. Similarly in Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 the plaintiffs claimed title on the basis of the sale Deed No.719 dated 24-4-1952 (Exhibit-X) and reconveyance Deed No. 720 dated 24-4-1952 (Exhibit-X-(1) is not proved mortgage at all under section 58 of Transfer of Property Act and the learned trial court rightly dismissed the said suit. Though the trial court dismissed the suit on different findings that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title and possession over the suit land and also failed to prove the dispossession from the suit land. So, we can easily rely on the decision reported in 32 DLR (AD), 233 which has been subsequently followed in the decision reported in 16 BLD (AD) 210 = 1 BLC (AD) 90, 1 BLC (AD) 164. 

 44. In Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 the heirs of Jahir Ali, Md Manik Mia and Sabiya Begum sought for partition in respect of 0.7 decimals of land as described in First Schedule of land and declaration for 0.02 decimals as described in second Schedule land to the plaint. Manik Mia as PW 1 in Title Suit No. 93 of 1994 in his chief stated: 

 46. The plaintiff No.1, Manik Mia, (son of Jahir Ali) admitted in his deposition that they had no title over 0.2 decimals out of 0.7 decimals. So, in this respect without praying for declaration of title, the suit for partition over 0.7 decimals is not maintainable. Moreover, Md Manik Mia, son of jahir Ali categorically stated in his chief that they sold 0.33 decimals. Thus it is evident that the second schedule land is from different Mouja which is not disputed in the suit and without declaration of title, the relief sought only for partition in respect of 0.7 decimals is not maintainable and the trial court rightly dismissed the suit. 

 47. The defendant Nos. 5-16 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 claimed they purchased 29.875 decimals by Exhibit-খ২,গ৩,ঘ৪,ঙ৫,চ৬, from Jahir Ali. On perusal of those Exhibits it appears by Exhibit- খ২,গ৩,ঘ৪,ঙ৫,চ৬, an area of land is 0.0425, 0.0625, 0.0625, 0.0550, 0.0550 respectively in total 28.75 decimals of land were purchased. Gokul Ram Malakar the plaintiff  No.1 of Title Suit Nos.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 and 15 of 1994/52 of 2001 admitted in cross stating that Jahir Ali sold his maximum property to Abdur Rahman and others. It may be mentioned that defendant Nos.7-16 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 are heirs of Abdur 

 Rahman, the defendant Nos.5-6 are Abdus Sattar and his wife. Manik Mia as PW 1 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/5 of 2001 in cross admitted that his father sold those lands. Thus it is proved that defendant Nos.5-16 became owners of total 28.75 decimals of land through purchase by Exhibits, খ২,গ৩,ঘ৪,ঙ৫,চ৬, respectively from Jahir Ali, father of plaintiff. 

 48. Having regard to facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the deed being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 upon which parties are claiming their respective title, the trial court on misconception of law and facts most illegally held the said deed is out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey constituted to be usufructuary mortgage for 7 years and on that basis decreed the Title Suit No. 51 of 2001 for redemption of mortgage and khas possession. Since we have found that heirs of Jahir Ali failed to prove the suit for partition over 0.7 decimals, and 0.2 decimals for declaration of title which is situated in different mouja and unspecified that has no nexus with the present claim, so the trial court rightly dismissed the Title Suit No. 93 of 1994 and Title Suit No. 52 of 2001. 

 49. In the result the First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 is allowed without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 30-11-2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet decreeing the Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 is set aside and the suit is dismissed.

parties:

VS

full_judgment:
Upon condoning a delay of 36 days in filing the civil revisional application Rule was issued in the instant Civil Revisional application calling upon opposite parties No. 1(ka)- 1(chha) to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 21-8-2016(decree signed on 15-9-2016) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Narayangonj in Title Appeal No. 22 of 2016 affirming the judgment and decree dated 13-1-2016 (decree signed on 20-1-2016) passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Bandar Adalot, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 73 of 2006 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The present petitioner as 'plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 73 of 2006 in the court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Bandar Adalat, Narayangonj praying for permanent injunction and subsequently mandatory injunction upon impleading the present opposites party as defendants. Upon hearing both sides the trial court dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 13-1-2016. 

 3. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial court dated 13-1-2016 in Title Suit No. 73 of 2006 the plaintiffs as appellants preferred Title Appeal No 22 of 2016 which was heard by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Narayartgonj and the court of learned Joint District Judge disallowed the appeal by its judgment and decree dated 21-8-2016. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the judgment and decree of the appellate court the sole plaintiff appellant as petitioner filed the civil revisional application which is before me for disposal. 

 4. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule in short is that Brajahari Das was owner of anarea of 3 decimals of land out of 9 decimals of plot No. 16 under CS khatian No. 49, 27 decimals of land out of 54 decimals of Plot No. 17 and undisputed land in area of 0.42 acres in total 0.72 acres of land. Before CS record Brajahori Das died leaving behind Chandra Mohan Das and Rajmohan Das and it was recorded in 11 annas share in CS record. Raj Mohan Das died unmarried and Chandra Mohan Das recieved sixteen annas share, who died leaving behind 39 three sons namely Mon Mohan Das, Gopal Chandra Das and Hari Charan Das. Hari Charan Das died leaving 1(one) son Laxmi Kanta Das. Gopal Chandra Das leaving behind 1(one) son Lal Mohan Das and SA record published in SA khatian No. 30. Laxmi Kanta Das died leaving his uncle Monmohan Das and cousin Lal Mohan Das. Monmohan Das and his brother's son each got 110 annas share who got 36 decimals of land each. Lalmohan Das got 1.33 acres of land from plot No. 16 and Lal Mohan Das got 9 decimals of land from Plot-17. Thereafter Lal Mohan Das while is possession of the land appointed one Julhas Bhuiyan as Attorney by dint of a power of Attorney Deed No. 2878 dated 14-5-1997.The power of attorney holder sold the suit land by registered deed No. 3257 to Sahida Akter on 25-5-1997. Sahida Akter got 9 decimals of land and used to possess the land by erecting two shed house which consists of 4(four) rooms, 2(two) pucca bathrooms, Latrine, Tube well. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit for declaration of title and correction of RS khatian in the Court of Second Assistant Judge, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 128 of 1997 and the said suit was transferred to the Assistant Judge, and renumbered as Title Suit No. 16 of 2001. The learned 4th Assistant Judge upon hearing was pleased to dismiss the suit. Thereafter the plaintiff filed an appeal in the court of learned District Judge, Narayangonj being Title Appeal No. 29 of 2000 and the appeal was transferred to the court of learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayan-gonj, The appellant filed an application for withdrawal of appeal being No. 29 of 2000 in the court of learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangoj and the court allowed the said application and dismissed the said appeal on 6-3-2004. Thereafter the defendants on 25-4-2004 at about 07-00 am attempted to disposess the plaintiff from the suit land but the defendants failed in their attempt and the plaintiff filed an application for permanent injunction. The defendants as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 17 of 2000 in the court of reamed Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Narayangonj and the said suit was decreed. Thereafter the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 17(being defendant in the present suit) filed Execution Suit No. 1 of 2000 and the said Execution Suit was decreed. The plaintiff in Title Suit No. 17 with the help of court and along with police forces went to take possession of 5 decimals of land on 11-2-2007 but while taking possession of the 5 decimals of land decreed they also dispossessed the present plaintiff from their 9 decimals of land with four rooms and two rooms wide poucca tin shed house, one kitchen room and two tube-well and consequently for that reason the plaintiff lost 1,50,000 (Taka one lac fifty thousand). The Advocate commissioner submitted a report and in the said report he reported that there were set-up houses and others structures in the said 9 decimals of land. The plaintiff filed an application for mandatory injunction before the learned court to restore his possession. 

 5. The defendants respondent Nos.1-6 contested the suit upon filing a written statement before the learned court alleging inter alia that Bashiram Das was recorded tenant in CS khatian No. 57 and CS Plot Nos. 16 and 17 and other plot No. 126. Bashiram died leaving behind one son Ram Mohan Das. Thereafter Ram Mohan Das died leaving behind one son Monoranjan Das and SA khatian No. 38 was prepared in the name of Monoranjan Das. Monoranjan Das possessed 3 decimals of land out of 9 decimals of land in CS plot No. 16 and also possessed 27 decimals of land out of 54 decimals of land in CS plot No. 17. Thereafter Monoranjan Das sold 1.50 decimals of land from the plot No. 16 and 13.50 decimals of land from the plot No. 17 dated 13-4-1974 to Amina Khatun and Monoranjan Das also sold 1.50 decimals of land from plot No. 16 and 13.50 decimals of land from the plot No. 17 dated 13-4-1974 to Saleha Khatun. Thereafter the said Amina Khatun and Saleha Khatun sold. 30 decimals of land to the defendant Nos. 3, 4 and 5 dated 8-8-1977, 9-8-1977 and 10-8-1997. CS khatian No. 45 was prepared in the name of the Gopal Chandra Das and the heirs of Gopal Chandra Das sold 16 decimals of land from Plot No. 16 and 17 to Mir Wazed Ali. Thereafter Mir Wazed Ali sold 15 decimals of land to Md Mohiuddin and others on 22-2-1980. Thereafter Md Mohiuddin and others sold the said land to the predecessors of Israfil Hossain defendant Nos. 2-5 vide 6 kabala deeds dated 17-5-1980, 18-5-1980, 16-5-1980, 22-6-1981, 23-6-1981 and 24-6-1981 in favour of defendant Nos. 3, 4 and 5. The recorded tenant of SA khatian No. 45 of plot Nos. 16 and 17 heirs of Gopal Chandra Das settled 16 decimals of land from plot Nos. 16 and 17 on 10th Chaitra, 1351 BS to Mr Wazed Ali. Mir Wazed Ali sold 15 decimals of land on 22-2-1980 to Md Mohiuddin and others. Subsequently Md Mohiuddin and others sold 15 decimals of land on 17-5-1980, 18-5-1980, 16-5-1981, 22-6-1981, 23-6-1981 and 24-6-1981 by 6 registered deeds to the predecessor of defen-dant Nos.2 to 5, Ismail Hossain subsequently Ismail Hossain Sarker died leaving behind defendant Nos.2-5. The plaintiffs father-in-law died in the year 1974 during the middle part when the plaintiff's husband was in Khulna. Plaintiff's mother in law became helpless and she prayed for shelter before the predecessor of defendant Nos.2-5, Israfil Hossain Sarker. Firstly he occupied plot No. 17 to live thereon, subsequently he gave permission to plaintiff's husband to live there temporarily. Plaintiff's mother in law Munchehara as a licensee bagan to live in the house by erecting houses thereon. Sub-sequently Ismail Hossain Sarker asked her to leave the premises. Later on defendant Nos. 3, 4 and 5 also asked them to do the same in 1985. Monchehara assured them that she would leave very soon, but instead of vacating the premises she filed a case for specific performance of contract by way Title Suit No. 75 of 1985. The said suit was dismissed against which she preferred Title Appeal No. 38 of 1995 before the court of learned District judge and the same was also dismissed. Later on plaintiff's mother in law preferred Civil Revision being No. 3602 of 1995 and Rule was discharged in Civil Revision No 3602 of 1995 and consequently the said judgment and decree is binding upon the plaintiff's mother in law, The present plaintiff was impleaded as defendant in the suit which was filed by the defendants in Title Suit No. 134 of 1995 wherein the schedule of suit land is the same land as in Title Suit No. 75 of 1985. The plaintiff filed a suit for declaration of Title in the court of learned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Narayangonj being Title Suit No. 16 of 2000 and the same was dismissed on 15-2-2002. 

 7. Learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that both courts below upon misreading and misappreciation of the evidences erroneously dismissed the suit and disallowed the appeal respectively. By way of elaborating his submissions he asserts that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 75 of 1985 filed by the mother in law of the plaintiff is not binding upon them mainly on the ground that the subject matter of Title Suit No. 75 of 1985 and the instant suit are not the same but that the courts below overlooked this material fact. In this context he submits that during delivery of possession the defendants while taking possession of the 5 acres of land in dag No. 16 and 17 by dint of court order also unlawfully encroached upon 9 acres of land of the plaintiff's land in the same dag and thereby unlawfully dispossessed the petitioner from her lawful possession. He further contends that the petitioner was in possession of the property but that she was unlawfully dispossessed by the defendants opposite parties. He further argues that the petitioner's claim arises by dint of a power of attorney given by the heirs of the original CS recorded owner to one Julhash Bhuiyan vide power of attorney deed No. 2878 dated 14-5-1997 and further pursuaded that by dint of that power of attorney dated 14-5-1997 the power of attorney holder lawfully registered the sale deed in favour of the petitoner by registered deed No. 3257 dated 25-5-1997. It is further contended that thereby the petitioner has been in lawful possession and holds lawful title to the 9 acres of suit land including other property. He stresses upon the issue that the petitioner was unlawfully evicted by the defendants opposite parties from her 9 acres of land. In support of his submissions that the judgment and decree of the trial court in Title Suit No. 75 of 1985 is not being binding on them since the subject matter of the 2 suits are different, he cites a decision of this court in the case of Md Rajiuddin Chowdhury vs Suruj Ali reported in 1996 BLD 96. On the issue of maintainability of the mandatory injunction he contends that the suit as a suit of mandatory injunction is maintainable. In support of his submissions that mandatory injunction is maintainable in the case of the petitioner, he cites a decision of this court in the case of Bangladesh vs Md Ferozur Rahman reported in 45 DLR 762. He continues his submissions asserting that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit for declaration of title and correction of RS khatian in the court of Assistant judge, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 128 of 1997 for declaration of title. He also submits that the plaintiff has been possessing 0.09 acres of land from plot No. 17 of SA khatian No. 30 whereas the defendant No. 1(ka) to 1(chha) and defendant No. 2 has claimed in respect of 0.05 acres of land from plot No. 16 of SA khatian No. 30. He contends that in these circumstances the courts below without solving the same evicted the petitioner on 11-5-2007 by demolishing houses from the land of the plot for which the plaintiff prays for mandatory injunction to restore the same but the court below did not consider her prayer causing failure of justice. He concludes his submissions upon assertion that the both the courts below overlooked all these materials factors and erroneously passed the two judgments and therefore the judgments ought to be set-aside and the Rule be made absolute for ends of justice. 

 8. On the other hand learned counsel for the opposite parties submits that the courts below correctly passed their judgments upon accurately reading into the evidences and upon proper appraisal of the deposition taken from the witnesses from both sides. By way of his contention he takes me to the records of the case and to the judgments of the courts below wherefrom he shows that the mother in law of the plaintiff filed a Title Suit being Title suit No. 75 of 1985 regarding the same schedule of land as the instant suit wherein parties were also the same. He points out that Title Suit No. 75 of 1985 was dismissed by the trial court and such dismissal was later affirmed by the appellate court against which the present petitioner filed a Civil Revision being Civil Revision No. 3602 of 1996 before the High Court Division and in which Rule was discharged. He also submits that against the judgment and order of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3602 of 1996 the petitioner did not take resort to the appellate division. He persuaded that such being the position the judgment and decree dated 14-3-1995 in Title Suit No. 75 of 1985 stands valid and it is in operation and cannot be questioned any more and the instant suit is barred by the principle of res-judicata. Controverting the submissions of the petitioner that the subject matter of the two suits are different the learned Advocate for the opposite parties opposes and submits that both courts below upon carefully sifting through the evidences and records arrived upon the finding that the subject matter of the two suits are the same. He agitates that therefore the instant suit of the plaintiff respondent petitioner is not maintainable in limine. Regarding the issue of eviction he submits that Title suit No. 75 of 1985 by the plaintiffs which was ultimately rejected up to the High Court Division by way of Civil Revision No. 3602 of 1996. He takes me to the record and shows that during pendency of the Civil Revision No. 3602 of 1996 the plaintiff respondent petitioner created a kabala deed being deed No. 3257 dated 25-5-1997 by dint of power of attorney being given by one Julhas Bhuiyan and claimed her title to the suit land there from by way of a "so called" purchase. 

 9. He continues that pursuant to the kabala deed No.3257 dated 25-5-1997 comprising of 10.33 decimals of land in total from dag Nos.16 and 17, the petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit for declaration of title and correction of RS khatian in the court of learned Assistant Judge, Narayangonj in Title Suit No.128 of 1997 for declaration of title which was subsequently transferred and renumbered as Title Suit No. 16 of 2000. He submits that in the said suit the trial court dismissed the suit and against which the petitioner as appellant preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 29 of 2000 but later on withdrew the appeal and the appeal was accordingly dismissed on 19-8-2002 and ultimately the petitioner filed an application for permanent injunction. He argues that subsequently the present opposite parties filed an eviction suit for declaration of title being Title Suit No. 134 of 1995 in the court of learned senior Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj and the case was heard by senior Assistant judge, 4th court, Narayangonj being renumbered as Title Suit No. 17 of 2000. The opposite parties continue that the eviction case which was dismissed on 15-2-2000 against which the present opposite parties filed- title Appeal No. 34 of 2000 and which appeal was allowed by judgment and decree dated 22-2-200. Against the Judgment and Decree in the Appeal the present petitioner filed a Civil Revision No. 1116 of 2001 against the eviction arising out of the evection case but the Rule in Civil Revision No. 1116 of 2001 was discharged by this division on 1-8-2006. In pursuance of the judgment of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1116 of 2001 affirming the order of the appellate court the opposite parties by dint of judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 17 of 2000 filed an execution case being execution case No.1 of 2001 for eviction of the defendant and delivery of possession through the court and thereby lawfully evicted the petitioner from the suit land on 11-2-2007 through a court order. Relying upon his argument he asserts that the defendants have been evicted from the suit land lawfully through the order of the court and further asserted that there is nothing on record to indicate that they were unlawfully evicted therefrom. He continues that the instant petitioner along with her mother-in-law was also a party in Title Suit No. 17 of 2000 which is the eviction case. He further submits that the plaintiff could not at any point prove during trial in the instant suit that they are in exclusive possession of the property. He draws this Court's attention to the effect that this division in Civil Revision No.3602 of 1996 made an observation that the plaintiff is only in possession upon permission to the mother in law of the plaintiffs and asserts that the mother in law was only in permissive possession under the defendant-opposite party Nos.3-16. He continues that therefore the plaintiff petitioners' case arising out of the same subject matter and holding the same interest as her mother in law, she has no right to claim any title or ownership to the property. He claims that the issue of title being settled in Title Suit No. 75 of 1985 and also in the subsequent Title Suit No. 134 of 1995 regarding the same land therefore since plaintiff was made a party in Title Suit No. 134 of 1995 subsequently renumbered as 17 of 2000, the plaintiffs petitioner cannot raise any further claim of title to the suit land by any other suit since it is a matter of res-judicata. In support of his submission that the courts below came upon concurrent finding of facts and evidences correctly, learned Advocate for the opposite parties cited a decision of this Court in the case of Bilkish Miah vs The State reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 297 = 3 BLC (AD) 182. In the light of his submission he concludes that both the courts having arrived into their finding upon proper sifting through evidences and proper appraisal into the facts and circumstances and in the absence of any illegality the judgment and decree of the courts below do not call for interference and the Rule bears no merit and ought to be discharged for ends of justice. 

 11. Upon perusal of the record and the judgment and decree of the courts below it appears from the record that the mother in law of the plaintiff in the instant suit filed a Suit being Title Suit No.75 of 1985 which was dismissed, appeal therefrom was also disallowed and Civil Revision No. 3602 of 1996 was also discharged by this division against the plaintiff's mother in law arising out of that suit. It also appears that the Title Suit No. 75 of 1985 which was filed by the mother in law of the plaintiff, the defendants in that suit were the instant opposite parties. Subsequently the instant opposite parties filed Title Suit No. 134 of 1995 which was later renumbered as Title Suit No. 17 of 2000 before the court of learned Assistant judge, Narayangonj for declaration of title and eviction of the defendant No.1 the mother in law of the petitioner. It is also revealed that instant petitioner was also added as defendant No. 2 in that suit. The suit ultimately went up to the High Court Division where the mother in law as petitioner filed Civil Revision No.1116 of 2001 and Rule was ultimately discharged on 1-8-2006.- Sub-sequently by dint of the order of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1116 of 2001 the opposite parties filed an execution case being Execution Case No.1 of 2001 and by dint of the execution case the concerned court passed an order on 11-2-2007 for delivery of possession and delivery of possession was made in favour of the present opposite parties by evicting the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 1116 of 2011 along with the instant petitioner from the suit land. It also appears from the records and from the judgments of courts below that after affirmation of the judgment and decree in title Suit No. 75 of 1985 which was ultimately affirmed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3602 of 1996, the plaintiffs in the instant suit show 'purchase' of the suit land from one Julhash Bhuiyan who supposedly is the power of attorney holder of Lal Mohon Das. The power of attorney deed is dated 14-5-1997 and the registered sale deed is dated 25-5-1997. In that event the Registered Deed for sale dated 25-5-1997 was executed only 11 days after the power of attorney Deed and it concerns the same property as in Title Suit No. 75 of 1985. It is needless to mention that once the title and ownership of property has been settled in a suit and which was ultimately affirmed by the higher court it cannot be questioned any more. It is only proved that the creation of the kabala deed dated 25-5-1997 is a forged deed created by the petitioner to seize the suit land. It is to be noted that in Civil Revision No. 3602 of 1996 in which the subject matter was the same as in the instant suit land, in that case this division observed that the plaintiff is in permissive possession of the land under the defendants No. 3-16 opposite parties. I am in respectful agreement with the observation of this division given that facts and circumstances and the deposition of the witnesses in the courts below suggest that truly the plaintiffs were only in permissive possession. During trial it could not be found any where from the records that plaintiffs are in exclusive possession of the property. It is also revealed from the records that the Kabala Deed No.3257 dated 25-5-1997 is relied upon by the plaintiffs in support of their claim to Title to the Suit land. The same Kabala Deed was pronounced by the Trial Court to be a "manufactured " Deed in Title Suit No.16 of 2000, and the Trial Court's Judgment was affirmed upon Appeal against which Civil Revision was filed in this Division but Rule was discharged. There is nothing on record to show that the matter went up to the Appellate Division. Therefore the Judgment of the trial Court is in operation and valid and so does its observation that the Kabala Deed of 1997 was a "manufactured deed". It was created upon collusion to unlawfully usurp upon the suit land. I have gone through the judgment of the courts below and I have found that both the courts elaborately discussed the deposition of the witnesses from both sides. It also appears that PW-1 admits that there is no identification of Lal Mohon Das from the records. Apparently Lal Mohan Das's name could not be found either in the voter list of the relevant period or anywhere else. Moreover Julhash Bhuiya who is supposedly the power of attorney holder of the so called owner Lalmohan Das was also not produced as a witness before court during trial. The p.w-1 also admits that there is no mention of any schedule in the kabala deeds. It is also admitted that there is no mutation in their names in the records. The judgment of the courts below in the previous cases pertaining to the suit land have been produced as exhibits besides the CS khatian, SA khatian, RS khatian and other relevant documents. From scrutiny it appears that the plaintiffs failed to produce any evidences to title in their name except the registered kabala deed dated 25-5-1997.As is evident, the said Kabala deed was pronounced to be a manufactured deed in the Judgment and Decree in Title Suit No. 16 of 2000 and which Judgment was ultimately affirmed up to the High Court Division. All the other documents that is RS, SA, CS, rent receipts etc. are in the name of the present opposite parties. 

 12. Learned Advocate for the petitioner agitated that both the courts below came upon an "incorrect" correct finding and overlooked the fact that the subject matter of the 2 suits are different in as much as that the schedule of the 2 suit lands are different and shown upon comparison the name of the schedules in the respective suits do not match with one another. Learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that during delivery of possession the defendants while taking possession of their 5 decimals of land by dint of court order also encroached upon 9 decimals of land belonging to the plaintiffs in the same dag and hence being aggrieved the petitioner was compelled to file the instant suit. In this regard the learned Advocate for the opposite parties by way of contention counters the petitioner's claim that no specification boundary of the land is mentioned in the kabala deed of 1997 through which the petitioner claims his title. Furthermore he argues that even if the petitioner believes that the defendants had encroached upon 9 decimals of the plaintiff's land during delivery of possession, the petitioner ought to have filed an application before the concerned court Order 21 Rule 100 and 101of the Code of Civil Procedure but instead in this case he filed a fresh suit mandatory injunction which is not maintainable. 

 15. Unfortunately, this decision is a misapplication in this case considering that as discussed above, the subject matters of the 2 suits have been proved to be the same upon concurrent findings of fact and upon comparison of the schedule land of the present suit with the schedules in the previous suits and therefore the principle of Res Judicata is not applicable in this case. 

 19. The petitioner's assertion that he is entitled to a grant of injunction, permanent or mandatory whatsoever was controverted by the Opposite Parties. By way of controverting the petitioner's claims the learned Advocate for the opposite parties cited a decision of the Apex Court in the case of Arefin Mehanati Bahomukhi Samabaya Samity Ltd vs ADC Revenue and others reported in 16 MLR (AD) 68. In that case it was held that "Temporary" injunction cannot be granted when the plaintiff has no prima facie right, title and interest to the property. Drawing an analogy therefrom, the learned counsel for the opposite parties contends that the same principle is applicable to the instant case since the present suit is also a suit for 'injunction' and the plaintiffs failed to prove any right, title or interest in the suit land prima facie or otherwise. I am inclined to draw support from the 16 MLR (AD) 68 given that the instant case is also a case for injunction. Initially suit was filed for permanent injunction and subsequently for mandatory injunction but the plaintiffs failed to show any right, title or interest in the suit land prima facie or otherwise and therefore is not entitled to any such relief. 

 20. The overall scenario of the case is that the plaintiff have failed to prove any prima title or interest in the suit land and further more has not been able to show their exclusive possession at any stage, by evidence or witness and therefore is not entitled to any relief and the suit is not maintainable being hit by the mischief of the principle of Res judicata.

parties:
Zakir Hossain and another
Vs.
Md. Yousuf Kabir and another
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique, J: This appeal has arisen out of the leave granted on 14.03.2011 in Civil Review Petition No.90 of 2010 directed against the judgment and order dated 06.05.2010 passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1359 of 2009 affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.05.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.181 of 2004 affirming those dated 13.05.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.59 of 1994. 

 3. The relevant facts, for the disposal of this appeal, are that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 herein as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.59 of 1994 and Money Suit No.2 of 2002 in the Second Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Title Suit No.59 of 1994 was for declaration of their title to the suit land; recovery of khas possession; for further declaration that the plaintiffs are not bound by the judgment and decree dated 15.11.1979 passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 by the Subordinate Judge, third Court, Dhaka; also for declaration that the kabala executed through Court on 27.02.1980 in execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 is fraudulent, collusive, illegal and void and same is not binding upon the plaintiffs and for permanent injunction. 

 4. Their specific case, in short, was that the land measuring an area of .0568 acre appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.241, C.S. Plot No.390/3940, S.A. Khatian No.197, S.A. Plot No.555, R.S. Khatian No.1511, 1522 and R.S. Plot No.1263 of Lalbag Mouza, Touzi No.61/1, Ward No.7, Sheet No.10, District-Dhaka, as described in the schedule to the plaint originally belonged to Khiroda Shundari Daishya. The suit property was sold in auction for arrear of rent in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 and the same was purchased by Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Monjurul Hoque on 20.06.1953. The sale was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and the sale certificate was issued on 19.11.1953. Possession of the suit land was delivered on 20.01.1954 to the auction purchaser. Ali Ahmed got his name mutated in the Khatian and paid rent to the Government. S.A. Khatian No.197 and R.S. Khatian No.1248 were prepared in his name. He died on 18.06.1975 leaving behind a widow, namely, Khatibunnessa, who inherited the entire suit property as his heir and as per provision of the 'Doctrine of Return'. Khatibunnessa died on 10.02.1978 leaving her only brother Abdul Mannan, who inherited her entire property including the suit property. He transferred the suit property to the plaintiffs by a registered heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 29.11.1979. Thus, the plaintiffs became owners of the suit property. The defendants forged some papers and tried to take over possession of the suit property forcibly but due to intervention of the respectable people of the locality, they could not take over possession of the same. On 06.07.1980, the defendants along with a process server of the Court and police tried to take over the possession of suit property again but the plaintiffs, by showing decree of the court, resisted them. After holding inquiry from the bailiff of the Court, the plaintiffs' father, Abdul Majid, came to know that the defendants had obtained a fraudulent decree on 15.11.1979 in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 from the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on the basis of an agreement dated 12.06.1972 executed by Rasheda Begum.  20. Another aspect is that it is well settled that the certificate of sale does not, by itself, create the title but is merely evidence of title. In the case of Ahmedabad Municipality Vs. Hazi Abdul reported in AIR 1971 SC 1201 it was observed by the Supreme Court of India that it is axiomatic that the purchaser at auction sale takes the property subject to all the defects of title and the doctrine caveat emptor (let the purchaser beware) applies to such purchaser. It is the "right, title and interest" of the judgment-debtor with all risk and defect and without any warranty of title either by the decree-holder or by the court that passes to a purchaser at a court sale, with the exception that where it is proved that the judgment-debtor had no saleable interest at all the purchaser may recover back the purchase-money. In this case, the alleged auction was held on 20.06.1953 showing Khiroda Sundari Saha and Lalit Mohon Saha as certificate debtors. But we have already found from C.S. Khatian (ext-1) shows that Khiroda Sundari Dashya was only C.S. recorded tenant and before holding auction she sold her rayoti interest to Salimunnessa on 27.03.1953 who was not impleaded in the certificate procedure. That is, Khiroda had no right and title at the time of holding auction in suit property so the auction purchaser had not acquired any title because, at the time of holding auction the certificate debtor had no title in the property, in question. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that Salimunnessa had notice of the alleged charges brought by R.L. Acquired Government Estate either actual or constructive. It is to be relevant here to reiterating that in Title Suit No.221 of 1964, the learned Munsif observed that Khiroda and Lalit Mohon were the certificate debtors who already sold their interest to Salimunessa with the knowledge of the defendant No.1, that is, predecessor of the present plaintiffs. Lalit Mohan and Khiroda had no subsisting interest on the date of holding auction sale and it cannot be said that the defendant No.1 (predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs) acquired 7 annas interest by his purchase in the certificate sale. That judgment was upheld in Second Appeal No. 1095 of 1966. That finding is binding upon the plaintiffs. The effect of a sale under the PDR Act being to pass to the purchaser merely the right, title and interest of the person named as judgment debtor in the certificate, the purchaser acquires no right if the person appears to have i no interest in the property at the date of sale. That is, auction purchaser Ali Ahmed did not get any title under it. In Title Suit No.221 of 1964, Title Appeal No.50 1966 and Second Appeal No.1 095 of 1966, the respective Courts had taken notice of the same. But the plaintiffs did not meet up the issue raised and explain the consequences of the same.

Their Sale Certificate and writ of delivery of possession are created documents. Accordingly, we find substance in the appeal.
