 69. From the impugned judgment and order, it further appears that respondent No.2, the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works, filed affidavit-in-opposition in Writ Petition Nos.968 of 1995, 975 of 1995 and 1398 of 1995. In Writ Petition No.975 of 1995, respondent No.2 categorically stated that as the original owner, Rafi Tehrani, had left the country before P.0.16 of 1972 came into being, the same automatically vested in the Government by operation of law. Neither the Government nor the other rival claimants in the property in question, namely, Abdus Sobhan, the appellant in CA No. 77 of 2003, did challenge that Rafi Tehrani was not the son of Zafar Tehrani. It is apparent from the decision of the Court of Settlement that the appellants in Civil Appeal No.10 of 2003 in support of their case that Zafar Tehrani (father of Rafi Tehrani) purchased 0.18 acre land and 0.22 acre land respectively of CS Plot Nos.327 and 328 from Khan Mohammad Nuruddahar of village-Ratoil, PS Kakhiani, formerly Faridpur, now Gopalganj by registered deeds being Nos. 5173 and 5241 dated 23-6-1953; that Zafar Tehrani purchased the land of CS Plot No. 329 from Motilal Dey MajuMd.er in the benami of his wife, Amena Sultana, by registered deed No. 5331 dated 14-10-1947 ad the land of CS Plot Nos. 325, 326 and 322 from Fazle Ahmed Karim, Khan Bandur Md. Solaiman, Sagiruddin Ahmed Sorwardi and Fatema Fazle in the benami of Amena Sultana, Nargis Khanam and Rokeya Sultana, his wife and daughters respectively by registered kabalas being deed Nos. 3485 dated 23-2-1960 and 3484 dated 23-2-1960 and 4208 dated 9-3-1960 respectively filed the documents before it. The Court of Settlement kept those documents outside their consideration on the ground that those "were not put and proved into evidence and marked exts", though it considered the other documents filed by the appellants, which were also not formally proved into evidence. Thus the Court of Settlement followed two different standards to consider the documents filed before it by the appellants. It is very significant to note that all these transferred deeds were executed and registered at a time when nobody thought of a law in the form of PO 16 of 1972 or the Ordinance and under section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, these deeds have a presumption of correctness. Moreso, none challenged those deeds. It is also very pertinent to state that it was the specific case of the appellants that SA Khatians in respect of those plots were prepared in the name of Zafar Tehrani and the other purchasers and those were filed before the Court of Settlement as have been clearly mentioned in its decision. 

 70. In spite of the fact that the Government admitted the ownership of Rafi Tehrani in the property in question, we consider it necessary to discuss the case of the appellants as to the acquisition of his (Rafi Tehrani) title therein. The specific case of the appellants was that Zafar Tehrani purchased land from the CS plots (plot numbers have been mentioned earlier) from its owners by registered kabalas in his own name and in the benami of his wife and daughters and he made an oral gift of all the lands and the properties in favour of his only son, Rafi Tehrani who having got possession of the land so transferred possessed the same with exclusive title and got a decree from the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 31 of 1972. From the plaint of Title Suit No. 31 of 1972, it appears that the same was filed by Rafi Tehrani clearly stating as the son of Mohammad Zafar Tehrani. In the suit, Mohammad Zafar Tehrani, his daughters, Mrs. Rokeya Sultana and Mrs. Nargis Khanam were impleaded as defendant Nos. 1-3 (Mrs. Amena Sultana, the mother was not made a party in the suit as she died in the meantime). In the schedule to the plaint as many as three separate properties were mentioned in three separate schedule being schedule-`A', 'B' and 'C'. We consider it profitable to quote the schedules which are as under: 

 All that pieces and parcels of land with occupancy right including the appurtenances, appeandeques rights, liberties, privileges easement rights adverse title and possession within mouza 280, Bara Magh Bazar. PS Tejgaon, Dacca, appertaining to:— 

 71. From the plaint of Title Suit No.31 of 1972, it appears that specific assertion was made therein that the plaintiff (Rafi Tehrani) was the only son of defendant No. 1, Zafar Tehrani and his wife, Mrs. Amena Sultana, they migrated to Dhaka from Burma in the year 1942 and permanently settled here and that after independence of Bangladesh, the plaintiff expressed his allegiance to the People's Republic of Bangladesh and had been carrying on usual profession. In the plaint, it was further averred that defendant No.1 and his wife, Mrs. Amena Sultana were the full owners of 'A' scheduled property acquired partly by purchase in their own name and partly in the benami of others, namely, defendant Nos. 2 and 3 (defendant Nos. 2 and 3 were Mrs. Rokyea Sultana and Mrs. Nargis Khanam, daughters of Zafar Tehrani); that Mrs. Amena Sultana, mother of the plaintiff died on 25th of September, 1971 leaving behind the plaintiff and defendant No.1 as the only legal heirs as per Mohammadan law; that the defendant No.1 out of natural love and affection for his son, the plaintiff, gifted away his portion of interest in the 'A' scheduled property and also the portion which he had inherited after the death of his wife to the plaintiff in presence of Mr. Majid Talukdar and Mr. Ruhul Amin of Dacca on 1-10-1971 (`A' scheduled property is the property in question). The plaintiff duly accepted the gift made by his father and the delivery of possession of the 'A' scheduled property was also handed over to him on the same day. The title deeds and other relevant document were also handed over to the plaintiff by defendant No.1 at the time of the oral gift in presence of the said witnesses. Defendant No.1 was also the full owner of 'B' and `C' scheduled properties and on the aforesaid date, he also gifted away orally these two properties in favour of the plaintiff in presence of the aforesaid witnesses. The delivery of possession was also given to the plaintiff and the relevant documents and papers were handed over at the same time. Before the aforesaid gift, the defendant also executed general power of attorney in favour of the plaintiff. By virtue of the said gift as well as inheritance from his mother, the plaintiff had become the sole owner of 'A', 'B' and 'C' scheduled properties since 1-10-1971 and had been enjoying the same free from any disturbance and or encumbrances and exercising all rights of possession and ownership; that for the purpose of mutation in the revenue record and register, it was felt necessary that a declaration be obtained in favour of the plaintiff to the effect that he was the sole owner of 'A', 'B' and 'C' scheduled properties from 1-10-1970. The oral gift made by the defendant in presence of two competent witnesses was good enough to establish the right, title and interest of the plaintiff in the said properties, but for convenience and for the purpose of mutation, the suit was filed to obtain a declaration to the above effect. 

 72. Prayer in the suit was made for declaration that the plaintiff was the sole legal owner of the properties as described in schedules `A', 'B' and 'C' and that he had the legal right, title and interest in the same. From the averment of the plaint as stated hereinbefore, it is clear that the story of devolution of title upon the plaintiff (Rafi Tehrani) was clearly stated. In the plaint, it was clearly asserted that the property described in schedule 'A' to the plaint, which was the property in question was purchased in the name of Zafar Teherani (defendant No. 1), his wife-Mrs. Amena Sultana and in the benami of defendant Nos. 2 and 3. The plaintiff (Rafi Tehrani) asserted that after the gift had been made to him by his father, Zafar Teherani, he accepted the gift of 'A' scheduled property and the delivery of possession thereof was made to him on the same day and that the title deeds and the other relevant documents were also handed over to him at the time of oral gift on 1-10-1971. 

 73. From the order sheets of the suit (Title Suit No. 31 of 1972), it appears that the summonses of the suit were duly served upon the defendants, but they did not appear, the suit was decreed ex-parte on 2-9-1972 declaring that the plaintiff was the sole legal owner of the properties shown in schedules `A-C' to the plaint and that he had right, title and interest therein. That decree is still valid. On behalf of the Government, no allegation whatsoever was made either before the Court of Settlement or before the High Court Division that the decree in the said suit (Title Suit No.31 of 1972) was obtained by Rafi Tehrani by practising fraud upon the Court or in collusion to attract the provisions section 44 of the Evidence Act. In the context, I am obliged to state that a Court or a Tribunal cannot and should not assume fact which the concerned party does not plead and fraud or collusion is surely a very big question of fact and that has to be pleaded specifically so that the adverse party may get chance to controvert or meet the same. Therefore, I do not see any scope to ignore the decree passed in Title Suit No.31 of 1972 where title of Rafi Tehrani in the property in question along with the two other properties was declared and thus to question the title of Rafi Tehrani in the property in question by oral gift from his father-Zafar Tehrani. The Court of Settlement totally failed to consider the averment made in the plaint of Title Suit No. 31 of 1972 as stated hereinbefore and totally misconceived and misinterpreted the decree passed therein and also failed to consider the legal implication of the decree passed by a competent civil Court declaring title of Rafi Tehrani in respect of the property in question along with the two other properties. In the plaint of Title Suit No.31 of 1972, the date of oral gift by Zafar Tehrani in favour of Rafi Tehrani was specifically mentioned being 1-10-1971, but the Court of Settlement observed that in the case petition, it was not mentioned when Zafar Tehrani made the oral gift inasmuch as when the said fact was stated in the plaint of the suit which was decreed, it was not at all necessary to state the said fact in the case petition. In the context, it is very pertinent to state that the fact of obtaining decree by Rafi Tehrani in Title Suit No. 31 of 1972 of the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, third Court, Dhaka was specifically stated in the case petition. In view of the above, the Court of Settlement acted beyond its jurisdiction in questioning the propriety of the decree passed in the suit (Title Suit No. 31 of 1972), as the Ordinance has not vested it with the power to sit over the decree of a civil Court. The Ordinance vested the Court of Settlement with the only jurisdiction to see whether a building, here the property in question enlisted in the list of abandoned buildings vested in the Government as an abandoned property within the meaning of PO 16 of 1972 and whether the same was liable to be excluded from the list of the abandoned buildings. The Court of Settlement also manifestly erred in observing that Hosne Ara Begum, petitioner No.7, "deposing as PW-1" save and except stating that "her husband gifted her the case property orally on 3-9-1972", said nothing more as to how the case property was acquired by her husband, Rafi Tehrani inasmuch as in view of the decree passed by the civil Court in Title Suit No. 31 of 1972, no other statement was necessary. The Court of Settlement also failed to consider another important and pertinent fact that it was only the two sisters of Rafi Tehrani, named Nargis Khanurn and Rokeya Sultana who could challenge or contest the claim of Rafi Tehrani as to his acquisition of title in the property in question by an oral gift by his father who claimed to have purchased the same in his own name, in the name of his wife and in the benami of his daughters (wife had died in the meantime). Though they were made parties in Title Suit No. 31 of 1972 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Dhaka, they neither appeared nor contested the suit. In view of the above, my irresistible conclusion is that Rafi Tehrani was the exclusive owner of the property in question. 

 75. Rafi Tehrani was present in Bangladesh during the relevant period (26th March, 1971-28th February, 1972) is clear from the fact that he filed Title Suit No.31 of 1972 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Dhaka on 11-5-1972 and deposed in the suit on commission before Mr. Zinnat Ali, learned Advocate Commissioner on 28-8-1972, to prove his case. Before the Advocate Commissioner, Rafi Tehrani was identified by Mr. Enayet Hossain Khan, a learned Advocate of this Court and he stated in his deposition as under: 

 77. From the deposition of Rafi Tehrani as quoted hereinbefore, it prima facie shows that he was present in Bangladesh during the relevant period and he asserted that after the oral gift had been made to him on 1-10-1971 in respect of the property in question along with two other properties, he accepted the same and the possession of the gifted properties was given to him and he also mentioned the name of the witnesses in whose presence the oral gift was made and one of the witnesses was Mr. Ruhul Amin who became the General Manager of Uttara Bank. The very assertion in his deposition that he was also holding an international passport issued by the Government of Bangladesh, prima facie proved that had he not been present in Bangladesh during the relevant time, then the question of issuing an international passport by the Government of Bangladesh in his name in 1972, would not have arisen. 

 78. It further appears that in connection with the prayer made by Rafi Tehrani to the then Officer-in-charge of Abandoned Properties for releasing house No. 21/1 Purana Paltan, Case No.1044/ap(Ramna)/1972 was started. In connection with the said prayer, Rafi Tehrani was asked to appear before him on 16-11-1972 with all the papers to prove his ownership and accordingly, he appeared before him personally on 25-11-1972 and he was identified by Mr. Enayet Hossain Khan, learned Advocate. By the order made on the said date decision was taken to drop the said house (21/1 Purana Paltan) from the list of abandoned properties as the same was not an abandoned property. In the order dated 25-11-1972, it was specifically mentioned that the owner of the house (21/1 Purana Paltan), Mohd. Rafi Tehrani, produced his international passport being No.A030853 issued by the Deputy Director Immigration and Passport, Government of Bangladesh, Dhaka and that he was a "Bangladeshi by national." In the order, the fact of gift of the house (21/1 Purana Paltan) by Jafar Tehrani in favour of Rafi Tehrani and the decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.31 of 1972 declaring his sixteen annas title therein were taken note of. 

 79. The order of the Officer-in-charge made on 25-11-1972 was approved by the Sub-Divisional Officer on 5-12-1972 with the endorsement "As proposed." Pursuant to the said decision of the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South), Dhaka, a letter was issued to the Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development, Abandoned Property Branch, Government of Bangladesh, vide Memo No.2915/ 1(1) AP/2/72 dated 23.12.1972 with reference to his Memo vide No.2P(V)-23/72/1258 dated 23-6-1972 clearly stating that on examination of the relevant papers and documents produced by Md.. Rafi Tehrani, it was proved that he was the owner of House No.21/1, Purana Paltan, Dhaka (B scheduled property of Title Suit No. 31 of 1972) who was a Bangladeshi national hence the "house in question is not an abandoned property within the meaning of PO No. 16 of 1972" and as such, the house was dropped from the list of abandoned property. In the said letter, it was further stated that from the record, it appeared that the house was allotted in favour of Jatia Sramik League vide the Memo under reference and request was made to cancel the allotment order with intimation to his office so that the possession of the same could be restored to its owner immediately. I consider it better to quote the said Memo in its entirety which reads as follows: 

 On examination of relevant papers and documents produced by Mr Mohd. Rafi Tehrani it has been proved that he is the owner of House 21/1, Purana Paltan, Dacca, who is a Bangladeshi national hence the house in question is not an abandoned property within the meaning of PO No.16 of 1972 and as such the house is dropped from the list of abandoned Property. But it appears from our office record that the house has been allotted in favour of Jatio Shramik League vide his memo referred to above. 

 81. In this regard, it is very pertinent and relevant to state that the property described in schedule-'C' to the plaint of Title Suit No.31 of 1972 was the property appertaining to Dhaka Collectorate Touzi No. 4827, Mouza Kawehakari 414, Khatian No.4/23, eastern portion of Plot No. 1948, area 1.65 acres and of Touzi Nos. 27/ 5397/ 4827 Khatian Nos.377/12 and 4/13, Plot No. 1940, area 0.9 acre total area being 1.74 acres with one semi-pucca tin roofed house and bounded with pucca pillars and barbed wires at Kaliakair was never enlisted as an abandoned property and Hosne Ara Begum (appellant No. 7) specifically asserted that she was in possession thereof. 

 82. The Court of Settlement doubted the acquisition of title by Rafi Tehrani and Hosne Ara Begum (appellant No.7) to the property in question on the observation that the khatians filed by firisti were the certified copies obtained on different dates after 1980 and that "If Rafi Tehrani and Hosne Ara got property getting delivery of possession, then they might produce original Khatians." In making the said observation, the Court of Settlement was totally oblivious of the fact that the Government did not at all challenge the ownership of Rafi Tehrani. Moreso, the Government did not at all challenge the genuineness or truthfulness of the khatians filed by the petitioners before it (the Court of Settlement). Further mere failure to file the originals of the khatians could not be ipsofacto disproved the acquisition of title of Rafi Tehrani in the property in question. The Court of Settlement also failed to consider that the Government did not at all challenge the fact that Rafi Tehrani was not the son of Zafar Tehrani and that in support of the case of the purchase of the property in question by Zafar Tehrani in his own name and in the name of his wife and daughters registered deeds were filed and in the context, it also failed to consider the legal inference and impact of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 31 of 1972 where the title of Rafi Tehrani to the property in question along with two other properties, one being 21/1 Purana Paltan was declared. 

 83. The Court of Settlement was equally wrong in making observation that "We are kept in darkness about Zafar Teherani. On perusal of this petition in which Hosne Ara Begum is petitioner No. 7, we find that Zafar Teherani made oral gift in favour of Rafi Teherani who again made oral gift and gift in writing in favour of Hosne Ara Begum. When Zafar Teherani made oral gift in favour of Rafi Teherani has not been mentioned in the case petition. Again what happened with Zafar Teherani is also not known. Whether he died here or died elsewhere out of the country is also not known as nothing on this matter was produced in the Court. Thus the question of inheritance from Zafar Teherani as mentioned plaint in Title Suit No. 31 of 1972 does not arise at all. This chronologically it comes down that the acquisition of this property by Zafar Tehrani, Rafi Teherani and Hosne Ara Begum (Before and after commencement of PO 16 of 1972) are in the mist and hence not true" in as much as the Government never challenged the ownership of Rafi Tehrani, son of Zafar Tehrani and the Ordinance did not also vest it (the Court of Settlement) with the authority and jurisdiction to inquire or investigate beyond the case of the Government and to sit over the decree of the civil Court. The above quoted observation of the Court of Settlement shows that it was bent upon any how to reject the claim of the appellants to exclude the property in question from the list of abandoned building though the same did not answer the description of an abandoned property. In making the above quoted observation, in fact, the Court of Settlement made out a third case by making a reference to the whereabouts of Zafar Teherani. However, in the context, it is necessary to state that in the plaint of Title Suit No.31 of 1972, it was specifically stated that Zafar Tehrani made the oral gift in favour of Rafi Tehrani on I -10-1971 and Hosne Ara Begum in her examination-in-chief categorically stated that her father-in-law (Zafar Tehrani) died in Bangladesh in the last part of 1972. And in the face of the decree passed in Title Suit No.31 of 1972, there was no scope to question the title of Rafi Tehrani in the property in question, particularly, when the respondent-Government did not raise any dispute about the ownership of Rafi Tehrani as pointed out earlier. 

 85. Now, the question that remains to be thrashed out is whether Hosne Ara Begum, appellant No.7, acquired any title to the property in question or not from her husband, Rafi Tehrani. Hosne Ara Begum claimed that Rafi Tehrani married her on 30-3-1970 and he (Rafi Tehrani) made an oral gift of the property in question in her favour on 3-9-1972 and that she accepted the oral gift and took physical possession thereof in presence of the witnesses. Hosne Ara Begum further asserted that oral gift was confirmed by a written deed dated 18-10-1972. 

 86. In support of her marriage, Hosne Ara Begum produced the kabinnama in original before the Court of Settlement. Kabinnama was also produced before the High Court Division. Kabinnama has also been included in the main paper book of this appeal. Kabinnama shows that Rafi Tehrani, son of Zafar Tehrani, married Hosne Ara Begum, daughter of Akkas Mia of 277/2, Azimpur, Lalbag Road. In the kabinnama, the address of Rafi Tehrani was shown at House No.5, Bara Maghbazar, Ispahani Colony, Dhaka. In the kabinnama, Rafi Tehrani has been clearly stated as the son of Zafar Tehrani. In the Kabinnama, the address of Hosne Ara Begum was mentioned at 277/2 Azimpur, being the address of her father which is quite natural. In her deposition before the Court of Settlement, Hosne Ara Begum categorically stated that she was married to Rafi Tehrani on 30-3-1970. She specifically asserted that in the kabinnama, there were signatures of Rafi Tehrani and herself. The original kabinnama was proved and marked as exhibit-1(ka). In Title Suit No.31 of 1972, the address of Rafi Tehrani was clearly mentioned as 5 Maghbazar, i.e. the property in question, but the Court of Settlement disbelieved the address on the ground that in the deposition of Rafi Teherani which was taken on commission by learned Advocate, Mr. Md.. Jinnat Ali in Title Suit No.31 of 1972 on 27-8-1972, his address was shown at CFSA, 46 Road No.116, Gulshan, Dhaka completely ignoring the fact that the com-mission as to the recording of deposition of a plaintiff can be held at any address. And merely because the commission in taking his deposition was held at a different place ipso facto did not disprove that Rafi Tehrani did not live at 5 Maghbazar. The Code of Civil Procedure has not also mandated that the holding of commission to record the deposition of a plaintiff must be done at the suit property or at the address given in the plaint. In this regard, it may be stated that before this Court, the learned Counsel for the appellants has argued that the commission in Title Suit No. 31 of 1972 was held at Gulshan address that being the working place of Rafi Tehrani at the relevant time. In the written submission filed on behalf of the appellant the same fact has been categorically stated. It has been stated that at the relevant time, Rafi Teherani was the Manager of JH Royner (Eastern) Ltd for Bangladesh, Burma and Nepal having office at CESA 46, Rd No.116, Gulshan Dhaka and this address was used when his deposition was recorded on commission. And we get support of this fact from the series of correspondences between Rafi Tehrani and JH (Eastern) Ltd. London office. These correspondences were proved in Title Suit No. 367 of 1981 as exhibits-'17(g)', '17(Ka)' and `17(L)' (these exhibits have been filed in the main paper book) (the decision of the Court of Settlement was given on 28-12-1994). 

 87. The Court of Settlement in a circuitous way disbelieved the marriage of Hosne Ara Begum with Rafi Tehrani and the gift made by him in favour of Hosne Ara Begum on the ground that the difference between the signature of Rafi Tehrani appearing in the kabinnama of the marriage between him and Hosne Ara Begum and the signature in the deed of gift "exposes Hosne Ara to falsehood." The above finding of the Court of Settlement is absolutely bereft of any factual basis and based on imagination and surmise inasmuch as it did not say how and in what manner the signature of Rafi Tehrani having appeared in the kabinnama and in the deed of gift differed. It appeared to me that the Court of Settlement made the said remark in a very casual manner without considering the serious social impact that would have on Hosne Ara Begum and her daughter, Hasina Tehrani apart from the claim of ownership to the property in question. When Hosne Ara Begum categorically stated in her deposition that she was married to Rafi Tehrani on 30-3-1970 and in support of marriage she produced the kabinnama asserting that in the kabinnama, there were signatures of Rafi Tehrani and herself and since the Court of Settlement allegedly found difference between the signatures of Rafi Tehrani having appeared in the kabinanama and in the deed of gift, it was its obligation to point the mode and manner of difference, but it did not. In the context, the most relevant and pertinent fact is that in Title Suit No.367 of 1981 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Dhaka filed by appellant 

 No.7, Hosne Ara Begum and 5(five) others against Md.. Jahangir Alam Khan and 23 (twenty three) others for declaratory decrees and for recovery of khas possession, similar objection was raised and the signatures of Rafi Tehrani having appeared on various documents with those of his signatures having appeared in the kabinnama and the deed of gift were sent to the Hand Writing Expert of Criminal Investigation Department for his opinion. It may further be stated that the Bureau of Anti-Corruption through its Inspector even seized the specimen signature of Rafi Tehrani from the then Muslim Commercial Bank, now Rupali Bank to take the opinion of the Hand Writing Expert. And the Hand Writing Expert opined that the signatures of Rafi Tehrani appearing in the nikanama and the deed of gift were genuine. The other ground on which the Court of Settlement found fault with the kabinnama and thus doubted the very marriage of Hosne Ara Begum with Rafi Tehrani was that although the property in question is at House No.5, Bara Maghbazar, the address of Rafi Tehrani in the kabinnama was shown at House No.5, Bara Maghbazar, Ispahani Colony completely ignoring the fact that because of using of a different address in the kabinnama, a marriage cannot be said to be disproved. Hosne Ara Begum in her deposition before the Court of Settlement categorically asserted the fact of her marriage with Rafi Tehrani on 30-3-1970 and the registration of the nikanama on 31-1-1972. She further asserted that in the kabinnama, there were signatures of herself and Rail Tehrani and in view of the opinion of the Hand Writing Expert that the signatures of Rafi Tehrani having appeared in the kabinnama and the deed of gift were of Rafi Tehrani, there was no scope of doubting the marriage of Hosne Ara Begum with Rafi Tehrani (the opinion of the Hand Writing Expert and the deposition of the CID Inspector have been included in the main paper book and in the additional paper book dated 22-11-2011 pages 269 and 172-175 respectively). 

 88. The further claim of Hosne Ara Begum is that Rafi Tehrani made an oral gift of the property in question in her favour on 3rd September, 1972 and also made a written gift to that effect on 18-10-972, Hosne Ara Begum filed Title Suit No.425 of 1978 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka to confirm the oral gift made by her husband in her favour and obtained a decree on 06-5-1980. In the suit, her husband-Rafi Tehrani showing his present address in London was made defendant No.1 . The said suit was decreed ex-parte and her title to the property in question along with 2 (two) other properties, one at 21/1, Purana Paltan, Dhaka and the other at Kaliakar was declared. Thereafter, Hosne Ara got her name mutated in the revenue record and paid rents and she transferred some land to appellant Nos. 1 -6 and 8 who got municipal holding number in respect of their respective portion of the land and they are paying all the taxes and bills etc. in respect of the property in question and till date the decree passed in Title Suit No.425 of 1978 is in force. Neither Rafi Tehrani nor any one has challenged the propriety of the said decree in any manner. Hosne Ara Begum in her deposition before the Court of Settlement categorically stated about the decree obtained by her in the said suit. During cross-examination, both the Government and the rival claimant challenged the decree passed in Title Suit No.425 of 1978 as collusive and fraudulent and no suggestion was ever given her to that effect, so there is no scope to doubt the propriety of the decree passed in Title Suit No.425 of 1978. The Court of Settlement overlooked the decree passed in the said suit on the comment that on perusal of the plaint, it appeared that Hosne Ara Begum resorted to "falsehood and fabrication" as nowhere in the plaint of that suit, the fact of written gift "is found but in the case petition as well as in her deposition PW 1 -Hosne Ara Begum said that a written gift was given to her by her husband, Rafi Tehrani on 18-10-1972. If there was any written document on gift, then the plaintiff could disclose it in the plaint of that suit. Thus, we firmly hold that there was no existence of any written document on gift, so the plaint was filed without disclosing any fact on written gift." 

 89. In holding so, the Court of Settlement totally misconceived and misconstrued the case of Hosne Ara Begum. The Court of Settlement failed to consider and comprehend that although the case of Hosne Ara Begum was that Rafi Tehrani made an oral gift of the property in question in her favour on 3-9-1972 and then a written deed of gift was made on 18-10-1972 and she also said so in her deposition before the Court of Settlement. In the plaint of Title Suit No.425 of 1978, Hosne Ara Begum clearly asserted the said fact of oral gift by her husband, Rafi Tehrani in her favour. The Court of Settlement found fault with the title of Hosne Ara Begum in the property in question for non-mentioning the fact of making the written gift by Rafi Tehrani in her favour in the plaint of Title Suit No.425 of 1978. In finding such fault, it totally failed to consider the legal implication that after the oral gift was made on 3-9-1972 and the same was acted upon, it was absolutely unnecessary to make any written gift and mere non-mentioning or omission to state such fact in the plaint of Title Suit No.425 of 1978 could in no way be construed to be "falsehood and fabrication", such finding is absolutely perverse. It is pertinent to state that the Court of Settlement did not say that the decree in Title Suit No.425 of 1978 was obtained by Hosne Ara Begum fraudulently or collusively. In the context, I do not find anything wrong on the part of Hosne Ara Begum to file the suit (Title Suit No.425 of 1978) for declaration that she was the sixteen annas owner of the suit land (which also included the property in question) inasmuch as the decree passed by the civil Court declaring title of a person to a property strengthened his/her right to a property in a case of oral gift. 

 91. The Court of Settlement also failed to consider the deposition of Hosne Ara Begum that written deed of gift was submitted in the civil Court. Since the oral gift made on 3-9-1972 by Rafi Tehrani in faovur of Hosne Ara Begum was acted upon, the learned Advocate who drafted the plaint of Title Suit No. 425 of 1978 rightly omitted to mention about the written gift. And by such omission in the plaint, the case of Hosne Ara Begum as to the acquisition of her title to the property in question by oral gift could in no way be negatived or disbelieved and the decree passed in Title Suit No.425 of 1978 could be ignored. The decree passed in this suit could be ignored or avoided within the meaning of section 44 of the Evidence Act having any fraud or collusion be established in obtaining the same, but as stated hereinbefore, such a case was never made out either by the Government or by the rival claimants. The Court of Settlement on total non-application of mind to the case of Hosne Ara Begum as to the acquisition of title to the property in question by oral gift and on misinterpretation and misconception of the law of oral gift under Mohammedan Law came to a wrong conclusion that "when gift by way of written document goes away and is disbelieved, then the fact of oral gift is disbelieved accordingly. When acquisition of property by Hosne Ara is doubtful, then everything is doubtful." In making the above quoted observation, the Court of Settlement made a fundamental mistake that the fact of oral gift took place first and then the written gift was made just as a reconfirmation of the oral gift made earlier and even if there was no written gift, that, in no way, could nullify the oral gift which had already been acted upon. The conclusion of the Court of Settlement that "These all taken together show that Rafi Tehrani never gifted the case property in favour of Hosne Ara Begum. The paper, namely, deed of gift has been manufactured, created, ante-dated and forged for the purpose of illegally grabbing the case property", is the result of sheer non application of mind to the case of Hosne Ara Begum, misreading, misconstruction of the documents filed before it, misconception of the provisions of oral gift under Mohammedan Law and on mere surmises and conjectures without any factual basis. 

 Begum never lived with Rafi Tehrani and "It thus appears from the above that no delivery of possession has taken place" ignoring the fact that 277/2 Azimpur, Lalbag, Dhaka was the address of her father and also ignoring the legal position that after the oral gift was acted upon the address of Hosne Ara Begum mentioned in an unnecessary or superfluous document, namely, the deed of gift could in no way nullify the same and therefore her case of acquisition of title of the property in question on the basis of oral gift made on 3-9-1972 by her husband, Rafi Tehrani cannot be doubted. The Court of Settlement also failed to consider that when Rafi Tehrani in the written gift admitted the fact of oral gift and the further fact that the same was acted upon mere using an address other than the property in question therein would not automatically make the oral gift false or disproved. And because of the use of a different address other than the property in question, in the deed of gift, it cannot be said that Hosne Ara Begum did not reside in the property in question, namely, 5 Maghbazar. In the context, the Court of Settlement also failed to consider that in the birth certificate of her daughter issued by the Registrar Gynac, Dhaka Medical College Hospital on 13-10-1981, Hosne Ara Begum was specifically described as the wife of Md.. Rafi Tehrani and this fortifies the case of Hosne Ara Begum that she was the wife of Rafi Tehrani. Hosne Ara Begum in her deposition categorically stated that she gave birth to a female child on 21-6-1972 at cabin No. 19, Dhaka Medical College Hospital. The Court of Settlement also ignored the testimony of Hasina Tehrani, daughter of Hosne Ara Begum who was examined in the case as PW 2. She (Hasina Tehrani) in unequivocal language stated that the name of her father was Rafi Tehrani who lived in London and that she had communication with her father through letters and her father had left for London while she was '3/312/1' years old. she further asserted that her father again married in London and built house there and kept her with her mother and gave his property to them. It is very pertinent to state that PW 2 was not at all cross-examined to dislodge the fact asserted by her that Rafi Tehrani was her father and that he had left for London while she was '3/31 2/1'years old. It is also significant to note that on behalf of the Government, no cross-examination was made to her (PW 2) and it was the petitioners of Case No.986 of 1988-595 of 1988 who cross-examined her. It will be clear if the entire cross-examination of PW 2 is looked into which reads as follows: 

 95. The Court of Settlement disbelieved the appellants' case of possession in the property in question firstly by Rafi Tehrani and then by Hosne Ara Begum giving reference to the case of the petitioner in Case No.586 of 1988 who stated that Rafi Tehrani never possessed the "case property" and that PW 1, Abdus Sobhan, in that case (Case No.586 of 1988) stated that he had heard that Rafi Tehrani lived in the Ispahani Colony, but there was no Ispahani Colony. The Court of Settlement also referred to the case of the other petitioners, namely, Case Nos.587, 588, 589, 590, 591, 592. 593, 594 and 595 all of 1988 (they were the transferees from Abdus Sobhan, appellant of CA No.77 of 1977) that Hosne Ara Begum never lived in the "case property' completely ignoring that they were the rival claimants and they were all to injure her by creating a cloud and confusion about her title in the property in question as well as its status and that the claim of the rival claimants could not disprove the possession of Rafi Tehrani and Hosne Ara Begum in the property in question as there were other positive and conclusive evidence in support of their claim of title to the property in question as well as their possession therein as discussed hereinbefore. In the context, I would like to add that merely because two rival parties claimed title to the property in question and prayed for its exclusion from the list of abandoned buildings in their favour could not oust the jurisdiction of the Court of Settlement to look into the papers/documents filed by them to decide the question whether the property in question was an abandoned property and the same vested in the Government and whether the same was liable to be excluded from the list of abandoned buildings and whether the documents produced prima facie entitled any of them to get an order of exclusion of the property in question in any one's favour without entering into the detailed enquiry as to their claim of title therein. 

 96. The Court of Settlement did not at all consider that Hosne Ara Begum in her examination-in-chief asserted the fact that her husband was in London and he had left for London in the same month in which Sheikh Mujib died and at that time, he (her husband) used to live in the property in question (In the deposition sheet, in Bangla, it has been recorded as "আমার স্বামী লন্ডনে আছেন। শেখ মুজিব ১৯৭৫ সালে মারা যাবার এক মাসে যান। মগবাজার বাসায় ঐ সময় থাকতেন)" and in cross-examination, she categorically asserted that during the war of liberation, Zafar Tehrani and Rafi Tehrani used to live at Maghbazar. The Court of Settlement also failed to consider the deposition of Rafi Tehrani in Title Suit No.31 of 1972 where he asserted that after the oral gift of the property in question by his father on 1-10-1971, he became its full owner and he had been possessing the same. It (the Court of Settlement) also failed to consider the decree passed in that suit in which his title to the property in question along with two other properties was declared. The Court of Settlement also failed to consider the order of the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South), Dhaka dated 25-11-1972 and the Memo dated 23-12-1972 sent by him to the Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development, Abandoned Property Branch, dropping the property of Purana Paltan of Rafi Tehrani from the list of abandoned property. The Court of Settlement erroneously took adverse view as to the possession of Hosne Ara Begum in the property in question relying on a statement in her cross-examination that during the war, she lived at the residence of her father (her father's house is at 277/2, Azimpur, Lalbag, Dhaka) inasmuch as in the context of 1971, there was nothing wrong if she lived at her father's residence during that period and that fact in no way could affect her case of acquisition of title in the property in question by oral gift from her husband, Rafi Tehrani, made on 3-9-1972 which she asserted both in her examination-in-chief as well as in her cross-examination. It is very significant to state that in taking the said adverse view, the Court of Settlement did not consider the other positive assertion of Hosne Ara Begum that during the war, Zafar Tehrani, Rafi Tehrani all used to live at Maghbazar (In the deposition sheet, in bangla, it has been recorded as "যুদ্ধের সময় আমি আমার বাবার বাড়ী ছিলাম। যুদ্ধ চলাকালে জাফর তেহরানী, রফি তেহরানী সবাই মগবাজার থাকত।”). Hosne Ara Begum became the owner of the property in question by virtue of the oral gift made by Rafi Tehrani, her husband, on 03-9-1972, so her right to the property in question and possession therein could in no way be disbelieved, if she stayed at her father's residence during the liberation war, in 1971. The crucial fact in the case was whether Rafi Tehrani was in Bangladesh during the relevant period, i.e. 26th March, 1971 to 28th February, 1972 which was clearly established by the evidence of PW 1, Hosne Ara Begum, before the Court of Settlement; by the evidence of Rafi Tehrani himself in Title Suit No.31 of 1972 and the decree passed therein as well as the order of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Sadar (South). Dhaka dropping the property of Purana Paltan of Rafi Tehrani from the list of abandoned property as discussed hereinbefore. 

 97. In deciding the factum of possession by Hosne Ara Begum in the property in question, the Court of Settlement failed to consider her testimony given before it that she had been in Maghbazar since the liberation of Bangladesh in proper perspective along with the other evidence as mentioned hereinbefore. Hosne Ara Begum in her deposition specifically stated that she being in possession of the property in question sold a portion of it to Shahidul Haque (appellant No. 1), Ayub (appellant No. 5), Ismail Hossain (appellant No.3), Rehana Anju (appellant No. 8), Showkat Khan (appellant No.4) and Shikha Haque and they were in possession in some portion of their purchased land and not in possession in some portion as well and she mutated her name of the remaining portion of the property in question in which she is in possession. In this respect, it is very pertinent to state that Hosne Ara Begum though stated in her deposition that Atiqur Rahman along with others illegally went into the possession (without mentioning specifically the property in question), but if her deposition is read as a whole it would appear that Atiqur Rahman and others entered into the possession of a portion of the property in question. And she along with the transferees from her already filed Title Suit No. 367 of 1981 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Dhaka for recovery of khas possession of the dispossessed portion from the property in question along with the prayer of their declaration of title therein and other prayers including a declaration that the ex-parte decree dated 30-4-1979 (decree signed on 4-6-1979) passed by the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 204 of 1977 was null and void and not binding upon them. And this also shows that her claim of title to the property in question and her possession therein was bona fide and had factual basis and she had every right to pray for excluding the same from the list of abandoned buildings. 

 99. It is true that in the depositions of Hosne Ara Begum (appellant No. 7) and Md.. Shahidul Haque Bhuiyan (purchaser from Hosne Ara Begum and appellant No. 1) who were examined in Case No. 649 of 1988 (giving rise to this appeal) they did not say about the payment of rents to the Government, payment of Municipal Tax and now City Corporation tax, payment of other bills for utility services, such as, electricity, gas, WASA, but before this Court, the documents have been filed showing that Hosne Ara Begum mutated her name with the revenue authority in respect of the property in question and she paid rents; papers have also been filed showing payment of rents by Md.. Shahidul Haque Bhuiyan (appellant No. 1), Mrs. Shikha Haque (appellant No.6), i.e. the purchasers from Hosne Ara Begum and the payment of bills for utility services, namely, electricity, gas and water supply. In the context, it may be stated that the documents have been also filed before this Court showing that Municipal holding was opened in the name of Zafar Tehrani and holding tax and other bills for utility services, such as, electricity, gas and WASA were paid in his name. The most important document produced by appellant No.1 and appellant No.6, i.e. the purchasers from Hosne Ara Begum is that the then Dhaka Improvement Authority (DIT) (now RAJUK) by its Memo dated 17-11-1982 gave them permission to construct a building in the property in question (the list of the abandoned buildings in which the property in question has been included was published in the official Gazette on 28-4-1986). The above mentioned purchasers obtained electricity supply line, took gas connection from Titas Gas Transmission and Company Limited and water supply line to their newly built houses. The approved plan has been also filed before this Court. It may be stated that in the writ petition, it was specifically stated that Hosne Ara Begum mutated her name and paid rents and those facts were not denied by the Government by filing any affidavit-in-opposition. The very fact that Hosne Ara Begum mutated her name with the revenue authority, paid rents prima facie showed that Hosne Ara Begum was in possession of the property in question when the Gazette notification was made under section 5 of the Ordinance. It is necessary to state that from the decision of the Court of Settlement, it is prima facie clear that the khatians in respect of the property in question were filed on behalf of the appellants of this appeal, but the Court of Settlement refused to consider those on the ground that the original khatians were not filed and that certified copies thereof were obtained on different dates after 1980. In the writ petition, it was also asserted that appellant No.1 (petitioner No. l in the writ petition) constructed a four-storied building and leased out the same to the National Bank of Bangladesh in 1989 and the said Bank is running a National Bank Public School and College and some of the correspondences between the Bank and appellant No.1 were annexed to the writ petition and they were marked as annexure-'C-C2', but the Government of Bangladesh, writ-respondent No.2 did not deny the said assertions by filing any affidavit-in-opposition 

 101. The Court of Settlement was also palpably wrong in holding that as Hosne Ara Begum transferred the "entire case property", she allegedly got by way of gift "to the rest applicants by registered deeds on different dates", she had no right, title and possession therein, so she had no locus standi to file the case as petitioner No.7 and that the statement made in the petition that "applicants are always in possession" are not true, "because petitioner No. 7 has no subsistence right, title and interest in the case property after alleged sale to the rest petitioners" inasmuch as Hosne Ara Begum did not sell the entire property in question and she in her deposition categorically stated that she mutated her name in respect of the portion of the property in question of which she is in possession (in the deposition sheet, in Bangla, it has been recorded as "আমার নামে আামার দখলী অংশের নামজারী আছে”) and this assertion of P WI was not challenged in cross-examination either by the Government or by the petitioner of other cases. In taking the above view, the Court of Settlement totally misconceived and misinterpreted the meaning of the words "sold out the same" as stated in the petition; the words "sold out the same" can in no way be construed that she had sold the entire property, she got from her husband. For argument's sake, if it is conceded that Hosne Ara Begum had sold out the entire property to the other applicants, then they (the other applicants) had every locus standi to file the application under section 7 of the Ordinance to exclude the property in question from the list of abandoned buildings, they being the bona fide purchasers from her and in possession of their portion of the purchased land, but their case was not considered on the erroneous view that as "Hosne Ara Begum did not live and thereby possess the case property, so they (rest petitioners) have not got their possession in the case property from Hosne Ara Begum." In holding so the Court of Settlement failed to consider that section 7 of the Ordinance has stipulated that any person claiming any right or interest in any building which is included in any list published under section 5 may, within a period of one hundred and eighty days from the date of publication of the list in the official Gazette, make an application to the Court of Settlement for exclusion of the building from such list or return or restoration of the building to him or for any other relief on the ground that the building is not an abandoned property and has not been vested in the Government under PO 16 of 1972 or that his right or interest in the building has not been affected by the provisions of that order. And this failure resulted in an erroneous decision by the Court of Settlement in rejecting the claim of the transferees to exclude the property in question from the list of abandoned buildings. 

 105. The Court of Settlement rejected the case filed by the appellant, Abdus Sobhan, along with Case Nos. 587, 588, 589, 590, 591, 592, 593, 594 and 595 of 1988 on the finding that on perusal of the evidence of PW 1, Abdus Sobhan, it appeared that he never possessed the case property immediately before commencement of PO 16 of 1972. The Court of Settlement relying on a solitary statement of PW 1, Abdus Sobhan, in his cross-examination that one Abdur Rashid, Advocate, went into the possession of the "case property" immediately after liberation of Bangladesh held that "the case property" was an abandoned property within the meaning of article 2(1) of PO 16 of 1972 and it vested in the Government under article 4 of said PO. The Court of Settlement rejected the claim of the other petitioners in the other cases on the ground that since all the transfers to them "took place after when the case property became abandoned property and duly vested in the Government", those transfers were hit by article 6 of PO 16 of 1972. The Court of Settlement in coming to the said finding did not at all consider the assertion made by Abdus Sobhan in his examination-in-chief that the property in question was not an abandoned property and he was in possession thereof and the further fact that he filed Title Suit No.183 of 1972 in the Court of the then Munsif, First Court, Dhaka in the wake of desire of the then Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South), Dhaka for taking up forcible possession of the property in question on 24-7-1972 and she obtained an order of temporary injunction against the Government. The Court of Settlement also failed to consider the case of the petitioner (Case No.586 of 1988) that before promulgation of PO 16 of 1972, Parkul Tea Estate was in occupation in a portion of the property in question being holding No.71 (New) as his tenant and after 1972, Bangladesh Tea Board took over possession of Parkul Tea Estate and that the Tea Board assured him of payment of rent as tenants after the decision in Title Suit No.183 of 1972 (renumbered as Title Suit No. 926 of 1981). 

 124. The Court of Settlement also failed to consider that the presumption attached to section 5 of the Ordinance is not sacrosanct and is rebuttable and in considering the presumption attached to section 5 of the Ordinance, it totally failed to consider the materials placed before it, particularly, the decree passed in Title Suit No.31 of 1972, the deposition of Rafi Tehrani in this suit, the order of the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South), Dhaka dropping the property of Purana Paltan of Rafi Tehrani from the list of abandoned buildings, the decree passed in Title Suit No.425 of 1978 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka, the mutation khatian in the name of Hosne Ara Begum and the rent paid by her which prima facie proved that during the relevant period, i.e. 26-3-1971 to 28.021972, Rafi Tehrani was in possession of the property in question and subsequently he divested his ownership on Hosne Ara Begum, his wife, by oral gift and that she was in possession thereof. Therefore, the property in question did not answer the description of an abandoned property within the meaning of article 2(1) of PO 16 of 1972 and the presumption attached to section 5 of the Ordinance was very well rebutted. In the context, it is necessary to state that section 5 of the Ordinance does not say that to get a notice for surrendering or taking over possession as an abandoned property, one need be in possession of the entire property. 

 125. As discussed hereinbefore, the petitioners of Case No.649 of 1988, particularly, Hosne Ara Begum conclusively proved that Rafi Tehrani, her husband, was a Bangladeshi citizen holding Bangladesh passport and was in possession of the property in question during the relevant period, i.e. from 26-3-1971 to 28-2-1972 as its rightful owner and after she had become the owner of the same by oral gift from her husband on 3-9-1972. She and her transferees were in possession thereof and therefore, they were entitled to get a notice under section 5(1)(b) of the Ordinance before the inclusion of the property in question in the list of abandoned buildings. This Court in the cases of the Ministry of Works vs Helaluddin Ahmed (supra), Bangladesh vs Amela Khatun and others (supra), Government of Bangladesh vs Marium (supra), Bangladesh vs Rehana Kamal (supra), Abdur Rashid Molla vs Bangladesh (supra), Bangladesh vs Md.. Shahjahan (supra), has consistently held that statutory notice as contemplated in sections 4 and 5 of the Ordinance is a sine qua non and in the absence of such notice, the inclusion of a disputed property in the `Kha' list of the abandoned buildings is illegal and without lawful authority. 

 126. This Division in the case of Secretary, Ministry of Works and Urban Development, Government of Bangladesh vs Rowshan Ara Begum, 57 DLR (AD) 167, rejected the objection as to the non-service of notice under section 5(1) of the Ordinance on the ground that no such objection was taken either before the Court of Settlement or before the High Court Division, so this case could not be relied upon or referred to as an authority on the question of non-service of notice under section 5(1)(b) of the Ordinance as sought to be relied upon by the learned Additional Attorney General. A review of this judgment was sought and this Division in the review held that "In the instant case the petitioner having not been able to establish before the Court of Settlement that the claimant of the property or for that matter her vendor Anwari Khatun were present in Bangladesh on 28-2-1972 and consequent thereupon the property having had assumed the character of abandoned property, the listing of the property in question, even if without service of notice as per provision of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985, is not material as the property because of non-service of notice for listing in the list of abandoned properties would not cease to be an abandoned property and consequent thereupon the claim of title made by the petitioner in the property in question is not legally sustainable or, in other words, the petitioner cannot raise any claim of title in the property in question since said property is an abandoned property. The ground contending which review of our judgment is sought merits no consideration." And in taking the said view, the earlier decisions of this Court as mentioned hereinbefore, were not at all taken into consideration. So this judgment can be termed to be a judgment per in curium and does not constitute a precedent. In the context, it is necessary to keep on record that at the time of hearing the review petition, the case of Ministry of Works vs Helaluddin Ahmed (supra) was cited, but that case was distinguished in the following way: 

 134. Now another pertinent question that looms large for decision is in whose favour order for exclusion of the property in question from the list of abandoned buildings should be passed. I find no difficulty in answering the question in favour of the appellants in CA No.10 of 2003, in view of the finding as to their title and possession therein given hereinbefore. At the same time, I must say that since the parties, namely, the appellants (CA Nos. 10 of 2003 and 77 of 2003) are litigating in the civil Courts as to their claim of title in the property in question in the suits now pending therein ultimate claim of the parties to the property in question shall be decided by the civil Court in the suits now pending between them. 

 135. In the result, the appeals are allowed. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division affirming the decision of the Court of Settlement in Case Nos. 649 of 1988 and 586 of 1988 rejecting the cases is set aside. The cases are allowed. Respondent No. 2 is directed to exclude the building being holding No. 5, Maghbazar (Outer Circular Road), presently 70/71, Outer Circular Road, from the list of abandoned buildings published in the official gazette, additional issue, on 28th April, 1986 in favour of the appellants of CA No.10 of 2003. But this order of exclusion of the property in question from the list of abandoned buildings in favour of the appellants of CA No. 10 of 2003 in no way shall affect the merit of the suits now pending between the parties, i.e. the appellants in the civil Court. The civil Court shall be at liberty to decide the title of the parties on the evidence to be produced by them keeping in mind that the property in question is not an abandoned property and the same did not vest in the Government.
