full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J: This Civil Appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 5-7-2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4041 of 1999 making the rule absolute setting aside the judgment and decree dated 14-9-1999 passed by the Additional District Judge, Bagerhat in Title Appeal No. 282 of 1994 affirming the judgment and decree dated 6-10-1994 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Bagerhat in Title Suit No.225 of 1994 decreeing the suit. 

 2. The appellant, as plaintiff, filed Title Suit No. 13 of 1993 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Bagerhat, which was subsequently transferred to the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Bagerhat and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 225 of 1994, for declaration of title in respect of 5.09 acres of land and for further declaration that the compromise decree passed in Title Suit No.173 of 1994, by the learned Subordinate Judge, Khulna is fraudulent, inoperative, void and not binding upon the plaintiff and also for further declaration that the enlistment of the suit land in the list of vested and non-resident property is not binding upon the plaintiff and for permanent injunction. 

 3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the land measuring 6.05 acres appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.152 of No. 3 Nalbaria Mouza originally belonged to Ganga Charan. Ganga Charan settled the said land to Ananta Kumar and Nittananda Hawlader by registered patta dated 24-3-1936. Ananta Kumar and Nittananda Hawlader subsequently transferred the said land to Burundi Hawlader the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant Nos. 44-60 by a registered kabala dated 27-8-1943. Burundi Hawlader died leaving behind the defendant Nos. 44-60 as his heirs. That the defendant Nos. 44-60 transferred 5.09 acres, of land out of that 6.05 acres of land to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 28-1-1993 and also delivered possession of the said land in favour of the plaintiff and since then the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land. Further case of the plaintiff is that at the time of RS operation the suit land was recorded in the name of Shashi Kumar Singh and Jogesh Chandra Shil wrongly. That Burundi Hawlader died just before RS operation and his heirs-the defendant Nos. 44-60 had no other capable man to look after the property and taking that opportunity Jogesh Chandra Shil-the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant Nos. 42 and 43 managed to record 4.36 acres of land of plot No. 2174 and 0.96 acre of land of plot No.796 of RS Khatian No. 791 in his name. Thereafter, at the time of SA.operation also the said land was recorded in the name of Jogesh Chandra Shil in SA Khatian Nos. 1114 and 1032. That although the suit land was recorded in RS and SA Khatians in the name of Jogesh Chandra Shil, but he had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. That the plaintiff has been possessing the suit-land and before him the heirs of Burundi Hawlader possessed the suit land. That due to erroneous recording of the suit land in RS and SA Khatians the plaintiff's title in the suit land has been clouded and hence the suit. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1, 7, 9, 11, 12-14, 20, 23, 25, 26(Ka)-26(Cha), 27, 28, 32-34, 36 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the case of the plaintiff. The material case of these contesting defendants is that the suit land originally belonged to Shashi Kumar Singh under the landlord Satya Charan Saha and Korman Akon. That while owning and possessing the suit land Shashi Kumar Singh settled the suit land along with other lands to the predecessor-in-interest of these contesting defendants on 1st Baishakh, 1355 BS at a rent of Taka 315 and delivered possession. That in pursuance of that settlement.the landlord executed an amalnama on 1st Ashar, 1355 BS and also granted dakhilas in favour of the defendants and their predecessors-in-interest. At the time of SA operation the suit land was erroneously recorded in the name of the original owner Shashi Kumar Singh in Khatian No. 1114. That Shashi Kumar Singh died leaving behind 2 sons, namely, Kanailal Singh and Hiralal Singh. These defendants brought Title Suit No. 173 of 1964 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Khulna against Kanailal Singh and Hiralal Singh and that suit was decreed on compromise on 8-9-1964. That on the basis of erroneous record of fight the local tahshilder claimed the suit land as vested and non- resident property and denied to receive rent of the suit land and then the defendants brought Title Suit No. 109 of 1971 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Khulna for declaration of their title and for further declaration that the enlistment of the suit land in the list of vested and non-resident property was void. That suit was decreed on 15-6-1972. Thereafter, the officials of the vested and non-resident property, in collusion with the local enemies of these defendants, threatened the defendants to dispossess them from the suit land and, as such, the defendants brought Title Suit No.207 of 1978 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Bagerhat for permanent injunction and obtained decree on 20-12-1980. Against the said judgment and decree the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Bagerhat and Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Sharankhola brought Title Suit No. 33 of 1985 for setting aside the said decree and that suit was dismissed on 8-6-1991. That the plaintiff has/had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. The defendant Nos. 37-41 (government officials) also contested the suit by filing written statements. The material case of these defendants is that the SA recorded landlord Mohadeb Singh brought rent suit against the tenant for non-payment of rent and obtained decree and took the suit land in his khas possession after purchasing the same in auction in Rent Execution Case No.2603 of 1941 arising out of Rent Suit No. 908 of 1941. At the time of RS operation the suit land was recorded in the name of Shashi Kumar Singh, son of Mohadeb Singh. Accordingly SA record of right also was prepared in the name of Shashi Kumar Singh. That Shashi Kumar Singh left this country for India before 1965 and, as such, the suit land was enlisted as enemy property. Neither the plaintiff nor the other defendants have had any right, title and possession in the suit land. That the suit is liable to be dismissed and the decree passed in Title Suit No. 173 of 1964 also is liable to be declared void. 

 7. Leave was granted to consider the submissions of the learned Counsel of the plaintiff-leave-petitioner to the effect that the High Court Division was wrong in making the rule absolute ignoring the concurrent findings and decision of the courts of facts relying on Exhibit-6 and other so-called decrees which were not at all binding upon the plaintiff; that the High Court Division, on misconception of law, failed to appreciate the so-called Exhibit-6 in its true purport, that the alleged sale certificate having not been substantiated by sale proclamation and writ of delivery of possession the alleged auction purchase was not established to have taken effect; that the High Court Division was wrong in finding the suit barred by limitation on misconception of law inasmuch as it is well settled that if the plaintiff comes with a suit for declaration that the entry made in the records of right is wrong, in that case Article 120 of the Limitation Act will be applicable, but the plaintiff is not bound to institute a suit for declaration that the entry is wrong, he can wait and when an invasion on his rights is made on the basis of wrong entry, he can sue for a declaration of his title on the ground that the record is wrong and, as such, the instant suit brought within 6 years from the date of threatened invasion is well within, time. 

 8. We have heard Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Senior Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant and Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Senior Advocate for the respondent Nos. 3-22 and Mr Pari mal Chandra Guha, the learned Advocate for the respondent Nos. 46 and 47-sons of Jogesh Chandra Shil. It should be mentioned here that these respondent Nos. 46 and 47 who were the defendant Nos. 42 and 43 in the original suit though did not contest in the trial court or appellate court below or in the High Court Division, but in this Division they, for the first time, have appeared and have submitted an additional paper book stating to the effect that they did not receive any notice of the original suit and, as such, could not contest the same, that they are recorded owners in possession of 0.79 acre out of the suit land. That the suit land belonged to Ganga Charan under landlord Mohadeb Singh who died leaving only son Shashi Kumai Singh. That the suit land was sold in auction for arrears of rent in Rent Suit No. 2603 of 1941 which was purchased by Shashi Kumar Singh on 17-1-1941, and delivery of possession was taken by him in Rent Execution Case No. 908 of 1941 and the sale certificate was confirmed on 20-1-1994. That Shashi Kumar Singh settled 2.96 acres of land to Jogesh Chandra Shil on 28th Chaitra 1347 BS Jogesh Chandra Shil possessed that land and RS Khatian and SA Khatian were prepared in his name rightly. Jogesh Chandra Shil subsequently died leaving two sons the respondent Nos. 46 and 47 and these respondent Nos. 46 and 47 have been possessing this land. That the plaintiff has got no right, title and possession in this land. 

 9. Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-appellant has mainly argued to the effect that it is an admitted fact that Ganga Charan was the CS recorded owner of the suit land; that the plaintiff has proved his case that this Ganga Charan settled the suit land to Ananta Kumar and Nittananda Hawlader by registered patta dated 24-3-1936 the Exhibit-5 and subsequently Ananta Kumar and Nittananda Hawlader sold the suit land to Burundi Hawlader by a registered kabala dated 27-8-1943 the Exhibit-5(Ka) and the heirs of Burundi Hawlader-the defendant Nos.44-60 subsequently, sold the suit land to the plaintiff by a registered deed dated 28-1-1993 the Exhibit-1. The learned Counsel has argued that all these above documents including the CS record of the suit land in the name of Ganga Charan sufficiently prove the plaintiff's case that he has acquired the suit land from its rightful owners. The learned Counsel has argued that though the contesting defendants have claimed that the suit land was sold in auction and Shashi Kumar Singh purchased the same in auction, but this alleged auction purchase of the suit land by Shashi Kumar Singh has not been proved at all. The learned Counsel has argued that so-called sale certificate the Exhibit-6 cannot, be relied on at all since this Exhibit-6 has not been substantiated by sale proclamation and writ of delivery of possession. The learned Counsel has argued that the appellate court below rightly did not put any reliance on this Exhibit-6, but the High Court Division dismissed the suit of the plaintiff most illegally relying on this Exhibit-6-the sale certificate which is not acceptable at all. The learned Counsel has argued also that the decisions of the courts off acts being founded on concurrent findings of fact the High Court Division in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure committed illegality in setting aside the concurrent findings and decision of the courts of facts without assigning any cogent reasonund. The learned Counsel has argued also that in none of the previous suits as alleged by the contesting defendants the predecessors of the plaintiff were made parties and, as such, the plaintiff is not bound by those decrees. The learned Counsel has contended that all those decrees were obtained collusively by practicing fraud upon the courts. The learned Counsel has argued also that in none of the earlier suits there has been any adjudication as to the title of the property in question and, as such, the decrees passed in those suits will not operate as res-judicata in the present suit. Mr Mahmudul Islam has argued also that the High Court Division was wrong in finding the suit as barred by limitation, that the plaintiff being in possession of the suit land has filed the suit for declaration of title, and, as such, the suit cannot be held as barred by limitation. The learned Counsel has contended that had it been a suit for declaration that the entry made in the record of right is wrong, in that case Article 120 of the Limitation Act would have been applicable, but the present suit is for declaration of title and it has been instituted when the defendants made an attempt to invade on plaintiff’s right on the basis of the wrong entry and, as such, this suit is well within time. 

 11. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Counsel for the respondent Nos. 3 to 22 has made submissions supporting the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. The learned Counsel has made argument to the effect that in this suit the plaintiff has totally failed to prove his right, title and possession in the suit land and in the circumstances the High Court Division rightly dismissed the suit. The learned Counsel has argued also that though the plaintiff has claimed that Ganga Charan the original owner of the suit land settled the suit land to Ananta Kumar and Nittananda Hawlader by registered patta 24-3-1936 and that subsequently, Ananta Kumar Nittananda Hawlader transferred the same to Hawlader the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant Nos. 44 to 60 by a registered deed dated 27- 8-1943 and have produced the certified copy of the two transfer deeds only, but could not adduce any other evidence whatsoever to prove that these two registered deeds were actually acted upon and that Ananta Kumar and Nittananda Hawlader possessed the suit land and thereafter, Burundi Hawlader possessed the suit land and after the death of Burundi Hawlader his heirs-the defendant Nos. 44 to 60 possessed the suit land and the plaintiff by so-called purchase from the defendant Nos. 44 to 60 got possession of the suit land and possessed the same. The learned Counsel has pointed out that admittedly the suit land was not recorded in the name of these alleged predecessors of the plaintiff in any of the records of right and there is no evidence at all to prove that they ever paid any rent for the suit land. The learned Advocate has argued that the witnesses whom the plaintiff adduced to support his case are not reliable and dependable witnesses at all and they also could not prove plaintiff's or his alleged predecessors possession in the suit land at all. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali has argued also that there are abundance of evidence on record to prove the contesting defendants' right, title and possession in the suit land and that the High Court Division, on consideration of these evidence of the contesting defendants and the facts and circumstances rightly dismissed the suit of the plaintiff. 

 12. Mr Parimal Chandra Guha the learned Advocate for the respondent Nos.46 and 47 has frankly admitted that the respondent Nos.46 and 47 though have claimed to have been in possession of certain portion of the suit land, but they have got no documents in support of their title in the suit land. 

 15. It is not denied that Ganga Charan was the C. S. recorded owner of the suit land. But the contesting defendants specific case is that for arrear of rent the suit land was sold in auction and Shashi Kumar Singh purchased the same on 17 November, 1941 and subsequently Shashi Kumar Singh settled the suit land along with other lands to the predecessors-in-interest of the contesting defendants and since then the predecessors-in- interest of the contesting defendants and thereafter the contesting defendants have been possessing the suit land. To substantiate this case the contesting defendants have filed the sale certificate which has been marked as Exhibit-6. It appears that in the appellate court below, at the instance of the contesting defendants, the relevant register also for proving this sale certificate was called for and it was produced before the appellate court below and the appellate court below examined the same. So, from this sale certificate the Exhibit-6 it appears that the suit land was sold in auction and Shashi Kumar Singh purchased the same. It has been argued from the side of the plaintiff that in the absence of sale proclamation and writ of delivery of possession this sale certificate-the Exhibit-6 alone cannot prove that this sale certificate was acted upon and Shashi Kumar Singh got delivery of possession of the suit land and became the owner of the same. It is true that the sale proclamation and writ of delivery of possession in support of this sale certificate the Exhibit-6 were not produced before the court. But it appears that there are some other strong evidence to substantiate the case of the contesting defendants that Shashi Kumar Singh became owner of the suit land by virtue of the auction purchase and he subsequently settled the same with the predecessors-in-interest of the contesting defendants and since then the predecessors-in-interest of the contesting defendants and the contesting defendants have been possessing the suit land. The contesting defendants filed a suit for partition being Partition Suit No. 173 of 1964 against the sons of Shashi Kumar Singh and got a decree on compromise in the year 1964 from a competent civil court. The contesting defendants filed another suit being Title Suit No. 109 of 1971 for declaration of their title in the suit land and for further declaration that the suit land was not enemy property against the enemy property authority and that suit also was decreed on 15-6-1972. On the basis of this decree dated 15-6-1972 the defendants also got the suit land mutated in their names by filing a Miscellaneous Case being No. 111973-74 under section 54 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Thereafter, the defendants filed another suit being Title Suit No. 207 of 1978 for permanent injunction against the enemy property authority and others and that suit also was decreed on 20- 12-1980. The Government filed Title Suit No.33 of 1985 for setting aside the decree dated 20-12- 1980 passed in Title Suit No .207 of 1978, but that suit also was dismissed on 33-6-1991. One of the defendants filed Petition Case No. 267 of 1984 under section 145 of the Criminal Procedure Code which was also allowed. The contesting defendants have filed the necessary papers of these above stated suits and case to substantiate their case. All these papers along with mutated khatian of the suit land in the name of the contesting defendants strongly supports the defendants case that their predecessors-in-interest acquired the suit land from Shashi Kumar Singh by way of settlement in the year 1355 BS and since then they and after them these contesting defendants have been possessing the suit land. 

 18. It is true that the plaintiff is not bound to institute a suit for declaration that the records of right of the suit land are wrong. It is true that when an invasion on the rights of a person is made on the basis of the wrong records of right he can file a suit for declaration of title and that suit, if brought within 6 years from the date of such invasion, is well within time. But in the present case, as it appears from the above discussion, none of the records of right was prepared in the name of the plaintiff's vendors or his alleged predecessors- in-interest and they never paid rent for the suit land. The plaintiff also purchased the suit land with the knowledge that in none of the records of right, of the suit  and the names of his vendors or their predecessors-in-interest were recorded. The plaintiff could not prove his possession or the possession of his alleged predecessors-in-interest in the suit land by adducing cogent evidence. It appears that the plaintiff has examined 6 witnesses including himself. The PW 1 is the plaintiff himself. The PW 2, in his examination-in-chief, though has stated that the plaintiff possesses the suit land and before that Ananta Kumar, Nittananda Hawlader and Burundi Hawlader possessed the suit land, but during cross-examination this witness has stated that he saw the heirs of Burundi Hawlader to possess the suit land 30/35 years before. The PW 3 though in examination-in- chief has deposed in support of the plaintiff's possession in the suit land, but during cross-examination this witness has stated that Ananta Kumar died two years before and Nittananda Hawlader died four years before and Ananta Kumar and Nittananda Hawlader possessed the suit land till their death. He stated "অনন্ত নিত্যানন্দ যতদিন জীবিত ছিলেন ততদিন উক্ত জমি দখল করতেন।" Evidently, this witness is a liar and has deposed falsely. The PW 4 also is not at all a competent person to depose as regards possession of the suit land. During cross- examination this witness has deposed to the effect that he resides 3 miles away from the suit land. During cross-examination this witness has admit- ted also that he is a close relation of the plaintiff and he has got to land in the suit mouza. This witness, during cress-examination, has admitted that he cannot say who possessed the suit land for what period during the last 48/49 years. This witness has stated "মামলার জমি আমি অনুমান ৪৮/৮৯ব ৎসর যাবত চিনি। এই ৪৮/৮৯ বছর ধারাবাহিকভাবে কেক বেদখল করিয়াছে তাহা সব বলিতে পারিনা।" The PW 5 is one of the alleged executants of the plaintiff's kabala and, as such, the most interested witness. During cross-examination this witness has stated that he used to possess the suit land, but he cannot say what quantum of land he possessed. This witness has stated also that there are 2/3 dwelling huts on the suit land. But the PW 2 has stated that there is no hut in the suit land. The PW 6 is a formal witness an employee of registry office who produced a register to prove the certified copy of the patta dated 24-2-1936. 

 21. In this appeal the respondent Nos. 44 and 47 though have claimed right, title and possession in certain portion of the suit land, but admittedly they have no evidence whatsoever in support of their alleged title in the suit land and there is also no evidence on record in support of their alleged possession in their claimed land. 

 22. However, from the above discussion, it is evident that, in this suit the plaintiff has failed to prove his alleged right, title and possession in the suit land by adducing necessary evidence rather the evidence adduced by the contesting defendants have disproved the case of the plaintiff. 

 This civil appeal, by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 5-7-2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4041 of 1999 making the Rule absolute setting aside the judgment and decree dated 14-9-1999 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Bagherhat in Title Appeal No.282 of 1994 affirming the judgment and decree dated 6-10-1994 passed by the then learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Bagherhat in Title Suit No. 225 of 1994 decreeing the suit. 

 25. The appellant instituted Title Suit No. 225 of 1994 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, second Court Bagerhat for declaration of his title in the suit property. His case, in short, is that the land measuring 6.05 acres appertaining to CS khatian No. 152.of No. 3 Nalbunia Mouza under Sharankhola Police Station originally belonged to Ganga Charan. He settled the said land to Ananta Kumar Dey and Nittananda Hawlader by a registered patta dated 24-3-1936 who again transferred the said land to Barundi Hawlader, the predecessor-in-interest of defendant Nos. 44-60 by a registered deed of sale dated 27-8-1943. After that, Barundi Hawlader died leaving behind defendant Nos. 44-60 as his heirs and they transferred 5.09 acres of land (the suit land) out of the said 6.05 acres of land by a registered deed of sale dated 28-1-1993 to the plaintiff and since then the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land. Barundi Hawlader, the predecessor in interest of defendant Nos. 44-60 (vendors of the plaintiff) had died just before RS operation and they had no other capable man to look after the property, and taking that advantage Jogesh Chandra, the predecessor-in-interest of defendant No.42 and 43 in collusion with Shashi Kumar Singh, son of previous landlord Mohadeb Chandra Singh got the suit land recorded partly in the name of Shashi Sekhar and partly in his own name, though none of them had any possession, title and interest in the suit land. The SA records were also prepared wrongly in their names. Such wrong recording has clouded the title of the plain- tiff in the suit land necessitating filing of the suit. Taking advantage of wrong records in respect of the suit land in the name of Shashi Kumar Singh, the predecessors of defendant Nos. 1-10, 11-13, 14-19, 20-26 and 27-36 forging the signatures of Shashi Kumar's sons, Kanai and Hiralal Singh brought Title Suit No. 173 of 1964 on false pleas, and suppressing summons and practicing fraud obtained a compromise decree on 8-8-1964. On the other hand, defendant Nos. 37-40 illegally enlisted the suit property as vested property. They never took over physical possession of the suit property. Defendant Nos. 1-36 and 3 7-40 collusively created obstructions to peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit property by the plaintiff and hence the title suit has been filed. 

 27. The case of defendant Nos. 1, 7, 11-14, 20, 23, 25-28, 30, 32-36, in short, is that the suit property originally belonged to Shashi Kumar Singh under the ex-landlord Satya Chandra Saha and Korman Akon. On first Baishakh, 1355 BS Shashi Kumar Singh settled the suit land along with other lands to the predecessor-in-interest of these defendants at a jama of Taka 315 by executing an amalnama on first Asar, 1355 BS and granted dakhilas therefore. At the time of SA operation, the suit land was erroneously recorded in the name of Shashi Kumar Singh in Khatian No. 1114. In the meantime, Shashi Kumar died leaving behind two sons, Kanai Lal Singh and Hira Lal Singh, so the defendant brought Title Suit No. 173 of 1964 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Khulna and on 8-9-1964, the suit was decreed on compromise. On the basis of wrong record of rights, the local Tahsilder claimed the suit land as vested and non-resident property and denied receiving rents. Then the respondents brought Title Suit No. 109 of 1971 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Khulna for declaration of their title together with the declaration that the enlistment of the suit property as vested and non-resident property is void, illegal and the suit was decreed on 15-6-1972. After that, the official/staff of the vested and non-resident property in collusion with the local enemies of the defendants threatened to dispossess them from the suit land. Accordingly, these defendants filed Title Suit No. 207 of 1978 in the Court of the Munsif, First Court, Bagerhat and obtained decree on 20-12-1980. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Bagerhat and TNO, Sharonkhola instituted Title Suit No. 33 of 1985 for setting aside the aforesaid judgment and decree. But their suit was dismissed on 8-6-1991. 

 28. The case of defendant Nos. 37-41, in short, is that the SA recorded tenant Mahadev Singh brought rent suit against the tenant for non- payment of rent and obtained decree and by filing a rent execution case took the suit land in his khas possession. Rent Execution Case No. 2604 of 1941 arising out of Rent suit No. 908 of 1941 of the First Court of Munsif, Bagerhat was filed. The auction was held on 17-1-1941 and Shashi Kumar Singh purchased the suit land in auction. During RS operation, the suit land was recorded in the name of Shashi Kumar Singh, son of Mahadev Singh. The SA record was prepared in the name of Shashi Kumar Singh who left this country for India before 1965 and accordingly, the suit property was enlisted as enemy property as perstatement of defendant Nos. 37-41. Neither the plaintiff nor other defendants had any right, title and interest in the suit land. These defendants took settlement of the suit land from Shashi Kumar Singh and, as such, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of Shashi Kumar Singh in order to avoid complications the defendant filed Title Suit No. 173 of 1964 and obtained the compromise decree. 

 29. The trial Court upon hearing the parties by its judgment and order dated 6-10-1994 decreed the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendants filed Title Appeal No.282 of 1994 before the learned District Judge, Bagerhat. On transfer, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, Bagerhat, who by his judgment and order dated 14-9-1999 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 I. Admittedly, Gonga Charan was the CS recorded owner of the suit land and the plaintiff proved his case that Ganga Charan settled the suit land to Ananta Kumar and Nittananda Hawlader by a registered patta dated 24-3-1936, Exhibit-5 and subsequently, Ananta Kumar Dey and Nittananda Hawlader sold their under tenancy right to Burundi Hawlader by a registered deed of sale dated 27-8-143, Exhibit 5ka and the heirs of Burundi Hawlader, defendant Nos. 44-60 sold the suit land to the plaintiff by a registered deed of sale dated 28-1-1993, Exhibit-I. And, as such, it has been proved beyond reasonable doubt that the plaintiff acquired title in the suit land. 

 II. The contesting defendants claimed that the suit land was sold in auction and Shashi Kumer Singh purchased the same but the auction purchase of the suit land by Shashi Kumer Singh was not proved at all. 

 VI. The finding that the suit was barred by limitation was wrong and the plaintiff being in possession of the suit land filed the suit for declaration of title as soon as his right was clouded by the claim of title of the defendants over the suit land. 

 VII. Respondent Nos. 46 and 47 the alleged heirs of Shashi Kumar Singh could not prove .that their predecessors acquired title and possession in the suit land pursuant to the auction sale dated 7-11-1941. 

 I.The plaintiff totally failed to prove his right, title and possession in the suit land and, as such, the High Court Division rightly dismissed the suit. 

 V. Defendant-respondent Nos. 3-22 by filing several suits obtained decrees in respect of the suit land and, as such, they acquired title to and possession in the suit land. 

 34. Mr Parimal Chandra Guha, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent Nos. 46 and 47, submitted that though respondent Nos. 46 and claimed to have possession in certain portion of the suit land, they have no document in support of their title in the suit land. 

 36. Admittedly Gonga Charan was the CS recorded owner of the suit land. According to the plaintiff, Gonga Charan settled the suit land to Ananta Kumar Dey and Nittananda Hawlader by a registered patta dated 24-3-1936 who transferred their under tenancy interest by a registered deed of sale dated 27-8-1943 to Burundi Hawlader, the predecessor-in-interest of defendant Nos. 44-60. Burundi Hawlader died leaving behind defendant Nos. 44-60 as his heirs and they transferred 5.08 acres of land (suit land) out of 6.05 acres of land by a registered deed of sale dated 28-1-1993 to the plaintiff. The contesting defendants claimed that for arrear of rents, the suit land was sold in auction and Shashi Kumar Singh purchased the same on 17-11-1941 and subsequently, Shashi Kumar Singh settled the suit land along with other lands to the predecessor-in-interest of the contesting defendants. To prove their case, the contesting defendants filed sale certificate marked as Exhibit-6. The alleged sale certificate has not been substantiated by any sale proclamation and writ of delivery of possession. A sale certificate is not conclusive but only prima facie evidence of title and it can be shown that it is wrong and relates to property, which was not sold. 

 37. Having gone through the sale certificate (Exhibit-6), it appears that the Gonga Charan was the judgment-debtor. Admittedly, GongaCharan created under tenancy by a registered patta dated 24-3-1936 in favour of Ananta Kumar Dey and Nittananda Hawlader. A certified copy of the said patta was marked Exhibit-5 without any objection. Ananta Kumar Dey and Nittananda Hawlader sold their under tenancy interest to Burundi Hawlader by a registered deed of sale dated 27-8-1943. A certified copy of the said deed was marked as Exhibit-5ka without any objection. Therefore, even if, the superior interest of Gonga Charan was sold in auction, there is nothing on record to show that Shashi Kumar Singh annulled the under tenancy created by Gonga Charan according to the provision of 167 of the Bengal Tenancy Act. The contesting defendants in their written statement did not state anything about annulment of the under tenancy created by Gonga Charan in favour of Ananta Kumar Dey and Nittananda Hawlader, who sold their under tenancy interest to Burundi Hawlader. The plaintiff could prove that the registered patta dated 24-3-1936 (Exhibit-5) and the registered deed of sale dated 27-8-1943 (Exhibit-5ka) by bringing the volumes from the Office of the Sub-Registrar through PW 6, Md Matab Ali Hawlader, a permanent Mohararof Khulna Sub-Registry Office. The contesting defendant respondent Nos. 3-22 did not challenge those documents. Unless the under tenancy is annulled it shall be deemed that Burundi Hawlader and subsequently his heirs continued in possession of 6.05 acres of land It is contended that the registered patta dated 24-3- 1936 and the deed of sale dated 27.08.1943 were not acted upon. According to the Registration Act, title passes to the transferee as soon as the registration of a deed is completed. So the above contention falls through. 

 42. Having considered sub-section 4 of section 167, it appears that in respect of protected interests as contained in clause-(c) of section 160 of the Bengal Tenancy Act the auction purchaser could sue for enhancement of rent but could not evict the under tenant when the nature of land comes within c\ause-3 of section 160 of the Bengal Tenancy Act. Having considered clause- (3) of section 160 and sub-section 4 of section 167 of the Bengal Tenancy Act, I am of the opinion that Burundi Hawlader could not be evicted by the auction purchaser Shashi Kumar Singh pursuant to the sale certificate (Exhibit-6). Shashi Kumar Singh only purchased the superior interest of Gonga Charan Hawlader and he was entitled to receive rent from the heirs of Burundi Hawlader. 

 43. In the light of discussion made before, there can be no shadow of doubt that the plaintiff by his purchase dated 28-1-1993 from Burundi Hawlader acquired valid title in the suit land. 

 44. The contesting defendants claimed that Shashi Kumar Singh died leaving behind two sons, namely, Kanai Lal Singh and HiraLal Singh. The contesting defendants brought Title Suit No. 173 of 1964 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Khulna against Kanai Lal Singh and HiraLal Singh and the suit was stated to have been decreed on compromise on 8-9-1964. The contesting defendants also stated that they brought Title Suit No. 109 of 1971 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Khulna for declaration of their title and for further declaration that enlistment of the suit land in the list of vested and non-resident property was void and obtained ex-parte decree on 15-6-1972. The contesting defendants also brought Title Suit No. 207 if 1978 in the First Court of Munsif, Bagherhat for permanent injunction and obtained ex-parte decree on 20-12-1980. Against the ex-parte decree, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Bagherhat and Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Sharonkhula, brought Title Suit No. 33 of 1985 for setting aside the said ex-parte decree and the Suit was dismissed on 8-6-1990. Admittedly, the heirs of Burundi Hawlader were not made parties in those suits and the compromise and the ex-parte decree were obtained behind their back and, as such, neither the heirs of Burundi Hawlader nor the plaintiff was at all bound by those decrees. The contesting defendants in order to grab the suit land managed to obtain a compromise decree in Title Suit No. 173 of 1964, ex-parte decrees in Title Suit No.109 of 1971 and in Title Suit No. 20 of 1978. When the contesting defendants failed to prove their title in the suit land these decrees cannot confer title on them, in which, the heirs of Burundi were not made parties. 

 45. The High Court Division came to the finding that the suit filed by the plaintiff was barred by limitation. It is well settled that if the plaintiff comes with a suit for declaration that the entry made in the record right is wrong, in that case Article 102 of the Limitation Act will be applicable, but the plaintiff is not bound to institute a suit for declaration that the entry is wrong. He can wait and when an invasion on his right is made on the basis of the entry, he can sue for declaration of his title on the ground that the record is wrong and, as such, a suit will be in time if brought within six years from the date of threatened invasion. Having considered the materials on record, I find that the plaintiff's suit is not barred by limitation as he filed the suit when his right was denied in the suit land by the contesting defendants. Mere non recording the name of Burundi Hawlader or the names of his heirs in the khatians or nor payment of rent could not extinguish the title of Burundi Hawlader and his heirs and the plaintiff by his subsequent purchases from the heirs of Burundi Hawlader acquired valid title in the suit land. 

 46. Admittedly, the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title simpliciter without any prayer for recovery of possession. Had the plaintiff not in possession of 5.05 acres of land as contained in Exhibit-l dated 28-1-1993 he would have brought a suit not only for declaration of title but also for recovery of khash possession. 

 49. The plaintiff examined 6 witnesses including himself. PWs 2, 3, 4 and 5 proved the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. PW 3 in his cross-examination stated that the suit land is three miles away from the house of the contesting defendant-respondent Nos. 3-22. On the other hand, defendant Nos. 3-22 examined only 2 witnesses including defendant No. 7 and both the witnesses miserably failed to prove the possession of contesting defendant-respondent Nos. 3-22 in the suit land. When evidence is adduced by both the parties the question of onus becomes immaterial. The plaintiff succeeded in proving his possession by examining PWs. 2, 3, 4, and 5. The contesting defendant-respondent examined only 2 DWs apart from defendant No.7 who was examined as DW 1 and they miserably failed to prove possession of defendant-respondent Nos. 3-22. 

 50. I have already found the plaintiff acquired valid title in the suit land and there is an age-old maxim 'Title follows possession'. In the light of the findings made before, I am of the opinion that the plaintiff had been able to prove his title to and possession in the suit land. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the judgment delivered by the High court Division is set aside.

full_judgment:
Nozrul Islam Chowdhury J: This appeal, at the instance of the plaintiffs as appellants, is directed against the judgment and decree dated November 28-11-1993 passed in Title Suit No. 6 of 1986 by the learned Subordinate, Judge, Jessore. 

 2. Facts in short, out of which this appeal has arisen are that the appellants as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 6 of 1986 before the Subordinate Judge, Jessore impleading the respondents as defendants seeking a decree for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and in the alternative a saham of 0.44 acres of land by way of partition. 

 3. The case of the plaintiffs in short, are that the suit land originally belonged to Balu Mollah as tenant under Erfan Mollah, and it was recorded in the name of Balu Mollah under CS Khatian No. 35; Balu Mollah having been in possession in exercise in his title therein, died leaving behind One son Aftab Mollah and a daughter Bindhu Bibi as his heirs. Thereafter, Aftab Mollah and Bindhu Bibi having been in possession and enjoyment of the suit land in exercise of their mourosui maliki right executed a mortgage deed on 20-1-1932 in favour of Satiya Charan and the mortgage was subsequently redeemed. Thereafter, Aftab Mollah and Bindhu Bibi jointly possessed the suit land. Subsequently, Aftab Mollah expressed his willingness to lease out 16½ decimals of land from plot No. 189(359) and one Hari Mohan was engaged to write the patta; said Hari Mohan collusively entered 0.27 acres of land of plot No. 187 and 0.39 acres of plot No. 190 in the registered patta deed dated 26-9-1940, behind the back of its executant Aftab Mollah; thereafter Aftab Mollah executed another patta on 6-3-1941 wherein it was disclosed that the patta registered on 26-9-1940 was not acted upon as there were mistakes; subsequently in the year 1943 Aftab Mollah died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs; the registered patta dated 26-9-1940 therefore did not confer any title in respect of the suit land in favour of Hari Mohan. When Bindhu Bibi daughter of Aftab Mollah found it difficult to retain her property she had to bring Title Suit No. 35 of 1953 before the Munsif, 3rd Court, Jessore impleading Hari Mohan Roy, Hari Dasi and others as defendants where Bindhu Bibi got a contested decree and in that suit the patta dated 26-9-1910 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Dasi was found as not sustainable in law. 

 39. When the plaintiffs had gone for cutting Segun tree from the suit land they were objected to by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and at that stage the plaintiffs for the first time came to know that the record of right in respect of the suit land had been prepared wrongly in favour of the father of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 although the defendants had no right, title, interest or possession in the suit land consequently the instant suit was brought for declaration of their title by the plaintiffs and for recovery of khas possession and in the alternative the plaintiffs, prayed for a sham to the extent of 0.44 acres in the suit land by partition in the form of preliminary decree. The plaintiffs also prayed for declaration that the patta dated 6-9-1940 in favour of Hari Mohan Roy executed by Aftab Mollah is null and void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and the added defendant 3(Ka) entered appearance in the suit upon filing two separate written statements; in the written statement filed by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 they denied the material allegations made in the plaint stating inter alia that the suit land along with other lands originally belonged to Balu Mollah and it was recorded in CS khatian No. 35 correctly who having been in possession and enjoyment of the suit land along with other lands, died leaving behind his only son Aftab Mollah and only daughter Bindu Bibi as his heirs. Aftab Mollah being in possession of the suit land transferred 0.66 acres of land at a salami of Taka 150 fixing 2.25 anas yearly rent upon executing a registered patta dated 26-9-1940 in favour of Hari Dasi the mother of defendant Nos.1 and 2, an area of 16½ decimals of land appertaining to plot No.189 and plot No. 356 not covered by suit land was also transferred in favour of Hari Mohan Roy the father of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by another registered patta dated 6-3-41 executed by Aftab Mollah and handed over possession where the predecessors of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 got possession by constructing house thereof; the patta executed by Aftab Mollah, in 1941 in favour of the father of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 being registered deed No. 194 contains an averment that patta dated 6-9-1940 being a mistaken one it was not acted upon but such an averment made by Aftab Mollah in his subsequent patta of 1941 was illegal and beyond authority; Aftab Mollah and his wife admitted the predecessor of the answering defendants as tenant upon receipt of rent from them. The answering defendants have been residing in the said house constructed by their father. The answering defendants have been in possession and enjoyment of the suit hind from the time of their predecessor right from the year 1940 therefore a title by adverse possession has also accrued in their favour. The answering defendant Nos. 1 and 2 also disclosed in the written statement that they have sold out 0.11-3/4 acres of land in favour of Gyanodabala by a registered kabala and had handed over possession where, on the death of Gyanodabala, her son has been in possession thereof. 

 7. In course of trial of the suit the plaintiffs examined two witnesses of them Jarina Khatun was examined a PW 1 and Rakib Mollah was also examined as PW 2. On the other hand, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 examined six witnesses on their behalf while the defendant No. 3(ka) examined one Guru Das as DW 1 in support of his case. Through the said witnesses the plaintiffs side produced CS Khatian No.35 as Exhibit-1, SA Khatian No.43,45,46 as Exhibit-1(ka)-1(ga), judgment passed in Title Suit No. 35 of 1953 Exhibit-2 an 1 decree drawn in Title Suit No.35 of 1953 Exhibit-3 , plaint of Suit No. 35 of 1953 Exhibit-4, while defendants 1 and 2 exhibited 33 rent receipt of the year 1954 marked as Exhibit-Ka-Ka-(33), tax receipt of Pourashava Exhibit-Kha-Kha(17) registered patta dated 26-9-40 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Dasi Exhibit-Ga, deed of patta dated 8-3-41 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Dasi Exhibit-Ga(1) judgment dated 19-2-43 passed in CR No. 1199 of 1942 Exhibit-Gha, judgment dated 31-01-54 passed in Title Suit No. 35 of 1953 marked as Exhibit-Gha(2), Judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 98 of 1948 and the decree drawn up in Title Suit No.35 of 1953 Exhibit-Uma series, depositions of Akarjan Bibi in Title Suit No. 21 of 1947 Exhibit-Cha, deposition of Krishna Lal Dutta Exhibit-Cha(1), SA Khatian No.46,43,45 Exhibit-Chha-Chha(2), application for amendment of the plaint filed in Title Suit No.247 of 1982 Exhibit-Ja, application for amendment filed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.87 of 1984 (Pauper) Exhibit-Jha(I), petition of Miscellaneous Case No 87 of 1984 Exhibit-Jha (Pauper), Commissioner's Report along with map submitted in Title Suit No. 247 of 1982, Exhibit-Neo, deposition of Hari Mohan Roy given in Title Suit No.21 of 1947 Exhibit-Ta, deposition of Rakib Mollah given in Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1990 (Exhibit-Ta.1) the document produced by defendant 3(ka) have been marked as Exhibit-Ka series, sale deed dated 2-2-70 Exhibit-Ka, Mutation Khatian separation parcha 1189/1 Exhibit-Kha, rent receipt Exhibit-Cha(1) -Kha(2) tax receipt of Pourashava Exhibit-Ga Series. Upon conclusion of the trial the learned Joint District Judge by his judgment and decree dated 28-11-1993 dismissed the suit. 

 10. Mr Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, also submits that in the year 1953 Bindhu Bibi instituted Title Suit No. 35 of 1053 impleading Hari Dasi Roy and Hari Mohan Roy as defendant Nos. 1 and 2 seeking a decree for partition and that suit was decreed on contest and the plaintiff Bindi Bibi was allotted a saham to the extent of 33 decimals of land. The plaintiffs used to enjoy and possess the suit land by enjoying usufructs there from but the defendants raised claim of the suit land on the basis of the aforesaid patta and subsequent record of right prepared in their names and on 21-3-1982 the plaintiffs were resisted to cut segun trees from the suit land by the defendants and finally on 12-1-1989 the plaintiffs were dispossessed from the suit land by the defendants, therefore, the suit was brought as aforesaid. 

 11. Mr Bhuiyan submits further, that admittedly the plaintiffs are the legal heirs of Aftab Mollah and consequently on his death his property devolved upon the plaintiffs as they are the legal heirs of Aftab Mollah. It is also submitted by Mr Bhuiyan that possession of the suit land all through remains with the plaintiffs and it has been established by the evidence of PWs and it is also proved through the evidence of a competent witness of convincing nature like PW 1 who categorically stated in her deposition that the plaintiffs were dispossessed from the suit land on 12-11-1989 and his testimonies have been substantially corroborated on this point but the learned Joint District Judge arrived at a finding to the contrary upon misreading of those evidence on record. 

 15. Mr Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan submits further that a case of title by adverse possession and the case on the basis of document cannot be claimed simultaneously as in the instant case. In substantiating his submission the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of Push pa Rani Saha Podder vs Rash Mohan Saha being dead his heirs Kartick Chowdhury Saha reported in 26 BLD (AD) 50 

 16. Mr. Bhuiyan also submits that the claim of title by adverse possession was neither specifically pleaded nor proved by the defendants and no issue was framed to that effect either, nonetheless the learned Joint District Judge, conferred the title on the plaintiffs by a gratuitous finding of adverse possession in their favour which is not sustainable. In this connection he placed reliance in the case of Mahaprabhu Ram vs Gopal Ram reported in 42 DLR (AD) 154 and the case of 1 Hazera Begum vs Roushan Ara Begum reported in 39 DLR (AD) 22, the case of Mst Ghulani Hain vs Muhammad Waris Khan reported in 10 DLR (FC) 174 and Tajuddin vs Moktar Ahmed reported in 1991 BLD (AD) 44. It is also submitted by Mr Bhuiyan that SA record prepared in the name of the defendants which has got no presumptive value of correctness in as much as it has no basis as such mere preparation of SA khantian in their names or payment of rent by them does not create any title in favour of the defendants. In this connection the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of Halima Begum vs Syed Ahmed reported in 21 DLR 854. The case of Chand Mali vs Md Hossain All being his heirs 1(ka) Md Sekander Ali reported in 3 BLC 364 and the case of Lal Mia being dead his heirs Momena Khatun vs Haji Md Ibrahim reported in 28 DLR (AD) 61. 

 17. It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellant that mere nonpayment of rent by the plaintiffs does not extinguish or affect their title to the suit land. In this connection the learned Advocate for the petitioner placed reliance in the case of Abdur Noor vs Aziruddin reported in 21 BLT (AD) 161. 

 18. Mr Bhuiyan submits further that the finding of fact arrived at by the learned Munsif in Title Suit No.35 of 1953 to the effect that the claim of the parents of defendant Nos.1 and 2 by patta of 1940 and 1941 were bad in law, till subsist since no appeal or cross-appeal or revision was filed against the said judgment and decree is such the said judgment is admissible in evidence in the instant case and binding upon the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 within the meaning of section 43 of the Evidence Act and it will also operate as resjudicata against them since their parents were party to that suit. In this connection the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of Nasim All vs Safina Bibi reported in 1988 BLD 493. 

 23. The learned Advocate for the respondents submits further that in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954, Exhibit-Ga was found to be bad in law only but it was not declared to be invalid. Therefore, the finding with respect to Exhibit-Ga in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 cannot raise the issue of resjudicata in the instant suit. 

 24. The learned Advocate for the respondents submits furt that possession under mistaken or invalid title is effective to extinguish owner's title. The plaintiffs did not claim their title by adverse possession is not enough to deny the relief lie is entitled to. In substantiating his submission the learned advocate placed reliance in the case of Sadak Ali vs Suruj Ali, reported in 7 DLR 95. 

 25. The learned Advocate for the respondent submits lastly that the apparent observation in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 with respect to Exhibit to the effect that the same is bad in law by the trial court was not given by framing any issue to that effect, therefore, such observation having no binding effect on any person whatsoever therefore does not raise any question of res judicata in the instant suit. 

 26. We have heard the learned Advocates for the parties, perused the materials on record including the depositions of the witnesses and the documents exhibited from both sides wherefrom it transpires that the main issue involved in this appeal as to whether patta dated 26-9-1940 purported to have been executed by Aftab Mollah one of the admitted original owner of the suit land in favour Hari Dasi Roy, Exhibit-Ga had divested Aftab Mollah of his title to the properties covered by the said patta or not, if the answer is in the affirmative in that case, case of the plaintiffs must fail. But if the answer is in the negative in that case, the plaintiffs must succeed, therefore, having concentrated our full attention to the said Exhibit-Ga, we find that Title Suit No.35 of 1954 (wrongly written as 1953 in some places) was instituted before the 3rd Court of Munsif, Jessore by Bindhu Bibi as plaintiff impleading Hari Mohan Roy and Hari Dasi Roy as main defendant Nos. 1 and 2 respectively along with 5 others as defendants seeking a decree for declaration of plaintiffs title to the extent of 5 annas 4 pai share in the suit land and possession therein by partition and in the said suit one of the six issues No. 5 was to the effect as under:— 

 "Has the plaintiff her alleged right title and interest in the land in suit." 

 27. It may be pointed out that Bindhu Bibi is the only daughter of Valu Mollah, the admitted original owner of the suit land, which was also averred in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954. Of course, Bindhu Bibi had only one brother named Aftab Mollah and this part of the case is also admitted by both the parties. 

 28. Having gone through the judgment delivered in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 carefully, we find that in that suit too Hari Mohan Roy and Hari Dasi Roy claimed their title in the suit land as defendants on the basis of two pattas one dated 26-9-1940 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Had Dasi Roy and the other dated 06-3-41 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Mohan Roy and in deciding the title the plaintiffs the learned Munsif clearly observed as under:— 

 31. In deciding the plaintiff’s title in the said Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 the learned Munsif arrived at a definite finding 10 the effect:— 

 32. We have also found that in the said Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 the validity of the two pattas, one in favour of Hari Mohan Roy dated 26-4-40 and other dated 6-3-1941 Exhibit-A and A(1) respectively in that suit were very much in issue before the learned Munsif and having considered the submission from both sides and upon consideration of the evidence on record available before him the learned Munsif arrived at a definite finding as quoted above. Therefore, findings in respect of both the two documents namely the aforesaid two pattas are very much binding upon the parties, involved in that suit, more particularly when it is an admitted position that the said judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 was not challenged before any higher forum and in such view of the matter we have no hesitation to hold that the finding with respect to patta dated 26-9-40 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Dasi Roy as arrived in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 operate as res judicata , therefore, no finding to the contrary with respect to the said document Exhibit-Ga in this appeal namely patta dated 26-9-40 executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Dasi Roy is possible, therefore, it can be safely held that the Exhibit-Ga did not confer any title in favour of Hari Dasi Roy or in other words divested Aftab Mollah of his title in respect of the land covered by the same. 

 are based on misreading and misconstruction of evidence of PWs 1 and 2 while the evidence on the point of resjudicata is totally misconceived and based on total misconstruction of the pleadings of the parties rather in this connection we have found the finding with respect to Exhibit-Ga arrived at by the learned Munsif in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 (wrongly written as 1953) operates as resjudicata on a finding to the contrary in respect of Exhibit-Ga in the present suit and the finding of the learned Munsif in the previous suit in this respect stands as final by operation of law. 

 38. Defendants, witnesses are six in number of them DW 1 Hem Chandra Roy who is defendant No. 1, DW 2 Md Shahabuddin, DW 3 Adiluddin Bepari, DW 4 Md Motiar Rahman, DW 5 Noban Ali and DW 6 Eakub Ali Biswas they have deposed in the case and supported the defendants story therein but for our purpose we do not feel it necessary to discuss the same elaborately in view of our finding to the effect that the Exhibit-Ga the patta dated 26-9-40 was never acted upon, therefore, it had not conferred any title either to Hari Dasi or her successor the defendants. On the contrary we have also noticed that by the patta dated Exhibit-Ga(1) executed by Aftab Mollah in favour of Hari Mohan Roy dated 8-3-41 relates to the same land beyond the suit land where the defendants claimed to have been in possession by erecting their homestead and the said land being adjacent to the suit land. The learned Joint District Judge got himself confused referring to different statements made by the witnesses and consequently dismissed the suit on the point of limitation holding to the effect that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession within 12 years from the date of institution of the suit. Therefore, the findings of the trial court with respect thereto are not at all sustainable in law members of his family moreover those rent receipts tax receipts do not attract the suit land as no specification of land is available therein. It may also be pointed out that the defendants took a duel plea in their pleading in a casual way one is that they claim title on the basis of patta dated 26-9-40 and the other one for adverse possession. The learned Joint District Judge dismissed the suit and arrived at a conclusion that the defendants acquired title both on the basis of their pattas as well as by adverse possession, which is not sustainable in law, in view of the principle of law enunciated in 26 BLD (AD) 50 to the effect that case of title by adverse possession and a case of title on the basis of document cannot be claimed simultaneously but in the instant case the plaintiffs did so. In this connection it may also be pointed out that the claim of title by adverse possession though accepted by the trial court was neither specifically pleaded nor proved by evidence. In the instant case and in the position like this the finding of title by adverse possession by the defendants as arrived by the trial court cannot but be treated as gratuitous finding of adverse possession and in this connection reference may be made to the case of Mahaprabhu Ram vs Gopal Ram Ram reported in 42 DLR (AD) 154. It may also pointed out that the learned Joint District Judge committed error of law without applying his judicial mind to the settled position of law that possession can never be adverse if it is referable to lawful title. Since in the instant case the defendants claim lawful title on the basis of two separate registered deed of patta, on the one hand, and title by adverse possession on the other, as such both the pleas taken by the out that the defendants took a duel plea in their pleading in a casual way, one is that they claim title on the basis of patta dated 26-9-40 and the other one for adverse possession. The learned Joint District Judge dismissed the suit and arrived at a conclusion that the defendants acquired title both on the basis of their pattas as well as by adverse possession, which is not sustainable in law, in view of the principle of law enunciated in 26 BLD (AD) 50 to the effect that case of title by adverse possession and a case of title on the basis of document cannot be claimed simultaneously but in the instant case the plaintiffs did so. In this connection it may also be pointed out that the claim of title by adverse possession though accepted by the trial court was neither specifically pleaded nor proved by evidence. In the instant case and in the position like this the finding of title by adverse possession by the defendants as arrived by the trial court cannot but be treated as gratuitous finding of adverse possession and in this connection reference may be made to the case of Mahaprabhu Ram vs Gopal Ram Ram reported in 42 DLR (AD) 154. It may also be pointed out that the learned Joint District Judge committed error of law without applying his judicial mind to the settled position of law that possession can never be adverse if it is referable to lawful title. Since in the instant case the defendants claim lawful title on the basis of two separate registered deed of patta, on the one hand and title by adverse possession on the other, as such both the pleas taken by the defendants must fail since in such a situation any court or tribunal becomes totally perplexed as to which version of their claim is to be believed or disbelieved. In this connection reference may be made to the case of Hazera Begum vs Rowshan Ara Begum reported in 39 DLR (AD) 22 and Mst Ghulam Hahi vs Muhammad Wanes Khan reported in 10 DLR (PC) 174. The learned Joint District Judge also failed lo appreciate that the defendants plea of adverse possession is not tenable in law against the plaintiffs since they are rightful claimants to the suit land. Reference may be made in this connection to the ease of Abdul Latif vs Abdul Malek Kazi reported in 1984 BLD (AD)15 = 38 DLR (AD) 2. It may also he pointed out that record prepared in the names of the defendants has got no presumptive value of correctness in as much as it has no basis particularly in view of our finding that Exhibit-Ga is not sustainable in law as such mere preparation of SA khatian in favour of the defendants or payment of rent by them to the Government do not create any title in their favour. In this connection reference may be made to the case Lal Miah being dead his heirs Momena Khatun vs Haji Md Ibrahim reported in 28 DLR (AD) 61. It may be pointed out further that the finding of the learned Joint District Judge on the point of resjudicata is patently wrong and not sustainable in law particularly in view of the settled principle that right to partition is a continuous right. Reference may made in this connection to the case of Mst Meheron Nessa vs Ali Ahmed Khan reported in 15 MLR 197 = 14 BLC 743 and in this connection it may be recalled that the finding of the learned Munsif, 3rd Court, Jessore in Title Suit No. 35 of 1954 to the effect that the pattas in favour of both the mother and father of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 executed in the year 1940 and 1941 were bad in law, is a finding which has been subsisting till date particularly in view of the fact that the judgment of the said suit was not challenged before any higher forum at any stage and more so when the predecessors of the defendants 1 and 2 were very much contesting parties in that suit and in such view of the matter the said judgment is admissible in evidence in the instant suit and the same is binding upon the contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 particularly in view of the provision of section 43 of the Evidence Act and in that view of the matter such finding with respect to the pattas of 1910 and 1941 operates as resjudicata in the instant case. In this connection reference may be made to the case of Nasim Ali vs Sakina Bibi reported in 1988 BLD 493. 

 41. The trial court ought to have held that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.21 of 1947 and Title Appeal No.98 of 1948 as also the judgment of Civil Revision Case No. 1190 of 1942 being not in the party those are not binding upon the plaintiffs and moreso judgment of a criminal proceeding cannot be admitted into evidence in deciding a civil suit and a contrary view being opposed to the settled principles of law those are not sustainable. 

 44. In view what has been stated above, we find substance in this appeal. Accordingly, the same is allowed without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-11-1993 passed by the Subordinate Judge now Joint District Judge, Jessore is hereby set-aside and Title Suit No. 6 of 1986 brought by the plaintiffs is hereby decreed as prayed for and the defendants are hereby directed to vacate the suit land upon removing the structures, if any, within 60 (sixty) days from the date of receipt of the judgment, failing which the plaintiffs are at liberty to recover khas, possession of the suit land through court by process of execution.
