2. The opposite-parties herein as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 in the Sub-ordinate Judge, First Court, Chittagong, on 28-9-.1991 impleading the petitioners Nos. 1-16 and opposite party Nos. 17-43 as defendants for declaration of title and partition of their shares in the land more fully described in the schedule to the plaint. Subsequently, same was transferred to the Joint District Judge, Second Court, Chittagong and renumbered as Other Suit No. 137 of 2001. Thereafter, the plaintiffs amended the plaint seeking relief for setting aside the final decree in previous partition suit and also for cancellation of auction purchase in the Decree Execution Case No. 18 of 1953. 

 4. That RS Khatian No. 2629/21 appertaining to RS plot No. 13119 and 13109 comprising an area of 0.10 + 0.06 = 0.16 acre were recorded in the names of Ahammad Khalil and Ahammad Kabir to the extent of 4 annas and 16 gandas each and the remaining 6 annas 8 gandas were recorded in the name of Hafizur Rahman, who by amicable settlement with other co-sharers lived in 0.6 acre homestead portion and same was recorded in his name. In this way plaintiff Nos. 1-16 inherited through their predecessor Aminulla 0.07 1/4 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/15, .04 from RS Khatian No. 2926/16, 0.34 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/17, 0.17 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/18 and 0.6 acre from RS Khatian No, 2926/21 totaling an area of 0.68 1/4 acre of land. The plaintiff Nos.1-16 have got their right, title interest and possession in the schedule properties. The defendant Nos. 3-16 are co-sharers of the disputed khatians for which they have been impleaded as defendants to avoid defect of parties. Since the names of other defendants are wrongly recorded in the BS khatian, they have also been impleaded in the suit. It was further stated in the plaint that the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, Md Abdul Monayem filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 in the Court of Fifth Munsif, Chittagong for Khas possession of 0.07 acre of homestead land of RS plot No. 13108 against three sons of Aminulla, Tazul Huda, Serajul Huq and Hedayetullah. They appeared in the said suit and filed joint written statement stating that they have no knowledge about Other Suit No. 39 of 1950. In that suit no notice was served upon the defendant and the decree was collusive, no auction sale was held in Decree Execution Case on 27-1-1954 and there was no commission report by the Advocate Commissioner and delivery of possession of the Property on 11-4-1957 through court. Ultimately the above suit was dismissed on compromise. In fact Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950, Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 are illegal, void, inoperative and without jurisdiction. The plaintiff tried to compromise the matter with the defendants through the arbitration of local Commissioner, but the defendants did not appear. Subsequently, the defendants with a view to harass the plaintiffs filed Non-GR No. 468 of 1986 under section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, Criminal Case No. 254 of 1990, and Panchlaish GR Case No. 33(8) of 1990 in local Police Station against the plaintiffs. The cause of action arose on 19-9-1991 when the defendants threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess them. Subsequently, by amending the plaint the plaintiff prayed for a declaration that the decree dated 31-7-1952 passed by the Fifth Munsif Court, Chittagong in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and auction sale held on 27-9-1954 in Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 are null and void, ineffective, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs and for partition. 

 5. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the said suit by filing joint written statement denying all the materials allegation made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in the present form, there is no cause of action and the suit is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the same is not maintainable without prayer for declaration of title and khas possession and further the suit is barred by waiver, Estoppel and acquiescence, the principle of res-judicata, defect of parties and also barred by limitation. The positive case of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are that the predecessor of the defendants are that, Abdul Monayem obtained the preliminary decree in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 on 31-7-1952 passed by the Munsif Fifth Court, Chittagong against Moulvi Aminulla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs in respect of the land described in the suit schedule alongwith other property. Accordingly, final decree was prepared on 5-3-1953 in which the decree-holder got saham of 0.342/7 acre in his share from RS plot No. 13104 and 13108. Thereafter in respect of cost of the suit he filed Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 in which he purchased 0.06 acre of land in auction sale from RS plot No. 13109 and took delivery of possession through court on 11-4-1957. Aminulla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was permitted to live in RS plot No. 13108 temporarily, but after his death his three sons Tazul Huda, Serajul Huq and Hedayetullah refused to surrendered possession to the predecessor of the defendants and for which he filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 in the Court of Fifth Munsif, Chittagong for eviction. Ultimately the suit was dismissed in terms of solenama on 16-8-1969. 

 6. The predecessor of the defendants, Abdul Monayem had recorded his name in appeal Case No. 2147 under section 19(2) of the EBSA and Tenancy Act vide order dated 11-6-1961 passed by the Appellate Officer after hearing the parties, wherein the predecessors of the present plaintiffs were parties and the appellate officer also observed that the present plaintiffs predecessors were found to be in possession of only 0.04 acre of homestead land in RS plot No. 13108. Schedule described RS plot No. 13105 comprises in all 0.33 acre of land from which defendant Nos. 1 and 2 purchased 0.04 acre of land by kabala No. 3129 registered on 5-6-1951 from Aminulla. After the death of CS recorded owner Abdul Bayesh his heirs and subsequent heirs of Halimunnessa, Khairul Islam, Safia Khatun, Nazu Mia, Mariam Khatun transferred by registered Kabala No. 3526 dated 20-10-1933 in favour of the predecessor of these defendants, Abdul Monayem, along with the land of some other khatians, in all 0.36 acre land described in the schedule of the plaint. The remaining lands of the schedule described RS plot No. 13105 have been purchased by three defendants by way of several deeds from other sharers on different dates. Under such circumstance the land of RS plot No. 13104 recorded exclusively in the name of Aminulla in Korfa title is not possible, so the record of RS khatian No. 2926 is wrong. The PS khatian have been recorded in the names of these defendants or in the name of their predecessors. BS record are also recorded in same manner in the names of these defendants and other sharers save and except RS plot No. 13109, which, in collusion with the survey employees, are recorded in their names, which is wrong and baseless. Practically, except the above mentioned 0.07 acre they were not in possession. 

 7. The plaintiffs have field the instant suit without paying required court fee on proper valuation of the suit land. These defendant along with other co-sharers are in possession of the suit land for more than 12 years by paying rents regularly, receiving rent-receipts. Hence they have got the absolute right, title, interest and possession over the suit land which the Plaintiffs have got no right to deny. The defendants have filed criminal case No. 523 of 1990 against the plaintiffs for theft of their fish from the pond of RS plot 13105 perhaps in turn of which they might have filed the present test suit which deserves to be dismissed. In fact the plaintiffs are well aware of the Final decree of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 and the auction sale which have been purchased by the predecessor of the defendants and all other deeds also. It is utter surprise to mentioned that where the plaintiffs have already admitted in their plaint about the sole decree dated 16-8-1969 passed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 how they can file the instant suit. Their predecessor-in-interest have specifically admitted the conditions save and except the possession of 0.07 acre of homestead land of RS plot No. 13108 they would never claim their previously sold out properties of all other khatians to the predecessor of the defendants. As per sole decree the predecessor of the defendants, Abdul Monayem had recorded his name correctly in BS khatian Nos. 693 and 695 which have finally been published in his name. After death, his heirs and subsequent heirs transferred 0.39 acre of land from BS plot Nos. 13252 and 13253 to Ashekane Awlia Abdul Monayem High School by registered Deed of Gift No. 7542 dated 1.6-12-1987 and delivered possession, which is within the schedule described in the plaint. Having been well aware of all these facts and circumstances, the plaintiffs intentionally did not make these defendants as parties to the suit. Now the defendants along with their transfers are, in fact, is in possession of their respective lands about which the plaintiffs are not at all entitled to claim any decree and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. The learned Joint District Judge upon consideration of materials evidence on record by his judgment dated 25-11-2008 decreed the suit. Against the said decree, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 16 of 2009 in the Court District Judge, Chittagong and in due course appeal was transferred to the Additional District Judge, First Court, Chittagong. In Title Appeal No. 16 of 2009 plaintiff filed an application on 13-6-2010 calling for the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 of Fifth Munsif Court, Chittagong and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 of the same court describing the papers and documents in the said application and same was rejected by the appellate court by order No. 17 dated 14-7-2010. Ultimately, the learned Additional District Judge after hearing the parties, dismissed the appeal by judgment and decree dated 9-9-2010 and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 12. During pendency of the revisional application before this court, the petitioner filed an application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 10-3-2013 for additional evidence stating the facts that the record of the Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 were called for in the present Other Class Suit No. 137 of 2001 and the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 was transmitted to the trial court but record of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 could not be transmitted as it was found missing at the relevant time. But due to bonafide Mistake of the learned Advocate for the defendants as well as the trial court the relevant order of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 was not exhibited. On the basis of such bonafide mistake, both the courts below erroneously found that the defendants did not take steps to prove the service of summons of Other Class Suit No. 39 of 1950 which was duly served upon the defendants. But on scrutinizing the order sheet of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950, it appears that the defendant No. 1 Aminulla, the predecessor of the present plaintiffs was appeared in that suit and filed written statement on 22-2-1951 (order No.8) It also transpired from the order sheet of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 that the defendant (present plaintiff) appeared in that title suit and filed written statement and ultimately the suit was decreed on compromise and accordingly compromise decree was drawn upon. It is pertinent to mentioned here that those documents were submitted by the plaintiffs in the appellate court but the appellate court below did not consider those documents as additional evidence. It was further stated that the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 are now before this hon'ble court and the petitioners on the advice of their learned Advocate collected certified copy of entire order sheet of Title Suit 53 of 1968 and written statement filed by defendants dated 10-3-1969. From those documents it will be crystal clear that summons were duly served upon the defendants in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 and they have contested the said suit by filing written statements in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 respectively. It is also stated that in paragraph No. 2 of the plaint of the present suit the plaintiffs admitted that they appeared and filed written statements in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968. Since the plaintiffs are admitting the facts of their appearance in the Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, which can be easily taken as additional evidence, as admitted facts need not be proved. 

 14. It is also denied that the decree holder Abdul Munayem gave 0.7 acre land to Aminullah for residing there temporary as licensee. It was further denied that Tajul Huda and his two brothers appeared and filed written statement on 10-3-1969 or on any other date in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 filed by Abdul Munayem. It is also denied that they filed a compromise petition on 7-8-1969 or any on other date and on the basis of said compromise petition suit was decreed. It was further stated that defendants had ample opportunities to exhibit the order sheet of Other Suit No. 39 of 1950 and both the courts below have given their findings on the decree passed in Other Suit No. 39 of 1950, the Execution Case arising there from and on Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 and hence the petitioners are not entitled to adduce additional evidence before the revisional court to patch up the weak part of their case which is not permissible under Order XII, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 15. Mr Khalilur Rahman with Mr Khalilur Rahman(Helal) and Mr Mohammad Zafar Ali Khan, the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the Defendant-petitioners. Mr Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the petitioners firstly, submits that the present suit was filed on 28-9-1991 challenging the decree passed in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, and the plaintiffs had knowledge about filing of earlier Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 which they have admitted in paragraph no. 2 of the plaint of the present suit. Since the present suit is filed long after 23 years from their knowledge, same is hopelessly barred by limitation. Secondly, Mr Khalil, submits that in respect of suit property, Abdul Munayem, father of the defendant nos. 1-2 filed Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 against the predecessors of the plaintiffs Aminullah who contested the said partition suit by filing written statement and ultimately preliminary and final decree was passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950. Thereafter, the predecessors of the defendant again filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Aminullah who appeared and contested the Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 by filing written statement on 10-3-1969 and the said suit was decreed on compromise on 7-8-1969. Thirdly, learned Advocate submits that the plaintiffs claimed title in the suit on the basis of korfa lease of their predecessors Aminullah and RS khatian was published in the name of their predecessor but they, failed to file any lease deed as such korfa lease and record of right does not create any title in the suit land. So, after passing of the final decree in a Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and compromise decree dated 7-8-1969 between the parties, and for the same self suit land, the present second suit is barred under the principles of res-judicata and not maintainable. Since the trail court failed to frame any issue in the present suit, whether the suit is barred by res-judicata and thus committed gross error of law in not dismissing the suit. Fourthly, the learned Advocate submits that the plaintiffs has miserably failed to prove that fraud was committed in the earlier suits being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 and also failed to prove that the summons were not duly served upon them in earlier suits. Fifthly, both the courts below failed to consider that most of the title deeds of the present defendants are 30 years old documents, but without considering this legal aspect of the suit, the courts below erroneously passed the decree declaring that those documents are forged documents. Sixthly, he submits that the plaintiff failed to established their title in the suit land, so they cannot challenge the title deeds of the defendants, who acquired title through the process of law. He lastly submits that both the courts below totally failed to consider the evidence, both oral and documentary and misread and non-considered the materials evidence on record and thus committed gross error of law in not dismissing the suit. Accordingly, the learned Advocate prayed that the rule should be made absolute. 

 17. On the other hand, Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Syed Mokaddas Ali, the learned Advocate submits that the suit is not barred by limitation because of the fact that the previous suit being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 filed by Abdul Munayam, predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of the present suit and the defendants Aminullah, predecessors of the present plaintiffs are not aware about the final decree passed in that suit. Since both the courts below concurrently found that no summons were served upon the defendants in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and the said decree was obtained by practicing fraud, then auction sale held in other Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 were not effective and thus the suit is not barred by limitation and same are not binding upon the plaintiffs. In support of his submission he referred two decisions reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167 and 19 DLR (SC) 433, He further submits that the lower appellate court concurred with the findings of the trial court that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land, thus the plaintiffs suit for declaration of title and partition is not barred by limitation. 

 He next submits that the defendants have failed to prove that the predecessor of the plaintiffs signed the solenama filed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 which was affirmed by the appellate court. Therefore, the present suit is not barred by the principles of res-judicata and waiver. He also submits that the trial court found that the RS record prepared in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs during the period from 1924 to 1930 in Chittagong region same has presumptive value and the defendants did not challenge the same in any court of law. The predecessors of the plaintiffs-Aminuddin being korfa lessee and his successors continued in possession for more than 12 years and on the basis of the RS khatian they acquired title in the suit land. In this respect he placed reliance two decisions reported in 16 DLR (SC) 287 and 54 DLR (AD) 173. He then submits that both the courts below concurrently found that the decree in the Other Suit No. 39 of 1950 was void and defendants did not try to prove by sufficient evidence that the solenama filed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 was actually executed by the three sons of Aminullah and therefore the defendants did not acquire any title by the said deeds, further the defendants did not appear in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 by filing written statement and compromise petition have been filed fraudulently by the plaintiffs of that suit. Since both the courts below concurrently found that the judgment and decree in the earlier partition suit are void, in-operative and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Therefore, the present partition suit filed by the plaintiffs is quite maintainable and it is not necessary to have a separate decree for cancellation of the registered two deeds of the defendants. He further submits that both the courts below in consideration of the evidence, found that the deeds through which the defendants claimed title did not confer any title or possession on the defendants and gave cogent reasons in support of their findings and the courts had jurisdiction to consider whether the deeds conferred title or possession on the defendants even though some of those were 30 years old documents and the genuineness of such documents may be challenged and there is no misreading or nonconsideration of the material evidence by the courts below and the defendants are not entitled to challenge those findings. In this connection he refers the decision reported in 17 BLD (AD) 199. He also submits that the trial court found that the defendants claimed that Abdus Sabur is the owner of land described in the first schedule to the plaint, and in that case the onus is upon the defendant to prove the claim of ownership of Abdus Sabur but they did not file any documents in support of the ownership of Abdus Sabur. DW 1 in his cross-examination admitted that he did not know about any deed showing title of Abdus Sabur. Moreover the document dated 19-6-1895 shows that in that deed ten gandas of land stating Moghi dags were mentioned. But in the written statement the corresponding CS and RS dags had not been mentioned. The defendants did not adduce any documentary or oral evidence to show that the land mentioned in the above deed dated 19-6-1895 and the lands described in the schedule to the plaint are the same land. He also submits that the RS khatian have got presumptive value relating to title in the Chittagong region and the RS record was prepared in Chittagong region from the years 1924 to 1930. After settlement with Aminulla, Abul Bashar and Ithairul Bashar have no title in the land settled with Aminulla. Since the korfa settlement was coupled with possession, the defendants are not entitled to challenge the settlement of Aminulla after 12 years from the time of preparation of RS khatian. He further submits that the defendants fails to prove that Aminulla the predecessor of the plaintiff are in permissive possession of some land was not prove either in the earlier suit or in the present suit. So, the auction was not effective and hence the defendants did not acquire any,title in the land allegedly sold in auction. He finally submits that the application regarding the additional evidence as provided under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure prescribed that the need for additional evidence must be felt by the court itself. This provision of law is clearly not intended to allow a litigant who has been unsuccessful in the lower court to fill up the omission. In this respect he referred to a decision reported in 36 DLR (AD) 220 and accordingly prayed for discharged of the Rule. 

 But the trial court miserably failed to appreciate and consider the order No.6 dated 22-1951 passed in Other Suit No. 39 of 1958 which, clearly proved that summons were duly served upon the defendants and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 prayed for one month time to file written statement and thereafter the defendants filed written statement and contested the suit. Thus it is evident that such finding of the trial court is apparently erroneous and not based on the material and evidence on record. 

 22. It also appears that the predecessor of the present defendant filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the present plaintiffs and in that title suit defendant appeared and filed written statement and said suit was decreed on compromise and accordingly compromise decree was drawn. To prove such facts the present defendants filed the application for compromise (Exhibit-Ja) and the sole decree (Exhibit-Ja(1) respectively, wherefrom it is evident that three sons of Aminulla executed the said solenama, but both the courts below failed to consider such vital aspect of the case and erroneously found that the defendants could not prove the said facts. It further transpires that the defendants filed an applications before the appellate court on 13-6-2010 for calling for the records of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, Title Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Execution Case No. 18 of 1953. The appellate court heard this application and rejected the same by order No. 17 dated 14-7-2010 on the ground that— “আপীলকারী বিবাদীপক্ষে আনীত দরখাস্তটি অনাবশ্যক বিধায় আপাতত না মঞ্জুর করা হইল, তবে অত্র মোকদ্দমার আপীল শুনানীঅন্তে উক্ত দরখাস্তের বিষয়বস্তু বিবেচনাযোগ্য। 

 23. But it transpires that at time of hearing of the appeal although the preliminary and final decree with Advocate Commissioner report (Exhibit- Ka and Kha) was considered but the compromise petition and decree passed in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 Exhibit Nos. Ja and Ja(1) were not considered but erroneously found that the appellants could not prove the those documents by sufficient evidence. Although the positive case of the defendants was that the predecessor of the plaintiffs was in permissive possession of the defendants and further that the compromise decree passed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 has been upheld. Since the appellate court failed to consider all those documents filed before the appellate court at the time of hearing of the appeal and when the appellate court rejected the application of the defendant observing that all those documents will be considered and dealt with at the time of hearing of the appeal. 

 24. It also appears that the defendants of the present suit claimed that the predecessors of the plaintiffs compromised the Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 by filing Solenama by which the plaintiffs admitted the right of the defendants-petitioners in the suit lands. Hence the plaintiffs had no cause of action in the present suit, which was denied by the plaintiffs. Normally, the onus of proof lies on the person who assert that the sole-decree had obtained by fraud. The onus of proving fraud was thus clearly on the plaintiffs and it was not the duty of the defendants to disprove the existence of fraud or collusion in anticipation of any case made out by the plaintiffs themselves. In this view of the matter, the courts below were totally wrong in taking view that the defendants failed to proved by calling of the records of earlier suit and erroneously found that summons were not duly served upon the predecessors of the plaintiffs in earlier two suits. 

 25. In this revision the defendant-petitioners have filed an application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure for additional evidence annexing certified copy of entire order sheets of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 and also written statement dated 10-3-1969 filed in the said suit by the defendants Tajul Huda and other, predecessors of the present plaintiffs, for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession filed by the predecessors of the present defendants, Abdul Munayam. 

 26. The learned Advocate for the defendants petitioners strenuously argued that the High Court Division conferred wide power in order to do justice in a case and it shows that in the instant case the appellate court failed to exhibits the aforesaid vital documents although the same was also filed before the appellate court but those documents were not considered at the time of hearing of the appeal. After consideration and appreciation of the materials and evidence on record it appears that the documents and papers filed by the defendants-petitioners are very much necessary for proper adjudication of the suit. It is, however, felt that ends of justice will be meet if both the parties should be given opportunity to prove their case by filing those documents in appellate court. In this connection reference is made to the case of Sunil Krishna Banki vs Kailash Chandra Saha reported in 36 DLR (AD) 220. Since the court below totally misread and non-considered the Exhibits namely, Exhibit Nos. Ka to Umo, Exhibit Nos. Ja and J(1) and also did not call for the record of the Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 which is very much material to consider that whether the present defendants, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 obtain any decree fraudulently against the predecessors of the present plaintiffs. The opposite parties has filed the present Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 137 of 2001 seeking, firstly prayed for declaration that both preliminary and the final decree passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and also the decree passed in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 are illegal collusive and fraudulent, Secondly, the BS khatian No. 693 and 695 are wrong and baseless and also for partition of total 0.90 acres land claiming entire 0.64 1/4 acres which was partitioned in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950. In that suit the predecessors of the defendant Nos. 1-2, Md Abdul Monayem was the plaintiff and predecessors of the present plaintiffs Aminullah was the defendant. 

 27. On going through the materials on record it is apparent that the heirs of the defendant of the earlier suit were all out to deprive the plaintiff of the said suit of the fruit of the decree and as last resort has filed the present Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 on 28-9-1991 after 41 years of the first suit and 23 years of the second suit seeking the relief primarily by way ul setting aside the decrees that were passed in those two suits under the shadow of the relief seeking separate saham in respect of the schedule land. It is seen from the materials on record and admitted by the plaintiffs of the present suit that the land which was the subject matter of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 has also been made subject matter of present Other Suit No, 92 of 1991. 

 28. It is not disputed from the side of the plaintiffs that relief sought for in Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 relates to seeking set aside the decree passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 but the courts below failed to frame any issue whether the decisions made in the former suits operates as res-judicata in the present suit. 

 30. It appears that in respect of the suit land preliminary and final decree was passed on 11-8-1953 in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and the defendants took possession of 34 2/7 acres of their saham on 20-6-1956 though court in Execution Case No. 18 of 1953. Thus after passing of the final decree in the said partition suit between the same parties, the second suit filed by the plaintiffs after 41 years is not maintainable and is barred by limitation. So, the decisions referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167 is not applicable in the present case. In the present suit, the plaintiffs have miserably failed to prove that the decree obtained fraudulently in the earlier suits being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the predecessors of the present plaintiffs and that the plaintiffs also failed to prove that the summons were not duly served upon them in earlier suits. Further, both the courts below failed to consider that most of the title deeds of the present defendants are 30 years old documents, but without considering this legal aspect of the suit, the courts below erroneously passed the decree declaring that those documents are forged documents. 

 31. I find that the lower appellate court has passed the impugned judgment without giving any specific finding in respect of those Exhibits. Since both the courts below failed to found that the defendants derived right, title and interest in the suit land on the basis of the decree passed in the earlier suits which seriously prejudiced the defendants. I have meticulously examined the oral and documentary evidence and relevant provisions of law and find that the court of appeal below failed to consider those materials evidence on record and committed error in law, in decreeing the suit. 

 33. Learned Advocate for the opposite party vehemently submits that since the predecessors of the plaintiff being a korfa lessee and continued in possession of the suit land and RS khatian was prepared in his name, so he acquired title in the suit land. This submission is absolutely fallacious in as much as the RS khatian are not document of title and that the khatians, if at all, record the possession and not title to the land. 

 36. In the suit plaintiffs based their claim as korfa lessee and RS record but they did not file any lessee deed to prove their claim and on the other hand defendant claimed their title on the basis of several deeds, starting from the year 1895, 1940, 1942. This is a well established principle of law that a registered kabala is an evidence of title which will prevail over the other records of rights as such until and unless such kabala is cancelled on specific allegation of fraud by any civil court in an appropriate civil suit. Reliance may be placed in case of Mr Sultanuddin. Chowdhury vs Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh reported in 32 DLR 252.

full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: Having aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 26-11-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Laxmipur in Title Appeal No. 21 of 1997 heard analogously with Title Appeal No. 50 of 1997 allowing the appeals thereby on reversing the judgment and decree dated 21-11-1996 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Laxmipur decreed Title Suit No. 56 of 1991. 

 4. It is the case of plaintiff that suit land comprising 29 decimals of land of dag No. 3246 of District settlement khatian No. 458 and No. 63 Nancha Nagar Mouzajoma of dag No. 21 originally belonged to Amzad Khalasi. Amzad Khalasi sold 10.5 decimals of land out of 29 decimals of land to Abul Hasim. Joynal Abedin purchased 7.5 decimals, Sabina Khatoon also purchased 4 decimals and 7.5 decimals of land purchased by Bazaler Rahman from Amzad Khalasi. The suit land having been recorded in 63 No. Bancha Nagar Mouza in khatian No. 909 in the name of Abul Hasim 4 annas share in the name of Joynal Abedin 2 annas share, in the name of Sabina Khatoon 4 annas share, 4 ann as share in the name of Bazaler Rahman correctly. In getting settlement, in khatian No. 909, the name of Sabina Khatoon has been wrongly recorded. Sabina Khatoon out of her share, sold 4 decimals of land by saf kabala dated 27th Falgun, 1339 B.S. corresponding to 11-3-1933 to Arafatunnessa. Abul Hasim sold his 6 annas share comprising 10.5 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman, Joynul Abedin in 4 annas share transferred 7.25 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman. In this way, Bazaler Rahman with his 4 annas share, purchased 10 annas share, in total purchased 14 annas share of 25 decimals of land, died leaving 3 sons, defendant No. 1-3. Arafatunnessa having owner of 4 decimals of land died leaving 2 sons, Abdul Aziz Patwari and Abdul Hasim Patwari and daughter, Anwara Begum. Abdul Aziz Patwari purchased 6 decimals of land from Bazaler Rahman by kabala dated 17-4-1944. In this way Abdul Aziz Patwari having owner of 7.5 decimals of land by purchase and by inheritance, died, leaving son, Sherajul Islam, 3 daughters, Parul Begum, Minara Begum, Shamsur Nahar and wife, Fatema Bibi. Fatema Bibi, Sherajul Islam and Shamsur Nahar jointly by saf kabala deed No. 12950 dated 29-11-1990 transferred 3 and 5/8 decimals of land to plaintiff Sherajul Islam and Shamsun Nahar sold 3 and 5/8 decimals of land by registered deed No. 1295 dated 29-11-1990 to plaintiff. At the time of death of Hossain Ahmed, he was survived by son, Shahab Uddin and daughter, Sabina Khatoon. On the death of Anwara Khatoon, her two sons, Shah Alam and Bachu Mea became owner of her property. Shahab Uddin, Shah Alam and Bachu Mea sold 3 decimals of land by baina, which was converted to registered document dated 20-4-1991. In this way plaintiff become owner by purchase and by inheritance of the scheduled land. After purchase, plaintiff went to pay rent to the local Tahsil Office on 15-2-1991 and came to know that out of suit land, during MRR survey, 29 decimals of land recorded in the name of his predecessor of No. 63 Bancha Nagar Mouza, Khatian No. 767, dag No. 8351. For total land of 29 decimals, plaintiff came to know that for aforesaid land in Mutation Case No. 111983-84 of the court of Assistant Commissioner (Revenue) the name of Bazaler Rahman was replaced and was recorded in the name of defendant Nos. 4-5 in holding No. 2405, khatian No.2404 and holding No. 2395 and khatian No. 2396. It is further case of plaintiffs that for the aforesaid wrong recording either in the name of Bazaler Rahman or in the name of defendant Nos. 3-4 or defendant No. 1-5, title, interest and possession of plaintiff has not been effected as the plaintiff purchased the suit land finding title of his predecessor and plaintiff could not know of the aforesaid wrong recording. The aforesaid wrong recording a cloud has been cast upon title of plaintiff which required to be removed, as such, plaintiff instituted the suit. For the cause of action of suit plaintiff has stated as :- 

 7.	The case of defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10 is that suit land consisting of 29 decimals recorded in PS khatian No. 909 and District Survey khatian No. 449 was demarcated as Abul Hasim in 6 anna, Joybul Abedin in 6 anna, Bazaler Rahman in 4 anna and Sabina Khatoon in 2 anna, with joma of Taka 2.25 which has been wrongly recorded in PS survey. JoynalAbedin in 4 annas share got 7.25 decimals of land and as plaintiff transferred his share to Bazaler Rahman and became titleless. Sabina Khatoon by registered kabala dated 27th Falgun, 1339 BS corresponding to 11-3-1933 transferred his share to Joynal Abedin and become titleless. Anjunnessa as mother of Bazaler Rahman, lived in joint mess and having satisfied with the nurse of Bazaler Rahman, transferred her entire purchased land i.e. 3 and 5/8 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman at first week of January, 1935 orally and become titleless. As aforesaid, Bazaler Rahman become owner of 10 annas share, consisting of 18 and 1/8 decimals of land. Thereafter for ejmali land, Bazaler Rahman and Abul Hasim amicably partitioned and registered deed was executed on 24th Badra 1344 BS and registered on 10- 5-1937. In that partition deed Bazaler Rahman was settled with 10 annas and Abul Hasim was settled by 6 annas of land. While defendant in possession, Abul Hasim on 27th Badra, 1348 BS corresponding to 13-9-1941 executed and registered saf kabala deed transferring 2 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman. While Abul Hasim was in possession on remaining 8 and 7/8 decimals of land, by saf kabala deed dated 23-1-1942, transferred the suit land to Jabed Ullah and become titleless. In that deed it was mentioned 10.5 decimals of land but in fact, Jabed Ullah got possession for 81/8 decimals of land. Jabed Ullah on 28-4-1944 by saf kabala deed, transferred the said land to Bazaler Rahman and became titleless. In this way, Bazaler Rahman became owner of entire 29 decimals of land. MRR khatain was prepared for the aforesaid land in the name of Bazaler Rahman and recorded in MRR khatian No. 767 correctly and was published accordingly. The entire claim regarding suit land of plaintiff against this fact is totally false and without any basis. Bazaler Rahman to the very knowledge of his brother, sister and of entire locality, possesses the said land i.e. 29 decimals for more than 12 years and his title became perfect. Bazaler Rahman died leaving 4 sons, defendant Nos. 1-3 and Sukku Mea who inherited his land. The case of plaintiff that Bazaler Rahman died leaving 3 sons is totally false each sons of Bazaler Rahman got 7.25 decimals of land. Subsequently, Nasir Ahmed, defendant No.3, sold 1 decimal ofland to Majibullah by safkabala dated 1-2-1960. Again, this Majibullah by kabala dated 23-10-1961 transferred 1 decimal of land to Ali Ahmed. Momin Ullah through his father, as heir, got 7.25 decimals of land, having title and possession, by saf kabala dated 22-6-1959 transferred 1 decimals of land to Ahmed Ali. Momin Ullah and Nasir Ahmed, defendant No.2 and 3 on 21-5-1960 by safkabala deed transferred 13 decimals of land to Ali Ahmed and delivered possession and also become titleless. Taher Ahmed and Chukku Mea, another two sons, through their father, Bazaler Rahman, inherited 14.5 decimals of land, which they sold to Lutfunnessa by registered saf kabala dated 27-8-1960 and became title less. Ahmed Ali being owner and possessor of his purchased land, by deed of gift dated 24-7-1967 transferred the said land to Lutfunnessa and became titleless. Although in that deed of gift, it is written 26 decimals of land but in fact Lutfunnessa got more land legally as got by donor, Ahmed Ali. In this way, Lutfunnessa become owner of 29 decimals of land. Lutfunnessa on 16-11-1972 by two saf kabala deeds, transferred entire 29 decimals of land to HasinaAkter and AKM Mohammad Ullah, defendant No.5, who mutated their names in Mutation Case No. 1/1983-84 and 2/1983-84 and separated joma and opened khatian No. 2395 and 2396. It may be mentioned, against the purchase of Hasina Akhter, AKM Mohammadullah, Oaziullah and Monir and other as co-sharer of adjacent land, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 1980 and 245 of 1974 for pre-emption and both the cases were dismissed on 1-7-1980. Hasina Akhter and AKM Mohammadullah possessed the said land for more than 12 years with the knowledge of all and perfected their title. AKM Mohammadullah, while in possession, having title of 14.5 decimals of land by kabala dated 9-6-1990 transferred the said land to defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10 by exchange and delivered possession. Ahmed Ali also exchanged 14.5 decimals of land on 9-6-1990 with defendant No. 10 and become titleless. Defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10 after getting the land as aforesaid, by Mutation Case No. 97/90-91, mutated their names, opened khatian and payed rents regularly till now. In the suit land plaintiffs have no right, title and interest. 

 8. The further case of these defendants is that basic deed of plaintiff dated 17-4-1944 and Bazaler Rahman are false, fabricated without any consideration and not acted upon, null and void. Bazaler Rahman did not transfer 6 decimals of land on 17-4-1944 but Abdul Aziz Patwari claimed plaintiff and Bazaler Rahman did not exe- cute and register the said deed. In the deed dated 17-4-1944 signature, left thump impression and place of execution of Bazaler Rahman are all false, fabricated and manufactured and left thump impression is a totally false one. Abdul Aziz Patwari never got possession of any land. The deed dated 17-4-1944 was executed on false personaion in place of Bazaler Rahman. Bazaler Rahman if transferred 6 decimals of land to Abdul Aziz Patwari then in MRR survey along with Bazaler Rahman, name of his brother, Abdul Aziz Patwari ought to be recorded. The deed dated 17- 4-1944 was never acted upon. The entire statement regarding transfer of land from Bazaler Rahman and Abdul Aziz Patwari made in the plaint are totally false. Plaint case that Abdul Aziz Patwari got possession of 7.5 decimals ofland and Abdul Aziz Patwari died leaving son, Sirajul Islam and 3 daughters, Parul Begum, Minara Begum and Shamsunnahar as made in the plaint are entire false and those persons are imaginary and false person and they never was in possession of the suit land. Abdul Aziz Patwari was a title less and possessionless person and on this point plaintiff did not inherit anything and his heirs have no possession or title and purchase of the land by plaintiff by deed dated 29-11-1990 for 29 decimals of land do not confer any title as Abdul Aziz Patwari was titleless. Fatema Begum and Sirajul Islam did not have any right, title, interest and possession of purchase land and deed dated 29- 11-1990 is false, fabricated, not acted upon, with- out consideration and was manufactured for the purpose of the suit. Bazaler Rahman was titleless and, as such, from Arafatunnessa, Abdul Aziz Patwari and Hasina Akhter, daughter of Anwara Khatun did not get or inherit any land of Arafatunnessa, Entire plaint case is false and plaintiffs have no possession over the suit land. Defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10 after getting suit land as aforesaid and also on adjacent to the suit land constructed some pucca constructions, the suit having filed on false avertments is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 9. This defendant in their additional written statement make out case that defendant Nos. 11- 12 are totally title less persons and plaintiffs purchased the said land from some title less and possessionless persons as such the statement of plaintiffs are totally false. 

 11. The case of defendant-petitioner Nos.11-12 is that, Amzad Khalasi was the original owner of the suit land having right, and title. Arafatunnessa by saf kabala dated 25-12-1926 purchased 4 decimals of land from Amzad Khalasi. Amzad Khalasi having title and khas possession for remaining 25 decimals of land, died leaving son, Abul Hasim and 4 daughters, Solema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon, Chaiera Khatoon and Fatema Khatoon, sold 2 decimals ofland to Jabed Ullah by saf kabala dated 27-6-1932. Abul Hashem, son of, Amzad Khalasi, died leaving son, Abul Hashem, who inherited the property of Abul Hashem, sold 10.5 decimals of land to Jabed Ullah by kabala dated 23-1-1942. Bazaler Rahman purchased the said land from Jabed Ullah by saf kabala dated 28-4-1944. Bazaler Rahman by purchase and after the death of Arfatunnessa, as heir, become owner of the land left by Arfatunnessa and Jabed Ullah.Bazaler Rahman died leaving sons, Taher Ahmed alias Jalal Ahmed, Momin Ullah alias Chaku Miah, who inherited the property of Bazaler Rahman. Ali Ahmed purchased I decimal of land from Momin Ullah by kabala dated 26-2-1951. Ali Ahmed also purchased 1 decimal of land from added defendant No. 11; Kulsum Begum purchased 1 decimal of land from Ahmed Ali by kabala dated 6-7-1967. After purchase Kulsum Begum constructed tin shed house and also semi pucca house on the south-west corner of dag and possessing the same. Over the said 1 decimal of land, excepting defendant No. 11, no one has any title or possession. Defendant No. 11 on behalf of plaintiff and defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 and 12 looked after the property. Momin Ullah and Nasir Ahmed, son of Bazaler Rahman, after the death of Bazaler Rahman, having title over the property, by kabala dated 27-8-1960 sold some land to Ahmed Ali. Md. Ali Ahmed by deed of gift dated 24-5-1967 gifted the said land to his wife, Lutfunnessa. Anar Ullah purchased 3 decimals of land from Sayera Khatun, daughter of Amzad Khalasi, dated 9th Jaistha, 1375 BS. Against that deed, Ali Ahmed filed Miscellaneous Case No. 128 of 1969 in the court of Munsif, 1st Court, Laxmipur for pre- emption. While pre-emption case was in progress, Ali Ahmed died, leaving wife, Lutfunnessa and son, Nur Alam and daughter, Rahima Khatoon, who was substituted in his place, pre-emption case was dismissed on 4-7-1970 on compromise. Nur Alam and Nasima Begum having been owner and having khas possession of the suit land, by kabala deed No. 4556 dated 14-3-1987 transferred the property to plaintiff-petitioner. Defendant No. 12 after becoming owner on exchange, constructed two storied tin shed house, bamboo house and also constructed pucca house and since then, enjoying the land. The said 3 decimals of land which defendant No. 12 got by exchange is only living place of defendant No. 12. Defendant No. 12 has no other place to live. Defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 did not acquire any title or possession over the suit land. This defendant open holding No. 36 2(Kha) and regularly paying Municipal taxes. In some portion of the land of this defendant plaintiffs have no possession. The case of defendant No.8, 9 and 10 are totally false and they have no construction on the suit land and that in part of land of defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 there is caretaker and not acted upon and on the basis of deeds, defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 was never in possession. Defendant No. 9 as plaintiff filed Petition Case No. 409 of 1991 in the court of Upazilla Magistrate wherein an enquiry was held by the Upazilla Magistrate who found structures and possession of defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10. Defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 thereafter filed preemption case was which dismissed on 18-5-1992. Defendant No. 8 was the witness of the case. Plaintiff having not been made any prayer for partition, the suit is liable to be dismissed. If the plaintiff's case for partition is to be decreed, then these defendants are entitled for saham for (1+3) = 4 decimals of land and excepting this land, if plaintiffs' suit be decreed, then these defendants have no objection, with these avertments, defendants prayed for disposal of the suit. 

 13. Learned Assistant Judge while dismissing the suit holding inter alia that gift in favour of Bazaler Rahman by his mother Arafatunnessa in 1935 with deliver of possession has been proved by exhibits 2 (Chha) and admitted by defendant Nos. 8-10 and plaintiff; plaintiff also proved that Bazaler Rahman is the owner of 26.5 decimals of land which is also admitted; on consideration of exhibit (Ga) learned Judge found that there was mutual settlement about the land between Bazaler Rahman and Abul Hasim by partition deed dated 10-5-1937, where it was amicably settled that Bazaler Rahman will got 10 annas, Abul Hasim will get 6 annas which is also an admitted position; by registered kabala dated 28-4-1944 exhibit (Ga) to (Ga) 15, Bazaler Rahman purchased 6 annas share from Abul Hasim. Learned Judge also considered the deposition of PW 2, Ali Ahmed and held that it is admitted position that Bazaler Rahman become 16 annas title holder of suit khatian. Learned Judge also considered that at the time of MRR survey the other daughters and sons of Arafatunnessa were alive but they did not raise any objection against 16 annas ownership of the suit land in favour of Bazaler Rahman. Defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10, it is found by the learned Judge that by document, proved oral gift in favour of Bazaler Rahman which has been supported by exhibits 2(Cha) to 2(Jha) to Neo that plaintiffs purchased suit land from the successive heirs of Arafatunnessa. Thereafter, learned Judge discussed oral evidence of the witnesses and found that DWs 2, 3 and 4 proved Bazaler Rahman had 4 other brothers and one sister and also learned Judge considered the deposition of PWs 1 and 2 who admitted that the name of husband of Arafatunnessa and father of Bazaler Rahman was Ayub Ali, which is the case of defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10. Defendant No.9 as sharer, title holder, by exhibit 2 Chha, sold 6 decimals of land, which plaintiffs purchased from Anwara Khatun. Defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 claimed this deed as false, fabricated and not-binding upon, and in their depositions and written statements demand from plaintiffs to produce original deed but plaintiff did not produced and plaintiff did not give any explanation either orally or in the plaint as to why they did not produce this deed in evidence. Plaintiff also did not produce the deeds dated 7-6-1944 and 9-6-1944 in its original and it is also found by the learned Judge that by the deed dated 7-6-1944, and 9-6-1944, the predecessor of plaintiff exhausted his title of the exchange land and thereby from purchase from Anwara Khatun plaintiff did not acquire any title. Learned Judge also considered the depositions of the witnesses and found that neither PW 1 nor PWs 2 and 3 in their earlier depositions did properly describe the scheduled land and also found that PW 3 is the neighbor of the suit property. Learned Judge found witnesses of defendant Nos. 8-10 reliable. Learned Judge also found plaintiffs did not prove the PS khatian which was prepared wrongly and not created which has presumptive value. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff did not prove title of i.e. 4 sons and daughter of Amjad Khalasi and by deed plaintiff admitted PS Jorip. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff did not prove MRR khatian as wrongly recorded. Learned Judge also considered that plaintiff raised objection against Mutation Case and separated joma as a whole on 27-7-1983 but failed to prove that said recording was wrong and illegal and PW 1 did not state anything about their said mutation and separation of joma. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff although demanded but did not pay advelorem court fees as such the suit is not maintainable as per Order VII, rule 11 (c) read with section 149C of the Code of Civil Procedure. Learned Judge on consideration of depositions of witnesses ultimately held as:- 

 14. Plaintiff and Abdul Barek alias Manik Mea filed Title Appeal Nos. SO of 1997 and 21 of 1997. Both these appeals were heard analogously by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Laxmipur who by judgment and decree allowed both the appeals and decreed the suit. Learned Judge in the body of the judgment found that it is admitted fact that 29 decimals of land of District Survey Khatian No. 458, plot No. 3246 originally belonged to Amzad Khalasi. Learned Judge on consideration of exhibit 2-2(Ka) decided the share of Sabina Khatoon at 4 decimals of land. Learned Judge thereafter considered the case of defendant Nos. 8-10 that they claimed that Arfatunnessa orally gifted her 4 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman but that oral gift was not at all proved. Learned Judge in support of such findings held that, principle of law that to prove gift, 3 essential ingredients must be proved, i.e. (i) there must have a declaration, (ii). acceptance of said declaration or offer and (iii) delivery of possession. It is settled principle of law that without delivery of possession no gift has been proved. Learned Judge found gift was executed in 1935 and Bazaler Rahman sold it by exhibit 2 Cha in 1944 but Bazaler Rahman did not make any respectful ground in exhibit 2 Cha that he got suit land by oral gift. Learned Judge also considered that bantaknama dated 10-5-1937 also did not mention in the recital of oral gift. Learned Judge considered that learned Judge of trial court committed gross illegality in not considering certified copy, exhibit 2 Cha dated 17-4-1944, in absence of original or in absence any explanation is in admissible, reversing that such finding of trial court as perverse as plaintiff stated that the said deed is aged about 50 years and the validity of said deed has not been challenged by Bazaler Rahman or his heirs as such at present, the validity of the deed cannot be questioned. Learned Assistant Judge took exhibit 2 Chha as illegal and on consideration exhibit 2 Cha dated 17-4-1944 learned Judge of the appellate court found that Abdul Aziz got 6 decimals of land and plaintiff purchased said 6 decimals of land from the heirs of Abdul Aziz, which plaintiff clearly proved and also proved possession of the plaintiff. Learned Judge also considered that defendant Nos. 8-10 claimed that Arafatunnessa had two other sons which had not been proved. Learned Judge thereafter found all the witnesses of plaintiff reside in and around of the suit land and witnesses of defendants are not adjacent to the suit land and people of suit property. Learned Judge also considered that Anwara Khatoon, daughter of Arafatunnessa, got 1 decimals of land through pre-emption case No. 147 of 1963 which was allowed on 8-6-1963, exhibit Chao. On these findings learned Judge found title of plaintiff and decreed the suit. 

 16. Mr AKM Nazrul Islam, learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant, submits that, the defendant-respondent-petitioners are owner of the suit land measuring 14.5 decimals of land on the basis of deed of exchange from the rightful owners and they also claim separate saham in the suit land, since in a suit for partition the defendant having status of plaintiff and the plaintiff having  status of defendant vice versa and accordingly, when the trial court dismissed the suit, the appellate court cannot decree the suit for partition without ascertaining the respective share of the parties, the judgment and decree passed in the appeal is highly erroneous and bad in law and it is an error apparent on the face of the record occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is liable to be set aside. Learned Advocate further submits that trial court found the plaintiff is out of possession of the suit property and also found that on the basis of the purchase he cannot get any share in the suit land measuring 10 decimals without any prayer for recovery of possession and partition without payment of advelorem court-fees is not maintainable and referred to the decision reported in 16 DLR 195 and the appellate court without ascertaining the share of the respective parties cannot pass the decree for partition and before realization of the advelorem court fees, the impugned decree is void ab-initio and, as such, cannot be given effect. Learned Advocate further submits that the appellate court hopelessly failed to consider genealogy of the transfer of the documents and illegally held that plaintiffs claim for partition is legal without ascertaining the title and possession of the plaintiff and in view of the fact that the trial court held that plaintiff has no title and possession and the suit is not maintainable without any prayer for khas possession on payment of advelorem court fees and, as such, the appellate court has not legally set aside the finding of facts arrived by the trial court. 

 17. Mr. Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate, appeared for the opposite parties on both the rules, on the other hand, submits that, Abdul Aziz had one son, Serajul Islam and three daughters, Parul Begum, Minara Begum and Shamsunnahar and wife, Fatema Bibi and Amzad Khalasi had one son Abdul Haque, 4 daughters, Halima Khhatoon, Solema Khatoon, Chaiera Khatoon and wife, Fatema Khatoon who by exhibit 2 Kha dated 14-7-1930 transferred 14 decimals of land to Jabed Ullah. Abdul Huq, his son, sold 10 decimals of land to Jabed Ullah. The learned Judge of appellate court considered exhibit 2 (Kha) to 2 (Chha) and thereafter, passed judgment rightly and legally. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant Bazaler Rahman did not have 4 brothers and one sister and it is the case of plaintiff that Bazaler Rahman had 3 brothers and one sister which the learned Judge of appellate court having found, defendant could not prove, that Bazaler Rahman had 4 brothers legally justified in allowing appeal. Learned Advocate further submits that court of appeal below rightly held that exhibit 2 Chha, a basic deed dated 17-4-1944 is of certified copy but this deed being 30 years old has a legal foundation which confer title over the suit property: Plaintiff in order to prove their title produced in court certified copy of the deed dated 7-6-1944 and 9-6-1944 and this being deed for more than 30 years old has presumptive value. Learned Advocate further submits that appellate court in fact did not feel it necessary to find as to whether Bazaler Rahman had 4 brothers or 3 brothers as it is not necessary for deciding the suit. 

 18. On the submissions of the learned Advocates and on consideration of the plaint case with amendment, and case make out in written statements, depositions of the witnesses and exhibits filed by the parties, four questions calls for determination as (i) whether Arafatunnessa gifted 2 anna share orally to Bazaler Rahman in exclusion of other sharers legally, (ii)" whether exhibit 2 Cha to 2 Chha, deed dated 17-4-1944 and 9-6-1944 in absence of original deed can be said to be good deed of title and (iii) whether Bazaler Rahman had 4 brothers and one sister or 3 brothers and one sister (iv).whether the suit can be maintainable in absence of payment of advelorem court fee after demanded by court. 

 19. Mr. Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate relied on the case of Abani Mohan Saha vs Assistant Custodian (SDO) Vested Property, Chand pur; 39 DLR (AD) 223 where it is held by the Appellate Division that "The plaintiff is claiming his title to the suit land on the basis of a deed of gift. I have got no doubt in my mind that the initial onus was on him to prove his title. The observation made in 32 DLR (AD) 29 would be of no avail to the appellant, as he failed to discharge his initial onus by proving his document of title. Had he succeeded to do so then the onus would have shifted on the enemy property authority to prove that the executants of the plaintiff's document, the sons of Surendra Mohan Saha, were residing in the enemy country at the relevant time," That means plaintiff is to prove his case. 

 22. The authority opined that if gift is made to the donee who is not living with the donor or if the subject matter of the gift is in possession of a third party then delivery of possession is a must to be given in presence of witnesses. If it is challenged then it required to be proved as per law. But if gift is made in favour of donor's wife, or husband or daughter or son or ward who reside in the same house, such delivery of possession is not required, only evidence of the donor and donee is enough. Defendant's case is that Arafatunnessa orally gifted her entire share to Bazaler Rahman who is son as formal proof of delivery of possession is enough. In Gift propositor can exclude any one but in will or osiyatnama propositors has limitation. In gift donor could divest his entire property which immune from challenge. Court of appeal below did not consider the relationship in between donor and donee. It is admitted fact that Arafatunnessa lived with Bazaler Rahman in the same house in the same mess as such onus shifted upon the plaintiff, it also lies on plaintiff, to prove it otherwise but plaintiff did not adduce any such evidence. So, first question decided against plaintiff. 

 23. Now to the second point i.e. producing of certified copy of the title deeds by the plaintiff, exhibits 2 Cha to 2 Chha. Defendants challenge these deeds as false, fabricated, illegal and not acted upon. Section 65 of the Evidence Act permit to produce certified copy but for that, an explanation is required, certified copy is not photo copy. When the documents have been challenged as false, forged and fabricated, then, it is incumbent upon the plaintiff to produce the original. Naturally, when original document is lost, there is other method to prove it. Original is required to produce to find whether the signature and left thump impression appeared there in is of the person who executed the same. In certified copy, signature or left thump impression of the executants do not appear. In photo copy it does. Defendants in their written statement as well as in their depositions challenge the basic documents of title of plaintiff as false and for non production of originals but the plaintiffs goes to show the apprehension of defendants in respect of falsity of claim of the plaintiff on false document is true, legal and genuine. 

 27. On the question of possession, it appears that trial court on consideration of a number of exhibits, held that plaintiff purchased the suit land from Ali Ahmed and Lutfunnessa but it appears that by this exhibit Ga series, title of Lutfunnessa has been extinguished, as such by purchase from titleless person plaintiff did not drive any title. On the question of possession the finding of trial court has not properly reversed by the appellate court but in cursory manner which is not lawful as such finding of the trial court stand. 

 31. The judgment and decree complained is set aside. Title Suit No. 56 of 1991 is dismissed.
