full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J : Erstwhile Dhaka Improvement Trust, shortly DIT, now Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha, shortly RAJUK, allotted plot No.CWN(B)34, New plot No.113 of the lay out plan of Gulshan Residential Model Town, the quantum of land is more or less 1(one) bigha, 1 (one) katha, 14(fourteen) chattaks, on 21-3-1962 to Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza. To grab this land through legal process 3(three) suits have been filed, first of which is Title Suit No.51 of 2004 was filed by MA Hashem on 8-2-2004 for Specific Performance of a Contract against Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza second one, Title Suit No.176 of 2004 was filed by a person claiming to be Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza for a direction upon RAJUK to issue sale permission and third one, Title Suit No.81 of 2006 was filed by the plaintiffs claimed to be the heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar for declaration that their father was the real allottee and for permanent injunction. Although aforesaid three suits are for three different distinct reliefs but the parties allowed disposing of the suits on the basis of oral evidence on adaptation but on different exhibits. 

 4. At first let me proceed with Title Suit No.51 of 2004 filed by MA Hashem for Specific Performance of Contract. 

 5. In the cause title of the plaint the defendants are Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of House No.11, Line No.6, Section 6/A, Mirpur, Dhaka and 3 others i.e. Md. Akhtaruzzaman, Director, Eastern Housing Limited as principal defendants and Chairman, Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha, RAJUK Bhaban, Dhaka and the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka as proforma-defendants. The suit is valued at Tk. 1,65,00,000 and it is stated in the plaint that schedule property was allotted by erstwhile DIT in favour of defendant No.1 vide allotment letter No.DIT/ Gulshan/2409 dated 2-3-1962 and it was registered between DIT and the principal defendant No. 1 vide lease deed No. 7198 dated 1-8-1962 and possession was handed over to the principal defendant No. 1 who duly mutated in respect of the suit land his name and has paid rents and taxes regularly to the government and having right, title, interest and possession, constructed some temporary structures in the schedule property and while principal-defendant No. 1 was in possession having right, title, interest thereto entered into agreement with the plaintiff on 29-12-2002 for sale of the scheduled property for a total consideration of Tk. 1,65,00,000 and a deed of agreement for sale was signed and executed on 29-12-2002 by principal defendant No.1 upon receipt of advance amount of Tk. 35,00,000 in cash, handed over all in original documents to the plaintiff in presence of witnesses. It was stipulated in the agreement that seller shall apply for obtaining all necessary permission, clearance certificate from RAJUK and other relevant authorities for sale of the land in favour of the plaintiff and plaintiff will be responsible for payment of transfer fee to RAJUK, gain tax, stamp duty, registration fee and all other charges and incidental costs and expenses and the execution and registration of the sale deed by the principal defendant No. 1 in favour of the plaintiff shall be completed within one year and the balance amount of Tk. 1,30,00,000 will be received by the principal defendant No. 1 from the plaintiff at the time of registration of the sale deed and that upon failure of the principal defendant No. 1 to execute and register the deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff, plaintiff shall be entitled to get the sale deed executed and registered through Court. Plaintiff informed RAJUK by letter dated 6-1-2003 about transfer of the schedule property by the principal defendant No.1 in favour of plaintiff on the basis of the said deed of agreement. Plaintiff by letter dated 1-8-2003, received by principal defendant No. 1 on 3-8-2003 requested him to take immediate steps i.e. permission from RAJUK for registering the deed of sale in his favour. After letter dated 1-8-2003 of the plaintiff, principal defendant No. 1 informed the plaintiff by letter dated 11-8-2003 that he having been suffering from physical and mental difficulties he could not take appropriate steps for registration of the sale deed and requested plaintiff No. 1 for further payment of Tk. 5,00,000 towards consideration, money on assurance that he will take appropriate steps immediately for executing and registering sale deed and shall also inform the plaintiff very soon thereabout. On 12-8-2003 plaintiff paid Tk. 3,30,000 to principal defendant No. 1 vide cheque. Cheque was given through a covering letter dated 12-8-2003 wherein request was made by the plaintiff to the principal defendant No.1 to take all necessary steps immediately, so that he can register the deed of sale in favour of plaintiff within the time schedule i.e. by 28-12-2003 and further requested defendant No. 1 to inform the plaintiff about the steps taken by principal defendant No.1. But up to 1-12-2003 principal defendant No. 1 failed to inform plaintiff about any development regarding executing and registration of the deed sale. Plaintiff always been ready and willing to perform his part of the obligations under the deed of agreement and there being only 27 days left of the time limit for registration the deed of sale as per agreement and out of consideration money defendant has received Tk. 38,20,000, plaintiff thus constrained to issue a notice on 1-12-2003 through his lawyer upon the principal defendant No. 1 requesting him to complete all formalities for registration of the deed of sale within 20-12-2003. It has been mentioned in the plaint that on 9-12-2003 plaintiff was shocked and surprised to learned from a biggopty (notification) published in the Daily Janakantha on 18-11-2003 which runs as follows:— 

 8. It has further been stated in the plaint that plaintiff could manage to look into the records of RAJUK and found that his application dated 6-1-2003 was in the file and also further learnt that some sort of plan has been approved by RAJUK for construction on the schedule property but the plaintiff could not collect the exact name and address of the person in whose favour or upon whose request the alleged plan was approved by RAJUK. Plaintiff went to the suit property on 22-12-2003 and found that some people were taking steps for construction upon removal of the old structures and upon query, he learnt that they are the employees and workers of the principal defendant No.2 who was claimed by them to be the owner of the land and plaintiff was further surprised and puzzled. Since the principal defendant No.1 failed to execute and register the deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff by 28-12-2003 and plaintiff lastly on 29-12-2003 after offering the balance amount in presence of the witnesses requested the principal defendant No.1 to execute and register the sale deed but principal defendant No.1 refused to do so. Hence the suit filed on 8-2-2004. 

 g) Any other or further order or orders, relief or reliefs the plaintiff may be entitled to get in law, equity and justice. 

 14. In the written statement defendants totally denied the plaint case. It is their case that disputed property was allotted to their father, deceased Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza who was BSc Engineer, originally residing at India and after creation of Pakistan, came to Dhaka and purchased six kathas of land at 157, Bara Mogbazar and constructed 3-storied building where he reside till his death. According to him PW 1 produced the bainapatra in original and other documents which are following: exhibits-1 is the allotment letter of DIT dated 21-3-1962, Exhibit-2 is the standard lease agreement of DIT dated 01-8-1962, Exhibit-3 is the 1st installment receipt of National Bank dated 26-3-1962, Exhibit-4 is the 2nd installment receipt of National Bank, dated 15-5-1963, Exhibit-5 is the 3rd installment receipt of National Bank dated 15-5-1964, Exhibit-6 is the deed of agreement dated 29-12-2002 by defendant No. 1 for sale in favour of plaintiff and 6/1 is the signature of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, Exhibit-7 is the letter dated 06-1-2003 and 7/1 is the signature of MA Hashem, Exhibit-8 is the letter dated 01-8-2003, exhibit 9 is the letter dated 11-8-2003 Exhibit-10 is the letter dated 12-8-2003, Exhibit-11 notice dated 03-12-2003, Exhibit-12 notice dated 18-11-2003, Exhibit-13 is the protest notice dated 15-12-2003 and exhibit 14 is the paper cutting regarding corrigendum dated 11-12-2003. He referring the deposition of PW 1 and exhibit 6 the bainapatra dated 29-12-2002 submits that it is the original one and the signature of the executant is proved by PW 1 as executants signed in presence of him. Further submits that PW 2 and 3 as attesting witnesses of bainapatra they also proved the signature of the executants. PW 2 and 3 also proved the payment of consideration supporting the case of PW 1. He fortify his submissions in respect of execution of bainapatra and passing the consideration saying all the PWs supported the case of plaintiff in accordance with law. Therefore, he lastly submits that the order of dismissal of the suit is not sustainable in law. 

 91. Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos.1 (a) to I (e) submits that defendant Nos. 1(a) to 1(e) contested the suit as the heirs of late engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza not as the heirs of defendant No. 1 Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur. He further submits that from a plain reading of the plaint and evidence of PW 1 it is manifest that the plaintiff entered into a contract with the Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur who is a fake person and no nexus with the suit property and engineer Md. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza who permanently had been residing in 157 Bara Moghbazar, was a executive engineer of C&B department. Later he was a director of BDC of Islam Group and never resides in Mirpur. So, there is no question of an agreement to sell the suit property to MA Hashem the plaintiff because earlier father of defendant Nos.1 (a) to I (e) Engineer Md. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza made an agreement with Eastern Housing Limited for construction of Multistoried Commercial Building and executed a registered power of attorney in favour of Eastern Housing LiMited. The possession of the suit property was handed over to the Eastern Housing Limited who approved the plan from Rajuk for construction of multi-storied commercial building and work of construction is going on. He further submits that all the papers and documents submitted by the plaintiff are forged and fabricated. Referring the evidence of PW 1 he submits that deposition of PW No. 1 is not only contrary to the facts and circumstances of the case, however, also beyond his pleadings. He further submits that the plaintiff must succeed to prove his own case. He further adds that in a suit for specific performance of a contract plaintiff must proved the genuineness of contract, payment of consideration, handing over of the original title deeds to the purchaser and possession of the suit property if handed over. Further to file the suit there must be either denial of facts or refusal of registration of title deed by the vendor although plaintiff was ready to perform his part and offered the rest consideration money. According to him in this suit by adducing evidences as stated herein above nothing were proved. He lastly submitted that when the father of the defendant Nos.1 (a) I (e) asserted the right, title and possession of the suit property by giving notice in the daily papers by stating some facts and denied the claim of other, the stating some facts and denied the claim of other, the plaintiff, firstly, denied his claim by publishing protest notice in papers. After the death of their father while defendant Nos.1 (a) to I (e) sought for addition of party firstly, opposed by plaintiff but unsuccessfully tried to make out a third case and attempt to prove that third parties are none but the heirs of the defendant No. 1 Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur who is his vendor. 

 93. In the title suit No.51 of 2004 at the time of filing of the suit plaintiff impleaded defendant No.1 Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur as his vendor and Md. Akhteruzzaman, Director of Eastern Housing Ltd as defendant No.2 as principal of Engineer Md. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza. Plaintiff in his plaint stated that defendant No.1 Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur made an agreement with him to sell the suit plot and took the part payment of 35,00,000 in cash on 29-12-2002 as consideration out of total consideration Tk. 1,65,00,000 and on 12-8-2003 Tk 3,20,000 cash vide cheque No.1279703 of AB Bank Limited, Principal Branch, Dhaka. But plaintiff in plaint admitted that before filing of the suit one Engineer Md. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza published a notice on 18-11-2003 stating as follows: 

 96. From the above pleadings of the plaintiff it is manifest that Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur and Engineer Md. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Gulshan is not the same person and dispute regarding the title of the suit property started before expiry of the Engineer Md. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza who died on 2-2-2004. The plaintiff filed the suit on 8-2-2004 impleading defendant No. 2 Mr. Aktheruzzaman as director of Eastern Housing limited as the attorney of the late Engineer Md. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza wherein the defendant No. 1 is the vendor of plaintiff. So, from the plaint it is crystal clear that Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza defendant No. 1 and Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza the Principal of Eastern Housing Limited is not same and one person. 

 97. Now, if I look into the order sheet of the case record. It appears that after filing the suit on 10-2-2004, 22-2-2004, 18-3-2004 plaintiff took the steps in the suit. On 20-3-2004 in the suit third party by an application under Order I Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure prayed for not substituting the defendant No.1 but for adding as defendants in the suit as the heirs of Engineer Md. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza because of fact that he died on 02-2-2004 and they got the information that instant title suit has been filed by the plaintiff on the basis of the false bainapatra created by him with fictitious person and filed the instant false suit for specific performance of contract having Rio title, interest and possession over the suit property. However, pending aforementioned application of third party plaintiff on 23-3-2004 by filing a fresh Vokalatnama prayed for hearing of the application dated 18-3-2004, upon hearing the application for temporary injunction the Court below issued the show cause notice upon the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why an order of temporary injunction should not be granted. On 27-5-2004 defendant Nos. 1-2 filed hajira. Plaintiff prayed for time, defendant No. 2 by an application under Order-III Rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure prayed for direction upon defendant No. 1 for his personal appearance before the Court. Then the Court below without passing any order regarding personal appearance of the defendant No. 1 on 15-7-2004 allowed the application for added party not as the 3rd party but as the heirs of defendant No. 1. Whereas on that application it has been stated that they are the heirs of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza not the heirs of defendant No. 1 Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur. So, from the record and conduct of the plaintiff it is crystal clear that the defendant No.1 Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur and Engineer Md. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Bara Moghbazar is not the same and one person. 

 99. From the above deposition it is further manifest that though plaintiff at the time of filing and sometime after filing of the suit did not admit rather clearly denied existence, right, title and possession of Engineer Md. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar and at the time of his deposition stated that “ইহা সত্য নহে যে মগবাজার নিবাসী শামসুল কবীর হুমায়ুন রেজা অনুমোদিত প্লান মতে ইমারত নির্মান করিয়া ভাড়াটিয়ার মাধ্যমে ভোগদখল করিতেন। but later only to escape and justify his earlier false activities admitted with a device that defendant Nos. 1 (a) to 1(e) are the legal heirs of defendant No. 1 i.e. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur by substituting but from the above testimony of PW 1 it is manifest that defendant No.1 Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and the father of the defendant Nos. 1(a) to I (e) is not the same and one person. 

 101. From the above mention deposition and cross examination it is crystal clear that PW1 in his deposition contradicted with his plaint case. In the cross examination he has stated so many contradictories testimony from which it is manifest and proved that plaintiff neither made a contract for sale with a genuine person nor those documents submitted in Court are the genuine and on the basis of that documents he cannot get the decree for Specific Performance of Contract rather it is transpired that total case of the plaintiff is nothing but a got up story only to grab the suit property on the basis of forged deeds and papers with a help of a fake person. From the discussions of the testimony of PW 1 made above it is crystal clear that he has failed to prove his alleged Bainapatra and payment, part payment of consideration money. 

 106. In the instant case from the discussions made above I am of the clear opinion that plaintiff not only failed to prove his own case but produced some forged and fabricated deeds and papers because from the facts and circumstances it clear that plaintiff PW 1 produced the exhibit 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 in the Court showing his vendor as custodian of those exhibit's who failed to appear before the Court and from the materials on record it is proved that he is none but a fake person. So, exhibit "6" is nothing but obviously the creation of forgery only to grab the suit property. Furthermore, the defence story and facts as set forth are quite believable not only by oral evidences, however, facts and circumstances with possession and documentary evidences, as find support from the testimony of PWs of title suit No.81 of 2006 which has been adopted in this case with the consent of all the parties. 

 108. Now I discuss and consider the appeal from original decree No.327 of 2009 arises which out of title suit No.176 of 2004 filed by living Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza. Plaintiff filed the suit against the Rajuk and other official of Rajuk on the following prayers: 

 A. Pass a decree in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants declaring that the plaintiff is legally entitled to get sale permission and the defendants are also bound to issue sale permission in respect of the scheduled property by receiving the proper transfer fees from the plaintiff as per rule of RAJUK. 

 2. Whether the plaintiff has got right, title and possession over the suit land? 

 3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get the relief as prayed for? 

 111. P. W. No. 1 claiming as Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza in his deposition has stated that he the Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza got, the allopient from Rajuk in the year 1962. Allotment letter being No. 2409 dated 21- 37,1962  produced before the Court and marked as exhibit 1. He has paid the entire lease many vide four receipts through National Bank of Pakistan which have been produced in the Court and marked as exhibit 2, 2 (ka), 2 (kha) and 2 (Ga) dated 26-2-62, 15-5-63, 15-5-64 and 546 respectively. He got the possession of the lease plot from, Rajuk. Possession hand over letter' dated 7-4-62 produced before the Court and larked as exhibit -3- Rajuk executed the lease deed and registered the same on 1-8-1962 being deed No.7198 which was produced and marked as exhibit 4. Exhibit 5 is the security money receipt of Tk-500/=. On an application plaintiff approved the plan from Rajuk being No. 4452 dated 29-10-1966 which is exhibit "6". Rajuk vide letter 4452 dated 29-10-2006 permitted plaintiff to construct the building which was produced before the Court and marked as Exhibit-7. Suit plot has been mutated in the name of the plaintiff and paid the rent those were produced before the Court and marked as exhibit 8, 8 (ka) and 8 (kha). Revisional survey record was prepared and published in the name of the plaintiff and khatian No. 1174 has been prepared in his name produced and marked as exhibit 9. Mahanagar record was prepared provisionally in the name of plaintiff. Plaintiff made an agreement with N.H. Bhulu for selling the suit property and prayed for sale permission on 18-2-2004. Rajuk did not accord permission nor refused the application for sale permission. Therefore, plaintiff on 20-4-2004 served a legal notice upon Rajuk by registered post with A/D which was received by the Rajuk, the copies of Registered A/D produced before Court and marked as exhibit 10 series. 

 113. From the above evidences it appears that the PW 1 though claimed he was a executive engineer but his testimony regarding service book, ACR and Organogram clearly prove that he is not a service holder at all. Not only that when a executive engineer admit that he has no bank account then question is, how he drew his salary which must be paid through A/C payee cheque. Moreover, from his docu-ments which have been exhibited it clearly show that it has been prepared in the name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157 Bara Moghbazar which is admittedly the permanent address of the engineer Shamsul Kabir Huma-yun Reza who is a different person. According to plaint case of title Suit No. 81 of 2006 wherein this plaintiff is the principal defendant No. 3 and contested that suit, now legal question is when other persons claimed the title and filed a title suit impleading this plaintiff as defendant that their father was the real owner and allottee of the same suit plot, then whether present suit simpliciter only for sale permission is maintainable. Especially when both the suits tried and heard by the same Judge simulta-neously and the suit for declaration of title and permanent injunction decreed against the contested defendants including instant plaintiff appellant, then natural consequence is that the suit for sale permission for same suit plot is not maintainable when plaintiff himself especially in the plaint and evidences admitted that he is out of possession. 

 114. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned advocate for the appellant submits that the trial judge erred in law in adopting the evidence of PW 1 as a evidence of DW 1 in the respective cases. He further submits that in violation of section 33 of Evidence Act such adoption is not sustainable in law. Therefore, according to him the impugned judgments are liable to be set aside. In support of his contentions he relied upon to the case of Allah Ditta vs State reported in 11 DLR (SC) 38, and the case of Ali Haider reported in 10 DLR (SC) 193. I have gone through the aforesaid decisions as referred by the learned advocate. I have respectful agreement with principles enunciated therein, but the facts leading to those cases are quite distinguishable to that of the present case. Therefore, I am unable to accept the submissions of the learned advocate for the appellant. It further appears from the record that the defendants by applications dated 30-6-09 prayed for adoption of their depositions given as PW 1 in title suit Nos. 176 of 2004 and 51 of 2004 respectively as deposition of D.W. in title suit No. 81 of 06 at their own risk. So it is the plaintiffs of TS NOrs. 51 of 2004 and 176 of 04 by whose instance the adoption has been made. It will not be out of place to mention here that when the plaintiffs themselves applied in Court for adoption of their deposition to later proceedings pending before the same Court in respect of same suit land. Appellants surely would not be allowed to raise such questions before the appellale. Court without raising any question in trial and taking any grounds in the memo of appeal. 

 "No body is entitled to take benefit of his own wrong. To claiin that since no document has been executed the claimant has no right is nothing but taking advantage one's own wrong" 

 116. Two appeals mentioned above have been preferred against the judgment and decree of dismissal. From the judgments of the trial Court it appears that both the title suit have been dismissed by the trial Court as respective plaintiffs have failed to proVe their case. In this respect I have respectful agreement with my learned brother as from his judgment it appears that he has discussed the plaint case and the evidences in support of the plaint case wherein both of plaintiffs of title suit No. 51 of 2004 and 176 of 2004 have failed to prove their cases in such situation I am of the view that provision of section 33 of Evidence Act has no manner of application in the instant appeal, in other words, it cannot be said that the trial judge erred in law in dismissing the title suit No. 51 of 2004 and 176 of 2004. 

 117. Now, II discuss and consider appeal from original decree No. 346 of 2009 preferred by Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza claiming himself as alive original Allottee and appeal from original decree No. 358 of 2009 preferred by MA Hashem defendant No.1 against the judgment and decree dated 06-8-2009 passed in title Suit No. 81 of 2006 filed by the Anowarul Hassan and others the heirs of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar decreed the suit. 

 118. In Title Suit No. 81 of 2006 the heirs of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza who were defendant Nos. 1(a) to 1(e) in title suit No. 51 of 2004 filed the instant suit on the following prayers 

 121. At the time of trial plaintiffs led the evidences to prove their case and they examined as many as 5 PWs PW 1 Nasiruddin Khan, PW 2 Shamima Zaman, PW 3 Shahin Rahman, PW 4 Md. Abdul Quiyum and PW 5 Md. Arifur Rahman. Plaintiff to prove the case produced some documents in the Court and marked as exhibits, exhibit 1 authorisation letter of Eastern Housing, exhibit 2 dated 11-2-2004 power of attorney, exhibit 3 series are power of Attorneys dated 24-2-2004 and 01-3-2004, Exhibit-4 series are Matriculation certificate, Intermediate certificate, Engineer Part-I and part II certificate original copy for the year 1946, 1948, 1950 respectively, Exhibit-5 domicile certificate original copy dated 17-1-1952, Exhibit-6 deed Nos. 9847 and 6 (Ka) deed Nos. 9849 dated 28-9-1957 certified copy compared with original copy, Exhibit-7 deed No.31901 dated 17-8-1979 certified copy compared with original, Exhibit-8 approved residential plan of 157 Bara Moghbazar, Exhibit-9 voter list ID card No. 44100, 16540310234 dated 08-8-1999 and 9 (Ka) passport M-0510358 dated 03-12-96 in original of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, Exhibit-10 series higher training certificates of Canada Government, original letter of promotion Exhibit-11 series original certificates as Assistant Engineer and letter of promotion, Exhibit-12 series letter of allotment in original of suit plot and installment receipt in original, Exhibit-13 series 5 original installment deposit receipt of the National Bank of Pakistan showing deposit money to DIT paid by the Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, Exhibit-14 possession hand over letter dated 07-4-1962 by DIT to Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, Exhibit-15 lease deed in original copy dated 01-8-1962 in favour of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza father of the plaintiffs and 15 (Ka) and 15 (Kha) are the signature of attesting witnesses. Exhibit-16 original copy of approved plan for the suit plot, exhibit 16 (Ka) is the permission of DIT. Exhibit-17 is the sanction letter of Housing Building Finance Corporation, exhibit 17 (ka) mortgage deed being No. 9022 dated 17-5-1967, Exhibit-18 series 10 copies deed of agreement for lease and rent agreement in respect of suit house, Exhibit-19 series Gas bill book, WASA demand notice, the taxes receipts of city corporation, exhibit 20 series are the assessment form, Tax and rent receipts, Exhibit-21 series copies of rent receipts, certified copy of RS record Exhibit-22, Exhibit-23 and 23 (Ka) are the Memorandum & Articles of Association, Exhibit-24 series are yearly report of Uttara Bank, Application receipt copy of Rajuk for approval of Rajuk for converting the suit plot residential to commercial plot is exhibit 25, the approval letter of RAJUK converting residential to commercial plot Exhibit-26, Exhibit-27 is the certified copy of power of attorney being No. 15902 dated 21-12-03 with photo executated by Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza in his life time in favour of Eastern Housing, exhibit 28 is the original received copy of RAJUK by which original power of attorney has been deposited to Rajuk office, Exhibit-29 series are the commercially approved plan copies of RAJUK, Exhibit-30 series are the notices dated 18-11-03 published in the Daily Inquilab, Janakantha, and the Observer and the protest notices dated 30-12-03, exhibit 31 series are the protest notice by which MA Hashem denied the existence of father of the plaintiffs, Exhibit-31(Kha) dated 2-2-04 is the copy of death certificate, exhibit 32 is the death certificate, Exhibit-33 is the notice dated 05-2-2004, Exhibit-34 is the certified copy of succession certificate issued in succession case being No. 439 of 2004 by Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka. Exhibit 35 is the Photostat certified copies of Judgment of CR No.358 of 2004 and C.R.4608 of 2004 Exhibit-36 is the certified copy of plaint of T.S. 176 of 2004. Exhibit-37 is the pay bill of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza. Exhibit-38 is the Passport No. B-057985 dated 15-1-75. 

 122. PW 1 produced and proved all the above mentioned exhibits in the Court at the time of his deposition without any objection from the defence. Considering the above exhibits it transpires that plaintiff Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza is the lessee of Dhaka improvement Trust now RAJUK and he had been exercising his right title and interest over the suit property from the year 1962 till his death within the full knowledge of all others. From Exhibit-15, 15 (ka), (15 kha) it reveals that its have been compared with the original standard lease deed kept in the custody of RAJUK. Therefore, RAJUK authority recognised the Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as his lessee. From Exhibit-14 dated 7-4-1962 it appears that possession of the suit plot was handed over to the father of the plaintiff, Exhibit-12 series are the original allotment letter and original copies of receipts of installment paid to the DIT by the father of the plaintiffs. Exhibit-17 sanction letter and 17 (ka) dated 17-5-1967 is mortgage deed of the suit plot in favour of the House Building. Finance Corporation and obtained loan mortgaging the suit land. Exhibit-18, 19 and 20 series are the bill copies of Gas, light, other taxes to the city corporation and rent receipt. Considering the above materials on record it appears that the father of the plaintiff after getting lease of the suit property from the RAJUK he has been exercising his continuous and uninterrupted title and possession over the same which proved beyond any doubt, Exhibit-25 and 26 proved that earlier suit plot was residential plot, however, at the instance of the plaintiff's father it has been converted to the commercial plot and Exhibit-27 and 28 proved that after converting to commercial plot RAJUK accepted the legal transfer fees and Exhibit-29 is approved plan of the multi-storied commercial plan of Eastern Housing Limited and accepted the Eastern Housing as the attorney of plaintiff's father from which is manifest and RAJUK accepted the father of the plaintiffs Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as lessee of RAJUK, however not accepted other two Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza one came from Mirpur and another living Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as impleaded in the instant suit as defendant No.1 and defendant No-3. In this connection it may not be out of place to mention here that other two Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza claiming the suit property admittedly without possession and both of them made agreement for sale of the suit property not as admitted lessee of Rajuk because their papers and documents filed in title suit No.51 of 2004 and 176 of 2004 never produced before Rajuk and claimed that they are the allottee of RAJUK. 

 124. PW 2 Shamima Zaman in her deposition stated that engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza was her father. He died on 02-2-2004 in Central Hospital, Dhaka. Her father was a resident of 157 Bara Moghbazar. Her father died leaving 3 (three) sons and 2 (Two) daughters. Her father was executive engineer of C&B department later he joined as director of BDC of Islam Group. He also was a director of Uttara Bank. Her father never lived in section 6 House No. 31, Road No. 2 of Mirpur. Her father made an agreement and executed power of attorney in favour of Eastern Housing Limited. After the death of her father all the sisters and brothers of her including herself made 3 power of attorney in favour of Eastern Housing. Her father never made any contract with MA Hashem or MH Bhulu by executing any deed of agreement, 2 deeds of agreement submitted by the defendants which are false and fabricated. Thus against false and fabri-cated bainapatra they have filed the instant suit for cancellation the same. Defendants created false and forged bainapatra following the deeds of her father. Defendants also created forged signature of her father. There are no existence of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur. They contested in the title suit No. 51 of 2004 as defendant Nos. 1 (a) - 1(e) as the heirs of Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar not as heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur, the evidence given in this suit may be adopted as the deposition of defendant nos. 1(a)-1(e) in title suit No. 51 of 2004. In cross examination he stated as per her deposition. In the cross examination the defence could not discover any contradictory statement nor made her evidences Shaky one. 

 126. PW 4 Md. Abdul Quiyum is a civil engineer of BUET. His father late Abdul Mannan was the friend of the plaintiff's father Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and both of them were the engineer of C&B they had been serving in the C&B department as engineer, later, his father transferred in DIT on deputation as executive engineer. His father was working as executive engineer in DIT while father of the plaintiffs got allotment of the suit plot. There was good relationship in between both of the family. There was communication between 2 family. There is a signature of his father in Exhibit-15 original lease deed dated 1-8-1962 made in between Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and the than DIT. He identified the signature of his father as exhibit 15 (ka) He further stated that in Exhibit-2 of title. suit No. 51 of 04 there is no signature of his father in the witness column, the Exhibit-2 has been created by forgery giving signature of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Moghbazar. He also confirmed that he knows the signature of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and signature in Exhibit-6 the alleged bainapatra of MA Hashem filed in title suit No. 51 of 2004 is not the signature of Executive Engineer Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza who is the friend of his father. 

 127. PW 5 Dr. Md. Arifur Rahman is the principle of National Medical College, Dhaka. He stated that on 3-7-77 he married the 2nd daughter Shahin Rahman of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza. So he knows all the sons and daughters of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza after their marriage they have been residing at 157 Bara Moghbazar with Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza. He died on 2-2-04 in Central Hospital, Dhaka. Before his death Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza came to know that one MA Hashem created forged bainapatra regarding his plot being No. 113 of Gulshan Avenue for which published a notice in the daily news papers stating that he did not make any contract agreement to anybody except Eastern Housing Limited. He further stated that late Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza never lived in outside of 157 Bara Moghbazar. His father in law never made any bainapatra with Mr. MA Hashem and with defendant No. 3 of this suit in other word with the plaintiff of title suit No. 176 of 2004. Bainapatra has been created by MA Hashem and the plaintiff of title Suit No. 176 of 2004 living Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza both the agreement are forged and executant of the bainapatra are the fake Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza not his father-in-law who was a civil engineer. His father-in-law at first joined in the C&B department in the year 1952 as Assistant Engineer and later on in the year 1960 he was promoted to the post of Executive Engineer. In 1964 he joined in BDC as director of Islam Group and thereafter in the year 1966 he became a share director of Uttara Bank and till his death he was the director of Uttara Bank. In cross examination he denied the suggestion of the defence and specifically and categorically stated the facts as per his deposition. Defence has failed to discover any contradiction to his deposition by cross examination. 

 128. From discussions made above it is manifest that plaintiffs of title suit No. 81 of 2006 proved his own case.

full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the Order No.24 dated 28-9-2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj in Title Suit No.31 of 2002 should not be set-aside. 

 2. Material facts of the case as necessary for the disposal of the Rule are that the petitioner, Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd. as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 27 of 1995 in the Court of. learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka against the defendant-opposite parties for recovery of its outstanding dues by selling the mortgaged property. Later on, the said suit was re-numbered on transfer as Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 in the Court of learned Joint District Judge and Additional Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka. The present-defendant opposite party No. 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint. The learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka after hearing the parties and on considering the materials on record decreed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 21-10-1999 (preliminary decree was signed on 31-10-1999 and final decree was drawn up on 5-9-2000). After obtaining the decree the petitioner as decree-holder-bank put the decree into execution by filing Title Execution Case No. 2 of 2002 on 12-1-2002 before the learned Joint District Judge and Additional Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka. 

 3. In this background of the case the judgment-debtor (opposite party No. 1) instituted Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 in the Court of 2nd Joint District Judge, Narayangonj against the defendants including decree holder, Al-Baraka Bank Ltd. praying a decree declaring that the judgment and decree dated 21-10-1999 ( preliminary decree singed on 31-10-1999 and final decree drawn up on 5-9-2000) passed in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 by the Additional Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka against the plaintiff (hereinafter called as "the opposite party No. 1) is illegal, irregular, collusive and not binding upon him and also declaring that irrevocable power of attorney, memorandum of deposit of title deeds as set forth in the schedule "Kha" in connection with the property as described in schedule "Ka" of the plaint are illegal, forged, collusive, made by false personation and of no legal effect. After filing of the said suit the present opposite party No.1 as applicant filed Misc. Case No. 39 of 2002 under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the learned Joint District Judge and Additional Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka with a prayer for stay of  the attachment and auction sale of the scheduled property of the Title Execution Case No. 02 of 2002. The present petitioner-Bank has appeared in the said miscellaneous case and the same is still pending for hearing. 

 4. The defendant-petitioner, Al-Baraka Bank Ltd. (hereinafter called as "the petitioner") appeared in the said Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 and filed an application under Order VII rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint stating that the judgment debtor as plaintiff instituted the suit against the defendant bank and others prying a decree declaring that judgment and decree dated 21-10-1999 (preliminary decree singed on 31-10-1999 and final decree drawn on 05-9-2000) passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 against him (opposite party No. 1) is illegal, irregular, collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff and Irrevocable General Power of Attorney and. Memorandum of Deposit of Title Deeds as Set forth in the schedule "ka" of the plaint are illegal, forged, fake collusive and made by false personating and of no-legal effect which is not only misconceived and also clearly barred by law because the Artha Rin Adalat Ain being a special legislation setting up special Court the remedies will follow as provided therein and there being specific remedy in the statute for filing appeal against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. Moreover, as per the express provisions of section 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 the decision or judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat is final and the same cannot be questioned in any Court or by any authority except under the provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain. 

 11. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Ziaul Hoque, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 supports the impugned order which was according to him just, correct and proper. Drawing our attention to the contents of the plaint Mr. Hoque, submits that in the suit the plaintiff not only challenged the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat also challenged the irrevocable power of attorney, memorandum of deposit of title deeds as produced or used before the Artha Rin Adalat in Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 and without taking evidence it is not at all possible to decide whether the irrevocable power of attorney is genuine or not and in that view of the matter the question of rejection of the plaint does not arise at all. He further points out that it is apparent from the judgment and decree dated 21-10-1999 that the learned Judge of the Adalat most illegally decreed the suit ex-party against the petitioner without considering whether the power of attorney or mortgaged deed was executed by the present plaintiff-opposite party or those documents were genuine or not whatsoever. The learned Advocate to fortify his argument relied on the decisions reported in 15 BLD (AD) 35, 56 DLR-588 and unreported decision dated 05-7-2004 HC-36 passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 738 of 2004. 

 12. These are the points which were argued by the learned Advocates for the respective parties. Now, to deal with the contentions raised by the parties before us it would be convenient for us to decide first of all the question of maintainability of the stilt preferred by the judgment-debtor challenging the judgment and decree dated 21-10-1999 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998. In order to decide this point the prayer portions of the plaint are required to be referred to for having a better view in the dispute in question. Reliefs 'Ka' and 'Kha' reads as follows: 

 13. From a plain reading of the above quoted prayer portions together with the averments of the plaint, it appears that the present suit was instituted in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj praying a decree declaring that the judgment and decree dated 21-10-1999 passed in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 by the Additional Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka against the plaintiff-opposite party is illegal, irregular, collusive and not binding upon him and also declaring that irrevocable power of attorney, memorandum of deposit of title deeds as set forth in the schedule "Kha" in connection with the property as described in schedule "Ka" of the plaint are illegal, forged, collusive and made by false personating and of no legal effect. 

 23. Mr. Ziaul Haque, the learned Advocate at the fag end of the hearing however, agitated a point that the Artha Rin Adalat has/ had no jurisdiction to decide whether the documents namely power of attorney and memorandum of deposit of title deeds as set forth in the schedule "Kha" in connection with the property as described in schedule "Ka" of the plaint were genuine or not and in that view of the matter no such issue was framed in the Artha Rin Suit and as such without taking evidence there is no scope to resolve this dispute. 

 24. In reply, Mr. Razzaque, the learned Advocate referring paragraph No.3 of the supplementary affidavit submits that the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 never appeared before the Court with clean hands inasmuch as it is apparent from the record that the opposite party No.2 availed overdraft facility of Tk. 20,00,000 vide sanction advise No. AB/MJ/CR/ 1237 dated 10-8-1986 from the petitioner-Bank and as security of the said credit facilities the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 mortgaged his land properties through executing memorandum of deposit of title deeds on 13-10-1986, an irrevocable general power of attorney on 9-10-1986 and the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 submitted all original title deeds of the mortgaged properties to the petitioner-defendant-Bank and in that view of the matter it does not lie in the mouth of the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 that the defendant-opposite party No.2 on practicing fraud used his original deeds beyond his knowledge. He adds that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain is a special statute, there is specific provision for the aggrieved party to prefer appeal against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat and in case of ex-party decree the judgment-debtor may prefer an application under section 6(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 or under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for setting-aside ex-parte decree upon depositing of certain amount as per provision of the said law. 

 25. On an overall consideration of the facts, circumstances of the case and materials on record, my view is therefore, that Mr. Razzaque, the learned Advocate for the petitioner-Bank is not wrong in submitting that the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 has never approached before the Court with clean hand. As already noticed the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 submitted his all original title deeds of the mortgaged properties to the petitioner-defendant-Bank as security of the credit facilities. 

 28. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned order dated 28-9-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 is hereby set-aside and the plaint of the suit is rejected under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 31. Here in this case an order passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj, in Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 (brought by OP No.1) rejecting an application under Order VII Rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure, shortly, "the Code" filed by the defendant-petitioner is impugned before us. More precisely, Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd. as defendant No.1, sought to challenge before us the impugned order, for that matter maintainability of the suit of the opposite party No.1, in all, on four grounds which essentially boil down to one: that the decree sought to be challenged in the suit is one passed by an Artha Rin Adalat against the opposite party No.1 as a third party mortgagor and others. A suit by a judgment-debtor in an Artha Rin suit challenging the decree is barred by express provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (briefly "the Ain") Subsequently a supplementary affidavit is filed by the petitioner-bank wherein the facts and law are more fully stated in support of its point. In the supplementary affidavit specific sections ie, sections 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 and section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 are quoted which on the face of them are ouster or exclusionary clauses, as they are so called. The ouster clauses are couched in similar languages and the one ie, section 20 of the Ain of 2003 seems to be absolute in nature which creates a complete bar on seeking relief before any court or authority impugning any proceeding pending in , order, judgment or decree passed by an Artha Rin Adalat. 

 32. It appears from records that the judgment and decree dated 21-10-1999 purportedly challenged in the instant suit was passed by the court of Joint District Judge and Additional Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 (arising out of TS No. 27 of 1995) wherein the present opposite party. No. 1 was impleaded as defendant No. 2. The sole case against the defendant 2 (OP No. 1 herein) was that he mortgaged the land described in schedule Ka of his plaint as collateral security against an overdraft facility of Tk. 20,00,000 availed by the present opposite party No. 2 (defendant No.1 before the Adalat) from the petitioner bank. To that effect he (OP-1) deposited the original title deeds under a memorandum of deposit of title deeds signed on 13-10-1986 and executed an irrevocable power of Attorney on 09-10-1986 in favour of the bank. 

 33. Admittedly the present opposite party No.1 did not appear in the suit tried by the Artha Rin Adalat. Therefore, the decree of the Artha Rin Adalat was passed ex-parte against him. The Artha Rin decree was put to execution giving rise to Title Execution Case No. 2 of 2002 for realization of the decretal amount which stood at an amount of one crore and odd. Opposite party No. 1, however, initially took an attempt to retain his possession and get the attachment of his property vacated by filing Miscellaneous Case No. 39 of 2002. But finally chose to file the instant suit, Title Suit No. 31 of 2002, in the 2nd Court of Joint District Judge, Narayanganj, as claimed by the petitioner, during pendency of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case. 

 34. In the instant suit opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff sought declaration, inter alia, that the judgment and decree dated 21-10-1999 passed by the Joint District Judge and Additional Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 is illegal, void, collusive, fraudulent, ineffective and not binding upon him; and that the irrevocable power of attorney and the memorandum of deposit of title deeds standing in his name purportedly creating equitable mortgage of his property are not executed by him. Those were created beyond his knowledge by way of fraud, forgery and impersonation, in collusion with bank officials. 

 37. Mr. Ziaul Haque, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the opposite party No.1 in his bid to support the impugned order contended that the opposite party No. 1 is set up by impersonation as a third party mortgagor in the loan case. He did never deposit title deeds in the bank nor created mortgage by signing the Memorandum of deposit of title deeds. He did not execute the so-called irrevocable power of attorney in favour of the bank. Those documents are created beyond the knowledge of plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 by forged signatures and title deeds might have been procured from the custody of any of his co-sharer-in title. He is not one anyway connected with the loan/credit facilities advanced by the bank. And in the circumstances, he contended, a separate suit is maintainable. In support of his contention learned Advocate cited a decision of a Division Bench of our High Court Division reported in 56 DLR 588 as well as the unreported judgment passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 738 of 2004 arising out of the aforesaid judgment reported in 56 DLR as aforesaid. 

 38. A plain reading of the plaint of the instant suit amply suggests that the suit arose out of a cause of action which is unique and hardly goes with most other cases of the kind. The plaintiff (OP-1) sets out therein a clear-cut case of his total dissociation with the loan transaction, asserting, as he does, that he is in no way connected with the loan/overdraft facility granted by the bank. He is figured therein as a mortgagor by fraud, forgery and impersonation completely beyond his knowledge. It is his specific case that he did never sign the Power of Attorney or the Memorandum of Deposit of Title deeds nor did he ever deposit the title documents in the bank creating any charge on them. He is not even aware of the overdraft facility taken by the opposite party No. 2. The title deeds might have been smuggled into the bank from the custody of one of his co-sharer-in- title. 

 41. In the case of Al-Baraka Bank Bangladesh Ltd. vs Rina Alam reported in 56 DLR 588, title documents were earlier deposited to create security against loan taken from the bank which was finally adjusted. Bank issued certificate as well to that effect but in spite of requests made did not return the title deeds to the mortgagor who happens to be a lady. Bank filed Artha Rin suit in 1992 against the principal borrower, a company, the lady as mortgagor and others for realization of loan money advanced to the defaulter company in which it was found that further charge was created on the unreturned documents as against the loan. As she claimed, she had no manner of connection nor did she create any charge on the unreturned documents to provide security to the loan account sued against. During tendency of the Artha Rin suit the lady filed a title suit in 1997 in the court of the court of the Joint District Judge and First Commercial Court, Dhaka, against the bank and another for declarations, inter alia, that she had no liability with the bank; the memorandum of deposit of title deeds purportedly made in her name was manufactured, forged and inoperative; return of her deeds and for compensation. The two suits continued side by side for quite sometime. Artha Rin Suit was contested by the lady wherein she was examined as a witness. Artha Rin suit was decreed on contest against the defendants including the lady. Subsequently the suit filed by the lady was also decreed in part on the findings, inter alia, that the memorandum of deposit of title deeds was created and forged and directed the bank to return the title deeds. Meanwhile upon an application under section 151 of the Code filed at the instance of the lady her property was released from the schedule of the decree of the Artha Rin Adalat against which a rule nisi was taken by the bank which was still pending. 

 43. The above, in terms of the barring clause, is a much worse case than the instant one. In the cited case the plaintiff of the subsequent suit was not only aware of the Artha Rin suit but also contested it. But during tendency of the Artha Rin suit, filed title suit in an ordinary civil court alleging fraud, forgery and her total dissociation with the loan transaction on trial in the Artha Rin Adalat. Both the suits continued side by side in two courts of different jurisdictions and earlier or later decrees were also passed in both the suits and finally the decree of the ordinary civil court was fought through by the bank up to the Appellate Division. The question chosen to be contested was the question of resjudicata not the statutory bar. And ultimately the decree of the ordinary civil court obtained by a judgment-debtor of the Artha Rin Adalat sustained. It does not go with the High Court Division to say that the questions we are dealing with were not in the notice of the Appellate Division while deciding the cited case. Therefore, the questions raised in the present case are answered by both the Divisions of the Supreme Court implicitly in the negative. 

 65. In view of law discussed above and the peculiar facts of the present case I am of the opinion that the opposite party No.1, before being proved as such, is not a 'judgment-debtor' as contemplated under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. By the same token, the suit filed by him questioning the applicability of the same cannot be said to be barred by the ouster clause of the Ain for the precise reason that on the event of his success in his suit the decree passed against him will turn into a nullity and no 'decree' passed under the Act. 

 68. In the instant suit, in particular, no less an issue than one involving allegation of making the plaintiff a third party mortgagor by fraud and forgery has to be tried which, if proved, would render the decree against him a nullity and no decree in the eye of law. The issues cannot be decided except on evidence taken in a full fledged trial before a competent civil court. Since law does not intend any person to suffer for no fault of himself the opposite party No. 1 cannot be made to suffer the stringent conditions and procedure of a special statute, even if available, for no fault of him and his property be taken away as is sought to be done by a decree of the Adalat. It follows; therefore, that the suit filed by the Opposite party No. 1 is fairly maintainable. 

 Nozrul Islam Chowdhury J:  This Rule is directed against Order No. 24 dated 28-9- 2003 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj in Title Suit No, 31 of 2003, at the instance of the defendant No.1 as petitioner, rejecting an application under Order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 72. Facts, in a nutshell, giving rise to this Rule issued by a Division Bench of this Court and heard by me sitting singly, are that the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 in the 2nd Court of Joint District Judge, Narayanganj seeking a decree for two declarations one is that the judgment and preliminary decree dated 21-10-99 and final decree dated 05-09-2000 in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 passed by the Sub-ordinate Judge, now Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Artha RM Adalat No. 1, Dhaka are illegal, collusive , fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff. In the said suit petitioner Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd. was impleacled as defendant No. 1 while two others as defendant Nos. 2 and 3. 

 73. The said Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 was brought by the petitioner as plaintiff seeking a decree for recovery of loan amounting of Tk. 99, 68,807,14 impleading the opposite party No. 1 and another as defendants and in that suit the opposite party No. 2 Mr. Aininuddirt was imp leaded as defendant No. 1 as loanee while the opposite party No. 1 Md. Salahuddin the plaintiff of the present suit was imp leaded as defendant No. 2 mortgagor. 

 74. During tendency of the said Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 the defendant No. 1 loanee entered appearance contesting the suit while the defendant No. 2 the mortgagor he the plaintiff of the present suit (Title Suit No. 31 of 2002) did not contest. 

 75. Eventually, the suit Was decreed on contest in preliminary form on 21-10-1999 and the final decree was drawn on 0542000 on contest against the defendant No.1 loanee while ex parte against the defendant No. 2 mortgagor the plaintiff of the present suit. Thereafter the said final decree dated 05-9-2000 iri Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 was put to execution in Execution Case No. 02 of 2002 by the decree holder Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd. and during pendency of the said execution case the defendant No. 2 mortgagor for the first time entered appearance in the said execution case upon filing an application under Order XX1 Rule 58 of the Cade of Civil Procedure praying for stay of the attachment and auction sale of the mortgaged land and lastly on his application filed as aforesaid the defendant No. 2 Md. Salahuddin of title Suit No. 54 of 1998 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 before the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj seeking two declaration one for setting aside the exparte preliminary decree dated 31-10-99 and the final decree dated 05.9-2000 in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 on the ground of fraud allegedly practiced in giving his property in mortgage, for obtaining the loan involved in that suit and the other declaration sought for by the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 is that the Memorandurn of Deposit of Title Deeds along with Irrevocable General Power of Attorney given for the purpose of obtaining loan involved in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 was forged, fake, collusive and the Power of Attorney bearing No. 4950 as illegal, forged and fake and 'created by false personation. 

 76. In the aforesaid Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 the defendant No. 1 Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd. entered appearance upon filing an application under Order VII rule 1.1 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for rejection of the plaint stating inter alia, that the mortgage involved in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 and the proceedings in that suit is governed by Artha Rin Adalat Ain,1990 and Section 6 of the said Ain is a legal bar in proceeding with Title Suit No. 31 of 2002, therefore, the said suit cannot proceed in accordance with law as such the. plaint ought to have been rejected. It was also contended in the said application under Order  VII rule 11 filed by the defendant No. 1 Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd. that Section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 provides for an appeal against the judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 though exparte against the defendant No. 2 of that suit. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 31 of 2000 had also another remedy namely an application under Order 9 Role 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the exparte decree passed in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 , the said application under Order VII rule 11 of the Code  Of Civil Procedure (is also available on record). 

 77. After hearing the parties the learned Joint District judge by his Order No. 24 dated 28-09-03 rejected the same. As against which the defendant of Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 as petitioner obtained the present Rule in Civil Revision No.e86 of 2601 

 80. Mr. ASM Abdur Razzaque, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has take me through both the judgments and the materials on record and then submits that the instant suit being Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 praying for setting aside an exparte decree passed by an Artha Rin Adalat, is not maintainable particularly in view of Section 6 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain,1990, or in otherwords, said Section 6 or in the alternative Section 20 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 is a legal bar in proceeding with the instant suit being Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 . 

 81. It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 31 of 2002, had two fold remedies against the impugned ex-parte decree such as, he could have brought an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree or in the alternative he could have preferred an appeal as contemplated under Section 7 of the Arthan Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 or Section 41 of Arthan Rin Adalat Ain 2003. To fortify his submission the learned Advocate for the petitioner placed reliance in the case of Messrs Sekander Jute Bailing Ltd. vs Sonali Bank reported in 18 BLD (AD) 268. In support of his submission to the effect that suit to set aside an ex-parte decree passed by Artha Rin Adalat is not maintainable in view of the remedy available under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain itself. 

 83. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Ziaul Hoque, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1 submits at the out set, drawing my attention to the prayers made in the plaint of Title Suit No. 31 of 2002, to the effect that there are in fact two fold prayers made in the plaint of Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 such as in the first prayer the decree of Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 has been sought to be set aside but in the other prayer a declaration has been sought to the effect that the registered Power of Attorney and the Memorandum of Deposit of Title Deeds are forged, fabricated and fraudulent transaction, therefore, he submits that so far as Section 6 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain,1990 or for that matter Section 20 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 cannot create any bar in proceeding with Title Suit No. 31 of 2000 since Order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot apply in respect of that particular prayer of the suit. 

 87. Heard the learned Advocates from both sides, perused the two judgments delivered by my, brothers including other materials relevant for the purpose wherefrom it transpires that the decision in the instant Rule, revolves round a precise question as to whether in view of the provisions in Section 6 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain,1990 or for that matter Section 20 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 creates a legal bar in proceeding with a suit like Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 for setting aside an ex parte decree passed by a Artha Rin Adalat granting decree in favour of the plaintiff against the loanee and the mortgagor thereof particularly with reference to Order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 Turning to the judgment referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner Mr. ASM Abdur Razzaquwe and from a plain reading of the case of Messrs Sikander Jute Bailing Ltd. vs Sonali Bank reported in 18 BLD (AD) 268 we find that a similar question arose in the said case and after consideration, their lordships were of the opinion that though a separate suit was brought on the ground of fraud and collusion in obtaining an ex-parte decree from the Artha Rin Adalat yet the same was not maintainable in view of the remedy available in the said Ain, therefore, the decision given by the learned Subordinate Judge rejecting the plaint and approved by the High Court Division in revision, there is no ground for interference and the Leave Petition was dismissed. 

 96. Elaborating his submissions the learned Advocate has drawn our attention to the prayer portion of the plaint of Title Suit No. 31 of 2002. On a close scrutiny of the prayer portion and the averments made in the plaint I find that the plaintiff as a matter of fact prayed for two fold declaration first is that the exparte decree obtained in Title Suit No. 54 of 1998 is not binding upon him and a declaration that the registered Power of Attorney and Memo of Deposit of Title Deeds were forged, fabricated and false ones. 

 97. Going through the judgment referred to by the learned Advocate for the opposite party No.1 particularly the one reported in 56 DLR 588, I find that in the instant case both the prayers made in the plaint could have been decided by the Adalat itself. Had there been an appeal against the same, under Section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 or Section 41 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, therefore, the question of absence of jurisdiction as contemplated in the case reported in 56 DLR is totally absent as such not applicable. The two other decisions relied upon by the opposite party, are also for the same reason namely both the prayer made in the plaint in Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 are well within the jurisdiction or competence of Artha Rin Court established under the Arthan Rin Adalat Ain 1990 and 2003 , therefore, none of the aforesaid two cases can be of any help for the opposite party No.1, on the other hand, going through the aforesaid judgment referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioner I find that in view of the position that section 6 of the Arthan Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 or for that matter Section 20 of Ain, 2003 create a bar in proceeding with a subsequent suit making a prayer for setting aside an ex-parte decree even on the ground of fraud or even with a prayer for another declaration for the Power of Attorney and Memorandum of Deposit of Title Documents as forged, fabricated and false rather the only remedy available for the opposite party No. 1 was to go for an application under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure or an appeal under Section 7 or Section 41 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 and 2003 respectively, therefore, I find that the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner has got substance , as such accepted. 

 98. In view what has been stated above, I am unable to persuaded myself in agreeing with the judgment delivered by learned brother Moazzam Husain, J rather I am inclined to agree with the judgment passed by my brother Sheikh Abdul Awal J, therefore, in my opinion the Rule is hereby made absolute and the impugned judgment and order No. 24 dated 28-09-2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj is hereby set aside and the plaint of Title Suit No. 31 of 2002 is rejected.

full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah, J: This first appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 31.03.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 decreeing the suit. 

 2. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 as plaintiffs filed the said title suit in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for declaration of title to the suit land on the averments, inter-alia, that the land of C.S. khatian No. 241 being plot No. 390/3940 measuring an area of 0568 ajutangsha originally belonged to Khiroda Shundari Daishya which was put to auction for arrear of rent in certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 and was purchased by Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Monjurul Hoque, son of late Munshi Nowab Ali of 74, Mirpur, Dhaka on 20.06.1953. The sale was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and sale certificate was issued in favour of said Ali Ahmed on 19.11.1953. The auction purchaser (Ali Ahmed) got possession of the auction purchased land on 20.01.1954 through court. Ali Ahmed being in possession of the auction purchased land (hereinafter referred to as the suit property) for more than 12 years mutated his name in the Government record and paid rents accordingly; S.A. Khatian being No.197 and R.S. Khatian being No.1248 were prepared in his name. Ali Ahmed while had been in possession of the suit property died issueless on 18.06.1975 leaving behind a widow, named, Khatibunnassa who inherited the entire suit property as her 4 annas share as his wife and the remaining 12 annas share because of the 'Doctrine of Return'. Khatibunnesa being the 16 annas owner of the suit property died on 10.02.78 leaving behind her only full brother Abdul Mannan who inherited the entire property of his deceased sister. While Abdul Mannan had been in possession of the suit property as the 16 annas owner, by a registered heba-bil-ewaj dated 29.11.79 being No. 45060 transferred the suit property in favour of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs being minors their father Abdul Majid as their natural guardian took over the possession of the transferred land. Thus the plaintiffs being the 16 annas owners of the suit property have been in peaceful possession thereof. Defendants having no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property by resorting to various tactics created forged papers and tried to take possession of the suit property forcibly, but due to the intervention of the respectable people of the mahalla failed. On 06.07.80 the defendants along with the process server of the Court and the police attacked (in the plaint in Bengali it has been written as “হামলা চালায়” in the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs by showing a decree. The bailiff of the Court having seen the valid title documents of the plaintiffs failed to execute the decree in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980. However, after making inquiry from the bailiff of the Court the father of the plaintiffs Abdul Mazid came to know that the defendants obtained a fraudulent decree on 15.11.79 in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka. On further query the plaintiffs came to know that a so-called bainapatra to sell the suit property allegedly entered into by one Rasheda Begum, wife of Salimuddin of 321, Lalbag Road, Dhaka on 12.08.92 with the defendants was the basis of the said decree. Rasheda Begum went to Pakistan Via Nepal after liberation of Bangladesh, so the alleged bainapatra was fraudulent and was not legally enforceable in respect of the suit property. Rasheda Begum had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property. Therefore, the defendants did not acquire any title to the suit property either on the basis of the bainapatra or their alleged purchase. The plaintiffs themselves and through their predecessor have been in possession of the suit property for more than 12 years since the purchase of the same in auction. The defendants got a kabala executed and registered in their names through court in execution of the ex-parte decree passed in the said suit, but by the said kabala they did not acquire right, tide and interest in the suit property. As neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor were made parties in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979, the decree passed therein suit was not binding upon them. The defendants were not entitled to get any relief by way of execution of the decree through Title Execution No. 3 of 1980 without filing a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession on payment of a advalorem court fees. The plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 in Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka against the defendants for permanent injunction which was decreed on 28.03.84 on contest. Against the said decree the defendants filed Title Appeal No. 196 of 1984 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Dhaka who heard the appeal allowed the same by judgment and decree dated 24.01.1987 and dismissed the suit. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed in the said appeal the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 76 of 1987 before this Division, but the rule was discharged on 27.05.92 and thus decree passed by the appellate court was up-held. Against the judgment and order passed in the said civil revision the plaintiffs filed Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 297 of 1972 before the Appellate Division. The leave petition was dismissed by the Appellate Division observing as under: 

 "The learned Subordinate Judge in dismissing the suit, inter-alia, found that since complicated question of law as well as facts was involved in the suit a simple suit for permanent injunction was not maintainable and the plaintiffs ought to have instituted a suit (sic) establishment of their title. The learned Judge of the High Court Division upon independently examining the facts of the case similarly case (sic) to the finding that a disputed question of title was very much involved in the matter chich cannot be decided in a suit for permanent injunction.
