The southern and northern boundary of the land in suit is common in the schedule 'Kha' of all the suits since from the description of the land given in the schedule of Ext.2 it is seen the land in suit is located on the south of temple road or in other words on the north of the land in suit is temple road and on the south '“দিঘী” or in other words on the north of the “দিঘী” the land in suit is located and the front side of the land is the northern boundary which is on the south of the road i.e. the temple road. Since the boundary of the land in respect whereof khas possession has been sought for is not the same and similar as contended on behalf of the appellants and it being the definite case of the plaintiff that upon dispossessing it from the land, which is part of the land in 'Ka' schedule, in 1973 the defendants' erected huts as described in schedule "Kha' and the defendants having not denied that they are not on the land as described in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint of the respective suits we are of the view the contention that the decree that has been passed by the appellate Court and affirmed by the High Court Division would not be executable is of no substance. It may be mentioned here that although it was the case of the defendants that they are on the land in suit for more than 30/40 but in support thereof did not produce any paper, rather it is found from the evidence of D.W.1 that he raised huts in the land in suit after 2/1 year of the liberation. It may be mention this D.W.1 is the defendant No.1 in Other Suit No.230 of 1984. D.W.2 has stated that he has no paper to show that his father possessed the land in suit from 1949 till 1973. It may be mention D.W. 1 has stated-that before 1973 huts on the suit land were burned. So from the evidence of this witness it is seen that the huts in the land in suit as gated by plaintiff were burned and it is the case of the plaintiff that huts were burned in 1971 by Pakistani army and that has been established by the plaintiff by the evidence of reliable witness. 

 16. The learned Counsel for the appellant upon referring to the discrepancy of the description of the land in suit as in 'Ka' schedule submitted that the land being not properly described or in other words being indefinite and for that trial Court having had dismissed the suit the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court were in error in arriving at the finding that the land in suit as contended by the defendants vague, indefinite and uncertain is not correct. It may be mentioned the suits, in all three, were filed on the same date and in the suits i.e. in Suit Nos.157 and 158 of 1984 in 'Ka' schedule southern and northern boundary was given as per the deed of title, but the eastern and western boundary were not as in the deed of title. In the other suit i.e. in Title Suit No.230 of 1984 the boundary of the land in 'Ka' schedule was given as per the deed of title i.e. Ext.2. The High Court Division on consideration of the evidence and the other materials on record held that the plaintiff has described the land mentioning the plot number and the khatian number and also described the land by mentioning the boundaries uniformly north and south, except in two suits stated eastern and western boundary different from the Ext.2, but for that it can not be said that the land in suit is indefinite and unspecified and vague since defendants were very much aware that the land in suit is of plot No.792 and they contested the claim of plaintiff as to the land in schedule 'ka' as the relief sought in the suit was as regard the land described in `ka' and `Kha' schedules. It is seen from the evidence of D.W.4, who is defendant No.1 in Title Suit No.158 of 1984, that the defendants being quite aware about the identity of the land in suit contested the suit and further defendants were aware which particular land was in suit or in other words as regard which particular land plaintiff was seeking relief evident from the cross examination directed by the defendants to the P.Ws. There is no dispute' that the land in suit was recorded in the name of Mela Committee in the R.S. khatian and the P.S. khatan was also prepared in the name of the Mela committee inspite of the observation   in Ext. C i.e. order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.95. It may be mentioned on Miscellaneous Case No.95 defendants of the instant cases were not parties and their names also do not find place in Ext. C. In the background of the said fact the appellate Court as well as the High Court Division held that there was no basis for the preparation of Ext. D i.e. B.S. khatian in the name of one of  the defendants and the payment of rent by the Exts. B-B(2) can not be made basis, since B.S. khatian and the rent receipts relate to the period subsequent to the dispossession of the plaintiff from the land in suit, for holding that the defendants have title and possession in the land in suit. The learned Counsel for the appellants also has submitted that fact being that in the suit land there is a mosque and club and also public latrine and the same having had not been impleaded relief as to declaration of title in the land in suit can not have and upon over looking those material facts the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court were in serious error in not holding that the suit is not maintainable. In repelling the aforesaid contention of the appellants the learned Advocate for the Respondent has referred to the evidence of P.W.1 who has stated that the mosque and the club are the plaintiff's lisencee and the said witness has also denied the existence of public latrine. P.W.1 has been corroborated by P.W.3 and P.W.5. I3ecause of afore mentioned evidence the contention of the appellants that without impleading the mosque and club the suit having been filed seeking the relief for declaration of title the same is not maintainable is of no merit. It may be mentioned it is more or less admitted fact or in other words undisputed fact that the land in suit belonged to the Sitakunda Mela Committee and possession of the said Committee has been established by the evidence of P.W.1, P.W.3 and P.W.4 as well as by the documentary evidence Ext.2 and the R.S. as well as P.S. khatians. The defendants although pleaded that the C.S. recorded tenant Elahi Boksha and Mowla Boksha were the owners of the land in suit, but the fact is that the defendants are not claiming the land through the C.S. recorded tenants. As mentioned hereinbefore their case was that the land in suit being covered by jungle and bush and they were being told by Revenue department that the land belong to the Government they cleared the jungle and bush and made the same usable and thereupon upon erecting huts they are possessing the land in suit. As stated herein before the land belonged to Sitakunda Mela Committee has been established by the oral as well as by the documentary evidence and on the basis of the evidence on record High Court Division as well as the appellate Court held that the land belonged to the Sitakunda Mela Committee and the plaintiff got the land from the Mela Committee. The appellate Court on consideration of the evidence and other materials on record held that plaintiff got the land from the R.S. recorded tenant Sitakunda Mela Committee by the Ext.2, deed of gift and possessed the land through monthly tenants and that the temporary structures in the land in suit burned in 1971. It may be mentioned it was the case of the plaintiff that in 1971 the huts wherein plaintiff had monthly tenants were burned by the Pakistani army and that taking advantage of the land being vacant defendants entered on the land and erected huts. As against the said case of the plaintiff it was the case of the defendants that they are in possession of the land for 30/40 years. It may be mentioned the appellate Court on scrutiny of one of the exhibits of B series i.e. rent receipt of 1975 found the same erased or in other words tampered and the other two rent receipts relates to the period subsequent to the year of dispossession as claimed by the plaintiff. The undisputed position is that R.S. and P.S. records stand in the name of the Sitakunda Mela Committee and in that background the appellate Court as well as the Court Division held that there was no basis for the preparation of the Ext. D in the name of one of the defendants. It is in the evidence of D.W.2 that he erected huts after '2/1' year of the liberation war of Bangladesh. I/W.2 has stated that he has no paper to show that his father and after him he is on the land from 1947 to 1973. On consideration of the evidence produced from the side of the plaintiff and the evidence lead from the side of the defendants the appellate Court as well as High Court Division arrived at the finding that the land in suit was possessed by the plaintiff and the defendants dispossessed the plaintiff therefrom. It was submitted by the learned Counsel for the appellants that evidence is absent from the side of the plaintiff to show that on the basis of Ext.2, the deed of gift, the plaintiff got the possession of the land in suit or that anybody handed over possession to the plaintiff and that evidence also is lacking about establishment of tole in the land in suit. The submission so made is not correct. As from the evidence of P. W.1 it is seen that in the light of the Ext.2 the possession was handed over to the plaintiff. P. W.1 has been corroborated by P.W.3. As regard the establishment of to be P.W.1 has stated about the establishment of tole and in support thereof submitted the resolution book (Ext.8) and he has been supported by P.W.2, member of the to be committee and also by the P.W.3 who has deposed about the fact of tole committee. As it has been stated herein before that it was the contention from appellants' side the land suit was in uncertain, unspecified and vague, but the evidence from the side of the defendants is otherwise, as the D. W.1 has stated that the land in suit is on the south of the temple road, that Jagabondhu's shop is west of the land in suit and D.W.4 has stated that the land in suit is of plot No.792. From the appellant's side a feeble argument was made as to acquisition of title by the defendants by adverse possession. There was no pleading of the defendants as to acquisition or claim of title in the land in suit by adverse possession. The appellate Court considered the aforesaid contention of the defendants and in the background of the materials on record held that papers i.e. Ext. C, Ext. D and the Exts. B-B(2) series have not given rise to any claim of adverse possession by the defendants since the admitted position is that R.S. and P.S. record of rights stand in the name of Mela Committee and the Ext. D and B series are the papers subsequent to the dispossession of the plaintiff from the land in suit by the defendants and inspite of the fact stated in Ext. C the land was recorded in the name of the Mela Committee and that in Ext. C name of the defendants do not appear and that in Miscellaneous Case No.95 wherein order was made on 25.11.1961 (Ext. C) the defendants were not parties. On the top of everything no evidence was lead from the side of defendants to establish the case of acquisition of title in the land in suit by adverse possession. It has also been submitted from the side of the appellants that in case decree is passed in the suits that would violate the provision of Rule 9 of Order 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The submission so made is of no merit since description of the land in suit as given in the schedule is quite sufficient to identify the same both by referring to the boundary as well as by referring to the survey plot number.

parties:
Nur Amin and others ------ Appellants
Vs.
Abdul Quddus and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: This is defendants appeal by leave against the judgment dated July 31, 2000 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 356 of 1990 making the Rule absolute upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated October 9, 1989 of the Court of District Judge, Noakhali, in Title Appeal No. 282 of 1987 allowing the same and thereby dismissing the suit upon reversing the judgment and decree dated November 18, 1987 of the Court of Assistant Judge, Upazilla Companiganj, Noakhali in Title Suit No. 54 of 1985 decreeing the same. The suit was filed seeking declaration that the judgment and decree dated 18-2-1980 passed in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 is null and void and the same is inoperative in respect of the land described in the schedule attached to the plaint. 

 2. The suit was filed stating, infer alia. that land of plot No. 203 of Mouza Dakhin Musapur was recorded in the name of the Government in khas khatian No.1, that the said plot comprises 100.80 acres of land, that Government took decision to settle the said land by sub-plotting to different persons, that Mohammad Mia, father of the plaintiffs, a retired defence person, took settlement of 2.50 acres of land of sub-plot No. 203/31 of plot No. 203 in 1968-69 on payment of salami amounting to Taka 125 through DCR dated April 24, 1970 and paid rent for the year 1376 BS by the rent receipt dated April 24, 1970 and he went into possession in 1970, that on the death of Mohammad Mia the plaintiffs were substituted in the settlement case on December 20, 1972 and kabuliyat was executed in favour of the plaintiffs by the Government on July 11, 1981, that defendant Nos. 1- 5 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 in the 2nd Court of Monsif (now Assistant Judge), Noakhali impleading Government as defendant and obtained decree in respect of the land of sub-plot No. 203/31 on February 14, 1980, that in the said suit i.e. Title Suit No. 43 of 1978, plaintiffs were not made parties, that the defendants on the basis of the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 got their names mutated in respect of the land of sub-plot No. 203/31, that the plaintiffs came to know from the Revenue Officer, that on obtaining the certified copy of the plaint and the decree it was noticed by the plaintiffs that the plaintiffs of the said suit i.e. Title Suit No. 43 of 1978, who are defendant Nos. 1-5 in the instant suit filed the said suit seeking declaration of their title in respect of the land of plot No. 203 and not sub-plot No. 203/31 but the defendant Nos.1-5 surreptitiously inserted in the decree sub-plot No. 203/31, that as the said decree in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 clouded the title of the plaintiffs in respect of the land of plot No. 203/31 they were constrained to file the suit, that cause of action arose on May 20, 1985 on which date they obtained the certified copy of the plaint and the decree of the Title Suit No. 43 of 1978. 

 3. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1-5 by filing joint written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that Afazuddin Mia was the owner and possessor of 2.50 acres of land of plot No. 7825 in mouza Musapur and in his name DS Khatian No. 2376 was prepared, that Afazuddin Mia died leaving the defendants as his heirs and after the death of Afazuddin Mia defendants continued possession, that during the diara survey land of DS plot No. 7825 was erroneously recorded in plot No. 203/31 and the khatian No.1 was prepared erroneously in the name of the Government. that the said wrong record having had clouded the title of the defendants they were constrained to file Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 seeking declaration of title in respect of 2.50 acres of land of plot No. 203/31 which is identical to the land of DS Plot No. 7825. 

 4. The Government contested the suit i.e. Title Suit No. 43 of 1978, by filing written statement and having had raised objection as to the identity of the land local investigation was held by survey knowing Advocate Commissioner for ascertaining the identity of the land in suit and the Advocate Commissioner filed his report stating that the land of plot No. 203/31 and land of DS plot No. 7825 are identical, that the Government in its written statement did not disclose that the land in suit was leased out to the plaintiffs predecessor. The suit, i.e. Title Suit No. 43 of 1978, was decreed on contest on February 18, 1980, that the allegation of forgery in the decree of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 is not true. that plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the land of plot No. 203/31. 

 5. The trial Court on consideration of the materials on record decreed the suit upon holding that Exhibit 2 i.e. kabuliyat, shows that the land in suit i.e. land of plot No. 203/31, was settled to plaintiffs father, that plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 surreptitiously inserted dag No. 203/31 in the decree of the said suit, that the identity of the land which was the subject matter of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was uncertain, that land of plot No. 203/31 was settled to plaintiffs predecessor in 1968-69 and as such, in 1978 when the defendant Nos.1-5 filed Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 they had no right, title and interest, that plaintiffs were necessary parties in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 but without impleading them the defendant Nos.1-5 obtained decree in the said suit, that in the usual course of transaction it can be said that plaintiffs father on payment of salami obtained possession of the land of plot No. 203/31 settled to him, that had the plaintiffs being not in possession they would not have executed the kabuliyat on July 11, 1981, that on perusal of the plaint of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 it is difficult to say that decree in the said suit was in respect of the land in suit i.e. land of plot No. 203/31 that as the defendant Nos. 1-5 had obtained the decree in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 without impleading the plaintiffs, as such, the decree so obtained is not binding on the plaintiffs. 

 6. Defendant Nos.1-5 went on appeal. The appellate Court on scrutiny of the original plaint (as well as the draft copy of the plaint which was produced before the Court at the time of hearing of the appeal) of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 arrived at the finding that the plaintiffs of the said suit filed the suit seeking declaration of their title in respect of 2.50 acres of land of Plot No. 203/31 which is identical to the land of DS plot No. 7825, that the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 in the face of objection taken as to the identity of the land by the Government prayed for local investigation for ascertaining the identity of the land of plot No. 203/31 and DS plot No. 7825 and in the petition for ascertaining identity of the land of the said Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 plot No. 203/31 was mentioned and the Civil Court Commissioner on ascertaining the land of DS plot No. 7825 and diara plot No. 203/31 submitted the report to the effect that 2.50 acres of land of DS plot No. 7825 is identical to 2.50 acres of land of plot No. 203/31, that the decree in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was drawn showing plot No. 203/31, that some unscrupulous person interpolated the decree passed in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 by overwriting figure 31 with a motive to show that the said figure has been inserted therein, that in the OCR dated April 24, 1970 whereby plaintiffs father was said to have paid salami originally dag number was 203/11 but later on figure 11 was changed to 31 and the change so made is quite visible in the DCR that no rent receipt has been filed although plaintiffs averred in the plaint that they paid the rent on April 24, 1970, that on the death of plaintiffs father the kabuliyat dated July 11, 1981 was executed in their names and therein plot No. 203/31 was mentioned, that plaintiffs have not filed any paper showing that their father or they were inducted in the land of plot No. 203/31 in 1376 BS, that as the plaintiffs came in the scene in July, 1981 and, as such, they were not necessary parties in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 which was decreed in February, 1980, that as the Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was decreed in presence of the Government in respect of the land of plot No. 203/31, the Government had no right to lease out the land in suit to the plaintiffs, that the plaintiffs have not called for the record to show that their father was the proponent for plot No. 203/31, that the plaintiffs are not competent to build a case on the basis of erroneous certified copy of the plaint upon interpolation of the figure 31 below dag number 203 by unscrupulous person, that the finding of the trial Court that the defendants obtained decree in respect of the block plot No. 203 is not correct since in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 identity of the land i.e. land of DS plot No. 7825 and diara plot No. 203/31, was ascertained and found identical. The appellate Court on consideration .of the evidence of the plaintiffs held that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession in the land in suit and finally, the appellate Court held that the plaintiffs have neither title nor possession in the land in suit and thereupon dismissed the suit upon setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The plaintiffs then moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. 

 7. The. High Court Division upon making the findings that the land in suit stands recorded in the name of the Government, that in the plaint of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 dag number 203 was mentioned but in the decree dag No. 203/31 was mentioned, that the trial Court disbelieved the case of the defendants, that land of plot No. 203/31 was settled in the name of plaintiffs father who paid the salami and went into possession, that insertion of plot No. 203/31 in the decree of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was mysterious, that plaintiffs were necessary parties in the Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 and, as such, decree in the said suit is not binding upon the plaintiffs, that the appellate Court did not consider the material fact and thereupon reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court and that the appellate Court wrongly held that the plaintiffs were not in possession in spite of the fact that land in suit was settled to plaintiffs father who on payment of salami went into possession and that plaintiffs case of being in possession of the land has been supported by PW 2, that the land in suit having been recorded in the name of the Government and the Government having had settled the land to the different lessees including the father of the plaintiffs as back as in 1968-69 and the fact of settlement to the father of the plaintiffs having not been denied by the defendant Nos. 1-5 and that on the date when Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was filed by the defendant Nos. 1-5 as the plaintiffs were owning and possessing the land of plot No. 203/31 and their names were recorded in the record of right, that plot No. 203/31 was wrongly inserted in the decree of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 although the said plot was not mentioned in the plaint, that Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was instituted long after the settlement of plot No. 203/31 to plaintiffs' father and that the plaintiffs of the instant suit were necessary parties in the said Title Suit made the Rule absolute upon observing that the trial Court "rightly decreed the suit in part but the learned District Judge reversed the judgment and decree against the weight of evidence, as such, the same is not sustainable in law" 

 8. Leave was granted to consider the contentions that in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 there was local investigation for establishing identity of land of DS plot No. 7825 and the land of Diara Plot No. 203/31 and the report of the survey commissioner was that the land of the said plots is identical, that the appellate Court on scrutiny of the materials, particularly DCR by which plaintiffs' father paid the salami, noticed that in the DCR plot number was 203/11 but later on by overwriting figure 11 was converted to 31 and that the plaintiffs by calling for record of the settlement case did not establish that the settlement case was initiated in the name of plaintiffs' father for the settlement of land of plot No. 203/31. 

 9. The learned' Counsel for the appellants submits that the appellants brought sufficient materials on record to establish that Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was filed in respect of the land of plot No. 203/31 and in the said Title Suit Government took objection as to the identity of the land in suit i.e. whether land of DS plot No. 7825 comprising 2.50 acres of land identical to the land of Diara Plot No. 203/31 comprising 2.50 acres of land and thereupon by local inspection the identity of the land was ascertained and the identity of the land having been ascertained the Court decreed the suit, i.e. Title Suit No. 43 of 1978, on February 25, 1980 against the Government. The decree so passed in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was not challenged by the Government. That being the state of the matter the plaintiff-respondents in whose name kabuliyat was executed by tile Government on July 11, 1991 were not competent to challenge the title of the defendant- appellants since prior to the execution of the kabuliyat by the Government, the Government ceased to be the owner of the land of Diara Plot No. 203/31. The learned Advocate also submits that the appellate Court being the last Court of fact on scrutiny of the materials on record as well as the evidence, both oral and documentary, having had arrived at the finding that the plaintiffs i.e. respondent Nos.1-4 herein, filed the instant suit on the basis of fictitious certified copy of the decree in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 and the said finding being based on consideration of the evidence, both oral and documentary, and the appellate Court having had not misread or left out of consideration the evidence in arriving at the said finding the High Court Division without discussing the evidence on record and without arriving at a finding that the aforesaid finding of the appellate Court was based on non consideration or misreading of the evidence was in serious error in reversing the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court. The learned Advocate further submits that the suit i.e. Suit No. 54 of 1985, was filed on the basis of interpolated DCR dated 24-4-1970 (Exhibit 1) and the finding of the appellate Court that Exhibit 1 has been interpolated for the purpose of filing the suit being based on consideration, of the evidence and upon scrutiny of the document itself the High Court Division without reversing the said finding of the appellate Court was in error in setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court. The learned Advocate continues that the High Court Division having had not reversed the aforesaid finding as regard Exhibit 1, nor having had held that the said finding of the appellate Court was not based on evidence or, rather to the contrary, to the evidence on record, was in error in reversing the judgment of the lower appellate Court. It has been submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellants that there is no holding in the name of the plaintiffs and also there is no khatian in the name of the plaintiffs in respect of the land in suit and that no material was placed on record from the side of the plaintiffs to show that on the partial payment of the salami plaintiffs father was inducted into the land for the settlement whereof the Settlement Case No. 20973 of 1968-69 was started. 

 10. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellants, the leaned Advocate-on-Record submits that the High Court Division has quite legally set aside the judgment of the appellate Court since prior to the filing of the Title Suit No. 43 of 1978, plaintiffs father got settlement of the land as regard which Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was filed and that as in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 plaintiffs were not made parties, the judgment and decree therein is not binding on the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate-on-Record also submits that the High Court Division on consideration of the evidence of PW 2 has quite correctly held that the plaintiffs are in possession of the land in suit. The learned Advocate-on-Record further submits that the High Court Division was quite correct in holding on the date of institution of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 the plaintiffs were owning and possessing the suit land and their names were recorded in the records of right but in the decree Dag No. 203/31 was wrongly inserted although it was not written in the plaint. Since the Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was instituted long after the settlement of the suit land in the name of the plaintiffs father, the plaintiffs were necessary parties in the suit and the learned Assistant Judge rightly decreed the suit in part 

 12. It was the case of defendant-appellants that land measuring 2.50 acres of DS Plot No. 7825 of Mouza Musapur bearing DS khatian No. 2376 was owned by their father Afazuddin Mia and that during diara survey land of the aforesaid plot of DS khatian No. 2376 was wrongly recorded in Diara plot No. 203/31 in the name of the Government and in the background of the said fact defendant- appellants filed Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 impleading the Government as defendant. In the said suit Government took objection as to the identity of the land in suit contending that the land of DS plot No. 7825 of DS khatian No. 2376 is not the land of diara plot No. 203/31. Thereupon plaintiffs of the said suit i.e. Title Suit No. 43 of 1978, filed an application for ascertaining identity of the land in suit by a survey knowing Advocate Commissioner, that the land of DS plot No. 7825 of DS khatian No. 2376 and the land of Plot No. 203/31 was relayed by a survey knowing Advocate Commissioner and he submitted the report in the affirmative i.e. land of diara plot No. 203/31 is identical to the land of DS plot No. 7825 of DS khatian No. 2376. Thereupon suit was decreed on February 25, 1980. It may be mentioned kabuliyat in the name of the plaintiffs was executed on July 11, 1981. In that state of the matter no title as regard the land said to have been settled to the plaintiffs vested on the execution of the kabuliyat. Since kabuliyat in the name of plaintiffs was executed on July 11, 1981 and, as such, while Title Suit No. 43 ofl978 was filed plaintiff-respondents were not necessary parties because at the time of filing the suit title as regard the land of said Title Suit was with the Government and accordingly Government was impleaded as defendant in the said suit and the Government contested the suit and the suit was decreed on contest in favour of the defendant appellants. In the afore state of the matter, the High Court Division, in our view, was in serious error in holding that in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 plaintiff-respondents were necessary parties as kabuliyat was executed in their names on July 11, 1981. It may be mentioned by the decree dated February 25, 1980 in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 title in respect of the land of plot No. 203/31 vested in the defendant-appellants. As stated hereinbefore although High Court Division observed that the record of right was in the name of the respondent Nos.1-4 herein but the said finding was made quite contrary to the materials on record in that, record of right, if any, could be prepared in the name of the respondent Nos.1-4 only after execution of the kabuliyat i.e. after 11th July, 1981. The High Court Division has observed that the possession of plaintiff-respondents in the land in suit was proved by the evidence of PW 2. With due deference to the learned Judge of the said Division we like to observe the learned Judge without discussing the evidence of the PW 2 made the finding as regard possession of plaintiff-respondents. The appellate Court on discussion of the evidence of PW 2 discarded the evidence of the said witness since the witness was of a different village that could not say the land in suit is of which particular mouza. The appellate Court also noticed that the witness is not a man of locality where the land in suit situates and also the witness has no land in the neighbor hood of the land in suit. Since the Court of fact on due scrutiny and consideration of the evidence of PW 2 found him an unreliable witness on the question of possession of the plaintiff-respondent Nos.1-4 in the land in suit the High Court Division in the absence of arriving at a finding that the consideration of the evidence as made by the last Court of fact perverse was in error in holding that PW 2 proved the possession of the plaintiff-respondent Nos.1-4. It may be mentioned that plaintiff No.4 examined himself as PW 1 and examined PW 2 in support of their case. The High Court Division without setting aside the finding of the last Court of fact arrived at on detailed consideration of the materials on record that the plaintiff-respondents filed the suit on the basis of fictitious certified copy of the decree of the Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 reversed the judgment of the appellate Court. It has not been held by the High Court Division that the finding of the lower appellate Court as to that plaintiffs filed the suit on fictitious certified copy was contrary to the evidence on record or that was based on non consideration and misreading of the evidence. In the absence of said situation the High Court Division in its revisional jurisdiction was not well founded in law to set aside the finding of the last Court of fact. The lower appellate Court on examination of the papers filed by the defendant-respondents in support of their case held that in the plaint of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 plot No. 203/31 was mentioned, but some unscrupulous persons blurred the figure 31 by over writing and thereafter replaced the said figure by different ink "with a motive to show that the number '31' was subsequently inserted below the number '203' with motive to create suspicion". The lower appellate Court also noticed that in DCR No. 40388 dated 24-4-1970 (Exhibit I) originally plot number was 203/11 but later on the same was changed to 203/31. The aforesaid finding of the appellate Court is based on critical examination of the DCR (Exhibit 1). It may be mentioned that had the plaintiff respondent Nos.I-4 been in enjoyment of the land or in other words, had plaintiffs father been inducted into possession of the land on the date of payment of the part of the salami on 24-4-1970 they would have certainly paid rent for the period starting from April 24, 1970 till the date of execution of the kabuliyat on July 11, 1981 but from the plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1-4's side no rent receipt was filed although pleading that they paid rent. The lower appellate Court also noticed that no khatian was opened in the name of the plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1-4. The appellate Court on consideration of the aforesaid facts as well as the other materials on record as mentioned hereinbefore arrived at a finding that plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1-4 were not in possession of the land in suit. It may be mentioned in Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 the Government raised question of identity of the land of DS Plot No. 7825 of DS khatian No. 2376 with the land of diara plot No. 203/31 of khatian No. 1. In the background of the said objection raised by the Government plaintiff of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 filed an application for relaying the land by survey knowing Advocate Commissioner. The lower appellate Court on perusal of the application so filed noticed that therein plot No. 203/31 was written. The lower appellate Court examined the original plaint of Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 and noticed that the plaintiffs filed the suit seeking declaration of title in respect of plot No. 203/31. The defendant-appellants filed sufficient materials before the Court wherefrom the appellate Court was satisfied that the Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was filed in respect of diara plot No. 203/31. The High Court Division without considering the materials noticed and considered by the lower appellate Court in arriving at the finding that Title Suit No. 43 of 1978 was filed in respect of the land of plot No. 203/31 and the said suit was contested by the Government and the Court decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs i.e. the appellants herein, set aside the judgment of the lower appellate Court. It is seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that the said Division set aside the judgment of the appellate Court without arriving at the finding that the findings arrived at by the last Court of fact i.e. lower appellate Court, was not based on evidence or that contrary to the evidence on record or that the lower appellate Court made the findings while dismissing the suit without considering as well as upon misreading the evidence on record The revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division in interfering with the finding of fact arrived at by the last Court of fact is limited to the one or more situations as stated here in over and in the absence of the said state of the matter it is beyond the jurisdiction of the High Court Division to interfere with finding of fact of the lower appellate Court and thereupon to reverse the judgment of the lower appellate Court.

caseno: Civil Revision No. 1461 of 2003 with Civil Revision No. 1462 of 2003.
parties:
Tara Bibi alias Tahera Begum & ors ----- Defendants-Petitioners 
vs. 
Salma Rani & ors  ----- Plaintiffs-Opposite
full_judgment:
The Rule in Civil Revision No. 1461 of 2003 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30-11-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-in-charge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999 (heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999) dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 25.2.1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 (heard analogous with Title Suit No. 22 of 1992) decreeing the suit. 

 2. The Rule in Civil Revision No. 1462 of 2003 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30.11.2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-in-charge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999 (heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999) dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 25.2.1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 (heard analogous with Title Suit No. 23 of 1992) dismissing the suit. 

 3. Short facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are, that the predecessor-in-interest of the Opposite Party Nos. 1-14 named Emdaduddin, as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 480 of 1978, subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 in the 1" Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka impleading Md Soleman, the predecessor-in-interest of petitioner No. 1 of this Rule seeking for the following relief: 

 4. The defendant Md. Soleman Ali submitted a Written Statement on 3-5-1979 in Title Suit No. 480 of 1979, subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 denying the material statements made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that he is the sixteen annals owner of the property mentioned in the schedule 'A' and 'B' by purchase on the strength of a registered lease deed of perpetuity dated 4-6-1956 being No. 6096 and by a deed of purchase of Quit Rent, being No. 6097 dated 4-6-1956 on payment of proper consideration from real owners. Since the date of purchase the defendant has been owning and possessing the schedule "A" property by erecting new structures thereon and living with the members of his family and carrying on business in a portion of it on getting his name recorded in the record of rights and on payment of rent to the proper authority and his name was also duly mutated in the Dacca Municipality and he is also paying Municipal taxes, WASA and Electric bills. The plaintiff was known to the defendant for a pretty long time and he was a peon, serving at settlement office at Dhaka, used to come to the defendant in times of need for help and the defendant also helped the plaintiff in various ways and after liberation of Bangladesh the plaintiff having no accommodation for himself and his family at Dhaka, approached the defendant allowing him to live in "B" Schedule property as his licensee, which is a small portion of "A" schedule property and the defendant out of sympathy as licensee allowed the plaintiff to live in a portion of suit land. The defendant is a Non Bengali Urdu speaking person who came from India as a refugee in the year 1950, after partition of India. After liberation war of 1971 and creation of Bangladesh the defendant had to remain absent from his house for some time leaving the schedule property (house) and business establishment including machineries thereof in the care, custody and supervision of the plaintiff on whom the defendant reposed full confidence, belief and trust. After liberation and during the disturbed post -liberation period the defendant could not manage his business and other family affairs and he had to depend on the plaintiff for such management. At that relevant period the plaintiff disclosed that to manage the business establishment and to look after the schedule property he requires a Power of Attorney in his favour by the defendant and the plaintiff had been constantly pressing for the same. In that state of affairs, the defendant had no other alternative but to agree to the proposal of the plaintiff and accordingly, a Power of Attorney was being got drafted by the plaintiff and the defendant was taken to the office of the Sub-Registrar, Dhaka for such registration of the same but the Sub-Registrar refused to register the same, on the plea that no Non Bengali is permitted under the present law to authorise or register any document in favour of anybody without permission from Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka. Being failure to get Power of Attorney registered in favour of the plaintiff by the defendant the plaintiff on a subsequent date took the defendant before one Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka and he was made to swear an affidavit dated 3-2-1973 giving the plaintiff authority and power to manage the affairs of the defendant. Even after swearing the above affidavit the plaintiff made several attempts to get a Power of Attorney executed and registered in favour of the plaintiff by the defendant and the defendant was taken to the Sub-Registrar's Office but no Power of Attorney could be registered although several attempts were made by the plaintiff in this regard. Since after liberation the plaintiff has been living in the "B" Schedule property, which is a small portion of the north eastern portion of the "A" Schedule property as a licensee of the defendant. The plaintiff being a local man and the defendant being a non-local had to get his business managed and he was also required to do other family affairs of the defendant at the relevant period. Curiously enough, the defendant got a notice from the Settlement office in the 1st week of September 1977, in the absence of the plaintiff wherein the defendant found that the plaintiff had filed an objection petition for canceling the name of the defendant in respect of the "A" schedule property in the recent RS Operation and for getting his name recorded. On the date of hearing of the said Objection Petition No. 329 of 1977 the defendant was present and raised objection and produced the relevant papers and documents in support of his title in respect of the schedule property to the Settlement Officer who on perusal of the papers and documents in possession of the defendant was pleased to reject the prayer of the plaintiff and upheld the previous record stood in the name of the defendant for the schedule property. On getting the notice from settlement office the defendant got suspicious about the activities and trustworthiness of the plaintiff and later on, the defendant came to learn that the plaintiff dishonestly removed all his machineries including a printing press machine and other goods and articles of the defendant from the said holding causing a loss of huge amount of Taka to the defendant and misappropriated the said amount. Some time thereafter, the defendant got a show cause notice and adinterim injunction notice of the instant suit from the Court, and the defendant caused his appearance on 14-11-1978 in the said suit and prayed for time to file Written Statement and on reading the plaint, the defendant could firstly come to know that the plaintiff had got a fraudulent and forged sale deed registered in his name in respect of the "A" schedule property by false personification. Thereafter, the defendant obtained a certified copy of the said forged and fraudulent document on 3-4-1979 and definitely could come to learn that a forged, fraudulent, collusive and illegal document has been created in favour of the plaintiff on false personification of the defendant to grab the valuable property of the defendant beyond his knowledge and without making any payment of consideration money whatsoever. The defendant did not put signatures on the said alleged sale deed. His signatures on the alleged document have been forged by some other person. All signatures as contained in the said deed are not the signature of the defendant and the said deed is forged, fraudulent and collusive deed and the deed was created by false personification. The defendant did not execute any sale deed for a sum of Taka 7,000.00 or for any amount on or before 13-11-1973 or any other date in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the schedule property or any portion thereof. The defendant had no or has no necessity of selling his only residential scheduled property. The said false, forged, collusive and illegal document has been created by the plaintiff in collusion with the scribe and other witnesses of the said alleged deed by illegally influencing them and some other lower category staff of the Sub-Registrar's office without making payment of any consideration money whatsoever. At that time the valuation of the property was much more than Taka 7000. The defendant did not put any signatures on any papers for bringing out Income Tax and Capital Gain Tax Certificates. Any certificates produced for registration of the said forged sale deed must have been produced by the plaintiff forging the signatures of the defendant and the plaintiff must be prosecuted for the criminal acts done by him. No right, title and interest have been passed to the plaintiff on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, illegal and void document and the plaintiff cannot seek any relief in the Court of law on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive, illegal and void document. The defendant is the lawful, rightful and absolute sixteen annas owner of the schedules properties. By creation of such a forged, fraudulent, illegal and void document the defendant's right, title and interest in the scheduled properties have not been affected in any way. The defendant informed the respectable persons in the locality about the illegal, fraudulent and collusive activities of the plaintiff and they made attempts to settle the matter amicably but failed. The defendant has filed the Title Suit No. 98 of 1979 in the 6th Court of Munsif, Dhaka against the plaintiff for cancellation of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive and illegal document and also for recovery of khas possession of the "B" schedule property as described in the schedule below after evicting the plaintiff therefrom. 

 5. The defendant Nos. 5-8 submitted a Written Statement on 14-2-1983 adopting the Written Statement submitted by the main defendant Md. Soleman and also claimed that they have purchased the suit property contending, inter alia, that Md Soleman was a Urdu-speaking man who came from India as a refugee in the year 1950, after partition of India and he was the owner and possessor of the entire suit property in his own right till his death. He could not read and write in Bengali. He always used to put his signature in English. He did not sign his name any where in any documents in Bengali. Md Soleman did not execute the alleged sale deed in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the suit holding. He had no reason or necessity to sell his only residential house—the suit holding. He had other sources of income to maintain his family. The plaintiff created the alleged sale deed fraudulently and in collusion with the scribe and other attesting witnesses without payment of consideration money whatsoever to grab the valuable property of said Md Soleman. The original owner Md Soleman did not put any signature on any papers for bringing out Income Tax and Capital Gain Tax Certificate. The plaintiff created the alleged sale deed in his favour by forging the signatures of said Md Soleman beyond his knowledge. His signatures on the alleged document have been forged by some other person. All the signatures as contained in the said deed are forged, fraudulent, void and collusive and are created by false personification. No right, title and interest have passed to the plaintiff on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, illegal and void document, and the plaintiff cannot seek any relief in the Court of law on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive, illegal and void document. By creating of such a forged, fraudulent illegal and void document, the defendant's right, title and interest in the schedule properties have not been affected in any way. The original defendant late Md Soleman had filed the Title Suit No. 98 of 1979 in the 6th Court of Munsif, Dhaka and the said suit of transfer to the Court has been renumbered as being Title Suit No. 516 of 1981. For cancellation of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive and illegal document and also for recovery of khas possession of the "B" schedule property as described in the plaint of the said suit, after evicting the plaintiff there from. These defendants purchased the entire suit holding from the heirs and successors of late Md Soleman in the year 1982 and they have been owning and possessing the same since their date of purchase and, at present, they are the real owners and possessors of the said property 

 6. Md Soleman on receipt of the notice of Title Suit No. 480 of 1978 presented a Title Suit being No. 98 of 1979 on 6-4-1979 before the 6th Court of Munsif, Dhaka seeking for the following relief: 

 (c) for passing a decree declaring that the plaintiffs are the rightful owners of the properties described in the schedule’s" and to deliver khas possession of the 'B' schedule property to the plaintiff after evicting the defendant there from with all his men and materials in execution of the decree;" imp leading Emdaduddin (the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 480 of 1978 and subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 to be the sole defendant) incorporating the whole case as made out in the written statement of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992. 

 7. Emdaduddin, the defendant (the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 480 of 1978 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992) submitted a Written Statement in Title Suit No. 98 of 1979 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 denying the material statements made in the plaint and incorporating the entire case as made out in the plaint of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992. 

 8. Thereafter, the Title Suit No. 480 of 1978 was transferred to the Court of learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.1, Dhaka and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992. 

 9. The Title Suit No. 98 of 1979 was also transferred to the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 22 of 1992. 

 (iii) Whether the plaintiff and the defendant has got their title and possession in the 'A' schedule to the plaint and whether they are licensee under the plaintiff of the respective suits in respect of 'B' schedule land to the plaint? 

 (iv) Whether the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 is entitled to get a decree for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in respect of 16 annals share in 'A' schedule land and entitled to get a recovery of khas possession in respect of 'B' schedule land to the plaint? 

 (v) Whether the kabala deed being No. 27265 dated 13-11-1973 in respect of 'A' schedule land to the plaint is forged and not binding upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 and whether the said deed is liable to be declared cancelled and whether the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree for recovery of khas possession in respect of 'B' schedule land as against the defendant of the suit? 

 (vi) What more relief the plaintiff is entitled to get? 

 11. The Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 was taken up for trial as being the parent suit and evidence was led in the said suit. 

 12. During tendency of the suit the plaintiff Emdaduddion and the defendent Soleman had died and their heirs were substituted. In Title Suit No. 23 of 1992, the following persons were made defendant (1) the Chairman, Water and Sewerage Authority, Ramna Chamber (2) Circle Officer (Revenue), Kotwali Circle, (3) Executive Engineer, Dhaka Electric Supply, English Road, (4) Md Khairul Alam (5) Md Nur Alamgir (6) Md Mohiuddin Alamgir (7) Md Intaz Ali Miah. 

 13. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 examined 3 PWs. The kabala deed in question dated 13-11-1973 alleged to have been executed by Soleman in favour of the plaintiff was marked as Exhibit 1. Some rent-receipts showing payment of rent after filing of the suit was marked as Exhibit 2, 2(Ka) and one rent-receipt showing payment of rent on 15-4-1977 was marked as Exhibit 2(Kha). Electric bill paid by the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 for the month of July 1980, July 1981 and May 1981 was marked as Exhibit 3, 3(ka) and 3(Kha) and one receipts showing payment of sewerage bill for the month of May, 1977 was marked as Exhibit 3. It is to be stated here that after the death of Soleman his heirs and legal representatives were imp leaded as plaintiff Nos. 1 (a)-1 (p) in the Title Suit No. 22 of 1992. In total 7 DWs were examined by the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 and their documents were admitted into evidence as being A(1)-A(7), B series, C, D, E, F, F(1), G, H, I, J, K(1), L, M series, N, 0 series, P, Q series, R series, S, T, U. 

 14. The learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka decreed the Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 and dismissed the Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 by the judgment and decree dated 25-2-1999. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree preferred Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999 and defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 preferred Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999 as against the said judgment and decree. 

 16. The defendants of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree have obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 1461 of 2003 and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 1462 of 2003 as against the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999. Both the Rules having arisen out of the same judgment and having been disposed off analogously this Court took up both the Rules together for disposal analogously. 

 17. Mr Mohammad Habibullah, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, on appearing before this Court, submitted that the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 having specifically pleaded that the Exhibit 1 was not executed by Soleman, that deed was created by false personification, and that no payment of consideration was made as against the said deed and Soleman did not execute the said deed it was the duty of the trial Court to decide specifically as to whether the said deed was executed by Soleman and any consideration was passed against the said deed. He submitted that the trial Court without giving any finding upon those vital facts decreed the suit in a slip shod manner. He further submitted that the defendant Nos. 5-8 have specifically pleaded in the Written Statement that Soleman was not conversant with the Bengali writing and could not know how to put his signature in Bengali but the deed in question was shown to have been executed in Bengali. He submitted the same to be a forged deed out and out. He further submitted that the defendant (the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992) by producing Exhibits D, K, M, Ml, O, O(1)-O(4) and also by adducing oral evidence has been able to prove the fact that Soleman used to put his signature in English, he did not put his signature ever in Bengali. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 had onus to prove due execution of Exhibit 1 by Soleman and also had onus to prove that consideration of Taka 7,000.00 was received by Solaiman as against the deed but the plaintiff has hopelessly failed to prove due execution of the said deed (Exhibit 1) and also failed to prove payment of consideration by adducing evidence either oral or documentary. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 also failed to prove that any possession was handed over in his favour on the strength of Exhibit 1. He submitted further that the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka without coming to his own finding as to execution of Exhibit 1 by Soleman and as to payment of consideration as against Exhibit 1 and as to delivery of possession as against Exhibit 1, blindly and erroneously held the Exhibit 1 to be a valid deed, only upon considering the fact, that Soleman did not make any attempt for getting compared his admitted LTI with the LTI as contained in the back of page 1 of Exhibit 1. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 has sought for recovery of khas possession in the 'B' schedule land in the plaint against Soleman alleging him to be a licensee under him. But the Courts below neither gave any finding upon the said relief nor discussion and considered any evidence in support of the said positive case of the plaintiff. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 by adducing 7 DWs and by exhibiting huge number of documents have been able to prove that Soleman did not ever put his signature in Bengali during his lifetime. He submitted that they have been able to prove that the Exhibit 1 was a forged deed out and out and have been able to prove too that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 was given accommodation as a licensee in a part of the suit homestead, in 1972 but the trial Court and as well as the appellate Court without discussing a single evidence, adduced by the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992, illegally dismissed their suit and decreed the other suit and the appellate Court, being the last Court of fact neither discussed any evidence nor gave his own finding in affirming the judgment of the trial Court. He submitted that onus heavily lay upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 to prove due execution of Exhibit 1. by Soleman, payment of consideration made by PW 1 and acceptance of said consideration by Soleman and handing over possession of the suit property by Soleman in favour of the PW 1 but the PW 1 having failed to do so by adducing evidence and the DW 17 by adducing oral and documentary evidence having been able to prove that the Exhibit 1 was a forged deed out and out, the judgment and decree impugned in the Rule are although concurrent is liable to be interfered by this Court in revision. He relied upon the case law upon onus of proving due execution of Exhibit 1 as reported in 1987 BLD (AD) 306. 

 18. Mr Md Lutfor Rahman Mondal, the learned Advocate for the opposite party on appearing before this Court, on the other hand, submitted that in view of section 101 of the Evidence Act, the burden of proof of the pleadings case cannot be shifted. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 came up before the Court with a specific pleadings but they failed to discharge their onus as per law. He further submitted that the Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 was filed during life time of Soleman and he died long after four years of filing of the suit but said Soleman did not make any attempt to compare the LTI as contained in the back of page No 1 of Exhibit 1 with his admitted LTI. He further submitted that no prayer was made by Soleman for making a comparison of the signature of LTI as contained in Exhibit 1 with his admitted signature and LTI to prove that the Exhibit 1 was not executed by Soleman. He further submitted that the Exhibit 1 was admitted into evidence and was marked as Exhibit 1 without having any objection from the defendant side. He further submitted that the Exhibit 1 being a registered instrument that carries a presumption of correctness and validity. In support of his contention he relied upon the case law reported in 1993 BLD (AD) 150 and the case of Abdullah and 3 others vs Abdul Hakim and others, reported in 20 DLR (SC) 205. He further submitted that the execution of Soleman has been proved beyond doubt by the plaintiff by adducing the evidence of PW 1 and PW 2 who corroborated each other. Mr Mondal submitted that the impugned judgment and decree being the judgment of affirmance there is nothing to interfere by this Court unless a strong case of no consideration of any evidence or no reading of any evidence or misreading of any evidence on record is made out. He relied upon the case law of Azifannessa vs Sakur Miah and others, reported in 30 DLR (AD) 41. He lastly submitted that the Exhibit 1 being a registered document and having been exhibited without any objection, the same shall be presumed to be correct and valid. In support of his contention he relied upon the decision reported in 1993 BLD (AD) 114. 

 22. On perusal of the judgment of the courts below it appears that neither the learned Joint District Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka, being the trial Court, discussed and considered any evidence of the defendants of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 nor the learned Additional District Judge being the last Court of facts made any discussion and consideration of any evidence of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992. So it appears that the judgments and decrees impugned in the Rule are based upon total no consideration of the evidence, both oral and documentary as adduced by the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 and the defendants of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992. It further appears that both the Courts below decreed the Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 upon assumption on saying অনুমতি হয় Mr Lutfor Rahman Mondal, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties in both the Rules, submitted that the judgment and decree impugned in the Rules being concurrent, there is no scope to interfere with those judgment and decree in revision. Mr Lutfor Rahman Mondal further submitted that this Court in exercise of its power under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is not entitled to enter into the evidence. Mr Mondal in support of his argument cited the case law reported in 5 DLR (FC) 147 and the case law of Ajufannessa vs Safar Mia and others reported in 30 DLR (AD) 41. 

 24. On perusal of the case law of Ajufannessa vs Safar Miah and others reported in 30 DLR (SC) 41 it appears that the said suit was a suit for declaration of title. The trial Court disbelieved the plaintiff's Dakhilas, which were marked as Exhibit 4 series and that finding was affirmed by the learned Additional District Judge in appeal. That concurrent finding were disturbed by the High Court Division in 2nd appeal and upon those disturbance of concurrent findings the Appellate Division held. "concurrent finding of file s as to the genuineness of the rent-receipts found by the two lower courts in 2nd appeal to the High Court, unless such finding is vitiated by error of law or procedure such finding is binding on the High Court." The above finding of the Appellate Division is by now the established principle of law. But in the instant case, the trial Court decreed the suit keeping totally out of consideration of the entire evidence of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 92 and the evidence of defendants of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992. So I am of the view that the above case law cited by Mr Mondal is not applicable in the instant case. 

 26. In the case of Sakhina Khatun and others vs Mansur Alam and others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 160 it has been settled that "there being a total non consideration of all the witnesses of the preempted, the learned Single Judge acted wrongly in refusing to exercise his revisional jurisdiction in a case where due to total non-consideration of the material evidence on record an erroneous decision has been arrived at occasioning a failure of justice. In that decision the concurrent findings of the trial Court, Appellate Court and of the High Court was set aside by our Appellate Division. The above authority, authorizes this Court to enter into the entire evidence of both the parties in view of the facts that admittedly the Courts below have given their findings upon no considering the entire evidence of the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 92 and the evidence of plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992. 

 27. Before entering into the evidence for discussion and consideration let us decide as to whether the trial Court and as well as the lower appellate Court were justified in shifting the burden of proving the forged nature of Exhibit 1 upon the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 and upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 and was justified in decreeing the Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 for granting a decree for eviction of the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 holding him to be a licensee under the plaintiff. 

 28. Mr Lutfor Rahman Mondal submitted that the burden of proof of pleadings case does not shift and submitted that the burden of proving that the Exhibit 1 is a forged deed was upon the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 and upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992. Mr Mondal in support of his contention relied upon section 102 of the Evidence Act and upon the case-law of Kambhu Lakshmana vs Tangirala Venkateshwala reported in 2 DLR 82. On perusal of the said case law it appears that the fact of that case is quite distinguishable from the fact of the instant case and the cited case law has got no manner of application in the instant case. 

 29. The plaintiff in Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 filed the suit for declaration of title, confirmation of possession in schedule 'A' land and recovery of Khas possession in the 'B' Schedule land of the plaint against defendant Md Soleman alleging, inter alia, that Soleman sold the suit property to him by a Kabala deed dated 31-11-73 at a consideration of Taka 7000.00. Md Soleman by filing a written statement totally denied the said sale and denied his execution as contained in Exhibit 1. Md Soleman denied to have receipt of any consideration money as against the Exhibit 1. Md Solaiman categorically asserted the Exhibit 1 to be a forged deed and made out a case that the said Exhibit 1 was created by false personification. The defendant Nos. 5-8 being the subsequent purchasers from the heirs and legal representatives of defendant Soleman have stated categorically in their written statement that Soleman was a no Bengali and could not know how to write Bengali. Those defendants also brought a specific case that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 had created the Exhibit 1 by false personification with the help of scribe and witnesses of the deed. The plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 also established a specific and distinct case that Soleman did not execute the Exhibit 1 and did not receive any single farthing towards consideration from the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 as against the Exhibit 1. It is their case that the Exhibit 1 was created by Emdad, the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 by false personification with help of the deed writer of Exhibit 1 and also with the help of witnesses as mentioned in the deed. 

 30. This is by now settled that whenever the execution of a deed is totally denied and a clear case of creation of a forged document is made out by false personification, in that case, the onus of proving due execution, payment of consideration and delivery of possession in the suit land entirely rests upon the alleged purchaser who claims title upon that deed. This view finds support from the case law reported in 47 DLR 248 and the case law reported in 44 DLR 79. 

 31. In view of the above it is my considered view that the onus of proving of due execution of Exhibit 1 by Soleman and payment of consideration was rested upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992. The onus of proving of granting license to Soleman in 'B' schedule land was also rested upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992. 

 32. Now let us consider as to whether the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 by adducing PW 1, PW 3 could be able to prove due execution of Exhibit 1, payment of consideration as against that document and the fact of granting licence to Soleman by adducing legal evidence. 

 34. On perusal of the decree passed by the trial Court, it appears that the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka, without discussing and considering a single documentary evidence of the defendant and without discussing and considering the specific case of both the parties as to granting of licensee have passed the judgment and decree in a slipshod manner. From the judgment of the appellate Court it also appears that he being the last Court of fact has affirmed the judgment of the trial Court blindly in a very slipshod manner and without discussing and considering any evidence on record. On perusal of the Written Statement of the defendant Nos. 5-8, it appears that they taken a very positive case that Md Soleman did not know how to write in Bengali, he used to put his signature in English. The DWs adduced evidence in support of the said contention. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 has exhibited the passport of Md Soleman and that was marked as Exhibit B. It appears from Exhibit B that his name was written in English just at the bottom of his photograph as contained in the passport. It further appears that Soleman had sworn affidavit before the Magistrate, 1st Class on 6-11-1979 wherein he put his signature in English and that was marked as Exhibit 8. Another affidavit was sworn by Soleman on 3-2-1973 before the Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka and that was marked as Exhibit K(1), the signature as contained in the said affidavit was written in English. From the Exhibit M and M 1, it appears that Soleman was a merchant, and he entered into import trade contract under the Government of Pakistan by putting his signature in English in the year 1961. From the Exhibit 0 it appears that he made a correspondence to the Controller of Import and Export of the Government of East Pakistan and he put his signature in English and other documents the Exhibits 1, 2, 3, 4 were also signed in English by Soleman. The Exhibit K2 is another affidavit sworn by Soleman before the Magistrate, 1st Class on 20-5-1972 and that was also signed in English. On the other hand, there is not a single document produced by the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 to prove that Soleman used to put his signature in Bengali. It is true, that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 ought to have taken positive step for comparing the LTI as contained in the back of the first page of Exhibit 1 with the admitted LTI of Md Soleman but from the record it appears that the suit came up for peremptory hearing after the death of Soleman. 

 35. In the instant case, the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 having totally denied the execution of Exhibit 1 and having specifically asserted that the instrument was a forged one. The PW 1 had to prove due execution, payment of consideration. On perusal of the evidence of the PW 1 it appears that to prove the fact of execution of Md Soleman he has simply adduced in his examination-in-chief “নালিশী সম্পত্তি আমি ১৯৭৩ সনে ৭০০০ (সাত হাজার টাকা)দিয়া মোঃ সোলেমানের নিকট হইতে খরিদ করিয়াছি। দলিল নং ২৭২৬৫ তাং ৭-১১-৭৩ (প্রদঃ নং ১)এই সেই সাফ কবলা দলিল। নালিশী সম্পত্তি খরিদ করিবার পর আমাকে দখল বুঝাইয়া দেন।” Save and except this evidence there is no other evidence available on record to show that the PW 1 adduced any positive evidence to prove due execution made by Soleman. The PW 2 being another witness has adduced “বাদী মৃত সোলেমানের নিকট হইতে ক্রয় করিয়াছিলাম। ক্রয়/বিক্রয়ের সময় আমি উপস্থিত ছিলাম। বিক্রয়ের পর অর্ধেক অংশের দখল বুঝাইয়া দেয় এবং অবশিষ্ট অংশের দখল হস্তান্তরের জন্য সময় নেয়।” Save and except this evidence there is no other evidence to prove that Soleman put his signature upon Exhibit 1. The PW 3 also stated in his examination-in-chief that “বাদী ক্রয় করিয়া নালিশী সম্পত্তি প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছে।” This PW 2 and PW 3 are neither witness to the deed nor are scribes of the deed. Due execution can be proved by the following modes : (1) by calling as a witness a person who wrote the document; (2) by citing a witness who saw the writing down of the deed and saw to put signature by the executants upon the deed; (3) who is qualified to express an opinion as to the writing by virtue of section 47 of the Evidence Act; (4) by comparison of the handwriting as specified under section 73 of the Evidence Act; (5) by the admission of the person against whom the documents is tendered and (6) by expert evidence. 

 38. On perusal of Exhibit 1, it further appears that the stamps used for the purpose of writing of the deed were purchased on 30-10-1973 and the fourth page was a demy paper. The date of execution mentioning "6-11-1973" was written in a different ink and by a different person as it appears from the said deed. The stamps used for the purpose of writing of affidavit in support of the transfer were purchased on 13-11-1973. From this it is very much incredible to believe that after purchase of stamps on 13-11-1973, how could a deed be executed on 6-11-1973. Moreover, the PW 2 did not adduce a single evidence that he saw execution by Md Soleman. From this evidence it is proved beyond doubt that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 hopelessly failed to prove due execution by Md Soleman. Moreover the DW 1 could not produce any document at the trial to prove Soleman used to put his signature in Bengali. Soleman entered his appearance in the suit through an Advocate and executed Vokalatnama in English. There is no evidence on record to believe that Exhibit 1 was executed by Soleman. So, it is my considered view that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 has hopelessly failed to prove due execution of Exhibit 1 by Soleman. 

 39. So far as payment of consideration is concerned the PW 1 was put a question in the following form দলিল লিখার কয় দিন পরে টাকা পয়সা লেনদেন হইল? he replied "রেজিষ্ট্রি যেদিন হয় সেদিন লেনদেন হয়।” Thereafter, he was asked the following question দলিল লিখার কয় দিন পরে টাকা পয়সা লেনদেন হইল? at this he replied "একমাস/দেড়মাস পরে লেনদেন হয়" It is the case of plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 that the deed was written some times before 6-11-1973 and thereafter the payment was made. So as per the PW 1, the payment was made in December 73 or January 1974. The PW 2 in his cross-examination has said "বাদী সোলায়মানকে সদর সাব রেজিষ্ট্রি অফিসের নীচের তলায় টাকা দিয়াছিল। সকাল ১০-৩০ মিনিটের সময় টাকা দিয়াছিল। ঐ দিন রেজিষ্ট্রি হয়।" This evidence is quite contradictory with PW 1. There is no other evidence available on record to show that any consideration was made. From the discussions made above it is crystal clear that no execution was made by Soleman and no payment of consideration was made as against the Exhibit 1. The Courts below having failed to discuss and consider this evidence have caused a serious miscarriage of justice by the impugned judgment and decree and the same is liable to be interfered by this Court in view of the case law of Sakhina Khatoon versus Mansur Alam, reported in 48 DLR (AD) 160. 

 40. Let us decide the other issue that is, whether the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 was accorded licence to be part of the suit land by Soleman or Soleman was accorded permission to reside in "B" schedule land to the plaint by PW 1. The evidences on record are sufficient to decide this question. The Courts below although did not decide this question specifically but the evidence having been found sufficient as adduced by the DW 17, I find that this issue should be decided by this Court to meet the ends of justice in view of the case of Kabir Ahmed versus Md Nurul Islam, reported in 4 MLR (AD) 1. 

 43. On the other hand, the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 could not adduce any positive evidence to prove that Soleman was granted licence to stay in the "B" schedule land to the plaint. Upon consideration of the above evidence it is very much clear that in fact, no transfer was made by Soleman in favour of the PW 1 and the PW 1 was granted permission by Soleman to stay in a part out of the suit homestead. Both the Courts below did not discuss and consider the, above evidence. From the facts and circumstances and discussions made, I have no hesitation but to hold that the Exhibit 1 was not executed by Soleman, no payment in consideration was made against the said deed and no delivery of possession was made in favour of PW 1 on the strength of that Exhibit. The Exhibit 1 is nothing but a forged deed. The judgment and decree impugned in the Rule are not sustainable in law and are liable to be set aside. There is merit in the Rules. 

 44. In the result, both the Rules are made absolute, however, without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree dated 30-11-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-in-charge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999 (heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999) dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 25-2-1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 (heard analogous with Title Suit No. 22 of 1992) decreeing the suit is hereby set aside. The judgment and decree dated 30-11-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-in-charge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999 (heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999) dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 25-2-1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 (heard analogous with Title Suit No. 23 of 1992) dismissing the suit is also hereby set aside. Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 is hereby decreed with cost and Title Suit No. 23 of 1993 is dismissed with cost. The kabala deed alleged to have been executed by Md. Soleman on 6-11-1973 and registered on 13-11-1973 in favour of PW 1, Emdaduddin is hereby declared void and the same is cancelled. The title of plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 is hereby declared and the possession of the opposite party plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 in part of the suit land are nothing but permissive possession granted by Soleman. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 is entitled to get recovery of khas possession after evicting the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992, on execution of the decree. All further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1999 now pending in the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka appear to be not maintainable as being infructuous one.
